commands.name: Alpha
commands.description: Returns the alpha component of a color value.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The color value. This must be a 32-bit RGBA value.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the value of the alpha component. The result will be between 0 and 255.
A value of 0 means fully transparent and a value of 255 means fully opaque.
commands.remarks:
To combine red, green, blue and alpha values in order to create a 32-bit RGB color,
use the RGBA() function.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

commands.name: AlphaBlend
commands.description: Returns the resulting 32-bit color from blending the two 32-bit colors.

parameters.name: Color1
parameters.description: The color that will be in front. It is blended on to 'Color2'.

parameters.name: Color2
parameters.description: The color that will be in the back.

commands.returnValue: Returns the combined color.
commands.remarks:
The RGBA() function can be used to create 32-bit colors with alpha transparency.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

commands.name: BackColor
commands.description: Set the default background color for graphic functions and text display.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
The new color to be used as the background color.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.
Whether or not the alpha channel is used depends on the drawing mode.

A color table with common colors is available here.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: Blue
commands.description: Returns the blue component of a color value.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The color value. This can be a 24-bit RGB or a 32-bit RGBA value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the blue component. The result will be between 0 and 255.
commands.remarks:
To combine red, green and blue values in order to create a 24-bit RGB color,
use the RGB() function.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

commands.name: Box
commands.description:
Draw a box of given dimensions on the current output. The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and size of the box in the current drawing output.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the box. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      y = 0
      For x = 0 To 95 Step 10
        Box(x, y, 200-2*x, 200-2*y, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
        y + 10        ; the same as y = y + 10
      Next x
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: BoxedGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have a box shape.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description:
The location of the gradient box.
The gradient ranges from the current background color at the center
of the box to the current front color at the edges of the box.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      BoxedGradient(0, 0, 200, 200)      
      Circle(100, 100, 100)
      BoxedGradient(225, -100, 150, 400)
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: Circle
commands.description:
Draw a circle on the current output.
The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The position of the center pixel of the circle.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the circle. This radius does not include the center pixel.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the circle. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For Radius = 100 To 10 Step -10
        Circle(100, 100, Radius, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
      Next
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CircularGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have a circular shape.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The location at which to apply the current background color.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: The radius around (x, y) at which to apply the current front color.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      CircularGradient(100, 100, 100)     
      Circle(100, 100, 100)
      CircularGradient(350, 100, 75)
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ClipOutput
commands.description:
Define a bounding box that restricts all drawing to the current drawing
output. Any pixels drawn outside of this box will be clipped.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description:
The position and size of the clipping box. The (x, y) coordinates are always absolute
and not affected by calls to SetOrigin().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command only has an effect on drawing outputs created by ImageOutput() or CanvasOutput().

The drawing origin is not modified by a call to this function. To make all drawing
relative to the upper left corner of the clipping box, a separate call to
SetOrigin() must be made if this is desired.

The Plot() and Point() commands perform no bounds checking for performance reasons and
therefore are also not affected by this command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200, 24, $FFFFFF) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))

      ClipOutput(50, 50, 100, 100) ; restrict all drawing to this region
      Circle( 50,  50, 50, $0000FF)  
      Circle( 50, 150, 50, $00FF00)  
      Circle(150,  50, 50, $FF0000)  
      Circle(150, 150, 50, $00FFFF)  
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Outlined)
      Box(50, 50, 100, 100, $000000)
         
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))      
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ConicalGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have a conical shape.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The center position of the conical gradient.

parameters.name: Angle.f
parameters.description:
The angle (in degrees) at which to start the gradient.
The gradient starts with the current background color at the given angle and
then changes towards the current front color counterclockwise until the angle is reached again.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      ConicalGradient(100, 100, 0.0)     
      Circle(100, 100, 100)
      ConicalGradient(300, 0, 90.0)     
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CustomFilterCallback
commands.description:
Specifies a callback that will be called for every pixel that is part of a drawing operation in
#PB_2DDrawing_CustomFilter drawing mode.

parameters.name: @FilterCallback()
parameters.description:
The address of a callback function to call. It must have the following form:

Procedure CustomCallback(x, y, SourceColor.l, TargetColor.l)
;
; Calculate ResultColor from the given input
;
ProcedureReturn ResultColor
EndProcedure

The callback will be called for every pixel that is drawn as a result of a call to drawing functions
like Line(), Box() or DrawText(). The SourceColor
parameter specifies the color given in the drawing operation and the TargetColor parameter specifies
the color of the target pixel in the drawing area. Both colors are always 32-bit with alpha channel
independent of the color depth of the output. The callback has to calculate the color that the target
pixel should have after the drawing and return that.

The x and y coordinate received in the callback are always relative to the upper left corner of
the drawing output. The coordinates are not affected by any calls to SetOrigin() or ClipOutput().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This callback will be called many times (for every pixel to draw) so it should be very small and
fast to not have a too big impact on the drawing performance.

Note: The #PB_2DDrawing_CustomFilter drawing mode
only works on ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
commands.example:
Procedure FilterCallback(x, y, SourceColor.l, TargetColor.l)
    ; Take only the Red component from the Source, do not modify the others
    ProcedureReturn RGBA(Red(SourceColor), Green(TargetColor), Blue(TargetColor), Alpha(TargetColor))
  EndProcedure
  
  UseJPEGImageDecoder()

  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    LoadImage(1, #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/3d/Data/Textures/clouds.jpg")
  
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      DrawImage(ImageID(1), 0, 0, 400, 200)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_CustomFilter)      
      CustomFilterCallback(@FilterCallback())
      Circle(100, 100, 100, $0000FF)   
      Circle(300, 100, 100, $000000)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CustomGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have a custom shape, defined by the given callback procedure.

parameters.name: @GradientCallback()
parameters.description:
The address of a callback procedure to define the gradient.
The callback must have the following form:

Procedure.f GradientCallback(x, y)
;
; Return a value between 0.0 and 1.0 to define the gradient for the x/y position.
;
ProcedureReturn 1.0
EndProcedure

The callback will be called for every pixel that is part of a drawing operation. The callback
has to return a value between 0.0 and 1.0 (not a color value) to define the gradient value at the given position.

The x and y coordinate received in the callback are always relative to the upper left corner of
the drawing output. The coordinates are not affected by any calls to SetOrigin() or ClipOutput().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
By default the value 0.0 represents the current background color and the value 1.0 represents
the current front color.
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

This callback will be called many times (for every pixel to draw) so it should be very small and
fast to not have a too big impact on the drawing performance.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
Procedure.f GradientCallback(x, y)
    ProcedureReturn Sin(x * 0.1) * Sin(y * 0.1) ; will be between 0 and 1
  EndProcedure

  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      CustomGradient(@GradientCallback())
      Circle(100, 100, 100)   
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: DrawAlphaImage
commands.description:
Draws an image to the current drawing output using alpha-blending.
The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description:
The ID of the image to draw. This value can be obtained
using the ImageID() function from the image library.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The position of the top/left corner of the image in the drawing output.

parameters.name: ConstAlpha (optional)
parameters.description:
The amount of extra transparency to apply to the image when drawing.
The value can range from 0 (fully transparent) to 255 (fully opaque). Even images
that have no alpha channel themselves can be drawn with transparency this way.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command works on all drawing outputs, even those that do not support the alpha-blending
flags in DrawingMode().
The image will be drawn at its original size.
ResizeImage() can be used to change the size of an image.

This command cannot be used to draw Icons (loaded from .ico files).

commands.name: DrawImage
commands.description:
Draws an image to the current drawing output.
The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description:
The ID of the image to draw. This value can be obtained
using the ImageID() function from the image library.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The position of the top/left corner of the image in the drawing output.

parameters.name: Width, Height (optional)
parameters.description:
The image will be resized and drawn. If these parameters are not specified then
the image will be drawn in its original size.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The image will be alpha-blended if the current DrawingMode() specifies one of the
alpha-blending flags, otherwise the image is just copied to the output. To draw an image using
alpha-blending in any case, use the DrawAlphaImage() command.

A number of backends (including WindowOutput() on Linux) can not ignore the alphachannel
when drawing images. So DrawImage() is equal to DrawAlphaImage() there. If you want consistent
results, just use DrawAlphaImage() which should produce the same output on all backends.

commands.name: DrawingBuffer
commands.description: Returns the drawing buffer for direct pixel manipulation.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the pixel data pointer if direct access is possible or zero if the pixel
data cannot be accessed directly.
commands.remarks:
This function has to be called again if other drawing commands of this library where used since the last pixel manipulation.
Once StopDrawing() has been called, the buffer is invalidated and can no more be used.

This function is for advanced programmers only. To get more information about the buffer,
the following functions are available: DrawingBufferPixelFormat() and
DrawingBufferPitch().

The returned address can be directly in video memory if the output is
ScreenOutput() or SpriteOutput()
and allows very fast pixel manipulation. With ImageOutput() this command allows
direct access to the pixels of the target image.
commands.example:
For an example of how the drawing buffer can be used to create a nice visual effect, take a look here:

DirectScreenDrawing.pb

commands.name: DrawingBufferPitch
commands.description: Returns the real length of one line of the current drawing buffer.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the length in bytes of one line in the output, including any additional padding
behind the pixel data of a line.
commands.remarks: DrawingBuffer() must be called before using this function.

commands.name: DrawingBufferPixelFormat
commands.description: Returns the pixel format of the current output.
commands.returnValue:
The result can be a combination (with bitwise or) of the following flags:

#PB_PixelFormat_8Bits : 1 byte per pixel, palletised
#PB_PixelFormat_15Bits : 2 bytes per pixel
#PB_PixelFormat_16Bits : 2 bytes per pixel
#PB_PixelFormat_24Bits_RGB : 3 bytes per pixel (RRGGBB)
#PB_PixelFormat_24Bits_BGR : 3 bytes per pixel (BBGGRR)
#PB_PixelFormat_32Bits_RGB : 4 bytes per pixel (RRGGBB)
#PB_PixelFormat_32Bits_BGR : 4 bytes per pixel (BBGGRR)
#PB_PixelFormat_ReversedY : The Y-Coordinate of the output is reversed in memory (the bottom row is stored first).
#PB_PixelFormat_NoAlpha : The pixel format is 32-bits but the alpha component is not used.
commands.remarks: DrawingBuffer() must be called before using this function.
commands.example:
If DrawingBufferPixelFormat() = #PB_PixelFormat_32Bits_RGB | #PB_PixelFormat_ReversedY
    ; 32-bit RGB with reversed Y coordinate
  EndIf
  
  If DrawingBufferPixelFormat() = #PB_PixelFormat_32Bits_RGB
    ; 32-bit RGB without reversed Y coordinate
  EndIf
  
  If DrawingBufferPixelFormat() & #PB_PixelFormat_32Bits_RGB
    ; 32-bit RGB, with or without reversed Y coordinate
  EndIf

commands.name: DrawingFont
commands.description: Sets the font to be used for text rendering on the current output.

parameters.name: FontID
parameters.description:
The font to be used.
The FontID can be easily obtained with the FontID() function
from the font library.

To restore the default system font, #PB_Default can be used as FontID.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: DrawingMode
commands.description: Change the drawing mode for text and graphics output.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The behavior for further drawing operations. It can be a combination of the following flags:

#PB_2DDrawing_Default

This is the default drawing mode when the drawing starts.
Text is displayed with a solid background and graphic shapes are filled.
If the current output has an alpha channel, the drawing operations will only modify the color components
and leave the alpha channel unchanged.

#PB_2DDrawing_Transparent

If this flag is set then the background will be transparent with the DrawText() command.

#PB_2DDrawing_NativeText

If this flag is set then the DrawText() and DrawRotatedText() commands will use native text output to have gadget-like text rendering.
All special effects like XOR, AlphaBlend, CustomFilters, etc. are not available with this mode.

#PB_2DDrawing_FastText

If this flag is set then the DrawText() and DrawRotatedText() commands will use a faster text rendering method but with less
precise unicode support (Windows only).

#PB_2DDrawing_XOr

Enables the XOR mode. All graphics will be XOR'ed with the current background. This mode cannot be combined
with the below alpha channel modes.

Note: This mode does not work with PrinterOutput().

#PB_2DDrawing_Outlined

If this flag is set then shapes will be drawn as outlines only and not filled. This applies to commands
such as Circle, Box, etc.

Note: The following modes only work with ImageOutput(), CanvasOutput() and SpriteOutput(). They are ignored for all other outputs:

#PB_2DDrawing_AlphaBlend

The drawing operations will be alpha-blended onto the background. The RGBA() command can be used
to specify colors with alpha transparency in commands like FrontColor(), Box(),
DrawText() etc.

#PB_2DDrawing_AlphaClip

The drawing operations will be alpha-blended onto the background like with the #PB_2DDrawing_AlphaBlend mode,
with the addition that the alpha channel of the drawing output acts as a mask. This means that areas of the output that are
transparent before the blending will also remain transparent afterwards. If the drawing output has no alpha channel then this
mode acts just like the #PB_2DDrawing_AlphaBlend mode.

#PB_2DDrawing_AlphaChannel

The drawing operations will only modify the alpha channel of the drawing output. All color information is ignored.
For example drawing a circle with a color value of RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0) will "cut" a hole
into the drawing output by making the circle area fully transparent. If the drawing output has no alpha channel, as the CanvasGadget,
then no drawing will have an effect in this mode.

#PB_2DDrawing_AllChannels

The drawing operations will modify the color channels and the alpha channel of the drawing output. The content of the
channels is replaced by the drawing operation without any blending. Drawing in this mode has the same effect as drawing
first using the #PB_2DDrawing_Default mode and then drawing the same operation using the
#PB_2DDrawing_AlphaChannel mode. If the drawing output has no alpha channel, as the CanvasGadget, then this mode is
equivalent to the #PB_2DDrawing_Default mode.

#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient

This mode allows drawing with a gradient instead of a solid color. The gradient shape can be defined with commands such as
LinearGradient(), CircularGradient() etc. and the colors used in the
gradient can be set with GradientColor(). The color parameters given to the individual drawing commands
will be ignored in this mode. This mode can be combined with the above alpha channel modes to have gradients with semitransparent
colors.

#PB_2DDrawing_CustomFilter

In this mode, the drawing of the pixels can be defined by a custom procedure with the CustomFilterCallback()
command. This allows the implementation of custom drawing effects while still using the default functions to do the actual drawing.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
To use several modes at once, you have to use the '|' (OR) operator. The following is an example for
XOR'ed outlined shapes:

DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Outlined | #PB_2DDrawing_XOr)

commands.name: DrawRotatedText
commands.description:
Displays the given text on the current output at the given angle. To have gadget-like text output,
the drawing mode #PB_2DDrawing_NativeText can be used.

parameters.name: x.d, y.d
parameters.description:
The location of the top/left corner of the text in the output.
This is also the location around which the string will be rotated.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to draw.

parameters.name: Angle.f
parameters.description:
The angle in degrees to rotate counterclockwise
starting from the normal text orientation.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the text. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.
The background of the rotated text is always transparent.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For Angle = 0 To 360 Step 45
        DrawRotatedText(100, 100, "Hello World!", Angle, RGB(0, 0, 0))
      Next Angle
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: DrawText
syntax: Result.d = DrawText(x.d, y.d, Text$ [, FrontColor [, BackColor]])
commands.description:
Display the given string on the current output at the given x,y position.
The current output is set with StartDrawing(). To have gadget-like text output,
the drawing mode #PB_2DDrawing_NativeText can be used.

parameters.name: x.d, y.d
parameters.description: The location at which to draw the text.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to draw.

parameters.name: FrontColor (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the text. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

parameters.name: BackColor (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the background. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with BackColor() will be used.

If the current DrawingMode() includes the #PB_2DDrawing_Transparent flag,
then this parameter is ignored and the background is transparent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the new x position of the text cursor (ie the location just after the printed text).
commands.remarks:
If DrawingMode() is set to non-transparent background
and the current drawing mode uses the alpha channel then the text is first blended onto the background
and then applied to the drawing output.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Transparent)
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For i = 1 To 30
        DrawText(Random(200), Random(200), "Hello World!", RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
      Next i
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.description:
Draw an ellipse in the current drawing output.
The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The position of the center pixel of the ellipse.

parameters.name: RadiusX, RadiusY
parameters.description:
The radius of the ellipse in the x and y direction. The center pixel is not
included in these values.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the ellipse. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For radius=50 To 10 Step -10
        Ellipse(100, 100, radius*2, radius, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
      Next radius
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: EllipticalGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have an elliptical shape.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The location at which to apply the current background color.

parameters.name: RadiusX, RadiusY
parameters.description: The radius around in the x and y direction at which to apply the current front color.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
       
      EllipticalGradient(100, 100, 150, 50)
      Circle(100, 100, 100)   
      EllipticalGradient(300, 100, 50, 150)
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: FillArea
commands.description:
Fill an arbitrary area starting from x,y position until the
OutlineColor is encountered. This is useful for filling any kind of shape.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The location at which the filling should start.

parameters.name: OutlineColor
parameters.description:
The color which should be considered the border to stop the filling.
If this parameter is set to -1 then the area defined by the color
found at the (x,y) coordinates will be filled, and filling stops at any color that
differs from the starting point.

On 32-bit images, the alpha channel is ignored when
determining whether a pixel counts as a border pixel or not.

parameters.name: FillColor (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for filling the pixels. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: This command does not work with PrinterOutput().
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 300, 300, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 300, 300) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 300, 300, RGB(255, 255, 255))

      Circle(150, 150, 125 ,$00FF00)
      Circle(150, 150, 120 ,$FF0000)
      LineXY(30, 150, 270, 150, $FFFFFF)
      FillArea(150, 155, -1, $0000FF) ; Replace -1 by $00FF00, and compare the result

      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 300, 300, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: FrontColor
commands.description: Set the default color for graphic functions and text display.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
The new color to be used as the foreground color.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.
Whether or not the alpha channel is used depends on the drawing mode.

A color table with common colors is available here.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: GetOriginX
commands.description: Get the X coordinate of the drawing origin that was set using SetOrigin().
commands.returnValue: The X coordinate of the drawing origin.

commands.name: GetOriginY
commands.description: Get the Y coordinate of the drawing origin that was set using SetOrigin().
commands.returnValue: The Y coordinate of the drawing origin.

commands.name: GrabDrawingImage
syntax: Result = GrabDrawingImage(#Image, x, y, Width, Height)
commands.description: Create a new image with the content of the given area in the current output.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description:
The number of the new image to create.
#PB_Any can be used to select a number automatically.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description:
The location and size of the area to copy into the new image.
The new image will be created with the specified width and height.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.
If #PB_Any was used as the '#Image' parameter then the number of the new image is returned.
commands.remarks:
This command does not work with PrinterOutput().

Any parts of the specified area that are outside of the drawing output will be undefined in the created image. Also if the current
output is WindowOutput(), any part of the window that is currently not visible may be undefined in the resulting image.

commands.name: GradientColor
commands.description: Adds the given Color at the given Position to the spectrum of the drawing gradient.

parameters.name: Position.f
parameters.description:
The position for the color in the gradient.
It must be a float value between 0.0 and 1.0.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
The color to be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
By default, the drawing gradient ranges from the current background color at position
0.0 to the current front color at position 1.0. With this command, additional colors
can be added Inbetween, or the colors at 0.0 and 1.0 can be overwritten.

The ResetGradientColors() command can be used to revert back to the default gradient.

The following commands can be used to specify the shape of the drawing gradient:

- LinearGradient()

- CircularGradient()

- EllipticalGradient()

- BoxedGradient()

- ConicalGradient()

- CustomGradient()

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($0000FF)
      GradientColor(0.4, $00FFFF)
      GradientColor(0.6, $FFFF00)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      LinearGradient(0, 0, 200, 200)    
      Circle(100, 100, 100)   
      LinearGradient(350, 100, 250, 100)
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: Green
commands.description: Returns the green component of a color value.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The color value. This can be a 24-bit RGB or a 32-bit RGBA value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the green component. The result will be between 0 and 255.
commands.remarks:
To combine red, green and blue values in order to create a 24-bit RGB color,
use the RGB() function.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

commands.name: Line
commands.description:
Draw a line of given dimensions on the current output.
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The origin of the line to draw.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description:
The dimension of the line to draw. These values include the starting point
so a Height of 1 draws a horizontal line while a Height of 0 draws nothing at all.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the line. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To draw a line given the coordinates of the start- and end point, use the LineXY() function.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For Width = 1 To 180 Step 5
        Line(10, 10, Width, 180, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
      Next Width
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: LinearGradient
commands.description: Sets the drawing gradient to have a linear shape defined by the two points x1,y1 and x2,y2.

parameters.name: x1, y1
parameters.description: The position at which to apply the current background color.

parameters.name: x2, y2
parameters.description: The position at which to apply the current front color.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Additional colors can be added to the gradient with the GradientColor() command.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 400, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 400, 200, $FFFFFF)
      
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Gradient)      
      BackColor($00FFFF)
      FrontColor($FF0000)
      
      LinearGradient(0, 0, 200, 200)    
      Circle(100, 100, 100)   
      LinearGradient(350, 100, 250, 100)
      Circle(300, 100, 100)
      
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 400, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: LineXY
commands.description:
Draw a line using the location of the start- and endpoint on the current output.
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x1, y1
parameters.description: The location of the startpoint of the line.

parameters.name: x2, y2
parameters.description: The location of the endpoint of the line.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the line. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To draw a line given the start coordinates and the dimensions, use the Line() function.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      Box(0, 0, 200, 200, RGB(255, 255, 255))
      For Angle = 0 To 360 Step 3
        LineXY(100, 100, 100+Cos(Radian(Angle))*90, 100+Sin(Radian(Angle))*90, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
      Next Angle
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: OutputDepth
commands.description: Returns the color depth of the current drawing output.
commands.returnValue: Returns the depth in bits per pixel.

commands.name: OutputHeight
commands.description: Returns the height of the current drawing output.
commands.returnValue: Returns the height of the output in pixels.

commands.name: OutputWidth
commands.description: Returns the width of the current drawing output.
commands.returnValue: Returns the width of the output in pixels.

commands.name: Plot
commands.description:
Draw a single pixel at the given location in the current output.
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description:
The location of the pixel to set.

For performance reasons there are no bounds checks performed on these coordinates, the specified
coordinates must be inside the current drawing area. OutputWidth() and
OutputHeight() can be used to verify that. This command is also not affected by any clipping
imposed by ClipOutput().

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the pixel. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      For x = 0 To 199
        For y = 0 To 199
          Plot(x, y, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
        Next y
      Next x
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: Point
commands.description: Return the color of a pixel in the current output.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description:
The location of the pixel in the output.

For performance reasons there are no bounds checks performed on these coordinates, the specified
coordinates must be inside the current drawing area. OutputWidth() and
OutputHeight() can be used to verify that. This command is also not affected by calls to
ClipOutput().

commands.returnValue:
Returns the color of the specified pixel.

This color will only contain alpha information if the output has a 32-bit color depth and the
current DrawingMode() is set to one of the alpha channel modes. Otherwise the alpha component
of the color is set to 0.
commands.remarks: This command does not work with PrinterOutput().

commands.name: Red
commands.description: Returns the red component of a color value.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The color value. This can be a 24-bit RGB or a 32-bit RGBA value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the red component. The result will be between 0 and 255.
commands.remarks:
To combine red, green and blue values in order to create a 24-bit RGB color,
use the RGB() function.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

commands.name: ResetGradientColors
commands.description:
Removes all colors from the drawing gradient and reverts back to a gradient from the current
background color to the current front color.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The GradientColor() command can be used to add additional colors to the gradient.

Note: This command only has an effect with ImageOutput() and CanvasOutput().
The gradient only affects the drawing commands when #PB_2DDrawing_Gradient is
set with the DrawingMode() command.

commands.name: RGB
commands.description: Returns the 24-bit color value corresponding to the Red, Green, Blue components.

parameters.name: Red, Green, Blue
parameters.description:
The value of the red, green and blue components for the color. Each value
must be between 0 and 255.

commands.returnValue: Returns the combined color value.
commands.remarks:
To extract the red, green and blue values from a 24 Bit color value, use
the Red(), Green() and Blue() functions.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

A color table with common colors is available here.

commands.name: RGBA
commands.description: Returns the 32-bit color value corresponding to the Red, Green, Blue and Alpha values.

parameters.name: Red, Green, Blue
parameters.description:
The value of the red, green and blue components for the color. Each value
must be between 0 and 255.

parameters.name: Alpha
parameters.description:
The alpha component of the color. The value must be between 0 and 255.
A value of 0 means fully transparent and a value of 255 means fully opaque.

commands.returnValue: Returns the combined color value.
commands.remarks:
To extract the red, green, blue or alpha values from a 32-bit color value, use
the Red(), Green(), Blue() and Alpha() functions.
These functions are useful to perform Drawing operations.

Result varies from 0 to 4 294 967 295 shades.
It is therefore advisable to use a 'quad', (Result.q) and set unused bytes to zero.
Indeed, on a 32-Bit operating system, Result is a Long integer (by default) with a
range of use from - 2 147 483 648 to + 2 147 483 647, so comparing two colors is
hazardous with a Long integer.
commands.example:
Debug RGBA(0, 0, 0, 0)         ; Completely transparent black  
  Debug RGBA(255, 255, 255, 255) ; White totally opaque

Alpha = 255
  
  ; Use a Quad (see remarks)
  Color24.q  = ColorRequester()
  
  Color32.q = RGBA(Red(Color24), Green(Color24), Blue(Color24), alpha) 
  Color32 = Color32 & $FFFFFFFF ; Zeroing unused bytes

  ; It's also possible to replace the two lines above with:
  ; Color32 = Color24 | Alpha << 24
  
  Debug "Red " + Red(Color32)
  Debug "Green  " + Green(Color32)
  Debug "Blue  " + Blue(Color32)
  Debug "Alpha " + Alpha(Color32)

commands.name: RoundBox
syntax: RoundBox(x, y, Width, Height, RoundX, RoundY [, Color])
commands.description:
Draw a box of the given dimensions with rounded corners on the current output.
The filling mode is determined by DrawingMode().
The current output is set with StartDrawing().

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and size of the box in the current drawing output.

parameters.name: RoundX, RoundY
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded corners in the x and y direction.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The color to be used for the round box. If this parameter is not specified, the default color
set with FrontColor() will be used.
This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      y = 0
      For x = 0 To 95 Step 10
        RoundBox(x, y, 200-2*x, 200-2*y, 20, 20, RGB(Random(255), Random(255), Random(255)))
        y + 10 
      Next x
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: SetOrigin
commands.description:
Set an offset at which all drawing in the current output takes place.
This defines the location of the coordinates (0, 0) within the output for
every following drawing command. By default, the origin is located in the
upper left corner of the drawing output.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description:
The new position of the drawing origin. This is an absolute location and is not
affected by any previous call to this function.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command affects the location of all future drawing commands with the exception of the
ClipOutput() command and the SetOrigin() command itself. Also, the coordinates received
in a CustomGradient() or CustomFilterCallback() callback are always absolute regardless
of any calls to this function.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "2DDrawing Example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CreateImage(0, 200, 200, 24, $FFFFFF) And StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
        
      ; Draw the same figure at different locations by moving the drawing origin
      For x = 0 To 120 Step 40
        For y = 0 To 120 Step 60
          SetOrigin(x, y)
          Box(0, 0, 30, 30, $FF0000)
          Circle(15, 15, 10, $00FF00)
        Next y
      Next x   
         
      StopDrawing() 
      ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))      
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: StartDrawing
commands.description:
Change the current drawing output to the specified output. After setting this,
all drawing functions are rendered to this output.

parameters.name: OutputID
parameters.description:
The output to draw on. It can be obtained with the following functions:

WindowOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Window

ScreenOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Screen (for games)

SpriteOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Sprite (for games)

ImageOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Image data (see CreateImage())

PrinterOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Printer

CanvasOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the CanvasGadget()

TextureOutput(): Graphics will be rendered directly on the Texture (for 3D games)

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if drawing is possible or zero if the operation failed.
commands.remarks:
Once all drawing operations are finished, StopDrawing() must be called.

If "Create thread-safe executable" is enabled in the compiler options then
every thread has its own current drawing output, which means two threads can do drawing on separate
outputs at the same time.

commands.name: StopDrawing
commands.description:
Once all the needed graphics operations (started with StartDrawing()) have been
performed, this function must be called to finish the drawing and free all associated resources.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If StartDrawing(WindowOutput(0))
    Box(10,10,20,20)
    Line(30,50,100,100)
    ....
    StopDrawing() 
  EndIf

commands.name: TextHeight
commands.description: Return the height of the given string in the current output using the current font.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to measure.

commands.returnValue: Returns the height of the given text.

commands.name: TextWidth
commands.description: Return the width of the given string in the current output using the current font.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to measure.

commands.returnValue: Returns the width of the given text.

commands.name: UnclipOutput
commands.description:
Remove any clipping imposed by the ClipOutput() command. The following drawing
commands will be able to draw to the entire drawing output again.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: This command only has an effect by drawing outputs created by ImageOutput() or CanvasOutput().

commands.name: ArraySize
commands.description: Returns the size of the array, as specified with Dim or ReDim.

parameters.name: Array()
parameters.description: The array to get the size from.

parameters.name: Dimension (optional)
parameters.description:
For multidimensional arrays, this parameter can be specified to get a specific dimension size.
The first dimension starts from 1.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the size of the array dimension.
If the array isn't yet declared (for example after FreeArray() or if its allocation has failed), it will return -1.
commands.remarks:
As specified with Dim, the number of elements is equal to the size + 1.
For example: Dim a(2) contains 3 elements from a(0) to a(2) for a size of 2.

Does not work with static arrays declared in Structures.
Use SizeOf instead.
commands.example:
Dim MyArray.l(10)
  Debug ArraySize(MyArray()) ; will print '10'
  
  Dim MultiArray.l(10, 20, 30)
  Debug ArraySize(MultiArray(), 2) ; will print '20'
  
  Dim MultiArray2.l(2,2,2)
  For n = 0 To ArraySize(MultiArray2(),2)
    MultiArray2(0,n,0) = n+1
  Next n
  Debug MultiArray2(0,0,0) ; will print '1'
  Debug MultiArray2(0,1,0) ; will print '2'
  Debug MultiArray2(0,2,0) ; will print '3'
  Debug ArraySize(MultiArray2(),2) ; will print '2'

Dim Test.q(99999999999999999)
  
  If ArraySize(Test()) <> -1
    Test(12345) = 123  ; everything fine
  Else
    Debug "Array 'Test()' couldn't be initialized."
  EndIf

Structure MyStructure
  ArrayStatic.l[3]        ; Static array, only in structures
  Array ArrayDynamic.l(4) ; Dynamic array
EndStructure

Debug SizeOf(MyStructure\ArrayStatic)  ; Display 12
Debug SizeOf(MyStructure\ArrayDynamic) ; Display 8

Ex.MyStructure
Debug ArraySize(Ex\ArrayDynamic()); Display 4

commands.name: CompareArray
commands.description:
Compare each elements of the two arrays for equality. Recursively compares
also contents of structured arrays with dynamic elements (such as embedded arrays, lists or maps).
The two arrays are considered the equal if they have the same type and dimensions and if each
pair of elements is equal.

parameters.name: Array1(), Array2()
parameters.description: The arrays to compare.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
Can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_String_CaseSensitive : String comparison is case sensitive (a=a). (default)
#PB_String_NoCase : String comparison is case insensitive(a=A).
#PB_Memory_FollowPointers: If a structure element is a pointer that is not 0, recursively compare the pointer target.
The default is to compare only the pointer value itself. See remarks below for details.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if both arrays are the same or zero if they differ.
commands.remarks:
The #PB_Memory_FollowPointers option is for advanced users and requires special care to avoid crashes.
If this option is used then all pointer values must point to valid and initialized memory or have the value 0.
It is also not allowed to have loops in the pointed elements (a chain of pointers that refers back to itself).
commands.example:
Dim A(4)
  A(0) = 10
  A(1) = 20
  A(2) = 30
  A(3) = 40

  Dim B(4)
  B(0) = 10
  B(1) = 20
  B(2) = 50 ; Not equal to A(2)
  B(3) = 40

  Debug CompareArray(A(), B()) ; Not equal

commands.name: CopyArray
commands.description:
Copy every element of 'SourceArray()' into 'DestinationArray()'.
After a successful copy, the two arrays are identical. The arrays must have the
same number of dimensions.

parameters.name: SourceArray()
parameters.description: The array to copy from.

parameters.name: DestinationArray()
parameters.description:
The array to copy to. Every element previously found in this array will be deleted.
This array must be of the same type (native or structured) and the same
number of dimensions of the source array.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the copy succeeded or zero if it failed.
commands.example:
Dim Numbers(5)
  Dim NumbersCopy(10)
  
  Numbers(0) = 128
  Numbers(5) = 256
  
  Debug "Array size before copy: "+Str(ArraySize(NumbersCopy())) ; will print 10
  
  CopyArray(Numbers(), NumbersCopy())
  
  Debug "Array size after copy: "+Str(ArraySize(NumbersCopy())) ; will print 5
  Debug NumbersCopy(0)
  Debug NumbersCopy(5)

commands.name: FreeArray
commands.description:
Free the specified 'Array()' and release all its associated memory. To access it again
Dim has to be called.

parameters.name: Array()
parameters.description: The array to free.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AudioCDLength
commands.description: Returns the total length of an entire audio CD.
commands.returnValue: Returns the length in seconds.

commands.name: AudioCDName
commands.description: Returns the system-dependent name associated with the current audio CD drive.
commands.returnValue:
Returns a string containing the name.

For example, it would return 'D:\' on a Windows-based system, if the audio CD is
associated as drive letter 'D'.

commands.name: AudioCDStatus
commands.description: Returns the actual state of the current audio CD drive.
commands.returnValue:
The return-value may take the following values:

-1: CD drive not ready (it is either empty or opened)

0: CD drive stopped (but the CD is in the drive and has been detected)

>0: Audio track which is currently being played.

commands.name: AudioCDTrackLength
commands.description: Returns the length of the specified track.

parameters.name: TrackNumber
parameters.description: The number of the requested track. The first track has an index of 1.

commands.returnValue: Returns the length (in seconds) of the specified track.

commands.name: AudioCDTracks
commands.description: Return the total number of tracks on the CD available to be played.
commands.returnValue: Returns the number of tracks.

commands.name: AudioCDTrackSeconds
commands.description: Return the number of seconds elapsed since the current track began to play.
commands.returnValue: Returns the number of seconds since the beginning of the track.

commands.name: EjectAudioCD
commands.description: Eject (open) or close the current CD drive.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
The action to take.
If State = 1, the CD drive is opened, else it is closed.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: InitAudioCD
commands.description: Try to initialize all the necessary resources in order to handle audio CD playback.
commands.returnValue:
If Result is 0, the initialization has failed or there are no
CD drives available, else Result contains the number of CD drives attached to the system.
commands.remarks: This function must be called before any other audio CD functions.

commands.name: PauseAudioCD
commands.description: Pause audio CD playback. The playback may be resumed by using the ResumeAudioCD() function.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: PlayAudioCD
commands.description: Start to play the audio CD from 'StartTrack' until the end of 'EndTrack'.

parameters.name: StartTrack
parameters.description: The first track to play. (The first track on the CD has an index of 1)

parameters.name: EndTrack
parameters.description: The last track to play.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ResumeAudioCD
commands.description: Resume audio CD playback, previously paused by the use of the PauseAudioCD() function.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: StopAudioCD
commands.description: Stop audio CD playback.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UseAudioCD
commands.description: Select the Drive to which the following AudioCD commands apply. It is possible to play several CDs at the same time.

parameters.name: AudioCDDrive
parameters.description:
The drive to use. The first drive has index 0. The amount of drives available in the system is
returned from the InitAudioCD() function.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddBillboard
commands.description:
Adds a billboard to the specified billboard group at the given position, relative
to the position of the billboard group. The billboard group must have previously
been created using the CreateBillboardGroup() function.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group you want to attach the new billboard to.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The coordinates to create billboard at, relative to the coordinates of the billboard group.

commands.returnValue:
The new billboard index. This value can be used to manipulate this specific billboard with
the commands which needs one.

commands.name: BillboardGroupCommonDirection
commands.description: Changes the billboard common direction.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The common direction vector (usually values between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BillboardGroupCommonUpVector
commands.description: Changes the billboard common up vector.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The common up vector (usually values between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BillboardGroupID
commands.description:
Returns the unique ID which identifies the given '#BillboardGroup' in the operating system. This
function is very useful when another library needs a billboard-group reference.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to use.

commands.returnValue: The unique ID which identifies the given '#BillboardGroup' in the operating system.

commands.name: BillboardGroupMaterial
commands.description:
Assigns a material to the specified billboard group. This material will be
used by all the billboards added to this group. A group can only have one material
assigned at any point in time.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group to assign a new material to.

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description:
The ID number of the material to assign to the billboard group (and billboards).
A valid 'MaterialID' can be easily obtained by using the MaterialID() function.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BillboardGroupX
commands.description: Determines the absolute position of the billboard group in the world.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group to get the position of.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'x' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'x' position of the billboard group in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'x' position of the billboard group relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: The absolute 'x' position of the billboard group.

commands.name: BillboardGroupY
commands.description: Determines the absolute position of the billboard group in the world.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group to get the position of.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'y' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'y' position of the billboard group in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'y' position of the billboard group relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: The absolute 'y' position of the billboard group.

commands.name: BillboardGroupZ
commands.description: Determines the absolute position of the billboard group in the world.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group to get the position of.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'z' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'z' position of the billboard group in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'z' position of the billboard group relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: The absolute 'z' position of the billboard group.

commands.name: BillboardHeight
commands.description:
Determines the height of a billboard which has been added to a billboard group.
The height is measured in the units used by the world.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The number of the billboard to get the height of.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: The height of the billboard, in world units.

commands.name: BillboardLocate
commands.description:
Moves a billboard to a new location within the billboard group which is it added to.
The position to move to is relative to the position of the billboard group. Use the
MoveBillboard() function to move a billboard relative to its own coordinates.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The number of the billboard to move.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position for the billboard.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BillboardWidth
commands.description:
Determines the width of a billboard which has been added to a billboard group.
The width is measured in the units used by the world.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to use.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: The width of the billboard, in world units.

commands.name: BillboardX
commands.description:
Returns the position of the billboard, relative to the position
of the group which it is in.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to use.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: The X position of the billboard.

commands.name: BillboardY
commands.description:
Returns the position of the billboard, relative to the position
of the group which it is in.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to use.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: The Y position of the billboard.

commands.name: BillboardZ
commands.description:
Returns the position of the billboard, relative to the position
of the group which it is in.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to use.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The number of the billboard group which contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: The Z position of the billboard.

commands.name: ClearBillboards
commands.description: Removes and destroys all billboards in the specified billboard group.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to clear.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CountBillboards
commands.description: Counts the number of billboards contained in a billboard group.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to use.

commands.returnValue: The number of billboards which have been added to the billboard group.

commands.name: CreateBillboardGroup
syntax: Result = CreateBillboardGroup(#BillboardGroup, MaterialID, DefaultBillboardWidth, DefaultBillboardHeight [, x, y, z [, VisibilityMask [, Type]]])
commands.description: Creates a new empty billboard group.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new billboard group. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description:
The material to use for all billboards added to this group, using the
AddBillboard() function. To get a valid material id use MaterialID().

parameters.name: DefaultBillboardWidth
parameters.description:
The default width (in world units) of billboards added to this group.
Although the size of each billboard can be set separately with the ResizeBillboard()
function, it is important to keep in mind that it will have a negative impact on performance
if all billboards are not the same size.

parameters.name: DefaultBillboardHeight
parameters.description:
The default height (in world units) of billboards added to this group.
Although the size of each billboard can be set separately with the ResizeBillboard()
function, it is important to keep in mind that it will have a negative impact on performance
if all billboards are not the same size.

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description: The absolute position of the new billboard group in the world.

parameters.name: VisibilityMask (optional)
parameters.description:
A mask to select on which camera the billboard group should be displayed. If this mask match the mask specified in
CreateCamera(), the billboard group will be displayed on the camera. See CreateEntity() to build correct masks.
If this parameter is omitted or set to #PB_All, then the billboard group will be visible on all cameras.

parameters.name: Type (optional)
parameters.description:
The billboard type. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Billboard_Point: standard point billboard, always faces the camera completely and is always upright (default).
#PB_Billboard_Oriented: billboards are oriented around a shared direction vector (used as Y axis) and only rotate around this to face the camera.
#PB_Billboard_SelfOriented: billboards are oriented around their own direction vector (their own Y axis) and only rotate around this to face the camera.
#PB_Billboard_Perpendicular: billboards are perpendicular to a shared direction vector (used as Z axis, the facing direction) and X, Y axis are determined by a shared up-vector.
#PB_Billboard_SelfPerpendicular: billboards are perpendicular to their own direction vector (their own Z axis, the facing direction) and X, Y axis are determined by a shared up-vector.

commands.returnValue:
Returns zero if the billboard group can't be created. If #PB_Any is used
as '#BillboardGroup' parameter, the new billboard group number is returned.

commands.name: FreeBillboardGroup
commands.description:
Frees the specified billboard group and any billboards contained within it.
All its associated memory is released and this object cannot be used
anymore.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining billboard groups are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining billboard groups are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: HideBillboardGroup
commands.description:
Changes the visibility of (hides or shows) a billboard group and any billboards
it contains.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to hide or show.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
It can take the following values:

#True : the billboard group is hidden
#False: the billboard group is shown

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: IsBillboardGroup
commands.description: Tests if the given billboard group number is a valid and correctly initialized billboard group.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to use.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the billboard group is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a billboard group is ready to use.

commands.name: MoveBillboard
commands.description:
Moves a billboard which is contained in a billboard group by the specified
x, y and z values. This is a relative move based on the current location of the
billboard. To perform an absolute move (actually, relative to the coordinates of the
billboard group) use BillboardLocate().

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to move.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group which contains the billboard.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The offset to add to the current position of the billboard.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MoveBillboardGroup
commands.description:
Moves a billboard group by the specified x, y and z values. This is by default a relative move,
based on the current location of the billboard group.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to move.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position of the billboard group.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative move, from the current billboard group position (default).
#PB_Absolute: absolute move to the specified position.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RemoveBillboard
commands.description: Removes a billboard from the specified billboard group.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to remove.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group which currently contains the billboard.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ResizeBillboard
commands.description:
Resizes a billboard, which is currently contained in a billboard group, to
a new width and height, specified in world units. Note that although you can
resize billboards independently with this function there will be some performance
lost if the billboards within a billboard group are all different sizes.

parameters.name: #Billboard
parameters.description: The billboard to resize.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group which currently contains the billboard.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The new size of the billboard, in world units.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RotateBillboardGroup
commands.description: Rotates the #BillboardGroup according to the specified x, y, z angle values.

parameters.name: #BillboardGroup
parameters.description: The billboard group to rotate.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new rotation to apply to the billboard group. The value are in degree, ranging from 0 to 360.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: absolute rotation (default).
#PB_Relative: relative rotation based on the previous billboard rotation.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CameraBackColor
commands.description:
Changes the camera background color. When a new camera is created, the default background color
is set to black.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: New color of the camera background. RGB() can be used to get a valid color value.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CameraCustomParameter
syntax: CameraCustomParameter(#Camera, ParameterIndex, Value1, Value2, Value3, Value4)
commands.description: Sets a custom parameter value to the camera shader script (either GLSL or HLSL).

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: ParameterIndex
parameters.description: The parameter index in the shader script.

parameters.name: Value1
parameters.description: The first parameter value.

parameters.name: Value2
parameters.description: The second parameter value (if the parameter only accept one value, this value will be ignored).

parameters.name: Value3
parameters.description: The third parameter value (if the parameter only accept two values, this value will be ignored).

parameters.name: Value4
parameters.description: The fourth parameter value (if the parameter only accept three values, this value will be ignored).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CameraDirection
commands.description: Changes the direction of a camera. The position of the camera is not changed.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The direction vector (usually values between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CameraDirectionX
commands.description: Returns the 'x' direction vector of the camera.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'x' direction vector. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'x' direction vector of the camera in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'x' direction vector of the camera relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'x' direction vector of the camera. This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.

commands.name: CameraDirectionY
commands.description: Returns the 'y' direction vector of the camera.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'y' direction vector. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'y' direction vector of the camera in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'y' direction vector of the camera relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'y' direction vector of the camera. . This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.

commands.name: CameraDirectionZ
commands.description: Returns the 'z' direction vector of the camera.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'z' direction vector. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'z' direction vector of the camera in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'z' direction vector of the camera relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'z' direction vector of the camera. This value is always between -1.0 and 1.0.

commands.name: CameraFixedYawAxis
commands.description: Change the fixed yaw axis of the camera. The default behaviour of a camera is to yaw around its own Y axis.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Enable
parameters.description:
Enable or disable the use of a custom yaw axis. If set to #True, a new axis vector has to be specified.
If set to #False, the camera will yaw around its own Y axis.

parameters.name: VectorX (optional)
parameters.description:
'x' vector direction of the new yaw axis (usually a value between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).
'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

parameters.name: VectorY (optional)
parameters.description:
'y' vector direction of the new yaw axis (usually a value between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).
'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

parameters.name: VectorZ (optional)
parameters.description:
'z' vector direction of the new yaw axis (usually a value between -1.0 and 1.0, if not it will be automatically normalized).
'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CameraFollow
syntax: CameraFollow(#Camera, ObjectID, Angle, Height, Distance, RotationPercent, PositionPercent [, Mode])
commands.description: Follow the specified object in a smooth manner, using interpolation.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object to follow. It can be one of the following type:

- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: The angle of the camera relative to the followed object.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The absolute height of the camera.

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: The distance of the camera relative to the followed object.

parameters.name: RotationPercent
parameters.description: Value to apply when the camera rotate to get it again in the correct angle. Valid values are from 0 to 1.

parameters.name: PositionPercent
parameters.description:
Value to apply when the camera moves to get it again in the correct position. Valid values are from 0 to 1.
