parameters.name: Files$
parameters.description:
The list of filenames or directories to drag. Multiple filenames should be separated with a
Chr(10) (linefeed) character. Each filename must include its full path, as the
target application will not know how to resolve relative names. The filenames must refer to existing files,
so the target application can access them.

parameters.name: Actions (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the files.
If the parameter is not specified, #PB_Drag_Copy will be the only allowed action.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_Copy: The files can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The files can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The files can be linked

The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drop target.
(On MacOSX, the actions are only treated as a suggestion. The drop target can still choose another action.)

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or
#PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.

Note that unlike with the other functions that start Drag & Drop, nothing should be done when #PB_Drag_Move
is returned. As the dragged data is only the filename and not the file itself, any action that is taken on the file
must be done by the drag target.
commands.remarks:
Drag & Drop can basically be started any time, but the
left mouse button should be currently pressed as otherwise the operation will end immediately without success.
The usual time to start a Drag & Drop operation is when a Gadget reported an event with
EventType() of #PB_EventType_DragStart. On MacOS X the #PB_EventType_DragStart event has to be handled using BindEvent() or BindGadgetEvent().
commands.example:
Procedure DragStartHandler()
    ExamineDraggedItems()
    While NextDraggedItem()
      Files$ + GetGadgetText(0) + GetGadgetItemText(0, DraggedItemIndex()) + Chr(10)
    Wend
    
    Debug "Dragging files: "+Files$
    
    DragFiles(Files$)
  EndProcedure

  ; Select some files or folders and drag them to another application
  ;
  If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 400, 400, "Drag & Drop")
    ExplorerListGadget(0, 10, 10, 380, 380, GetHomeDirectory(), #PB_Explorer_MultiSelect)
    
    ; BindGadgetEvent() is required to handle the drag start event
    BindGadgetEvent(0, @DragStartHandler(), #PB_EventType_DragStart)
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()  
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: DraggedItemIndex
commands.description: Return the current dragged item index. This function has to be called after NextDraggedItem().
commands.returnValue: Returns the index of the current dragged item (first index is zero).

commands.name: DragImage
commands.description: Starts a Drag & Drop operation with image data.

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description: The image to drag. ImageID() can be used to get this ID for an image.

parameters.name: Actions (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the image.
If the parameter is not specified, #PB_Drag_Copy will be the only allowed action.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_Copy: The image can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The image can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The image can be linked

The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drop target.
(On MacOSX, the actions are only treated as a suggestion. The drop target can still choose another action.)

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or
#PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.

Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the
dragged image from your application.
commands.remarks:
Drag & Drop can basically be started any time, but the
left mouse button should be currently pressed as otherwise the operation will end immediately without success.
The usual time to start a Drag & Drop operation is when a Gadget reported an event with
EventType() of #PB_EventType_DragStart. On MacOS X the #PB_EventType_DragStart event has to be handled using BindEvent() or BindGadgetEvent().
commands.example:
; Drag the image to an application that can accept images like an office or graphic program.
  ;
  If LoadImage(1, #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/data/PureBasicLogo.bmp")
    If OpenWindow(1, 200, 200, 400, 90, "Drag & Drop", #PB_Window_SystemMenu)
      ImageGadget(1, 10, 10, 380, 70, ImageID(1))
    
      Repeat
        Event = WaitWindowEvent()      
        If Event = #PB_Event_Gadget And EventGadget() = 1 And EventType() = #PB_EventType_DragStart
          DragImage(ImageID(1))
        EndIf      
      Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
    EndIf
  EndIf

commands.name: DragOSFormats
commands.description:
Starts a Drag & Drop operation with a list of custom data formats. The types of formats available and the
way in which they are represented depends on the Operating system. This function offers the possibility to
work with formats not natively supported by PureBasic, while still using the simple mechanisms provided
by this library to carry out the Drag & Drop operation.

parameters.name: Formats()
parameters.description:
An array of DragDataFormat structures
containing one or more formats to drag.
The structure has the following form:

Structure DragDataFormat
Format.i ; The OS specific ID for the format to drag (see below for more information)
*Buffer ; The memory buffer containing the data in this format
Size.i ; The size of the data in the buffer
EndStructure

Windows:

On Windows, the 'Format' field specifies a CLIPBOARDFORMAT value. It can be any standard clipboard format
(found in the Windows SDK), or a format registered with the RegisterClipboardFormat_() API.

Linux:

On Linux, the 'Format' field specifies a GdkAtom value. It can be created with the gdk function gdk_atom_intern_().
Widely understood atoms are the common mime types (ie "text/html" for html data). The atom can also be
created with any string that is understood by the target application.

MacOSX:

On MacOSX, the 'Format' field specifies a clipboard scrap type. These are 4 letter numeric character constants,
for example 'TEXT'. There are a number of predefined scrap types, but also custom values
can be used if the target program understands them.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description:
The number of formats in the array.

If multiple formats are dragged, the target will accept the first one it recognizes. So
the format that provides the most information (i.e. represents the data most accurately) should be
first in the array, with less descriptive but more common formats later. This way each application
will get the best representation of the data that it understands.

parameters.name: Actions (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the data.
If the parameter is not specified, #PB_Drag_Copy will be the only allowed action.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_Copy: The data can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data can be linked

The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drop target.
(On MacOSX, the actions are only treated as a suggestion. The drop target can still choose another action.)

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or
#PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.

Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the
dragged data from your application.
commands.remarks:
Drag & Drop can basically be started any time, but the
left mouse button should be currently pressed as otherwise the operation will end immediately without success.
The usual time to start a Drag & Drop operation is when a Gadget reported an event with
EventType() of #PB_EventType_DragStart.

commands.name: DragPrivate
commands.description:
Starts a "private" Drag & Drop operation. Unlike the other functions that start Drag & Drop, this data can
only be dropped inside the application (Data dragged with functions like DragText() or
DragImage() can be accepted by other applications as well). This function should be used
to add Drag & Drop functionality between Gadgets or Windows with
data that would not be understood by other applications.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
This parameter can be any integer value that identifies the data to be dragged in the application. The same value must be
specified for EnableGadgetDrop() or EnableWindowDrop()
for those Gadget/Windows that should accept this data.

This way it can be exactly defined which private drag operation will be accepted by Gadget/Window,
which allows complex Drag & Drop schemes to be realized.

parameters.name: Actions (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the data.
If the parameter is not specified, #PB_Drag_Copy will be the only allowed action.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_Copy: The data can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data can be linked

The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drop target.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or
#PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.
commands.remarks:
Drag & Drop can basically be started any time, but the
left mouse button should be currently pressed as otherwise the operation will end immediately without success.
The usual time to start a Drag & Drop operation is when a Gadget reported an event with
EventType() of #PB_EventType_DragStart.

If the operation was not aborted, the event loop will receive a #PB_Event_WindowDrop or
#PB_Event_GadgetDrop event of type #PB_Drop_Private.
commands.example:
Enumeration ; Gadgets
    #List1
    #List2
  EndEnumeration
  
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 415, 410, "Drag from List1 to List2", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    ListIconGadget(#List1, 5, 5, 200, 400, "List1" , 140)
    ListIconGadget(#List2, 210, 5, 200, 400, "List2" , 140)
    
    For i = 0 To 9
      AddGadgetItem(#List1, -1, "Item " + Str(i))
      AddGadgetItem(#List2, -1, "Item " + Str(i + 10))
    Next
    
    ; Allows dragging an element from #List1 to #List2
    EnableGadgetDrop(#List2, #PB_Drop_Private, #PB_Drag_Copy, 1)
    
    Repeat
      Select WaitWindowEvent()
        Case #PB_Event_GadgetDrop ; the drag event
          Select EventGadget()
            Case #List2
              Select EventDropType()
                Case #PB_Drop_Private
                  tmp = GetGadgetState(#List2)
                  AddGadgetItem(#List2, tmp, tmp$)
                  tmp = GetGadgetState(#List1)
                  RemoveGadgetItem(#List1, tmp)
              EndSelect
          EndSelect
        Case #PB_Event_Gadget
          Select EventGadget()
            Case #List1
              Select EventType()
                Case #PB_EventType_DragStart
                  tmp = GetGadgetState(#List1)
                  If tmp <> -1
                    tmp$ = GetGadgetItemText(#List1, tmp)
                    DragPrivate(1) ; set drag type = 1 until successful drop action (into #List2)
                  EndIf
              EndSelect
          EndSelect
        Case #PB_Event_CloseWindow
          End
      EndSelect
    ForEver
  EndIf

commands.name: DragText
commands.description: Starts a Drag & Drop operation with text data.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to drag.

parameters.name: Actions (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the data.
If the parameter is not specified, #PB_Drag_Copy will be the only allowed action.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_Copy: The text can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The text can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The text can be linked

The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drop target.
(On MacOSX, the actions are only treated as a suggestion. The drop target can still choose another action.)

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the above Drag & Drop action values to indicate what action the user took, or
#PB_Drag_None if the user aborted the Drag & Drop operation.

Note that if #PB_Drag_Move is returned, it is your responsibility to remove the
dragged text data from your application.
commands.remarks:
Drag & Drop can basically be started any time, but the
left mouse button should be currently pressed as otherwise the operation will end immediately without success.
The usual time to start a Drag & Drop operation is when a Gadget reported an event with
EventType() of #PB_EventType_DragStart. On MacOS X the #PB_EventType_DragStart event has to be handled using BindEvent() or BindGadgetEvent().
commands.example:
Procedure DragStartHandler()
    ExamineDraggedItems()
    While NextDraggedItem()
      Text$ + GetGadgetItemText(0, DraggedItemIndex()) + Chr(10)
    Wend
    
    Debug "Dragging text: " + Text$
    
    DragText(Text$)
  EndProcedure

  ; Select some files or folders and drag them to another application
  ;
  If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 400, 400, "Drag & Drop")
    ListViewGadget(0, 10, 10, 380, 380, #PB_ListView_MultiSelect)
    AddGadgetItem(0, -1, "Item 1")
    AddGadgetItem(0, -1, "Item 2")
    AddGadgetItem(0, -1, "Item 3")
    
    ; BindGadgetEvent() is required to handle the drag start event
    BindGadgetEvent(0, @DragStartHandler(), #PB_EventType_DragStart)
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: EnableGadgetDrop
commands.description:
Enables a gadget to be a target for Drag & Drop operations of a specific format.
When the user drags data of this format over the gadget, the cursor will indicate that
the data can be dropped there.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description: The PureBasic gadget number for the gadget in question.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description:
The data format, which can be one of the following values, or an OS specific ID for
a custom format (see DragOSFormats() for more information).

#PB_Drop_Text : Accept text on this gadget
#PB_Drop_Image : Accept images on this gadget
#PB_Drop_Files : Accept filenames on this gadget
#PB_Drop_Private: Accept a "private" Drag & Drop on this gadget

parameters.name: Actions
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the data.
The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drag source.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_None: The data format will not be accepted on the gadget
#PB_Drag_Copy: The data can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data can be linked

parameters.name: PrivateType (optional)
parameters.description:
The type of private Drag & Drop to accept if 'Format' is #PB_Drop_Private.
See DragPrivate() for more information.
This parameter is ignored for other formats.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Multiple formats can be allowed on the same gadget. If the drag source provides multiple formats
that match the list of accepted formats, the one that was added last will be accepted. So the preferred
format in which to receive data should be enabled last.

If data was dropped on the gadget, the program will receive a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop event.
EventGadget() will indicate the target gadget and the Event functions of this
library can be used to get the dropped data.
commands.example:
; Drag a file to one of the gadets and you will receive the file path
  ;
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 500, 200, "Drop File Here", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  
    StringGadget(0, 10, 10, 500 - 20, 30, "")
    EditorGadget(1, 10, 50, 500 - 20, 140)
    
    EnableGadgetDrop(0, #PB_Drop_Files, #PB_Drag_Copy)
    EnableGadgetDrop(1, #PB_Drop_Files, #PB_Drag_Copy)
  
    Repeat
        Select WaitWindowEvent()
            Case #PB_Event_GadgetDrop
                Select EventGadget()
                    Case 0 ; gadgets that received a file/folder drag and drop event
                        If Not FindString(EventDropFiles(), Chr(10))
                            SetGadgetText(0, EventDropFiles())
                        EndIf
                    Case 1
                        SetGadgetText(1, EventDropFiles())
                EndSelect
            Case #PB_Event_CloseWindow
                CloseWindow(0)
                End
        EndSelect
    ForEver
  EndIf

commands.name: EnableWindowDrop
commands.description:
Enables a window to be a target for Drag & Drop operations of a specific format. Only the area not covered
by any gadgets will be the target area. When the user drags data of this format over the window, the cursor
will indicate that the data can be dropped there.

parameters.name: #Window
parameters.description: The PureBasic window number for the window in question.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description:
The data format, which can be one of the following values, or an OS specific ID for
a custom format (see DragOSFormats() for more information).

#PB_Drop_Text : Accept text on this window
#PB_Drop_Image : Accept images on this window
#PB_Drop_Files : Accept filenames on this window
#PB_Drop_Private: Accept a "private" Drag & Drop on this window

parameters.name: Actions
parameters.description:
A combination of the Drag & Drop actions that should be allowed for the data.
The user can decide which of these actions to take by pressing modifier keys like Ctrl or Shift. The actions
that can really be taken also depend on the actions allowed by the drag source.
Possible actions are: (they can be combined with '|')

#PB_Drag_None: The data format will not be accepted on the gadget
#PB_Drag_Copy: The data can be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data can be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data can be linked

parameters.name: PrivateType (optional)
parameters.description:
The type of private Drag & Drop to accept if 'Format' is #PB_Drop_Private.
See DragPrivate() for more information.
This parameter is ignored for other formats.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Multiple formats can be allowed on the same window. If the drag source provides multiple formats
that match the list of accepted formats, the one that was added last will be accepted. So the preferred
format in which to receive data should be enabled last.

If data was dropped on the window, the program will receive a #PB_Event_WindowDrop event.
EventWindow() will indicate the target window and the Event functions of this
library can be used to get the dropped data.

commands.name: EventDropAction
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent(), this
function returns the action that should be taken with the data.
commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_Drag_Copy: The data should be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data should be moved (The drag source is responsible for removing the original data)
#PB_Drag_Link: The data should be linked

commands.name: EventDropBuffer
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with an
OS specific format, this function can be used to access the data.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the memory address where the dropped data is located. The EventDropSize() command
returns the size of this buffer.
commands.remarks:
The returned memory buffer is internal to the library and should not be freed. It is also only valid
until the next call to WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent(),
so the data should be copied if it is required for longer than that.

commands.name: EventDropFiles
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with a format (can be get with EventDropType()) of #PB_Drop_Files,
this function returns the dropped filenames.
commands.returnValue:
Returns a list of filenames or directories, all with full path. The individual names are separated
by a Chr(10) (linefeed) character.

commands.name: EventDropImage
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with a
format (can be get with EventDropType()) of #PB_Drop_Image,
this function can be used to retrieve the dropped image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description:
The number for the new image to create.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Depth (optional)
parameters.description: The color depth for the new image. Supported values are 24 and 32-bit. 24-bit is the default.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was successfully created and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Image parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

commands.name: EventDropPrivate
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with a
format (can be get with EventDropType()) of #PB_Drop_Private,
this function returns the 'PrivateType' that was dropped.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the private type value used when starting the Drag & Drop operation.
(See DragPrivate() for more information.)

commands.name: EventDropSize
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with an
OS specific format, this function returns the size of the dropped data.
commands.returnValue: Returns the size in bytes of the memory buffer returned by EventDropBuffer().

commands.name: EventDropText
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent() with a
format (can be get with EventDropType()) of #PB_Drop_Text,
this function returns the text that was dropped.
commands.returnValue: Returns the dropped text.

commands.name: EventDropType
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent(), this
function returns the format of the dropped data.
commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values, or an OS specific ID for a custom format (see
DragOSFormats() for more information)

#PB_Drop_Text : Text was dropped. (use EventDropText() to retrieve it)
#PB_Drop_Image : An image was dropped. (use EventDropImage() to retrieve it)
#PB_Drop_Files : Filenames were dropped. (use EventDropFiles() to retrieve them)
#PB_Drop_Private: A "private" operation finished. (use EventDropPrivate() to know its type)
commands.remarks: To handle OS specific formats, EventDropBuffer() and EventDropSize() can be used.

commands.name: EventDropX
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent(), this
function returns the X position at which the data was dropped.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the x coordinate of the drop location relative to the gadget or window in which the data
was dropped.

commands.name: EventDropY
commands.description:
After a #PB_Event_GadgetDrop or #PB_Event_WindowDrop is received by
WaitWindowEvent() or WindowEvent(), this
function returns the Y position at which the data was dropped.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the y coordinate of the drop location relative to the gadget or window in which the data
was dropped.

commands.name: ExamineDraggedItems
commands.description:
Start to examine the dragged items with the functions NextDraggedItem() and DraggedItemIndex(). It has to be used after a #PB_Event_DragStart.
This function is supported for the following gadgets: ExplorerListGadget(), ExplorerTreeGadget(), ListIconGadget(), ListViewGadget() and TreeGadget().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Procedure DragStartHandler()
    
    ; Start to examine the dragged items. Have to be after a #PB_EventType_DragStart event
    ;
    ExamineDraggedItems()
    
    ; Iterate over the dragged items
    ;
    While NextDraggedItem()
      Debug "Dragged item: " + GetGadgetText(0) + GetGadgetItemText(0, DraggedItemIndex())
    Wend
  EndProcedure

  ; Select some files or folders and drag them to another application
  ;
  If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 400, 400, "Drag & Drop")
    ExplorerListGadget(0, 10, 10, 380, 380, GetHomeDirectory(), #PB_Explorer_MultiSelect)
    
    ; BindGadgetEvent() is required to handle the drag start event
    BindGadgetEvent(0, @DragStartHandler(), #PB_EventType_DragStart)
    
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()  
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: NextDraggedItem
commands.description: This function must be called after ExamineDraggedItems(). It will iterate over dragged items.
commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if another dragged item is available or zero if there are no more dragged item.

commands.name: SetDragCallback
commands.description:
A callback function to be called during a Drag & Drop operation initiated from this application.
The callback allows to modify the Drag & Drop process provided by PureBasic, for example by providing
a custom cursor through the API of the Operating system.

parameters.name: @DragCallback()
parameters.description:
The address of a function to call during a drag operation.
The form and purpose of the callback is dependent on the OS.
It must take the following form:

Windows:

Procedure DragCallback(Action.l)

ProcedureReturn #True
EndProcedure

The callback is called during the Drag & Drop operation. Action specifies the action that would be taken
if the user released the mouse at this point. It can be one of these values:

#PB_Drag_None: The data will not be accepted if dropped here
#PB_Drag_Copy: The data will be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data will be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data will be linked

The callback can provide a custom cursor or drag image. If it does so, it should return #False.
Returning #True will cause the default cursor to be used.

Linux:

Procedure DragCallback(*Context.GdkDragContext, isStart.l)

EndProcedure

The callback is only called at the start and the end of a Drag & Drop operation. The '*Context' parameter
specifies the gdk drag context of this operation, 'isStart' specifies whether this is the start or the
end of the operation. The return-value of the callback is ignored.

Gtk functions like gtk_drag_set_icon_pixbuf_() can be used in the callback to set a different drag image
for the operation.

MacOSX:

Not supported.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetDropCallback
commands.description:
A callback function to be called when data is dragged over a gadget or window that allows
data to be dropped (see EnableGadgetDrop() / EnableWindowDrop()).
The callback allows to modify the Drag & Drop process provided by PureBasic, for example by providing
extra visual notification on the target gadget or window.

parameters.name: @DropCallback()
parameters.description:
A callback to be called during a drop operation.

The callback is called as the mouse enters, moves and leaves the target gadget or window and allows to
provide additional feedback to the user, for example by highlighting the target item or area.
Furthermore the callback can deny the currently intended action and this way specify more detailed
where within a gadget or window the data can be dropped.
The cursor should not be modified here, as the drag source is responsible for this.

The form of the callback is described below:

Procedure DropCallback(TargetHandle, State, Format, Action, x, y)

ProcedureReturn #True
EndProcedure

The first parameter specifies the OS specific handle for the target gadget or window.
On Windows this is a HWND value, on Linux a GtkWidget pointer and on MacOSX it is a ControlRef or WindowRef value.
These are the same values as returned by GadgetID() or WindowID()
for the target gadget or window.

'State' specifies the current state of the Drag & Drop operation and is one of the following values:

#PB_Drag_Enter : The mouse entered the gadget or window
#PB_Drag_Update: The mouse was moved inside the gadget or window, or the intended action changed
#PB_Drag_Leave : The mouse left the gadget or window (Format, Action, x, y are 0 here)
#PB_Drag_Finish: The Drag & Drop finished

'Format' specifies the data format and can be one of the following values, or an OS specific ID for
a custom format (see DragOSFormats() for more information).

#PB_Drop_Text : Accept text on this gadget or window
#PB_Drop_Image : Accept images on this gadget or window
#PB_Drop_Files : Accept filenames on this gadget or window
#PB_Drop_Private: Accept a "private" Drag & Drop on this gadget or window

'Action' specifies the action that would be taken if the user released the mouse at this point.
It can be one of these values:

#PB_Drag_None: The data will not be accepted if dropped here
#PB_Drag_Copy: The data will be copied
#PB_Drag_Move: The data will be moved
#PB_Drag_Link: The data will be linked

By returning #True, the callback allows the action to take place at this point.
By returning #False, the callback denies the action (the cursor will be
changed to a "forbidden" cursor by the drag source, except on Linux GTK).
Especially if 'State' is #PB_Drag_Finish, returning #False will cause
the whole Drag & Drop operation to fail.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: Add3DArchive
commands.description:
Add a new absolute or relative path to the current 3D path list. All the 3D functions which need
to load data (e.g. texture, mesh, sky,
world) will use this path. It needs to be put after OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen().

You may wonder why there is a special way to handle the files for 3D functions? Because it makes the data access more flexible and now,
you can access the data using the standard filesystem or directly via the archive file like a .zip file. It's a
very cool feature because you can pack all your data in one big compressed file, and then access the assets as
if these were contained a standard directory.

parameters.name: Path$
parameters.description: The path to add to the 3D path list. It can be a real filesystem path, or a ZIP archive.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_3DArchive_FileSystem : Standard directory
#PB_3DArchive_Zip : Compressed zip file

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Add3DArchive("MyData.zip", #PB_3DArchive_Zip) ; Add the .zip as a directory in the path
  LoadTexture(0, "MyTexture.jpg")               ; load the MyTexture.jpg from the zip
  LoadTexture(1, "World/Grass.jpg")             ; load the Grass.jpg from the zip, in the World\ path

commands.name: AmbientColor
commands.description: Changes the ambient color of the world.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The new ambient color to set. RGB() can be used to get a valid Color value.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AntialiasingMode
commands.description:
Changes the fullscreen antialiasing mode. This function has to be called before OpenScreen() to have
any effect.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following constants:

#PB_AntialiasingMode_None: No antialiasing (default).
#PB_AntialiasingMode_x2 : x2 fullscreen antialiasing (FSAA).
#PB_AntialiasingMode_x4 : x4 fullscreen antialiasing (FSAA).
#PB_AntialiasingMode_x6 : x6 fullscreen antialiasing (FSAA).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: Depending of the graphic card, this command can have a severe impact on rendering performance.

commands.name: BodyPick
syntax: Result = BodyPick(#Camera, Picked, x, y, Locked)
commands.description: Simulates a mouse click and starts the manipulate the entity at the specified coordinate.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: Picked
parameters.description:
If #True, the picked body won't be released until a new function call with this parameter sets to #False.
It can only have one picked body at the same time.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The coordinates, in pixels, of the point.

parameters.name: Locked
parameters.description:
If set to #True, the picked body won't be able to freely rotate when moving it. If set to #False, the body will rotate
freely according to body move.

commands.returnValue: The #Entity picked, or -1 if no entity are found at these coordinates.

commands.name: ConvertLocalToWorldPosition
commands.description:
Converts the local x,y,z coordinates into world coordinates. GetX(), GetY() and GetZ()
will be used to get the converted coordinates.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object ID to convert the coordinate from. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The local coordinates to convert.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ConvertWorldToLocalPosition
commands.description:
Converts the world x,y,z coordinates into local coordinates. GetX(), GetY() and GetZ()
will be used to get the converted coordinates.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object ID to convert the coordinate from. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The world coordinates to convert.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateWater
syntax: CreateWater(WaveTextureID, FoamTextureID, WaterColor, SkyColor, Distance.f, WaveBig.f, WaveLittle.f, Swell.f, Foam.f)
commands.description: Creates a world wide water plane.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EnableWorldCollisions
commands.description: Enable or disable the collisions in the world.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
If nonzero, the collisions will be enabled (default). The collisions is applied to all the entities which
have a body set with CreateEntityBody(). Collisions only work if the physics engine is enabled with EnableWorldPhysics().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EnableWorldPhysics
commands.description: Enable or disable the physics engine in the world.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
If nonzero, the physics engine will be enabled (default). The physics engine is applied to all the entities which
have a body set with CreateEntityBody(). Collisions can be enabled with EnableWorldCollisions(). To have working collisions, the physics
engine has to be enabled.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: Engine3DStatus
commands.description: Gets the 3D engine current status.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Engine3D_NbRenderedTriangles: Nb rendered triangles in the last frame.
#PB_Engine3D_NbRenderedBatches : Nb rendered batches in the last frame.
#PB_Engine3D_CurrentFPS : Current frame rate.
#PB_Engine3D_AverageFPS : Average frame rate achieved since the engine started running.
#PB_Engine3D_MaximumFPS : Best frame rate achieved since the engine started running.
#PB_Engine3D_MinimumFPS : Worst frame rate achieved since the engine started running.
#PB_Engine3D_ResetFPS : Reset all the frame rate related statistics.

commands.returnValue: The value depending of the specified 'Type'.

commands.name: ExamineWorldCollisions
commands.description:
Examine the collisions which have occurred in the world since the last call. Collisions have to be
enabled with EnableWorldCollisions() before using this command. To step through the collisions,
use NextWorldCollision().

parameters.name: Contacts
parameters.description:
If set the #True, contact information about the colliding objects are collected and can be retrieved with
WorldCollisionContact(), WorldCollisionNormal() and WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse(). If set to #False,
no contact information are collected (faster).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the collisions can be examined, returns zero otherwise.

commands.name: FetchOrientation
commands.description:
Get the orientation of the specified object. GetX(), GetY(), GetZ() and GetW()
will be used to get orientation values.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object ID to get the orientation. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the orientation. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute orientation of the object in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the orientation of the object relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FirstWorldCollisionEntity
commands.description: Returns the #Entity number of the first object in the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions().
commands.returnValue: Returns the #Entity number of the first object in the current collision.

commands.name: Fog
commands.description:
Creates a fog at the specified distance of the camera. The fog effect is
applied to all cameras. The fog is also applied automatically to
the SkyBox() and SkyDome() commands if called before them.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The fog color. RGB() can be used to get a valid color value.

parameters.name: Intensity
parameters.description: The fog intensity. If sets to zero, the fog effect is disable.

parameters.name: StartDistance
parameters.description: The distance from the camera (in world units) where the fog should start.

parameters.name: EndDistance
parameters.description: The distance from the camera where the fog is fully opaque.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: GetW
commands.description: Returns the w value of the last called command. The only supported command is FetchOrientation().
commands.returnValue: Returns the w value of the last called command.

commands.name: GetWorldAttribute
commands.description: Get the specified attribute of the world.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute value to get. The following attributes are available:

#PB_Shadow_FarDistance : get shadow far distance.
#PB_Shadow_Color : get the current shadow color as RGBA().
#PB_SkyDome_SkyColor : get the color of the sky as RGBA().
#PB_SkyDome_RiseColor : get the sun rise color as RGBA().
#PB_SkyDome_NbCloudLayers: get the number of cloud layer.
#PB_SkyDome_CloudsHeight : get the height of the clouds in world unit.
#PB_Water_WaterColor : get the water color as RGBA().
#PB_Water_SkyColor : get the sky color as reflected in the water as RGBA().
#PB_Water_WaveHeight : get the wave height.
#PB_Water_WaveSmall : get the wave riddle amplitude.
#PB_Water_Swell : get the water swell intensity.
#PB_Water_Foam : get the foam intensity.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the specified attribute.

commands.name: GetX
commands.description:
Returns the x value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation(), ConvertLocalToWorldPosition()
and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition().
commands.returnValue: Returns the x value of the last called command.

commands.name: GetY
commands.description:
Returns the y value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation(), ConvertLocalToWorldPosition()
and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition().
commands.returnValue: Returns the y value of the last called command.

commands.name: GetZ
commands.description:
Returns the z value of the last called command. Supported commands are FetchOrientation(), ConvertLocalToWorldPosition()
and ConvertWorldToLocalPosition().
commands.returnValue: Returns the z value of the last called command.

commands.name: InitEngine3D
commands.description:
Initializes the 3D environment for later use. You must put this function at
the top of your source code if you want to use any of the 3D functions.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Engine3D_NoLog : No log will be written to disk or printed to the console (default).
#PB_Engine3D_DebugLog : A debug log file named 'Ogre.log' will be created in the current directory, to help
debugging or user reports. A lot of actions are logged in this file, but it shouldn't
affect performances so it can even be activated for a release product.
#PB_Engine3D_DebugOutput: The actions are printed to the console. You must remember to set the executable format
to 'Console' when you are compiling your programs.

parameters.name: LibraryName$ (optional)
parameters.description:
Name of the Engine3D file which should be loaded. If it is put to another place than the current
directory, it could be specified here.

commands.returnValue:
Returns non-zero if the library has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
If initialization fails, the program should quit or all 3D function calls should be disabled.
commands.remarks:
InitEngine3D() tries to load the Engine3D library (named 'Engine3D.dll' on Windows, 'engine3d.so' on Linux
and 'engine3d.dylib' on OS X, found in the PureBasic/compilers/ directory). If it fails, it's probably because the library
is not found or doesn't match the current PureBasic version. On Windows, a recent version of openGL drivers needs to be installed.

After calling this function, you will not be able to use the ScreenOutput() function.

commands.name: LoadWorld
commands.description:
This function loads an entire world. Currently, the Quake3 BSP format is the only one supported but more formats will follow.
The Filename$ must be accessible in the 3D path, so the Add3DArchive() function should be used
before calling this function. A world can be easily created using third party tools like 'Quark'. A world can contain a sky,
building, lights and more. Actually, all Quake 3 maps can be loaded out of the box with full detail.
If the 'Result' is 0, the world could not be loaded.

The BSP format is owned by iD Software and can only be used in freeware programs. Commercial software must acquire a license
from iD to use this format. The license scheme is beyond PureBasic and Fantaisie Software can't be responsible
for the incorrect use of this function.

commands.name: MousePick
commands.description:
Simulates a mouse click and returns which object is under the specified 2D point on the
specified camera.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The coordinates, in pixels, of the point.

parameters.name: PickMask (optional)
parameters.description:
The entity mask used while performing the ray cast. Only the entities with a mask matching
the PickMask value will be reported. If this parameter is omitted, all the entities are valid
for the ray detection. The mask can be a combination, to select more than one entity group.
To have more information about pick mask, see CreateEntity().

commands.returnValue:
The returned value can be:

-1 : Nothing has been detected
#PB_World_WaterPick: the click occurred on the water.
0 and above: the click occurred on the #Entity. The entity pick is based on its bounding box, not on its mesh.

To get more information about the picked object position, use PickX(), PickY() and PickZ().

commands.name: MouseRayCast
commands.description:
Casts a ray from the 2D point through the scene, and checks if an object is
crossing the ray. This function doesn't rely on the physic engine. The normals
value at the impact point are available with NormalX(), NormalY() and NormalZ().

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The coordinates, in pixels, of the point.

parameters.name: PickMask
parameters.description:
The entity mask used while performing the ray cast. Only the entities with a mask matching
the PickMask value will be reported. If this parameter is omitted, all the entities are valid
for the ray detection. The mask can be a combination, to select more than one entity group.
To have more information about pick mask, see CreateEntity().

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of the object in contact with the ray, -1 otherwise.

commands.name: NextWorldCollision
commands.description:
Go to the next collision. ExamineWorldCollisions() needs to be called successfully before using this command.
To get more information about the current collision, use FirstWorldCollisionEntity(),
SecondWorldCollisionEntity(), WorldCollisionContact(), WorldCollisionNormal() and WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse().
commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if there is another collision to be examined, or zero if there is no more collisions.

commands.name: NormalX
commands.description: Returns the 'x' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast(), RayCollide() or MouseRayCast().
commands.returnValue: Returns the 'x' normal value at the crossed point.

commands.name: NormalY
commands.description: Returns the 'y' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast(), RayCollide() or MouseRayCast().
commands.returnValue: Returns the 'y' normal value at the crossed point.

commands.name: NormalZ
commands.description: Returns the 'z' normal value at the crossed point, after RayCast(), RayCollide() or MouseRayCast().
commands.returnValue: Returns the 'z' normal value at the crossed point.

commands.name: Parse3DScripts
commands.description:
Parses all the .materials OGRE scripts found in the paths set with Add3DArchive(). This
allows the use of meshes with complex materials scripts directly in PureBasic.
When creating the entity the constant #PB_Material_None
has to be specified, so all the material information will be taken from the
script, if it was correctly loaded.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: More information about OGRE material scripts can be found at OGRE online manual.

commands.name: PickX
commands.description:
After MousePick() or RayPick(), it returns the 'x' position of the picked object in world coordinates.

After PointPick(), it returns the 'x' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.

commands.name: PickY
commands.description:
After MousePick() or RayPick(), it returns the 'y' position of the picked object in world coordinates.

After PointPick(), it returns the 'y' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.

commands.name: PickZ
commands.description:
After MousePick() or RayPick(), it returns the 'z' position of the picked object in world coordinates.

After PointPick(), it returns the 'z' direction of the picked point, between -1 and 1.

commands.name: Pitch
commands.description: Pitch the specified object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The entity to pitch. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The pitch value (in degree).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The pitch mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative pitch, from the current pitch.
#PB_Absolute: absolute pitch (default).

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local pitch.
#PB_Parent: pitch relative to the parent.
#PB_World : pitch relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: PointPick
commands.description:
Allows to get the direction the specified 2D point on the
specified camera.

parameters.name: #Camera
parameters.description: The camera to use.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The coordinates, in pixels, of the point.

commands.returnValue:
Returns non-zero if the pick was successful.
To get the point direction, use PickX(), PickY() and PickZ().

commands.name: RayCast
syntax: Result = RayCast(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ, PickMask)
commands.description:
Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an object is
crossing the ray. This function doesn't rely on the physic engine. The normals
value at the impact point are available with NormalX(), NormalY() and NormalZ().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The first point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ
parameters.description: The second point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: PickMask
parameters.description:
The entity mask used while performing the ray cast. Only the entities with a mask matching
the PickMask value will be reported. If this parameter is omitted, all the entities are valid
for the ray detection. The mask can be a combination, to select more than one entity group.
To have more information about pick mask, see CreateEntity().

commands.returnValue: Returns -1 if the ray has collided with any object.

commands.name: RayCollide
syntax: Result = RayCollide(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ [, CollisionGroup , CollisionMask]])
commands.description:
Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an entity is
colliding the ray. This function relies on the physic engine, which needs to be activated with EnableWorldPhysics() before using this command.
Only entities with bodies will react to the ray.
To get the position about the collide point, use PickX(), PickY() and PickZ().
The normals values at the collide point are available with NormalX(), NormalY() and NormalZ().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The first point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ
parameters.description: The second point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: CollisionGroup, CollisionMask (optional)
parameters.description:
The collision group and collision mask to use. Can be useful to filter which entity should collide to the ray. Collision
group and mask can be changed with SetEntityCollisionFilter().

commands.returnValue: Returns the entity number if the ray has collided with one, or -1 if no collision has occurred.

commands.name: RayPick
syntax: Result = RayPick(x, y, z, DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ [, PickMask])
commands.description:
Casts a ray between the first point and the second point, and checks if an object is
crossing the ray.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The first point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: DestinationX, DestinationY, DestinationZ
parameters.description: The second point coordinates, in world unit.

parameters.name: PickMask (optional)
parameters.description:
The entity mask used while performing the ray pick. Only the entities with a mask matching
the PickMask value will be reported. If this parameter is omitted, all the entities are valid
for the ray detection. The mask can be a combination, to select more than one entity group.
To have more information about pick mask, see CreateEntity().

commands.returnValue:
The returned value can be:

-1 : Nothing has been crossed.
#PB_World_WaterPick: the ray crossed the water.
0 and above: the ray crossed an #Entity. The entity detection is based on its bounding box, not on its mesh.

To get more information about the picked object position, use PickX(), PickY() and PickZ().

commands.name: RenderWorld
commands.description:
Renders the whole world on the screen. This function should be called once all 3D operations are
finished and only one time per frame.

parameters.name: ElapsedPhysicTime (optional)
parameters.description:
If set it will force the physic engine to use this value, in milliseconds, as elapsed time since the last call of RenderWorld.
It can be useful to makes the physic simulation faster or slower than real-time.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the elapsed time since the last frame in milliseconds. It can be useful to have an accurate time based simulation
if the frame render time isn't stable.
commands.remarks:
Once the RenderWorld() function has been performed, it's possible
to use regular 2D functions like DisplaySprite() to display 2D sprites over the 3D world.

commands.name: Roll
commands.description: Roll the specified object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The entity to roll. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The roll value (in degree).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The roll mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative roll, from the current roll.
#PB_Absolute: absolute roll (default).

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local roll.
#PB_Parent: roll relative to the parent.
#PB_World : roll relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SecondWorldCollisionEntity
commands.description: Returns the #Entity number of the second object in the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions()().
commands.returnValue: Returns the #Entity number of the second object in the current collision.

commands.name: SetGUITheme3D
commands.description:
As CEGUI support skinning, this command allow to select which theme and which font to use for the GUI.
This command has to be called before any other GUI commands to have an effect.

parameters.name: ThemeName$
parameters.description: The new theme to use, specified without the '.scheme' extension.

parameters.name: FontName$
parameters.description: The new font to use, specified without the '.font' extension.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: For more information about skins, visit the CEGUI web site.

commands.name: SetOrientation
commands.description: Set the orientation of the specified object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object ID to set the orientation. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: x, y, z, w
parameters.description: The new orientation value.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetRenderQueue
commands.description: Change the render order of the specified object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object ID to convert the coordinate from. It can be one of the following type:

- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Queue
parameters.description:
The queue number to use to render the object. Queue number can be from 0 (background) to 100 (foreground). The default queue is 0, and is render
behind all the other render queues.

parameters.name: Priority (optional)
parameters.description: The priority to use within the queue. Valid values are from 0 (background) to 10000 (foreground).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetWorldAttribute
commands.description: Set the specified attribute of the world.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute value to set. The following attributes are available:

#PB_Shadow_FarDistance : set shadow far distance
#PB_Shadow_Color : change the current shadow color
#PB_SkyDome_Free : free the sky dome previously created by SkyDome()
#PB_SkyDome_SkyColor : the color of the sky as RGBA()
#PB_SkyDome_RiseColor : the sun rise color as RGBA()
#PB_SkyDome_NbCloudLayers: set the number of cloud layer (value between X and X)
#PB_SkyDome_CloudsHeight : set the height of the clouds in world coordinates
#PB_Water_WaterColor : set the water color as RGBA().
#PB_Water_SkyColor : set the sky color as reflected in the water as RGBA()
#PB_Water_WaveHeight : set the wave height (value between 0 to 3).
#PB_Water_WaveSmall : set the wave riddle amplitude (value between 0 to 3).
#PB_Water_Swell : set the swell intensity (value between 0 to 2).
#PB_Water_Foam : set the foam intensity (value between 0 to 1).
#PB_Water_Free : free the world water plane previously created with CreateWater()

commands.returnValue: Change the value of the specified attribute.

commands.name: ShowGUI
commands.description:
Shows or hides the whole GUI elements, which are composed of 3d windows and
3d gadgets.

parameters.name: Transparency
parameters.description: Transparency level of the GUI. Valid values are between 0 (hidden) and 255 (fully opaque).

parameters.name: ShowMouse
parameters.description:
Change the mouse cursor visibility. If ShowMouse = 1, the mouse cursor will be displayed,
if ShowMouse = 0 it will be hidden.

parameters.name: #Camera (optional)
parameters.description: If set the GUI will be displayed or not on this camera. Works together with the following 'Enable' parameter.

parameters.name: Enable (optional)
parameters.description: Enable or disable the GUI display on the previously selected camera. Works together with the previous '#Camera' parameter.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SkyBox
syntax: Result = SkyBox(TextureName$ [, FogColor, FogIntensity, FogStartDistance, FogEndDistance])
commands.description:
Loads a 6 face cube and creates an artificial box which is far away from the camera but close to the world.
This is a very useful function to easily make a closed world.

parameters.name: TextureName$
parameters.description:
The textures must be in a path previously declared with the Add3DArchive() function.
The base name of the textures, which should be named using the following rule:

TextureName_BK ; BacK face
TextureName_FR ; FRont face
TextureName_DN ; DowN face
TextureName_UP ; UP face
TextureName_LF ; LeFt face
TextureName_RT ; RighT face

parameters.name: FogColor (optional)
parameters.description:
The fog color. RGB() can be used to get a valid color value. If not specified, the fog settings are inherited from
the Fog() command.

parameters.name: FogIntensity (optional)
parameters.description: The fog intensity. If sets to zero, the fog effect is disable.

parameters.name: FogStartDistance (optional)
parameters.description: The distance from the camera (in world units) where the fog should start.

parameters.name: FogEndDistance (optional)
parameters.description: The distance from the camera where the fog is fully opaque.

commands.returnValue:
Returns non-zero if the SkyBox has been successfully created. If the textures can't be loaded, the skybox is created with
blank textures.

commands.name: SkyDome
syntax: Result = SkyDome(TextureID, SkyColor, RiseColor [, NbCloudLayers, Height.f, SpeedX.f, SpeedZ.f])
commands.description: Creates a new SkyDome which is a curved moving sky displayed using the specified cloud texture.

parameters.name: TextureID
parameters.description: The cloud texture id to use. TextureID() can be used to get a valid value.

parameters.name: SkyColor
parameters.description: The sky color as RGBA().

parameters.name: RiseColor
parameters.description: The sun rising color as RGBA().

parameters.name: NbCloudLayers (optional)
parameters.description: The number of clouds layer, starting from 1.

parameters.name: Height (optional)
parameters.description: The clouds height in world unit.

parameters.name: SpeedX, SpeedZ (optional)
parameters.description: The clouds moving speed

commands.returnValue: Returns non-zero if the SkyDome has been successfully created.
commands.example:
#EndDistance = 1024*4

  InitEngine3D() : InitSprite() : InitKeyboard()

  ExamineDesktops() : dx = DesktopWidth(0)*0.9 : dy = DesktopHeight(0)*0.9
  OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, DesktopUnscaledX(dx), DesktopUnscaledY(dy), "SkyDome - Press ESC to quit", #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID(0), 0, 0, dx, dy, 0, 0, 0)

  Add3DArchive(#PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/3d/Data/Textures", #PB_3DArchive_FileSystem)
  Parse3DScripts()

  ; Camera
  CreateCamera(0, 0, 0, 100, 100)
  MoveCamera(0,0,5,0) 
  CameraLookAt(0,2,5,10)

  ; Sky
  TextureSky = LoadTexture(#PB_Any,"sky.png")
  SkyDome(TextureID(TextureSky), $cc6600, $0088ff, 3, 400, -0.5, 0)

  ; Sun
  CreateLight(0, $ff88ff, 20000, 40000, 20000)
  AmbientColor($010101)
  Fog($554488,1, 0, #EndDistance)

  Repeat
    While WindowEvent() : Wend
    ExamineKeyboard()
    
    RenderWorld()
    FlipBuffers()    
  Until KeyboardReleased(#PB_Key_Escape)

commands.name: WorldCollisionAppliedImpulse
commands.description:
Returns the applied impulse about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions().
ExamineWorldCollisions() 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working.

Fetch contact information about the collision being examined with ExamineWorldCollisions()().
ExamineWorldCollisions() 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working.
The contact vector values can be retrieved with GetX(), GetY() and GetZ().

ExamineWorldCollisions() 'Contacts' parameter has to be set to #True to have this command working.

commands.name: WorldDebug
commands.description: Changes the world debug mode. This can be very useful to help finding issues with collisions or picking for example.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
Can be a combination of the following constants:

#PB_World_DebugNone : no debug information (default).
#PB_World_DebugEntity: shows the entities bounding boxes.
#PB_World_DebugBody : shows the physics bodies, both static and dynamic.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: WorldGravity
commands.description: Changes the gravity of the world when the physics engine is enabled with EnableWorldPhysics().

parameters.name: Gravity
parameters.description: The new gravity to set. The default gravity value is set to -9.806 (which is Earth's gravitational value).

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description: The gravity force vector to use, to change the gravity direction.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: WorldShadows
commands.description: Sets how shadows will be rendered in the world.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
Type can be one of the following values:

#PB_Shadow_None : No shadows will be displayed in the world. This can save a lot of CPU
power if shadows aren't needed (default)
#PB_Shadow_Modulative: shadows will be displayed for entities that have the cast
shadow set with EntityRenderMode() and #PB_Entity_CastShadow.
This shadow mode is the fastest available, but is not very good-looking as the shadows are not translucent.
#PB_Shadow_Additive : shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast
shadow set with EntityRenderMode() and #PB_Entity_CastShadow.
This mode is slower than the modulative mode, but it looks much better as the shadows are translucent.
Also if some shadows overlap, the shadows will be added resulting in a more realistic darker result.
#PB_Shadow_TextureAdditive: shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast
shadow set with EntityRenderMode() and #PB_Entity_CastShadow. This mode
is average in speed and quality between modulative and additive shadow, and will work even with water.
#PB_Shadow_TextureModulative: shadows will be displayed for the entities which have the cast
shadow set with EntityRenderMode() and #PB_Entity_CastShadow.
This shadow mode is the faster than #PB_Shadow_TextureAdditive but is not very good-looking as the shadows are not translucent.

parameters.name: Distance (optional)
parameters.description: Maximum distance from the camera, in world unit, above which the shadows won't be calculated anymore.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description: Color of the shadows. RGB() can be used to get a valid Color value.

parameters.name: TextureSize (optional)
parameters.description:
Pixel size of the texture used to render the shadow. The bigger it is it, the better the shadow
will be looking, but the slower it will be. The default value is 512, and this value shouldn't be
bigger than 4096.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: Yaw
commands.description: Yaw the specified object.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The entity to yaw. It can be one of the following type:

- Camera : use CameraID() to get a valid ID.
- Entity : use EntityID() to get a valid ID.
- Light : use LightID() to get a valid ID.
- Mesh : use MeshID() to get a valid ID.
- Node : use NodeID() to get a valid ID.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() to get a valid ID.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() to get a valid ID.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() to get a valid ID.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The yaw value (in degree).

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The yaw mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative yaw, from the current yaw.
#PB_Absolute: absolute yaw (default).

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local yaw.
#PB_Parent: yaw relative to the parent.
#PB_World : yaw relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddSubEntity
syntax: Result = AddSubEntity(#Entity, #SubEntity, Type, [OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ [, SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ [, AxisX, AxisY, AxisZ]]])
commands.description: Add a sub entity to an entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: #SubEntity
parameters.description: The entity to add.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
Type defines how the physic engine will handle this entity. It can be one of the following constants:

#PB_Entity_StaticBody : The body is a static only, which means the mesh can't be animated.
This mode allows very precise collisions, as it's done against triangles
(also known as tri-mesh collision). It's also fast when colliding with
a box or sphere entity body type. It's perfect when using a mesh for
a ground or static world.
#PB_Entity_PlaneBody : A 'virtual' plane is set on the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_ConeBody : A 'virtual' cone is set around the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_BoxBody : A 'virtual' box is set around the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_SphereBody : A 'virtual' sphere is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody : A 'virtual' cylinder is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody : A 'virtual' capsule is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_ConvexHullBody : A 'virtual' complex form deduced from the real mesh is set around the entity
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities. This mode is
slower than basic collide forms.
#PB_Entity_CompoundBody : A 'virtual' Compound body is set around the entity and this is the fastest kind
of arbitrary shape. It is defined by a cloud of vertices but the shape formed is the
smallest convex shape that encloses the vertices.

parameters.name: OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ (optional)
parameters.description: Offset of the translation of the body.

parameters.name: SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ (optional)
parameters.description:
The bounding box size of the body. It only applies to the following body type:

#PB_Entity_BoxBody : SizeX, SizeY and SizeZ are available.
#PB_Entity_SphereBody : SizeX is available.
#PB_Entity_ConeBody : SizeX and SizeY are available.
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody: SizeX and SizeY are available.
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody : SizeX, SizeY and SizeZ are available.

If SizeX = -1 then it uses the BoundingBox.

parameters.name: AxisX, AxisY, AxisZ (optional)
parameters.description:
The axis of the body' orientation. It only applies to the following body type:

#PB_Entity_PlaneBody
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody

commands.returnValue: Returns zero if the entity can't be created.
commands.remarks:
It is necessary to use the CreateEntityBody() function with the
#PB_Entity_CompoundBody option after adding all sub-entities.

commands.name: ApplyEntityForce

commands.name: ApplyEntityTorque

Apply a rotation impulse to the entity. The new impulse is added to the rotation force previously

The applied rotation impulse mode. It can be one of the following values:

commands.name: AttachEntityObject
syntax: AttachEntityObject(#Entity, Bone$, ObjectID [, x, y, z, Pitch, Roll, Yaw])
commands.description: Attach an existing object to an entity bone. An object can be detached from an entity with DetachEntityObject().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description:
The bone name in the OGRE mesh, or as specified in CreateBone(). If the bone name is empty, then the object is not attached to a bone
but directly to the entity.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object to attach. It can be one of the following types:

- Entity : use EntityID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Camera : use CameraID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Light : use LightID() as 'ObjectID'.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() as 'ObjectID'.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Node : use NodeID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() as 'ObjetID'.

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description: The relative offset position of the attached object.

parameters.name: Pitch (optional)
parameters.description: The pitch to apply to the attached object.

parameters.name: Roll (optional)
parameters.description: The roll to apply to the attached object.

parameters.name: Yaw (optional)
parameters.description: The yaw to apply to the attached object.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CopyEntity
commands.description:
Creates a #NewEntity which is the exact copy of the specified #Entity. If #PB_Any is used
as '#NewEntity' parameter, the new entity number will be returned as 'Result'.

If the 'Result' is 0, the entity copy has failed. If #NewEntity was already created,
it will be automatically freed and replaced by the new one.

commands.name: CreateEntity
syntax: Result = CreateEntity(#Entity, MeshID, MaterialID, [x, y, z [, PickMask [, VisibilityMask]])
commands.description: Creates a new #Entity using the specified Mesh and Material.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new entity. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: MeshID
parameters.description:
The mesh to use to create the entity. To get a valid mesh id, use MeshID().
Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description:
The material to use to create the entity. To get a valid material id, use MaterialID().
#PB_Material_None can be used as parameter value, to use the .material script associated
to the mesh. Parse3DScripts() should be called before using #PB_Material_None.

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description: The position of the new entity in the world.

parameters.name: PickMask (optional)
parameters.description:
A special value used by RayPick() and MousePick() to select which entity group will be handled.
As it's a mask, each value should be a power of two. 31 different masks are available.
To create a mask value easily, the '<<' operator can be used:

- 1 << 1 : First valid mask value
- 1 << 2 : Second valid mask value
- 1 << 3 : Third valid mask value
- ...
- 1 << 31 : Last valid mask value

To ease the use, constants should be used to store the mask value and used later. When calling the pick functions, masks can be combined with the '|' operator
to select more than one type of entity.

parameters.name: VisibilityMask (optional)
parameters.description:
A mask to select on which camera the entity should be displayed. If this mask match the mask specified in
CreateCamera(), the entity will be displayed on the camera. See 'PickMask' to build correct masks.
If this parameter is omitted, then the entity will be visible on all cameras.

commands.returnValue:
Returns zero if the entity can't be created. If #PB_Any is used
as '#Entity' parameter, the new entity number is returned.

commands.name: CreateEntityBody
syntax: CreateEntityBody(#Entity, Type [, Mass [, Restitution, Friction [, Axis [, SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ]]]])
commands.description:
Changes the type of the body associated with the #Entity.

To have its collisions managed by the physic
engine, an entity has to set a body. In fact, only the body is known by the physic engine, which will
do all the calculation about the entity, check the mass, friction and if it collides will move back
the real entity.

To have any effect, the physic engine needs to be activated with the EnableWorldPhysics().

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
Type defines how the physic engine will handle this entity. It can be one of the following constants:

#PB_Entity_None : No body is associated to the entity (default)
#PB_Entity_StaticBody : The body is a static only, which means the mesh can't be animated.
This mode allows very precise collisions, as it's done against triangles
(also known as tri-mesh collision). It's also fast when colliding with
a box or sphere entity body type. It's perfect when using a mesh for
a ground or static world.
#PB_Entity_PlaneBody : A 'virtual' plane is set on the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_ConeBody : A 'virtual' cone is set around the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_BoxBody : A 'virtual' box is set around the entity (with the same dimensions)
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_SphereBody : A 'virtual' sphere is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody : A 'virtual' cylinder is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody : A 'virtual' capsule is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.
#PB_Entity_ConvexHullBody : A 'virtual' complex form deduced from the real mesh is set around the entity
and is used to manage the collision against the other entities. This mode is
slower than basic collide forms.
#PB_Entity_CompoundBody : A 'virtual' Compound body is set around the entity and is used to manage the collision
against the other entities.

parameters.name: Mass (optional)
parameters.description: Mass of the object. Don't use too big value or it could produce physic incoherencies (1 is the preferred value).

parameters.name: Restitution (optional)
parameters.description: Restitution of the object. This value can also be get or set via GetEntityAttribute() and SetEntityAttribute()

parameters.name: Friction (optional)
parameters.description: Friction of the object. This value can also be get or set via GetEntityAttribute() and SetEntityAttribute()

parameters.name: Axis (optional)
parameters.description:
The axis of the body.

It only applies to the following body type:

#PB_Entity_PlaneBody
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody

parameters.name: SizeX, SizeY, SizeZ (optional)
parameters.description:
The bounding box size of the body. It only applies to the following body type:

#PB_Entity_BoxBody : SizeX, SizeY and SizeZ are available.
#PB_Entity_SphereBody : SizeX is available.
#PB_Entity_ConeBody : SizeX and SizeY are available.
#PB_Entity_CylinderBody: SizeX and SizeY are available.
#PB_Entity_CapsuleBody : SizeX, SizeY and SizeZ are available.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: DetachEntityObject
commands.description:
Detach a previously attached object from an #Entity bone. The supported objects are the following:

- Entity : use EntityID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Camera : use CameraID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Light : use LightID() as 'ObjectID'.
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() as 'ObjectID'.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() as 'ObjectID'.

An object can be attached to an entity bone with AttachEntityObject().

commands.name: DisableEntityBody

Disable an entity body. The physic engine doesn't affect the entity anymore

parameters.name: #Entity

If set to #True, the entity body is disabled. If set to #False

It can be one of the following value:

#True : the manual bone control is enabled.

parameters.name: InheritOrientation (optional)

Tells if the bone orientation should inherit from the entity orientation. It can be one of the following value:

#True : the manual bone orientation inherit from the entity.
#False: the manual bone orientation doesn't take in account the entity orientation.

commands.returnValue: None.

syntax: Result = EntityBoneZ(#Entity, Bone$ [, OffsetX, OffsetY, OffsetZ])

commands.name: EntityBoundingBox
commands.description: Returns the position of the bounding box, either in local or world coordinate.

Flags can be one of the following values:

#PB_Entity_MinBoundingBoxX: Min 'x' position of the bounding box

#PB_Entity_MinBoundingBoxY: Min 'y' position of the bounding box
