combined with one of the following values:

commands.returnValue: Returns the position of the bounding box, either in local or world coordinate.

commands.name: EntityCollide
commands.description:
Checks if the two specified entities are colliding.

To have its collisions managed by the physic engine, an entity needs a body created with CreateEntityBody().

To have any effect, the physic engine needs to be activated with the EnableWorldPhysics().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The first entity to test.

parameters.name: #Entity2
parameters.description: The second entity to test.

commands.returnValue: Return non-zero if the two entities are colliding.

commands.name: EntityCustomParameter
syntax: EntityCustomParameter(#Entity, SubEntity, ParameterIndex, Value1.f, Value2.f, Value3.f, Value4.f)
commands.description:
Set a custom parameter value to the #Entity material shader script. To have any effect, the material
associated to the entity should have a shader script (either GLSL or HLSL).

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: SubEntity
parameters.description: The sub-entity to use. First sub-entity index starts at 0 (representing the main entity).

parameters.name: ParameterIndex
parameters.description: The parameter index in the shader script.

parameters.name: Value1
parameters.description: The first parameter value.

parameters.name: Value2
parameters.description: The second parameter value (if the parameter only accept one value, this value will be ignored).

parameters.name: Value3
parameters.description: The third parameter value (if the parameter only accept two values, this value will be ignored).

parameters.name: Value4
parameters.description: The fourth parameter value (if the parameter only accept three values, this value will be ignored).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityDirection
syntax: EntityDirection(#Entity, x, y, z [, Mode, LocalDirectionVector])
commands.description: Set the direction for the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The direction vector (value between -1.0 and 1.0).

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The direction mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

parameters.name: LocalDirectionVector (optional)
parameters.description:
The local direction vector. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Vector_X
#PB_Vector_Y
#PB_Vector_Z
#PB_Vector_NegativeX
#PB_Vector_NegativeY
#PB_Vector_NegativeZ

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityDirectionX
commands.description: Get the 'x' direction of the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'x' direction of the entity.

commands.name: EntityDirectionY
commands.description: Get the 'y' direction of the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'y' direction of the entity.

commands.name: EntityDirectionZ
commands.description: Get the 'z' direction of the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'z' direction of the entity.

commands.name: EntityFixedYawAxis
commands.description: Change the fixed yaw axis of the entity. The default behaviour of a entity is to yaw around its own Y axis.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Enable
parameters.description:
Enable or disable the use of a custom yaw axis. If set to #True, a new axis vector has to be specified.
If set to #False, the entity will yaw around its own Y axis.

parameters.name: VectorX (optional)
parameters.description: X vector direction of the new yaw axis (value between -1.0 and 1.0). 'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

parameters.name: VectorY (optional)
parameters.description: Y vector direction of the new yaw axis (value between -1.0 and 1.0). 'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

parameters.name: VectorZ (optional)
parameters.description: Z vector direction of the new yaw axis (value between -1.0 and 1.0). 'Enable' parameter has to be set to have any effect.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityID
commands.description:
Returns the unique ID which identifies the given '#Entity' in the operating system. This
function is very useful when another library needs a entity reference.

commands.name: EntityLinearFactor
commands.description:
Changes the linear factor for the #Entity. When moved, the entity linear velocity
is multiplied by the linear factor to get the final velocity. This is very useful
to constraint an entity move on one or several axis. By default, the linear
factor is 1 for all axis meaning no impact on the velocity. The entity needs a physic body to support
linear velocity constraint.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The 'x' linear factor value. If set to the 0, the entity won't be able to move on the 'x' axis anymore.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The 'y' linear factor vector. If set to the 0, the entity won't be able to move on the 'y' axis anymore.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: The 'z' linear factor vector. If set to the 0, the entity won't be able to move on the 'z' axis anymore.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityLookAt
syntax: EntityLookAt(#Entity, x, y, z [, DirectionX, DirectionY, DirectionZ])
commands.description:
The point (in world unit) that an entity is facing.
The position of the entity is not changed.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The position (in world unit) to point the entity at.

parameters.name: DirectionX, DirectionY, DirectionZ (optional)
parameters.description: The vector direction of the entity (values between -1.0 and 1.0).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityParentNode
commands.description: Returns the parent NodeID().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the parent NodeID(), if any. This can be either a real node, or a bone if the entity is attached to a bone.
If the entity has no parent node, it will returns 0.

commands.name: EntityPitch
commands.description: Get the pitch of the #Entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the pitch. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute pitch value, ignoring the current pitch of the parent (default).
#PB_Relative: get the pitch value relative to the current pitch of the parent.

combined with one of the following value:

#PB_Engine3D_Raw : the pitch is the raw value, but it can't be used in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation (default).
#PB_Engine3D_Adjusted: the pitch is adjusted, so it can be put back in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation.

commands.returnValue: The current pitch value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.

commands.name: EntityRenderMode
commands.description: Changes the render mode of the specified entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
Can be a combination (using the '|' operator) of the following values:

#PB_Entity_CastShadow : casts entity shadow if the WorldShadows() has been activated (default)
#PB_Entity_DisplaySkeleton : displays the entity skeleton
#PB_Shadow_None : turns off shadow casting for individual mesh/object entity (useful with "grounds")

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityRoll
commands.description: Get the roll of the #Entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the roll. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute roll value, ignoring the current roll of the parent (default).
#PB_Relative: get the roll value relative to the current roll of the parent.

combined with one of the following value:

#PB_Engine3D_Raw : the roll is the raw value, but it can't be used in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation (default).
#PB_Engine3D_Adjusted: the roll is adjusted, so it can be put back in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation.

commands.returnValue: The current roll value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.

commands.name: EntityVelocity
commands.description:
Changes the linear velocity of the #Entity. The linear factor is applied to the entity
before any move. To get the final value, see EntityLinearFactor() for more information.
The entity needs a physic body to support linear velocity. To get the current
entity velocity, use GetEntityAttribute().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The velocity vector force.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityX
commands.description: Returns the current position of the entity in the world.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'x' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'x' position of the entity in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'x' position of the entity relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'x' position of the entity.

commands.name: EntityY
commands.description: Returns the current position of the entity in the world.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'y' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'y' position of the entity in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'y' position of the entity relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'y' position of the entity.

commands.name: EntityYaw
commands.description: Get the yaw of the #Entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the yaw. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute yaw value, ignoring the current yaw of the parent (default).
#PB_Relative: get the yaw value relative to the current yaw of the parent.

combined with one of the following value:

#PB_Engine3D_Raw : the yaw is the raw value, but it can't be used in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation (default).
#PB_Engine3D_Adjusted: the yaw is adjusted, so it can be put back in RotateEntity() to get back the same orientation.

commands.returnValue: The current yaw value of the specified entity. This value is always between -180.0 and 180.0 degrees.

commands.name: EntityZ
commands.description: Returns the current position of the entity in the world.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode to get the 'z' position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: get the absolute 'z' position of the entity in the world (default).
#PB_Relative: get the 'z' position of the entity relative to its parent.

commands.returnValue: Returns the 'z' position of the entity.

commands.name: FetchEntityMaterial
commands.description: Fetch the material associated to the specified #Entity with SetEntityMaterial().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The new create material number.

parameters.name: SubEntity (optional)
parameters.description: The sub-entity to get the material from. First sub-entity index starts at 0 (representing the main entity).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.

commands.name: FreeEntity
commands.description:
Free the specified #Entity created with CreateEntity() before.
All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining entities are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining entities are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: FreeEntityBody
commands.description: Free the body associated with the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeEntityJoints
commands.description: Free all joints associated with the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: GetEntityAttribute
commands.description: Get the specified attribute of the given entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute value to get. The following attributes are available:

#PB_Entity_Friction : Get the friction value.
#PB_Entity_Restitution : Get the restitution value.
#PB_Entity_LinearVelocity : Get the current linear velocity (all axis).
#PB_Entity_LinearVelocityX : Get the current linear velocity on 'x' axis.
#PB_Entity_LinearVelocityY : Get the current linear velocity on 'y' axis.
#PB_Entity_LinearVelocityZ : Get the current linear velocity on 'z' axis.
#PB_Entity_MassCenterX : Get the mass center 'x' position.
#PB_Entity_MassCenterY : Get the mass center 'y' position.
#PB_Entity_MassCenterZ : Get the mass center 'z' position.
#PB_Entity_NbSubEntities : Get the number of sub-entities.
#PB_Entity_LinearSleeping : Get the minimum linear velocity value under which the entity will be sleeping.
#PB_Entity_AngularSleeping : Get the minimum angular velocity value under which the entity will be sleeping.
#PB_Entity_DeactivationTime: Get the time to wait (in milliseconds) before putting the entity in sleep mode when the above conditions are met.
#PB_Entity_IsActive : Get if an entity body is active (not sleeping).
#PB_Entity_AngularVelocityX: Get the current angular velocity on 'x' axis.
#PB_Entity_AngularVelocityY: Get the current angular velocity on 'y' axis.
#PB_Entity_AngularVelocityZ: Get the current angular velocity on 'z' axis.
#PB_Entity_AngularVelocity : Get the current angular velocity (all axis).
#PB_Entity_HasContactResponse: Check if the entity body has contacts.
#PB_Entity_ScaleX : Get the current entity scale on 'x' axis.
#PB_Entity_ScaleY : Get the current entity scale on 'y' axis.
#PB_Entity_ScaleZ : Get the current entity scale on 'z' axis.
#PB_Entity_InheritScale : Get if the entity has inherit scale.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the specified attribute or 0 if the entity does not support the attribute.

commands.name: GetEntityCollisionGroup
commands.description: Get the current entity collision group, as set with SetEntityCollisionFilter().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: The current entity collision group.

commands.name: GetEntityCollisionMask
commands.description: Get the current entity collision mask, as set with SetEntityCollisionFilter().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: The current entity collision mask.

commands.name: GetEntityMesh
commands.description: Returns the #Mesh used by the entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the #Mesh used by the entity.

commands.name: HideEntity
commands.description:
Hides or shows the specified #Entity.

'State' can take the following values:

1: the #Entity is hidden
0: the #Entity is shown

commands.name: IsEntity
commands.description:
Tests if the given #Entity is a valid and correctly initialized entity.

This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and
initialized, else it returns zero. This is the correct way to ensure an entity is ready to use.

commands.name: MoveEntity
commands.description: Move the specified entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position of the entity.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The move mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative move, from the current entity position (default).
#PB_Absolute: absolute move to the specified position.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MoveEntityBone
syntax: MoveEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode)
commands.description: Move the specified entity bone. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description: The bone name in the OGRE mesh, or as specified in CreateBone().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position of the bone.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The move mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative move, from the current bone position (default).
#PB_Absolute: absolute move to the specified position.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RotateEntity
commands.description: Rotates the entity according to the specified x,y,z angle values.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The rotation to apply, in degree. Valid values are from to 0 to 359.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The rotation mode. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: absolute rotation (default).
#PB_Relative: relative rotation based on the previous entity rotation.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RotateEntityBone
syntax: RotateEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode)
commands.description: Rotates the entity bone according to the specified x,y,z angle values. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description: The bone name in the OGRE mesh, or as specified in CreateBone().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The rotation to apply, in degree. Valid values are from to 0 to 359.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The rotation mode. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Absolute: absolute rotation (default).
#PB_Relative: relative rotation based on the previous entity bone rotation.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ScaleEntity
commands.description:
Scales the entity according to the specified x,y,z values. When using #PB_Relative mode,
this is a factor based scale which means the entity size will be multiplied with the
given value to obtain the new size.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The scaling to apply.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The scale mode. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Relative: relative scale, based on the previous size (default). Using 1.0 for scale value will let this value unchanged.
#PB_Absolute: absolute scale, in world unit.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
ScaleEntity(0, 2, 2, 2) ; Double the current size of the entity
  ScaleEntity(0, 1, 1, 1) ; Don't change the size of the entity (multiply by 1 don't change anything
  ScaleEntity(0, 3, 1, 1) ; Make the width of the entity 3 times larger
  ScaleEntity(0, 1, 1, 1, #PB_Absolute) ; Reset the entity size to 1,1,1.

commands.name: ScaleEntityBone
syntax: ScaleEntityBone(#Entity, Bone$, x, y, z, Mode)
commands.description: Scale the specified entity bone. The bone has to be in manual mode, set with EnableManualEntityBoneControl().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description: The bone name in the OGRE mesh, or as specified in CreateBone().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new scale of the bone.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The scale mode. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Relative: relative scale, based on the previous size (default). Using 1.0 for scale value will let this value unchanged.
#PB_Absolute: absolute scale, in world unit.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetEntityAttribute
commands.description: Set the specified attribute value to the given entity.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute to set. The following attributes are available:

#PB_Entity_Friction : Change the friction value.
#PB_Entity_Restitution : Change the restitution value.
#PB_Entity_MinVelocity : Set the minimum linear velocity of the entity. As this value isn't stored,
it needs to be called every time the entity is moved.
#PB_Entity_MaxVelocity : Set the maximum linear velocity of the entity. As this value isn't stored,
it needs to be called every time the entity is moved.
#PB_Entity_ForceVelocity : Set the linear velocity of the entity. As this value isn't stored,
it needs to be called every time the entity is moved.
#PB_Entity_LinearSleeping : Change the minimum linear velocity value under which the entity will be sleeping.
#PB_Entity_AngularSleeping : Change the minimum angular velocity value under which the entity will be sleeping.
#PB_Entity_DeactivationTime: Time to wait (in milliseconds) before putting the entity in sleep mode when the above conditions are met.
#PB_Entity_DisableContactResponse: Disable or enable the physic contacts for this entity. Value can be #True or #False.
#PB_Entity_InheritScale : Disable or enable if the entity has inherit scale. Value can be #True or #False

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Value of the attribute to set.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetEntityCollisionFilter
commands.description: Set the entity collision group and mask.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: CollisionGroup
parameters.description: The new collision group.

parameters.name: CollisionMask
parameters.description: The new collision mask.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetEntityMaterial
commands.description: Assign a material to the specified #Entity. An entity can only have one material assigned at once.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The new created material number.

parameters.name: SubEntity (optional)
parameters.description: The sub-entity to set the material. First sub-entity index starts at 0 (representing the main entity).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddEntityAnimationTime
commands.description: Add time to the specified #Entity animation.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description: The time to add (in milliseconds) to the specified animation, relative to the current animation time.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: EntityAnimationBlendMode
commands.description: Changes the #Entity animation blendmode.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The blend mode can be one of the following value:

#PB_EntityAnimation_Average: The blend will result of the average of the two animations (default). For example, if
the first animation rotates an arm 40 degrees and the second animation rotates the arm 90 degrees,
the arm will rotate (40+90)/2 = 65 degrees (if the both animation are played with full weight).
#PB_EntityAnimation_Cumulative: The blend will sum the two animations. For example, if the first animation rotates an arm 40 degrees
and the second animation rotates the arm 90 degrees, the arm will rotate 40+90 = 130 degrees
(if the both animation are played with full weight).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
When switching from an animation to another with SetEntityAnimationWeight(),
a blend is applied to have a smooth transition between the animations.

commands.name: EntityAnimationStatus
commands.description: Return the specified #Entity animation status.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

commands.returnValue:
The return value can be one of the following constants:

#PB_EntityAnimation_Stopped: The animation is stopped (or has ended).
#PB_EntityAnimation_Started: The animation is running.
#PB_EntityAnimation_Unknown: The animation doesn't exist in the mesh object.

commands.name: GetEntityAnimationLength
commands.description: Returns the #Entity animation length.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

commands.returnValue: The entity animation length (in milliseconds).

commands.name: GetEntityAnimationTime
commands.description: Returns the current #Entity animation time.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

commands.returnValue: The current entity animation time (in milliseconds) or 0 if the animation isn't running.

commands.name: GetEntityAnimationWeight
commands.description:
Returns the #Entity animation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once.
For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce
progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

commands.returnValue:
The current entity animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation
has no effect. If the weight is 1, then animation is fully playing.
commands.remarks: The EntityAnimationBlendMode() also affects how animations are mixed.

commands.name: SetEntityAnimationLength
commands.description: Change the #Entity animation length.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The new entity animation length (in milliseconds).

commands.name: SetEntityAnimationTime
commands.description:
Changes the current #Entity animation time. This is an absolute time position. To change the
time relative to the current time, use AddEntityAnimationTime().

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description: The absolute time to set (in milliseconds).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetEntityAnimationWeight
commands.description:
Changes the #Entity animation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once.
For example to do a smooth transition from one animation to another, it is possible to reduce
progressively the weight of the first animation and increase the weight of the second animation.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

parameters.name: Weight
parameters.description:
The new entity animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation
has no effect. If the weight is 1, then animation is fully playing.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: The EntityAnimationBlendMode() also affects how animations are mixed.

commands.name: StartEntityAnimation
commands.description: Start the specified #Entity animation. The animation is always started from the beginning.

parameters.name: #Entity
parameters.description: The entity to use.

parameters.name: Animation$
parameters.description:
The animation name. The animations are stored in the mesh object in a case-sensitive manner
(ie: "Walk" will be a different animation than "walk"). If the animation isn't
found or the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, this function will have no effect.

parameters.name: Flag
parameters.description:
Flags can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_EntityAnimation_Once: Play the animation only once. By default the animation loops automatically when its end is reached.
EntityAnimationStatus() can be used to detect the animation end.
#PB_EntityAnimation_Manual: Start the animation in manual mode, the time won't be automatically added after each RenderWorld().
AddEntityAnimationTime() needs to be called to update the animation time manually.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CloseFile
commands.description: Close the specified file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to close. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining files are closed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Once the file is closed, it may not be used anymore. Closing a file ensures the buffer will
effectively be put to the disk.

All remaining opened files are automatically closed when the program ends.

For an example see the ReadFile() or the CreateFile() functions.

commands.name: CreateFile
commands.description: Create an empty file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new file. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The filename and path to the new file. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination (using the '| operand) of the following values:

#PB_File_SharedRead : the opened file can be read by another process (Windows only).
#PB_File_SharedWrite: the opened file can be written by another process (Windows only).
#PB_File_NoBuffering: the internal PureBasic file buffering system will be disabled for this file.
FileBuffersSize() can not be used on this file.
#PB_File_BOM : the file will be created with a BOM.

combined with one of the following values (the following flags affect the WriteString()(), WriteStringN(),
ReadString(), ReadCharacter() and WriteCharacter() behaviour):

#PB_Ascii : all read/write string operation will use ASCII if not specified otherwise.
#PB_UTF8 : all read/write string operation will use UTF-8 if not specified otherwise (default).
#PB_Unicode: all read/write string operation will use Unicode if not specified otherwise.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the file was created successfully and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
If the file already exists, it will be overwritten by the new empty file.
The FileSize() function can be used to determine whether a file exists so the
user can be prompted before overwriting a file.

To open an existing file for reading/writing, use the OpenFile() function. To open a file for
reading only, use ReadFile().
commands.example:
If CreateFile(0, "Text.txt")         ; we create a new text file...
    For a=1 To 10
      WriteStringN(0, "Line "+Str(a))  ; we write 10 lines (each with 'end of line' character)
    Next
    For a=1 To 10
      WriteString(0, "String"+Str(a))  ; and now we add 10 more strings on the same line (because there is no 'end of line' character)
    Next
    CloseFile(0)                       ; close the previously opened file and store the written data this way
  Else
    MessageRequester("Information","may not create the file!")
  EndIf

commands.name: Eof
commands.description: Checks whether the end of the file has been reached.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the read-pointer is at the end of the file or zero if not.
commands.remarks: For an example see the ReadFile() function.

commands.name: FileBuffersSize
commands.description: Changes the size of the memory buffer used for file operations.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description:
The file to change. If #PB_Default is used as this parameter, then the
new buffer size will apply to all newly opened files with OpenFile(),
CreateFile() or ReadFile().

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The new size (in bytes) for the memory buffer. A size of 0 disables memory buffering on the file.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
For performance reasons, the buffer size should be kept large enough (1028 seems
to be ok as a minimum). When buffers are used, the information is really written to the disk once the
cache buffer is full or when the file is closed. The FlushFileBuffers() function
forces the cache buffer to be written at the time the function is called.
The default buffer size is 4096 bytes per file.

commands.name: FileID
commands.description: Returns the operating system handle of the file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the file handle.

commands.name: FileSeek
commands.description: Change the read/write pointer position in the file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

parameters.name: NewPosition.q
parameters.description: The new position relative to the beginning of the file in bytes.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The seek mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Absolute: the 'NewPosition' parameter will be an absolute position with the file (default).
#PB_Relative: the 'NewPosition' parameter will be an offset (positive or negative) relative to the current file pointer position.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
File$ = OpenFileRequester("Select a file","","All files (*.*)|*.*",0)
  If File$
    If ReadFile(0, File$)
      
      ; Read length of file
      Length = Lof(0)                       
      Debug "File length: "+FormatNumber(Length, 0)+" bytes"
          
      ; Set the file pointer 10 bytes from end of file
      FileSeek(0, Length - 10)                                
      Debug "Position after seek: "+FormatNumber(Loc(0), 0)
      
      CloseFile(0)
    Else
      Debug "Can't read the file: "+File$
    EndIf
  EndIf

commands.name: FlushFileBuffers
commands.description: Ensures that all buffered operations are written to disk.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the buffer has been successfully written the disk. If an error occurred (ie: disk full, disk error),
it will return zero.
commands.remarks: See FileBuffersSize() for more information about file buffer management.

commands.name: IsFile
commands.description: Tests if the given #File number is a valid and correctly initialized file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #File is a valid file and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a file is ready to use.

commands.name: Loc
commands.description: Returns the read/write pointer position in the file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the file pointer position relative to the start of the file in bytes.
commands.remarks: For an example look at the FileSeek() function.

commands.name: Lof
commands.description: Returns the length of the specified file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the length of the file in bytes.
commands.example:
file$ = OpenFileRequester("Select a file","","Text (.txt)|*.txt|All files (*.*)|*.*",0)
  If file$
    If ReadFile(0, file$)
      length = Lof(0)                            ; get the length of opened file
      *MemoryID = AllocateMemory(length)         ; allocate the needed memory
      If *MemoryID
        bytes = ReadData(0, *MemoryID, length)   ; read all data into the memory block
        Debug "Number of bytes read: " + Str(bytes)
      EndIf
      CloseFile(0)
    EndIf
  EndIf

commands.name: OpenFile
commands.description: Opens a file for reading/writing or creates a new file if it does not exist.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description:
The number to identify the file. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The filename and path to the file. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination (using the '| operand) of the following values:

#PB_File_SharedRead : the opened file can be read by another process (Windows only).
#PB_File_SharedWrite: the opened file can be written by another process (Windows only).
#PB_File_Append : the file pointer position will be set at the end of file.
#PB_File_NoBuffering: the internal PureBasic file buffering system will be disabled for this file.
FileBuffersSize() can not be used on this file.
#PB_File_BOM : if the file contains a BOM, it will be handled automatically (no need to use ReadStringFormat()).
The detected format will be automatically used by the read and write string functions.

combined with one of the following values (the following flags affect the WriteString(), WriteStringN(),
ReadString(), ReadCharacter() and WriteCharacter() behaviour):

#PB_Ascii : all read/write string operation will use ASCII if not specified otherwise.
#PB_UTF8 : all read/write string operation will use UTF-8 if not specified otherwise (default).
#PB_Unicode: all read/write string operation will use Unicode if not specified otherwise.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the file was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
This function fails if the file cannot be opened with write permission, for example if the file is located on a read-only
file-system like a CD. To open a file for reading only, use the ReadFile() function. To overwrite an existing
file with a new and empty file, use the CreateFile() function.

The file pointer will be positioned at the beginning of the file. To append data to the end of the file, use the
#PB_File_Append flag to set the pointer to the end of the file.
commands.example:
If OpenFile(0, "Test.txt")    ; opens an existing file or creates one, if it does not exist yet
    FileSeek(0, Lof(0))         ; jump to the end of the file (result of Lof() is used)
    WriteStringN(0, "... another line at the end.")
    CloseFile(0)
  EndIf

parameters.name: Filename$

The filename and path to the file. If the filename does not include a full path, it

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:

#PB_File_SharedRead : if the file has been already opened by another process or thread for read operation,
this flag is needed to access it (Windows only).
#PB_File_SharedWrite: if the file has been already opened by another process or thread for write operation,
this flag is needed to access it (Windows only).
#PB_File_NoBuffering: the internal PureBasic file buffering system will be disabled for this file.
FileBuffersSize() can not be used on this file.
#PB_File_BOM : if the file contains a BOM, it will be handled automatically (no need to use ReadStringFormat()).
The detected format will be automatically used by the read and write string functions.

combined with one of the following values (the following flags affect the behaviour of ReadString()
and ReadCharacter()):

#PB_Ascii : all read string operation will use ASCII if not specified otherwise.
#PB_UTF8 : all read string operation will use UTF-8 if not specified otherwise (default).
#PB_Unicode: all read string operation will use Unicode if not specified otherwise.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the file was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any was used as the #File parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
To open a file for reading and writing, use the OpenFile() function.
To create a new and empty file, use the CreateFile() function.
commands.example:
If ReadFile(0, "Text.txt")        ; if the file could be read, we continue ...
    Format = ReadStringFormat(0)
    While Eof(0) = 0                ; loop as long the 'end of file' isn't reached
      Debug ReadString(0, Format)   ; display line by line in the debug window
    Wend
    CloseFile(0)                    ; close the previously opened file

commands.name: ReadString
commands.description:
Read a string from a file until an 'End Of Line' or a 'Null' character is found (Unix, DOS and Macintosh
file formats are supported).

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to read from.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The flags to apply while reading the string. It may be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : reads the string as ASCII
#PB_UTF8 : reads the string as UTF8
#PB_Unicode: reads the string as UTF16

combined with:

#PB_File_IgnoreEOL: ignores the end of line (but the resulting string will still contain them) until the specified
length or the end of file.

If this flag isn't set, then the format for reading the string depends on the related setting at
the previously used CreateFile(), OpenFile() or ReadFile() command.

parameters.name: Length (optional)
parameters.description:
Read the file until the length (in characters) have been reached. If an end of line is encountered
before the length is reached, the read will stop (unless the flag #PB_File_IgnoreEOL has been set).

commands.returnValue: Returns the read string, or an empty string if the read has failed.
commands.remarks:
For detecting the string encoding format (byte order mark) used in a file there is the
ReadStringFormat() function available.

For an example see the ReadFile().

commands.name: ReadStringFormat
commands.description:
Checks if the current file position contains a BOM (Byte Order Mark) and tries to identify the
String encoding used in the file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : No BOM detected. This usually means a plain text file.
#PB_UTF8 : UTF-8 BOM detected.
#PB_Unicode: UTF-16 (little endian) BOM detected.

#PB_UTF16BE: UTF-16 (big endian) BOM detected.
#PB_UTF32 : UTF-32 (little endian) BOM detected.
#PB_UTF32BE: UTF-32 (big endian) BOM detected.

The #PB_Ascii, #PB_UTF8 and #PB_Unicode results may be used directly
in further calls to ReadString() to read the file. The other results represent string
formats that cannot be directly read with PureBasic string functions. They are included for completeness so that an
application can display a proper error-message.
commands.remarks:
If a BOM is detected, the file pointer will be placed
at the end of the BOM. If no BOM is detected, the file pointer remains unchanged.

The Byte Order Mark is a commonly used way to indicate the encoding for a textfile. It is usually placed
at the beginning of the file. It is however not a standard, just a commonly used practice. So if no BOM is
detected at the start of a file, it does not necessarily mean that it is a plain text file. It could also
just mean that the program that created the file did not use this practice.
WriteStringFormat() may be used to place such a BOM in a file.

For more information, see this Wikipedia Article.

More information about using unicode in a PureBasic program can also be found here.

    CloseFile(0)                         ; close the previously opened file and so store the written data
