#PB_UTF8 : Writes the string in UTF8 format
#PB_Unicode: Writes the string in UTF16 format

If this flag isn't set, then the format for writing the string depends on the related setting at
the previously used CreateFile() or OpenFile() command.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
Because of file buffering, this function may return successful even if there is not enough
space left on the output device for the write operation.
The file must be opened using a write-capable function (i.e. not with ReadFile()).
The null ending string character is not written to the file.

To place a BOM (byte order mark) to later identify the string encoding format of a file
use the WriteStringFormat() function.
To write a string including a newline sequence, use the WriteStringN() function.

For an example see the CreateFile() function.

commands.name: WriteStringFormat
commands.description: Writes a BOM (Byte Order Mark) at the current position in the file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to write to.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description:
The format for which the mark should be written. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Writes no BOM at all (this is usually interpreted as a plain ASCII file.)
#PB_UTF8 : UTF-8 BOM
#PB_Unicode: UTF-16 (little endian) BOM

#PB_UTF16BE: UTF-16 (big endian) BOM
#PB_UTF32 : UTF-32 (little endian) BOM
#PB_UTF32BE: UTF-32 (big endian) BOM

The #PB_Ascii, #PB_UTF8 and #PB_Unicode correspond to the flags supported
by WriteString() and WriteStringN(). After placing such a BOM,
the strings which follow should all be written with this flag. The other formats represent string
formats that can not be written directly with the PureBasic string functions. They are included only for completeness.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
Because of file buffering, this function may return successful even if there is not enough
space left on the output device for the write operation.
The file must be opened using a write-capable function (i.e. not with ReadFile()).

The Byte Order Mark is a commonly used method with which to indicate the encoding of a textfile. It is usually placed
at the beginning of the file. It is however not a standard, just a commonly used practice. So if no BOM is
detected at the start of a file, it does not necessarily mean that it is a plain text file. It could also
just mean that the program that created the file did not use this practice.
ReadStringFormat() may be used detect a BOM within a file.

For more information, see this Wikipedia Article.

More information about using unicode in PureBasic program can also be found here.

commands.name: WriteStringN
commands.description: Write a string to a file and add an 'end of line' character.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to write to.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The string to write.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format in which to write the string. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Writes the string in ASCII format
#PB_UTF8 : Writes the string in UTF8 format
#PB_Unicode: Writes the string in UTF16 format

If this flag isn't set, then the format for writing the string depends on the related setting at
the previously used CreateFile() or OpenFile() command.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
Because of file buffering, this function may return successful even if there is not enough
space left on the output device for the write operation.
The file must be opened using a write-capable function (i.e. not with ReadFile()).

To place a BOM (byte order mark) to later identify the string encoding format of a file
use the WriteStringFormat() function.
To write a string without a newline sequence, use the WriteString() function.

For an example see the CreateFile() function.

commands.name: WriteUnicodeCharacter
commands.description: Write a unicode character (2 bytes) to a file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to write to.

parameters.name: Number
parameters.description: The unicode character value to write.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
Because of file buffering, this function may return successful even if there is not enough
space left on the output device for the write operation.
The file must be opened using a write-capable function (i.e. not with ReadFile()).

For an example see the CreateFile() function - with WriteUnicodeCharacter() only a unicode character is written, instead of a string.

commands.name: WriteWord
commands.description: Write a word number (2 bytes) to a file.

parameters.name: #File
parameters.description: The file to write to.

parameters.name: Number
parameters.description: The value to write.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
Because of file buffering, this function may return successful even if there is not enough
space left on the output device for the write operation.
The file must be opened using a write-capable function (i.e. not with ReadFile()).

For an example see the CreateFile() function - with WriteWord() only a word variable is written, instead of a string.

commands.name: CheckFilename
commands.description:
Checks if the specified Filename$ doesn't contain invalid characters for the file-system. For example, on Windows
'/' and '\' characters are not allowed in the filename.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename to check without a path.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the filename does not contain invalid characters and zero if it does.
commands.remarks:
Even if the syntax-check of this function doesn't complain, there are different 'forbidden' filenames on
different OS. For example on Windows filenames containing "COM1" till "COM9", "LPT1" till "LPT9" or "aux"
are not allowed. For more information see here.

commands.name: CopyDirectory
commands.description: Copy the contents of the source directory to the destination.

parameters.name: SourceDirectory$
parameters.description: The directory to copy.

parameters.name: DestinationDirectory$
parameters.description: The destination to copy the directory to.

parameters.name: Pattern$
parameters.description:
A pattern identifying the files to copy. For example: "*.*" will copy any files in the directory.
"*.exe" will copy only the .exe files. By default, a null Pattern$ ("") will copy all the files.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
Options for the copy operation. It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Recursive: Copy the directory with all subdirectories.
#PB_FileSystem_Force : Overwrites the files which are protected (read-only).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
If the target directory already exists, its content will be overwritten automatically. The
FileSize() function can be used to determine if the target exists or not.
commands.example: Debug CopyDirectory("D:\Games\MyGame\", "D:\Games\Backup\", "", #PB_FileSystem_Recursive)

commands.name: CopyFile
commands.description: Copy the source file to the destination.

parameters.name: SourceFilename$
parameters.description: The file to copy.

parameters.name: DestinationFilename$
parameters.description: The location to copy the file to.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
If the destination file already exists, it will be overwritten. The FileSize() function
can be used to determine if the target exists or not. If source file and destination file
are the same, a copy will not occur and zero will be returned.

commands.name: CreateDirectory
commands.description: Creates a new directory.

parameters.name: DirectoryName$
parameters.description: The name of the new directory.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
This function fails if the parent directory of the new directory does not exist. To create
multiple levels of directories, this function has to be called for each directory level
to create separately.

commands.name: DeleteDirectory
commands.description: Deletes the specified Directory$ or files in that Directory$ matching the provided pattern.

parameters.name: Directory$
parameters.description: The directory to delete.

parameters.name: Pattern$
parameters.description:
A pattern for deleting files within the directory. For example: "*.*" will delete any files in the directory.
"*.exe" will delete only the .exe files. By default, a null Pattern$ ("") will delete all the files.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
Options for the delete operation. It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Recursive: Deletes the directory with all subdirectories.
#PB_FileSystem_Force : Deletes even the files which are protected (read-only).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

commands.name: DeleteFile
commands.description: Deletes the specified file.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The file to delete.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
Options for the delete operation. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Force: Also deletes the files which are protected (read-only).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful or zero if it failed.

commands.name: DirectoryEntryAttributes
commands.description:
Returns the attributes of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory() and
NextDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

commands.returnValue:
Returns the attributes of the current file.

On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden
#PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time
#PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed
#PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes
#PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode
#PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file

On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values:

#PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link
#PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user
#PB_FileSystem_WriteUser
#PB_FileSystem_ExecUser
#PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group
#PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users
#PB_FileSystem_WriteAll
#PB_FileSystem_ExecAll
commands.remarks:
To check if one attribute is actually set, just use the '&' (binary AND) and the attribute constant value:

[...]

FileAttributes = DirectoryEntryAttributes(#Directory)
If FileAttributes & #PB_FileSystem_Hidden
Debug "This file is hidden !"
EndIf

commands.name: DirectoryEntryDate
commands.description:
Returns the date of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory() and
NextDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

parameters.name: DateType
parameters.description:
The kind of date to return. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Date_Created : returns the file creation date.
#PB_Date_Accessed: returns the last file access date.
#PB_Date_Modified: returns the last file modification date.

commands.returnValue: Returns the specified date of the current directory entry in the format of the PureBasic Date library.
commands.remarks:
On Linux and Mac OSX, the date returned for #PB_Date_Created is the same as the date for
#PB_Date_Modified, because most file systems do not store a file creation date.

commands.name: DirectoryEntryName
commands.description:
Returns the name of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory() and
NextDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

commands.returnValue: Returns the name of the current directory entry.
commands.remarks:
The pseudo-directories "." and ".." can be returned in a directory enumeration, so they have to be filtered if they should not
be included in the program output.

commands.name: DirectoryEntrySize
commands.description:
Returns the size of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory() and
NextDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

commands.returnValue: Returns the size of the current directory entry in bytes.

commands.name: DirectoryEntryType
commands.description:
Returns the type of the current entry in the directory being listed with ExamineDirectory() and
NextDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_DirectoryEntry_File : This entry is a file.
#PB_DirectoryEntry_Directory: This entry is a directory.

commands.name: ExamineDirectory
commands.description:
Start to examine a directory for listing with the functions NextDirectoryEntry(),
DirectoryEntryName() and DirectoryEntryType().

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new directory listing. #PB_Any can be used as
a parameter to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: DirectoryName$
parameters.description: The directory to examine.

parameters.name: Pattern$
parameters.description:
A pattern to filter the returned entries by.
For example: A 'Pattern$' like "*.*" or "" will list all the files (and sub-directories) in the directory.
A 'Pattern$' like "*.exe" will list only .exe files (and sub-directories ending with .exe if any).

Please be aware of a MS Windows specific behaviour: When using a 3-char file name extension any extension
starting with those 3 chars will match, e.g. "*.log" will also match a file name/extension "test.log_1".

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the directory can be enumerated or zero if there was an error. If #PB_Any
was used as the #Directory parameter then the generated directory number is returned.
commands.remarks:
Once the enumeration is done, FinishDirectory() must
be called to free the resources associated to the listing.

Specific OS path separator characters are available #PS, #NPS, #PS$ ('\') and #NPS$ ('/').
commands.example:
Directory$ = GetHomeDirectory() ; Lists all files and folder in the home directory
  If ExamineDirectory(0, Directory$, "*.*")
    While NextDirectoryEntry(0)
      If DirectoryEntryType(0) = #PB_DirectoryEntry_File
        Type$ = "[File] "
        Size$ = " (Size: " + DirectoryEntrySize(0) + ")"
      Else
        Type$ = "[Directory] "
        Size$ = "" ; A directory doesn't have a size
      EndIf

      Debug Type$ + DirectoryEntryName(0) + Size$
    Wend
    FinishDirectory(0)
  EndIf

commands.name: FileSize
commands.description:
Returns the size of the specified file. This function can also be used to check if a file or directory
exists or not.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename to get the size from.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the size of the file in bytes, or one of the following values:

-1: File not found.
-2: File is a directory.

commands.name: FinishDirectory
commands.description:
Finish the enumeration started with ExamineDirectory(). This frees
the resources associated with the #Directory listing.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: GetCurrentDirectory
commands.description: Returns the current directory for the program.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the full path of the current directory.
It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise).

It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
commands.remarks:
All files accesses are relative to this directory, when
no absolute path is specified. To change the current directory, use SetCurrentDirectory().

commands.name: GetExtensionPart
commands.description: Retrieves the file extension part of a full path.

parameters.name: FullPathName$
parameters.description: The full path to get the extension from.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the file extension. For example, if the full path is
"C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "exe".
commands.remarks:
To retrieve the file or the path part from a full path, look at the
GetFilePart() and GetPathPart() functions.
If the path does not contain a file name then the result may be random.
For example GetExtensionPart(".htaccess")" or GetExtensionPart(".access.") are not valid.

commands.name: GetFileAttributes
commands.description: Returns the attributes of the given file.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The file to read the attributes from. This can also specify the name of a directory.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the attributes of the file. If the file does not exist or the attributes cannot be read,
the result is the value -1.

On Windows, Attributes is a combination of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden
#PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time
#PB_FileSystem_Compressed: File is compressed
#PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes
#PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode
#PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file

On Linux or MacOSX, Attributes is a combination of these values:

#PB_FileSystem_Link : The file is a symbolic link
#PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user
#PB_FileSystem_WriteUser
#PB_FileSystem_ExecUser
#PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group
#PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users
#PB_FileSystem_WriteAll
#PB_FileSystem_ExecAll
commands.remarks:
To check if one attribute is actually set, just use the '&' (binary AND) and the attribute constant value:

FileAttributes = GetFileAttributes("C:\Text.txt")
If FileAttributes & #PB_FileSystem_Hidden
Debug "This file is hidden !"
EndIf
commands.example:
Value = GetFileAttributes("c:\autoexec.bat")

  If Value = -1
    Debug "Error reading file attributes!"
  Else
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_Hidden     : txt$ + "H" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_Archive    : txt$ + "A" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_Compressed : txt$ + "C" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_Normal     : txt$ + "N" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly   : txt$ + "R" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    If Value & #PB_FileSystem_System     : txt$ + "S" : Else : txt$+"-" : EndIf
    Debug txt$
  EndIf

commands.name: GetFileDate
commands.description: Returns the date of the specified file.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The file to get the date from.

parameters.name: DateType
parameters.description:
The kind of date to return. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Date_Created : returns the file creation date.
#PB_Date_Accessed: returns the last file access date.
#PB_Date_Modified: returns the last file modification date.

commands.returnValue: Returns the requested date in the format of the PureBasic Date library.
commands.remarks:
On Linux and Mac OSX, the date returned for #PB_Date_Created is the same as the date for
#PB_Date_Modified, because most file systems do not store a file creation date.

commands.name: GetFilePart
commands.description: Retrieves the file part of a full path.

parameters.name: FullPathName$
parameters.description: The full path to get the filename from.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_NoExtension: Get the filename without its extension (if any).

commands.returnValue:
Returns the file name. For example, if the full path is
"C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "PB.exe".
commands.remarks:
To retrieve the extension or the path part from a full path, look at the
GetExtensionPart() and GetPathPart() functions.

commands.name: GetHomeDirectory
commands.description: Returns the home directory path of the currently logged user.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the full path of the home directory.
It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise).

It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
commands.remarks:
The home directory is the directory for the user data (preferences, plugins etc.) of the current user.
Read and write access should be possible in this directory.

commands.name: GetPathPart
commands.description: Retrieves the path part of a full path.

parameters.name: FullPathName$
parameters.description: The full path to get the path part from.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the path part. For example, if the full path is
"C:\PureBasic\PB.exe", the result will be "C:\PureBasic\".
commands.remarks:
To retrieve the extension or the file part from a full path, look at the
GetExtensionPart() and GetFilePart() functions.
commands.example: Debug GetPathPart(ProgramFilename())

commands.name: GetTemporaryDirectory
commands.description: Returns the temporary directory name.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the full path to the temporary directory. It will end with a path separator #PS,
#PS$ ('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise).

It's very unlikely, but if this function fails, it will return an empty string.
commands.remarks:
This directory provides read and write access and should be used to store temporary files. Depending on the operating system
and settings, the contents of this directory may be deleted on a regular basis. It is however better to delete temporary files
when they are no longer needed and not rely on such automatic cleanup.

commands.name: GetUserDirectory
commands.description: Returns the directory path of the specified directory type.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of directory to get the path. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Directory_Desktop : desktop directory of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Downloads : downloads directory of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Documents : documents directory path of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Videos : videos directory path of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Musics : musics directory path of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Pictures : pictures directory path of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_Public : public directory of the current logged user
#PB_Directory_ProgramData: program data directory of the current logged user.
On Linux and OSX, it is the home directory followed by '/.' to be able to create
hidden config directory in the home user.
#PB_Directory_AllUserData: common program data directory (accessible to all users)
#PB_Directory_Programs : global program files path (can be read only)

commands.returnValue:
Returns the full path of the specified directory. It will end with a path separator #PS, #PS$
('\' for Windows or '/' otherwise).
If the type is not found it will return an empty string.
commands.example:
; List some of the user directories:
  Debug "#PB_Directory_Downloads = " + GetUserDirectory(#PB_Directory_Downloads)
  Debug "#PB_Directory_Documents = " + GetUserDirectory(#PB_Directory_Documents)
  Debug "#PB_Directory_Programs  = " + GetUserDirectory(#PB_Directory_Programs)

commands.name: IsDirectory
commands.description: Tests if the given directory number is a valid and correctly initialized directory enumeration.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory enumeration to test.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the given input is a valid enumeration and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a directory is ready to use.

commands.name: NextDirectoryEntry
commands.description:
This function must be called after an ExamineDirectory(). It will go step-by-step into
the directory and list its contents.

parameters.name: #Directory
parameters.description: The directory examined with ExamineDirectory()

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if a new entry was read from the directory and zero if there are no more entries.
commands.remarks:
The entry name can be read with the DirectoryEntryName()
function. If you want to know whether an entry is a subdirectory or a file, use
the DirectoryEntryType() function.

commands.name: RenameFile
commands.description: Rename the old file to the new file.

parameters.name: OldFilename$
parameters.description: The old name of the file.

parameters.name: NewFilename$
parameters.description: The new name of the file.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
The old and new filename do not have to be in the same directory, so this function can be used
to move a file to a different directory. This function can also be used to rename/move directories.
commands.example:
If RenameFile("C:\test.txt", "D:\temp\test_backup.txt")
    Debug "Moving and renaming successful."    ; Moving and renaming of the file was successful
  Else
    Debug "Moving and renaming failed."        ; Moving and renaming failed, e.g. because of a not found source file
  EndIf

commands.name: SetCurrentDirectory
commands.description: Changes the current directory for the program.

parameters.name: Directory$
parameters.description: The full path to the new current directory, or a path relative to the existing current directory.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the current directory has been successfully changed, return zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
All files accesses are relative to this directory, when
no absolute path is specified. To get the current directory, use GetCurrentDirectory().

Specific OS path separator characters are available #PS, #NPS, #PS$ ('\') and #NPS$ ('/').

commands.name: SetFileAttributes
commands.description: Set the attributes of the given Filename$.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The name of the file to modify. This can also specify the name of a directory.

parameters.name: Attributes
parameters.description:
The new attributes.

On Windows, 'Attributes' is a combination of the following values:

#PB_FileSystem_Hidden : File is hidden
#PB_FileSystem_Archive : File has been changed and not archived since the last time
#PB_FileSystem_Normal : Normal attributes
#PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly : File is in read-only mode
#PB_FileSystem_System : File is a system file

On Linux and MacOSX, the following values can be used:

#PB_FileSystem_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user
#PB_FileSystem_WriteUser
#PB_FileSystem_ExecUser
#PB_FileSystem_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group
#PB_FileSystem_WriteGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ExecGroup
#PB_FileSystem_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users
#PB_FileSystem_WriteAll
#PB_FileSystem_ExecAll

To combine several attributes, just use the '|' (binary OR) operand:

SetFileAttributes("C:\Text.txt", #PB_FileSystem_Hidden | #PB_FileSystem_ReadOnly)

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.

commands.name: SetFileDate
commands.description: Changes the date of the specified file.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The name of the file to modify.

parameters.name: DateType
parameters.description:
The kind of date to modify. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Date_Created : change the file creation date.
#PB_Date_Accessed: change the last file access date.
#PB_Date_Modified: change the last file modification date.

parameters.name: Date
parameters.description: The date to set. This has to be a value from the Date library.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
On Linux and Mac OSX, the date used for #PB_Date_Created is the same as the date for
#PB_Date_Modified, because most file systems do not store a file creation date.

commands.name: FontID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the #Font.

parameters.name: #Font
parameters.description: The font to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the unique system ID of the font.
This result is sometimes also referred to as a 'Handle'. Take a look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for
more information.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 222, 130, "FontID()", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    ButtonGadget(0, 10, 10, 200, 30, "Click to change the font...")
    Font1 = LoadFont(#PB_Any, "Arial"  ,  8, #PB_Font_Bold)
    Font2 = LoadFont(#PB_Any, "Verdana", 12, #PB_Font_StrikeOut)
    UsedFont = 1
  EndIf
  
  Repeat
    Event = WaitWindowEvent()
    
    If Event = #PB_Event_Gadget
      If EventGadget() = 0
        If UsedFont = 1
          SetGadgetFont(0, FontID(Font2))
          UsedFont = 2
        Else
          SetGadgetFont(0, FontID(Font1))
          UsedFont = 1
        EndIf
      EndIf
    EndIf
  Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow

commands.name: FreeFont
commands.description: Free the given Font, previously loaded with LoadFont().

parameters.name: #Font
parameters.description: The font to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining fonts are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining fonts are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: IsFont
commands.description: Tests if the given #Font is a valid and correctly initialized font.

parameters.name: #Font
parameters.description: The font to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #Font is a valid font and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value.
If Result is not zero then the object is valid and initialized,
otherwise it returns zero. This is a good way to check that a font is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadFont
commands.description: Tries to open the specified font.

parameters.name: #Font
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new font. #PB_Any
can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The name of the font to load.

parameters.name: YSize
parameters.description: The vertical size of the font in points.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination of the following constants:

#PB_Font_Bold : The font will be bold
#PB_Font_Italic : The font will be italic
#PB_Font_Underline : The font will be underlined (Windows only)
#PB_Font_StrikeOut : The font will be strikeout (Windows only)
#PB_Font_HighQuality: The font will be in high-quality mode (slower) (Windows only)

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the font was loaded successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any
was used for the #Font parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
If another font was previously loaded with the same #Font number, then the
older font will be automatically freed when loading the new one.

On Windows and OS X the font mapper will always attempt to locate a font.
If a font name which does not exist such as: "Tim Now Ronin", is used,
then the font mapper will attempt to find the closest match. This will be
based upon such criteria as: the font name, the font height, the style and
so forth. Therefore, the assumption can not be made that a font will not be
loaded, due only to an incorrect font name, size, etc.

On Windows and macOS, you can change the size and style of the application's
system font without specifying its name like this: LoadFont(1, "", 24)
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 270, 160, "Loading font...", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If LoadFont(1, "Arial", 24)
      SetGadgetFont(#PB_Default, FontID(1))
      TextGadget(0, 10, 10, 250, 40, "Arial 24")
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: RegisterFontFile
commands.description:
Register a font file for use with the LoadFont() command. All fonts contained in the
file are then available.

parameters.name: FileName$
parameters.description: The file containing the font. The file must be in TrueType format.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the file was successfully registered, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
The font file is registered for the current program only. This means that the font(s) are not
accessible by other programs and will be unregistered when the program ends.
No system-wide changes are made by this command.

You cannot use a registered font with the VectorDrawing library.
commands.example:
; Now let's use a new font, which was downloaded from the internet to the temporary directory...
  ; The font name is "ascii" and the font file is "ascii.ttf"
  If RegisterFontFile(GetTemporaryDirectory() + "ascii.ttf") ; We have to register it before to use it
    LoadFont(0, "ascii", 12) ; Now we can load the font, the operating system knows it
    SetGadgetFont(0, FontID(0))
  ...

commands.name: AbortFTPFile
commands.description:
Aborts the current background file transfer previously started with SendFTPFile()
or ReceiveFTPFile(). If no file transfer is in progress, this function has
no effect.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The FTP connection to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CheckFTPConnection
commands.description: Checks if the specified #Ftp connection is still connected to the server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The FTP connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the connection is still open and zero if the server closed the connection.

commands.name: CloseFTP
commands.description:
Closes the specified #Ftp client connection previously opened with OpenFTP()
and free any associated resources.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to close. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining FTP connection are closed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining ftp connection are automatically closed when the program ends.

commands.name: CreateFTPDirectory
commands.description: Creates a new directory on the FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The FTP connection to use.

parameters.name: Directory$
parameters.description:
The name of the directory to create.
The new directory will be created in the current directory (see GetFTPDirectory() and SetFTPDirectory()).
It is not possible to specify a subpath in the Directory$.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.

commands.name: DeleteFTPDirectory
commands.description: Deletes a directory on the FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: Directory$
parameters.description:
The directory to delete. The directory has to be in the current
directory (see GetFTPDirectory() and SetFTPDirectory()). It is not possible to specify a subpath in the Directory$.
The directory has to be empty, or the delete with fail.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the directory was deleted or zero if the operation failed.

commands.name: DeleteFTPFile
commands.description: Deletes a file on the FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The file to delete. The file has to be in the current directory (see GetFTPDirectory()
and SetFTPDirectory()). It is not possible to specify a subpath in the Filename$.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the file was deleted or zero if the operation failed.

commands.name: ExamineFTPDirectory
commands.description: Starts to examine the content of the current FTP directory.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded or zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
For now, only Unix-like servers are supported for directory listing. The FTP protocol doesn't specify
how a directory listing has to be returned, so every server has its own way to returns the directory information.
Fortunately, most of the world servers are running under Unix/Linux and uses the same way to return the
data. That said, there is no warranty that the listing works on every servers. This command will be updated
on demand to automatically handle more servers type. If the server isn't supported, please use FTPDirectoryEntryRaw()
to get back the raw information about each entry.

The functions
NextFTPDirectoryEntry(), FTPDirectoryEntryName(), FTPDirectoryEntryType(),
FTPDirectoryEntryAttributes(), FTPDirectoryEntryDate() and FTPDirectoryEntrySize()
can be used to read the directory entries. To change the current directory, use SetFTPDirectory().
commands.example:
If OpenFTP(0, "ftp.free.fr", "anonymous", "")
    If ExamineFTPDirectory(0)
      While NextFTPDirectoryEntry(0)
        Debug FTPDirectoryEntryName(0)
      Wend
      FinishFTPDirectory(0)
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Can't connect to ftp.free.fr"
  EndIf

commands.name: FinishFTPDirectory
commands.description:
Finishes the enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory(). This allows to free
the resources associated with the FTP listing.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntryAttributes
commands.description:
Returns the attributes of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with the ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns a combination of the following values:

#PB_FTP_ReadUser : Access flags for the owning user
#PB_FTP_WriteUser
#PB_FTP_ExecuteUser
#PB_FTP_ReadGroup : Access flags for the owning user's group
#PB_FTP_WriteGroup
#PB_FTP_ExecuteGroup
#PB_FTP_ReadAll : Access flags for all other users
#PB_FTP_WriteAll
#PB_FTP_ExecuteAll
commands.example:
[...]
  
  FileAttributes = FTPDirectoryEntryAttributes(#Ftp)
  If FileAttributes & #PB_FTP_ReadUser
    Debug "This file has the ReadUser flag"
  EndIf

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntryDate
commands.description:
Returns the date of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the date of the entry in the format of the Date library.

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntryName
commands.description:
Returns the name of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the entry name.

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntryRaw
commands.description:
Returns the raw line of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions, as it has been sent by the FTP server. It can be useful when
the server isn't supported by ExamineFTPDirectory(), so the information about the directory listing
can still be retrieved and parsed accordingly.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the entry line as sent by the FTP server.
commands.example:
If OpenFTP(0, "ftp.free.fr", "anonymous", "")
    If ExamineFTPDirectory(0)
      While NextFTPDirectoryEntry(0)
        Debug FTPDirectoryEntryRaw(0)
      Wend
      FinishFTPDirectory(0)
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Can't connect to ftp.free.fr"
  EndIf

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntrySize
commands.description:
Returns the size of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the size in bytes.

commands.name: FTPDirectoryEntryType
commands.description:
Returns the type of the current entry in the FTP enumeration being listed with ExamineFTPDirectory() and
NextFTPDirectoryEntry() functions.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following constants:

#PB_FTP_File : This entry is a file.
#PB_FTP_Directory: This entry is a directory.

commands.name: FTPProgress
commands.description:
Returns the progress of the current file transfer, started either with ReceiveFTPFile() or
SendFTPFile().

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the actual number of bytes which has been received/sent or one of the following values:

#PB_FTP_Started : The file transfer is in the initialization phase.
#PB_FTP_Finished: The file transfer is finished correctly.
#PB_FTP_Error : The file transfer is finished but an error occurred.

commands.name: GetFTPDirectory
commands.description: Returns the current FTP directory.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Return the current FTP directory, relative to the FTP root.
commands.remarks: To change the current directory, use SetFTPDirectory().

commands.name: IsFtp
commands.description: Tests if the given #Ftp number is a valid and correctly initialized ftp client.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the given number is a valid and correctly initialized client connection.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof
and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and
initialized, else it returns zero. This is the correct way to ensure an ftp handle is ready to use.

commands.name: NextFTPDirectoryEntry
commands.description: Moves to the next entry in an enumeration started with ExamineFTPDirectory().

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the next entry is available or zero if there are no more entries to examine.
commands.remarks:
The entry name can be read with FTPDirectoryEntryName(). To know whether an
entry is a file or directory, use FTPDirectoryEntryType().

commands.name: OpenFTP
syntax: Result = OpenFTP(#Ftp, ServerName$, User$, Password$ [, Flags [, Port]])
commands.description: Tries to open a connection on the specified FTP or SFTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new connection. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: ServerName$
parameters.description:
The URL or address of the server to connect to. To connect to a SFTP server the prefix "sftp://" has to be
added before the server address.

parameters.name: User$
parameters.description: The user name to authenticate on the server.

parameters.name: Password$
parameters.description: The password to authenticate on the server.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_FTP_Active: Enable active connection mode for the connection. If not specified, the connection is etablished using passive mode.
#PB_FTP_Debug : to print in the console debug information.

parameters.name: Port (optional)
parameters.description: The port to use for the connection. The default is port 21 for FTP and 22 for SFTP.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the connection was established correctly and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any is used as the #Ftp parameter then the generated number for the connection
is returned on success.
commands.example:
If OpenFTP(0, "ftp.free.fr", "anonymous", "")
    Debug "Successfully connected"
  Else
    Debug "Can't connect to ftp.free.fr"
  EndIf

If OpenFTP(0, "sftp://test.rebex.net", "demo", "password") ; Use a public SFTP test server
    Debug "Successfully connected"
  Else
    Debug "Can't connect to test.rebex.net"
  EndIf

commands.name: ReceiveFTPFile
commands.description: Receives a file from a FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: RemoteFilename$
parameters.description:
The name of the file to download. It has to be in the current ftp directory
(see GetFTPDirectory() and SetFTPDirectory()).

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The location to save the file on the local system. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.
If the file exists, it will be overwritten.

parameters.name: Asynchronous (optional)
parameters.description:
If set to a #True, the transfer will be made in the background. The default is to block the program
until the file has been received. The progress of an asynchronous transfer can be received with the FTPProgress()
command and it can be aborted using the AbortFTPFile() command.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the file was downloaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly.
On failure, the return-value is zero.
commands.remarks: Only one file can be downloaded or uploaded (see SendFTPFile()) in the background at once.

commands.name: RenameFTPFile
commands.description: Renames a file on the FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The name of the file on the server to be renamed.
The renamed file has to be in the current directory (see GetFTPDirectory()
and SetFTPDirectory()). It is not possible to specify a subpath in the Filename$.

parameters.name: NewFilename$
parameters.description:
The new name for the file on the server.
The renamed file has to be in the current directory (see GetFTPDirectory()
and SetFTPDirectory()). It is not possible to specify a subpath in the NewFilename$.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the file was renamed successfully and zero otherwise.

commands.name: SendFTPFile
commands.description: Sends a file to a FTP server.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The name of the file to send. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: RemoteFilename$
parameters.description:
The remote filename.
It has to be in the current ftp directory
(see GetFTPDirectory() and SetFTPDirectory()).

parameters.name: Asynchronous (optional)
parameters.description:
If set to a #True, the transfer will be made in the background. The default is to block the program
until the file has been fully sent. The progress of an asynchronous transfer can be received with the FTPProgress()
command and it can be aborted using the AbortFTPFile() command.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the file was uploaded correctly, or the asynchronous transfer was initialized correctly.
On failure, the return-value is zero.
commands.remarks: Only one file can be downloaded or uploaded (see ReceiveFTPFile()) in the background at once.

commands.name: SetFTPDirectory
commands.description: Changes the current #Ftp directory, relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: #Ftp
parameters.description: The connection to use.

parameters.name: Directory$
parameters.description:
The directory to change to. This parameter must refer to a directory inside
the current FTP directory. Nested paths are not allowed. Use the value ".." to return
to the parent directory of the current directory.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation was successful and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks: To get the current FTP directory, use the GetFTPDirectory() function.
commands.example:
If OpenFTP(0, "ftp.free.fr", "anonymous", "")
    
    Debug "Successfully connected"
    
    If SetFTPDirectory(0, "pub")
      If SetFTPDirectory(0, "Linux")
        Debug "Cool, changed to '/pub/Linux'"
        Debug GetFTPDirectory(0)
      Else
        Debug "Can't change to '/pub/Linux'"
      EndIf
    Else
      Debug "Can't change to 'pub'"
    EndIf
    
  Else
    Debug "Can't connect to ftp.free.fr"
  EndIf

commands.name: AddGadgetColumn
commands.description: Adds a new column to the specified gadget.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description:
The column index where the new
item should be inserted. Column indexes start from 0, which is the leftmost column, and increase
by 1 for each column to the right. When you add a column, all the old columns which are on the right
of the new column will have a position which is one more than they previously had.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description: The text for the column header.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The initial width of the new column.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command can be used with the following types of gadgets:

- ListIconGadget()

- ExplorerListGadget()

For ExplorerListGadget() you can use this function to completely customize the information that
the gadget displays, by first removing the standard columns with RemoveGadgetColumn() and adding
new ones of your choice. Note that the 'Name' column doesn't need to be the first one in the gadget.

Note: To update the gadget contents after you have added new columns, use SetGadgetText().
To fill in a custom column, use SetGadgetItemText() for each item, after you have received a
#PB_EventType_Change event for the gadget.

When adding a column, use one of the following constants in the Title$ field to create a column whose
contents will be automatically updated by the gadget, or use any title string you wish to create an
empty column which you can then fill with SetGadgetItemText().

#PB_Explorer_Name : displays the name of the file/directory
#PB_Explorer_Size : displays the filesize in Kb
#PB_Explorer_Type : displays a string describing the filetype
#PB_Explorer_Attributes : displays the attributes of the file/directory
#PB_Explorer_Created : displays the time the file/directory was created
#PB_Explorer_Modified : displays the time the file/directory was last modified
#PB_Explorer_Accessed : displays the time the file/directory was last accessed
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 400, 150, "ListIcon - Add Columns", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    ListIconGadget(0, 10, 10, 380, 100, "Standard Column", 150, #PB_ListIcon_GridLines)
    ButtonGadget(1, 10, 120, 150, 20, "Add new column")
    index = 1     ; "Standard column" has already index 0
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()
      If Event = #PB_Event_Gadget
        If EventGadget() = 1
          AddGadgetColumn(0, index, "Column "+Str(index), 80)
          index + 1
        EndIf
      EndIf
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: AddGadgetItem
syntax: Result = AddGadgetItem(#Gadget, Position, Text$ [, ImageID [, Flags]])
commands.description: Add a new item to the specified gadget.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description:
The item index where the new item should be inserted. To add
the item at the start, use an index of 0. To add this item to the end of the current
item list, use a value of -1. Remember that when you add an item that all current
items which come after the new one will have their positions increased by 1.

For the MDIGadget() this parameter specifies the #Window number for the new MDI childwindow.
#PB_Any can be used, in which case the return-value will be the new number assigned by PB.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description:
The text for the new item.

When adding an item to a ListIconGadget(), this parameter can contain the text for multiple columns
separated by a Chr(10) character.

parameters.name: ImageID (optional)
parameters.description:
An optional image to use for the item in gadgets that support it.
The used image should be in the standard 16x16 size. Use the ImageID() command to get the ID
for this parameter.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
This parameter has a meaning only for the following gadget types:

TreeGadget()

This parameter specifies the new sublevel for the item.
If the sublevel is greater than that of the previous item, the new one will become this item's child. If it is lower, it will
be added after the parent of the previous item.

MDIGadget()

This parameter can be used to specify the flags for the new window (see OpenWindow()). The
#PB_Window_Borderless, #PB_Window_Screencentered and #PB_Window_WindowCentered flags are
not supported for MDI windows.

commands.returnValue:
The return-value is only valid with the MDIGadget(). If #PB_Any was used as the 'Position' parameter when adding an item to the MDIGadget(),
the return-value is the number that identifies the new MDI window.
commands.remarks:
The following gadgets are supported:

- ComboBoxGadget() : supports the ImageID if the #PB_ComboBox_Image is set.

- EditorGadget()

- ListIconGadget() : supports the ImageID.

- ListViewGadget()

- MDIGadget() : ImageID can contain an icon for the childwindow titlebar. Flags can specify the new window flags.

- PanelGadget() : supports the ImageID.

- TreeGadget() : supports the ImageID. 'Flags' is required and specifies the new sublevel.

commands.name: BindGadgetEvent
commands.description:
Bind a gadget event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic,
which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent() / WaitWindowEvent()
commands. It also allows to have real-time event notifications as
the callback can be invoked as soon as the event occurs (useful for
ScrollBarGadget(), ScrollAreaGadget() etc.). A gadget event can be unbound with UnbindGadgetEvent().

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description: The gadget to bind the event to.

parameters.name: @Callback()
parameters.description:
The callback procedure to call when the event occurs. It has to be declared like this:

Procedure EventHandler()
; Code
EndProcedure

Regular functions like EventGadget(), EventWindow(), EventMenu(), EventType() and EventData() are
available within the callback to get more information about the event.

Note: WindowEvent() and WaitWindowEvent() should never be called from inside the callback
or the program can be locked or have wrong behavior.

parameters.name: EventType (optional)
parameters.description:
The event type to bind the event to. For a full list of supported types, see EventType().
#PB_All can be used to bind the event to any type.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Procedure ButtonHandler()
    Debug "Button click event on gadget #" + EventGadget()
  EndProcedure
  
  OpenWindow(0, 100, 100, 200, 90, "Click test", #PB_Window_SystemMenu)
  
  ButtonGadget(0, 10, 10, 180, 30, "Click me")
  BindGadgetEvent(0, @ButtonHandler())
  
  ButtonGadget(1, 10, 50, 180, 30, "Click me")
  BindGadgetEvent(1, @ButtonHandler())
  
  Repeat
    Event = WaitWindowEvent()
  Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow

commands.name: ButtonGadget
syntax: Result = ButtonGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$ [, Flags])
commands.description: Create a button gadget in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description:
The position and dimensions of the new gadget.
Note: on OS X, using an height of 25 will enable the fixed height button type, which is
commonly used in OS X applications. It will also make the #PB_Button_Default flags available.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to display on the button.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
A combination (using the bitwise OR operator '|') of the following constants:

#PB_Button_Right : Aligns the button text at the right. (not supported on Mac OSX)
#PB_Button_Left : Aligns the button text at the left. (not supported on Mac OSX)
#PB_Button_Default : Makes the button look as if it is the default button in the window (on OS X, the height of the button needs to be 25).
#PB_Button_MultiLine : If the text is too long, it will be displayed on several lines. (not supported on OSX)
#PB_Button_Toggle : Creates a toggle button: one click pushes it, another will release it.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
A 'mini help' can be added to this gadget using GadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to control the gadget:

- SetGadgetText(): Changes the text of the ButtonGadget.

- GetGadgetText(): Returns the text of the ButtonGadget.

- SetGadgetState(): Used with #PB_Button_Toggle buttons to set the actual state (1 = toggled, 0 = normal).

- GetGadgetState(): Used with #PB_Button_Toggle buttons to get the actual state of the button (1 = toggled, 0 = normal).
commands.example:
; Shows possible flags of ButtonGadget in action...
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 222, 200, "ButtonGadgets", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    ButtonGadget(0, 10, 10, 200, 20, "Standard Button")
    ButtonGadget(1, 10, 40, 200, 20, "Left Button", #PB_Button_Left)
    ButtonGadget(2, 10, 70, 200, 20, "Right Button", #PB_Button_Right)
    ButtonGadget(3, 10,100, 200, 60, "Multiline Button  (longer text gets automatically wrapped)", #PB_Button_MultiLine)
    ButtonGadget(4, 10,170, 200, 20, "Toggle Button", #PB_Button_Toggle)
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ButtonImageGadget
syntax: Result = ButtonImageGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, ImageID [, Flags])
commands.description: Create a button gadget with an image in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description:
The image for the gadget. Use the ImageID() function to get this ID from an image.
This parameter can be zero to create a button without an image. The SetGadgetAttribute()
function can be used to change the image later.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
This parameter can be #PB_Button_Toggle to create a toggle-button (one which has an on/off state).
A push-button is created by default.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
A 'mini help' can be added to this gadget using GadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to control the gadget:

- GetGadgetState() can be used to get the toggle state of the gadget.

- SetGadgetState() can be used to set the toggle state of the gadget.

- GetGadgetAttribute() with the following values:

#PB_Button_Image : Get the displayed image ID, e.g. ImageID(#MyImage).
#PB_Button_PressedImage: Get the displayed image ID when the button is pressed, e.g. ImageID(#MyImagePressed).

- SetGadgetAttribute() with the following values:

#PB_Button_Image : Set the displayed image.
#PB_Button_PressedImage: Set the image displayed when the button is pressed.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 60, "ButtonImageGadget", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered) 
    If LoadImage(0,  #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/PureBasic.bmp")    ; change 2nd parameter to the path/filename of your image
      ButtonImageGadget(0, 10, 10, 180, 40, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CalendarGadget

Create a calendar gadget in the current GadgetList. This gadget displays a month calendar and lets the
user select a date.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Date (optional)
parameters.description: The initial date to set. The default is the current date.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
This parameter can be set to #PB_Calendar_Borderless to create a gadget without
a border (not supported on Linux).

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
The dates used by this gadget and the functions for it use the same date format as the
date library.

A 'mini help' can be added to this gadget using GadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used for this gadget:

- SetGadgetState(): Set the currently displayed date.

- GetGadgetState(): Get the currently displayed date.

- SetGadgetAttribute(): With the following attributes:

#PB_Calendar_Minimum: Set the minimum selectable date
#PB_Calendar_Maximum: Set the maximum selectable date in this gadget.
(Note: Limitation of the selectable date isn't supported on Linux.)

- GetGadgetAttribute(): With the following attributes:

#PB_Calendar_Minimum: Get the minimum selectable date
#PB_Calendar_Maximum: Get the maximum selectable date of this gadget.
(Note: Limitation of the selectable date isn't supported on Linux.)

This gadget supports the SetGadgetColor() and GetGadgetColor() functions with
the following values as 'ColorType':
