commands.name: CloseHID
commands.description: Close the specified HID device.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to close.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: Once the HID device is closed, it may not be used anymore. All resources associated with the device are released.

commands.name: DisableHIDBlockingMode
commands.description:
Enable or disable blocking mode for the specified HID device.
When blocking mode is disabled, read operations will return immediately even if no data is available.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to configure.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: The blocking mode status (nonzero to disable blocking, zero to enable).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ExamineHIDs
commands.description: Start the enumeration of available HID devices.

parameters.name: VendorId (optional)
parameters.description: Filter devices by specific vendor ID.

parameters.name: ProductId (optional)
parameters.description: Filter devices by specific product ID.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the enumeration was started successfully and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
Use this function to begin enumerating HID devices. After calling ExamineHIDs(), use NextHID() to iterate through
the available devices.
commands.example:
If ExamineHIDs()
    While NextHID()
      Debug "Found HID device: " + HIDInfo(#PB_HID_Product)
    Wend
  EndIf

commands.name: GetHIDIndexedString
commands.description:
Get the specified indexed string value from the HID device.
HID devices can store multiple strings at different indices, such as product name, manufacturer, etc.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to query.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The index of the string to retrieve.

commands.returnValue: Returns the string value, or an empty string if there was an error.

commands.name: GetHIDReportDescriptor
commands.description: Get the HID report descriptor from the device as memory buffer.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to query.

commands.returnValue: Returns the report descriptor as a memory buffer. To get the size of the descriptor, use MemorySize(). Once the descriptor is no more needed, it can be freed with FreeMemory().
commands.remarks: The report descriptor describes the data format and capabilities of the HID device.

commands.name: HIDError
commands.description: Read the last error information.
commands.returnValue: Returns a string describing the last HID error that occurred.
commands.remarks: This function can be called after any HID operation fails to get more information about the error.

commands.name: HIDInfo
commands.description: Get more information about the HID device.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of information to retrieve. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_HID_Path : the platform-specific device path.
#PB_HID_VendorId : the device vendor ID.
#PB_HID_ProductId : the device product ID.
#PB_HID_SerialNumber : the serial number.
#PB_HID_ReleaseNumber : the device release number in binary-coded decimal, also known as device version number.
#PB_HID_Manufacturer : the manufacturer.
#PB_HID_Product : the product.
#PB_HID_UsagePage : the usage page this device.
#PB_HID_Usage : the usage for this device.
#PB_HID_InterfaceNumber: the USB interface which this logical device represents (only valid for USB devices)
#PB_HID_BusType : the underlying bus type. Can be one of the following value:
0: Unknown
1: USB
2: Bluetooth
3: I2C
4: SPI

parameters.name: #HID (optional)
parameters.description: The HID device to query. If not specified, uses the current device from enumeration started with ExamineHIDs().

commands.returnValue:
Returns a string containing the requested HID information.

If ExamineHIDs()
While NextHID()
Debug "Found HID device: " + HIDInfo(#PB_HID_Product)
Debug "Found HID device: " + HIDInfo(#PB_HID_Manufacturer)
Debug "Found HID device: " + HIDInfo(#PB_HID_Path)
Debug "---------------------------------------------------"
Wend
EndIf

commands.name: IsHID
commands.description: Check if the given '#HID' is an initialized HID object.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to check.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #HID is a valid HID device and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value to ensure a HID device is ready to use.

commands.name: NextHID
commands.description: Get the next HID device in the enumeration started with ExamineHIDs().
commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if another HID device was found and zero if there are no more devices.
commands.remarks: This function must be called after ExamineHIDs() to iterate through available HID devices.

commands.name: OpenHID
commands.description: Open the specified HID device for read or write operations.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The number to identify the HID device.

parameters.name: VendorId
parameters.description: The vendor ID of the device to open.

parameters.name: ProductId
parameters.description: The product ID of the device to open.

parameters.name: SerialNumber (optional)
parameters.description: The serial number of the specific device to open (if multiple devices with same VID/PID exist).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the device was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
This function opens a HID device by its Vendor ID and Product ID. If multiple devices with the same
VID/PID exist, specify the SerialNumber to open a specific device.

commands.name: OpenHIDPath
commands.description: Open the specified HID device for read or write operations using a device path.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The number to identify the HID device.

parameters.name: Path$
parameters.description: The platform-specific device path to open.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the device was opened successfully and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks: This function opens a HID device by its specific device path, which can be obtained through device enumeration with ExamineHIDs().

commands.name: ReadHIDData
commands.description: Read data from the specified HID device.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to read from.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to store the read data.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The number of bytes to read.

parameters.name: Timeout (optional)
parameters.description: The timeout in milliseconds for the read operation.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes actually read, or zero if there was an error or timeout.

commands.name: ReceiveHIDFeatureReport
commands.description:
Receive a feature report from the HID device.
Feature reports are used for bidirectional configuration and status information.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to receive from.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to store the received report.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the buffer.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes received, or zero if there was an error.

commands.name: ReceiveHIDInputReport
commands.description:
Receive an input report from the HID device.
Input reports are used for device-to-host communication and include the report ID.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to receive from.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to store the received report.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the buffer.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes received, or zero if there was an error.

commands.name: SendHIDFeatureReport
commands.description:
Send a feature report to the HID device.
Feature reports are used for bidirectional configuration and status information.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to send to.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer containing the report to send.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the report.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes sent, or zero if there was an error.

commands.name: SendHIDOutputReport
commands.description:
Send an output report to the HID device.
Output reports are used for host-to-device communication and include the report ID.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to send to.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer containing the report to send.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the report.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes sent, or zero if there was an error.

commands.name: WriteHIDData
commands.description: Write data to the specified HID device.

parameters.name: #HID
parameters.description: The HID device to write to.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer containing the data to write.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The number of bytes to write.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes actually written, or zero if there was an error.

commands.name: AbortHTTP
commands.description:
Aborts the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile() or
ReceiveHTTPMemory().
It's also usable for HTTPRequest() and HTTPRequestMemory() (if #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used).

parameters.name: HttpConnection
parameters.description: The HTTP connection to abort.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: The value #PB_HTTP_Aborted will be returned by HTTPProgress(). FinishHTTP() has to be called once the download has been aborted.

commands.name: FinishHTTP
commands.description:
Free the resources associated to the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile() or
ReceiveHTTPMemory(). It must be always called after a successful call of ReceiveHTTPFile() or ReceiveHTTPMemory().

parameters.name: HttpConnection
parameters.description: The HTTP connection to finish.

commands.returnValue:
Depending on which Receive command was used to start the download, FinishHTTP() returns one of the following results:

ReceiveHTTPFile(): Amount of received bytes (size of the stored file).

ReceiveHTTPMemory() with the #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous flag set: Address of the memory area where the received
data was stored. With MemorySize() the amount of received data can be determined then.
commands.remarks: The value #PB_HTTP_Aborted will be returned by HTTPProgress().

commands.name: GetURLPart
commands.description: Get a specific part of the given URL$. This can be a named parameter in the URL string or another part of the URL.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description:
The URL$ to get the part from.
The URL$ may contain parameters, which are useful when a scripting language
such as: (PHP) is being used on that server. The syntax is as follows: (http://www.purebasic.com/index.php3?test=1)
Here, the parameter is named "test" and its associated value is "1".

parameters.name: Parameter$
parameters.description:
The parameter to return from the URL$. The parameters are not case-sensitive.
This parameter can also specify one of the following constants to access other parts of the URL:

#PB_URL_Protocol: returns the protocol from the URL$
#PB_URL_Site: returns the site from the URL$
#PB_URL_Port: returns the port from the URL$ (if specified)
#PB_URL_Parameters: returns all the parameters from the URL$
#PB_URL_Path: returns the path from the URL$
#PB_URL_User: returns the username from the URL$ (if specified)
#PB_URL_Password: returns the password from the URL$ (if specified)

commands.returnValue: Returns the parameter value or other part of the URL.
commands.example:
URL$ = "http://user:pass@www.purebasic.com:80/index.php3?test=1&ok=2"

  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Protocol) ; Will print "http"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Site)     ; Will print "www.purebasic.com"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Port)     ; Will print "80"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Parameters) ; Will print "test=1&ok=2"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Path)     ; Will print "index.php3"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_User)     ; Will print "user"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Password) ; Will print "pass"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, "test")           ; Will print "1"
  Debug GetURLPart(URL$, "ok")             ; Will print "2"

commands.name: HTTPInfo
commands.description:
Returns information about an HTTP request created with HTTPRequest() or
HTTPRequestMemory().

parameters.name: HttpRequest
parameters.description: The HTTP request to get the info.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The specific info to get. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Http_StatusCode : the server status code (200: OK, 404: page not found etc.).
#PB_Http_Response : the server response, as text. To get the raw server response, use HTTPMemory().
#PB_Http_Headers : the request headers.
#PB_Http_ErrorMessage: the HTTP request error message, if something goes wrong (mostly for debugging purpose).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the HTTP response or header encoding. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_UTF8 (default)
#PB_Ascii

commands.returnValue: A string depending of the 'Type' parameter.
commands.example:
HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com")
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPMemory
commands.description:
Returns a memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request created with HTTPRequest() or HTTPRequestMemory().
Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory(). If the flag #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous was used when calling HTTPRequest()
or HTTPRequestMemory(), this command is only valid if the request has been successful.

parameters.name: HttpRequest
parameters.description: The HTTP request to get the raw response.

commands.returnValue:
A memory buffer containing the whole response of an HTTP request.
Once done with it, the buffer needs to be freed with FreeMemory().
commands.example:
HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com")
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    
    *Response = HTTPMemory(HTTPRequest)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
    
    Debug "Response size: " + MemorySize(*Response)
    FreeMemory(*Response)
    
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPProgress
commands.description:
Returns the progress of the specified asynchronous download, started either with ReceiveHTTPFile() or
ReceiveHTTPMemory().

parameters.name: HttpConnection
parameters.description: The HTTP connection to monitor.

commands.returnValue:
The status of the download. It can be the current number of received bytes or one of the following values:

#PB_Http_Success : the download has been successfully finished.
#PB_Http_Failed : the download has failed.
#PB_Http_Aborted : the download has been aborted with AbortHTTP().
commands.example:
Download = ReceiveHTTPMemory("http://www.purebasic.com/download/OgreAssimpConverter.zip", #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous)
  If Download
    Repeat
      Progress = HTTPProgress(Download)
      Select Progress
        Case #PB_Http_Success
          *Buffer = FinishHTTP(Download)
          Debug "Download finished (size: " + MemorySize(*Buffer) + ")"
          FreeMemory(*Buffer)
          End

        Case #PB_Http_Failed
          Debug "Download failed"
          FinishHTTP(Download)
          End

        Case #PB_Http_Aborted
          Debug "Download aborted"
          FinishHTTP(Download)
          End
          
        Default
          Debug "Current download: " + Progress
       
      EndSelect
      
      Delay(500) ; Don't stole the whole CPU
    ForEver
  Else
    Debug "Download error"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPProxy
commands.description:
Specify a proxy to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile(),
ReceiveHTTPMemory(), HTTPRequest() and HTTPRequestMemory().

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description:
The URL to use for the proxy. Default is HTTP proxy if no prefix is specified. Available
prefixes to specify proxy type:

http:// - HTTP proxy (default)
socks4:// - SOCKS4 proxy
socks4a:// - SOCKS4 proxy with domain name support rather than IP address
socks5:// - SOCKS5 proxy
socks5h:// - SOCKS5 proxy and ask the proxy to do the hostname resolving

parameters.name: User$, Password$ (optional)
parameters.description: The user and password to use to connect to the proxy (if any).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
On Linux, 'libcurl' needs to be installed to have this command working (most of Linux
distributions comes with it already installed).
commands.example:
HTTPProxy("socks4://127.0.0.1")

  Filename$ = SaveFileRequester("Where to save index.php ?", "", "", 0)

  If ReceiveHTTPFile("http://www.purebasic.com/index.php", Filename$)
    Debug "Success"
  Else
    Debug "Failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPRequest
syntax: Result = HTTPRequest(Type, URL$ [, Data$ [, Flags [, Headers()]]])
commands.description:
Send an HTTP request with optional text data. If binary data needs to be sent, HTTPRequestMemory() can be used.
This command is designed to handle REST like web APIs easily. FinishHTTP() needs to be always called once the request has been executed.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of the request. Can be one of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Get : GET request ('Data$' parameter will be ignored)
#PB_HTTP_Post : POST request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Put : PUT request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Patch : PATCH request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Delete : DELETE request ('Data$' parameter will be sent if specified)

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to send the request to.

parameters.name: Data$ (optional)
parameters.description: The text data to send with the request (will be sent as UTF-8 format).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Asynchronous: starts the download asynchronously.
#PB_HTTP_NoRedirect : don't follow automatic redirections.
#PB_HTTP_NoSSLCheck : don't check if the SSL certificate is valid (can be useful for testing purpose).
#PB_HTTP_HeadersOnly : gets headers only.
#PB_HTTP_WeakSSL : to support older servers (not recommended due to weak/broken transport security).
#PB_HTTP_Debug : to print in the console debug information.

parameters.name: Headers() (optional)
parameters.description:
A map of string pair to specify additional headers for the request. Example:

NewMap Header$()
Header$("Content-Type") = "text/plain"
Header$("User-Agent") = "Firefox 54.0"
Header$("NoParamHeader") = "" ; When putting no string value, it will an empty parameter

commands.returnValue:
Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo() can be
used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous
was specified, HTTPProgress() can be used and AbortHTTP() must be used.
HTTPMemory() can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory()).
FinishHTTP() has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.
commands.remarks:
On Linux, 'libcurl' needs to be installed to have this command working (most of Linux
distributions comes with it already installed).
commands.example:
HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com")
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

NewMap Header$()
  Header$("Content-Type") = "plaintext"
  Header$("User-Agent") = "Firefox 54.0"
  
  HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com", "", 0, Header$())
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.purebasic.com/download/PureBasic_Demo.zip", "", #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous)
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    
    Repeat
      Progress = HTTPProgress(HttpRequest)
      Select Progress
        Case #PB_HTTP_Success
          Debug "Download finished"
          *Buffer = HTTPMemory(HTTPRequest)
          If *Buffer
            Debug "Memory buffer size: "+MemorySize(*buffer) ; Here the buffer can be written to disk or used directory
            FreeMemory(*Buffer)
          EndIf
          FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest) ; Always call FinishHTTP() when request is finished
          Break
          
        Case #PB_HTTP_Failed
          Debug "Download failed"
          FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest) ; Always call FinishHTTP() when request failed
          Break
          
        Case #PB_HTTP_Aborted
          Debug "Download aborted"
          FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest) ; Always call FinishHTTP() when request is aborted
          Break
      
        Default
          Debug "Current download: " + Progress ; The current download progress, in bytes
          Delay(100)
      EndSelect
    ForEver
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPRequestMemory
syntax: Result = HTTPRequestMemory(Type, URL$ [, *Data, DataSize [, Flags [, Headers()]]])
commands.description:
Send an HTTP request with optional binary data. If text only data needs to be sent HTTPRequest() can be used.
This command is designed to handle REST like web API easily. FinishHTTP() needs to be always called once the request has been executed.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of the request. Can be one of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Get : GET request ('*Data' parameter will be ignored)
#PB_HTTP_Post : POST request ('*Data' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Put : PUT request ('*Data' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Patch : PATCH request ('*Data' parameter will be sent if specified)
#PB_HTTP_Delete: DELETE request ('*Data' parameter will be sent if specified)

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to send the request to.

parameters.name: *Data (optional)
parameters.description: The memory buffer to send with the request.

parameters.name: DataSize (optional)
parameters.description: The size (in bytes) of the memory buffer to send with the request.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Asynchronous: starts the download asynchronously.
#PB_HTTP_NoRedirect : don't follow automatic redirections.
#PB_HTTP_NoSSLCheck : don't check if the SSL certificate is valid (can be useful for testing purpose).
#PB_HTTP_HeadersOnly : gets headers only.
#PB_HTTP_WeakSSL : to support older servers.
#PB_HTTP_Debug : to print in the console debug information.

parameters.name: Headers() (optional)
parameters.description:
A map of string pair to specify additional headers for the request. Example:

NewMap Header$()
Header$("ContentType") = "octectstream"
Header$("User-Agent") = "Firefox 54.0"
Header$("NoParamHeader") = "" ; When putting no string value, it will be an empty parameter

commands.returnValue:
Returns the HTTP request identifier if the call has been successfully initialized, zero otherwise. HTTPInfo() can be
used to get some info about the request. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous
was specified, HTTPProgress() and AbortHTTP() can be used.
HTTPMemory() can be used to get the result as a raw buffer (the raw buffer must be freed with FreeMemory()).
FinishHTTP() has to be always called to finish a successfully initialized HTTP request, even if the call was synchronous.
commands.remarks:
On Linux, 'libcurl' needs to be installed to have this command working (most of Linux
distributions comes with it already installed).
commands.example:
HttpRequest = HTTPRequestMemory(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com")
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: HTTPTimeout
commands.description:
Specify timeout to use for the following HTTP commands: ReceiveHTTPFile(),
ReceiveHTTPMemory(), HTTPRequest() and HTTPRequestMemory().

parameters.name: ConnectTimeout
parameters.description:
The timeout, in milliseconds, to abort the HTTP request if the remote host doesn't connect. The default timeout is set
to 30 seconds. #PB_Default can be used to revert to the default timeout value (30 seconds).

parameters.name: GlobalTimeout (optional)
parameters.description:
The global timeout, in milliseconds, to abort the HTTP request if it is still not finished. There is no timeout by default.
#PB_Default can be used to revert to the default behaviour (no timeout). Note: if a connection is slow, it could abort
a valid unfinished request.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
If "Create thread-safe executable" is enabled in the compiler options then
every thread has its own timeouts, which means two threads can have different timeouts at the same time.
commands.example:
HTTPTimeout(5000) ; Allows 5 secs to connect to the server

  HttpRequest = HTTPRequest(#PB_HTTP_Get, "https://www.google.com")
  If HttpRequest
    Debug "StatusCode: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_StatusCode)
    Debug "Response: " + HTTPInfo(HTTPRequest, #PB_HTTP_Response)
    
    FinishHTTP(HTTPRequest)
  Else
    Debug "Request creation failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: ReceiveHTTPFile
commands.description: Download a file to disk from the given URL$.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to download from.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The local filename to write the file to. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.
If the file exists, it will be overwritten.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Asynchronous: starts the download asynchronously.
#PB_HTTP_NoRedirect : don't follow automatic redirections.
#PB_HTTP_NoSSLCheck : don't check if the SSL certificate is valid (can be useful for testing purpose).
#PB_HTTP_WeakSSL : to support older servers.
#PB_HTTP_Debug : to print in the console debug information.

parameters.name: UserAgent$ (optional)
parameters.description:
Change the user agent for the HTTP request. Default user agent is set to
"Mozilla/5.0 Gecko/41.0 Firefox/41.0" for maximum compatibility.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the download was successful, zero otherwise. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous
was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress(),
AbortHTTP() and FinishHTTP(). When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP() needs to be called
when the download is finished (successfully or not).
commands.remarks:
On Linux, 'libcurl' needs to be installed to have this command working (most of Linux
distributions comes with it already installed).

If the remote file was not found, it will contains the webserver error.
commands.example:
Filename$ = SaveFileRequester("Where to save index.php ?", "", "", 0)

  If ReceiveHTTPFile("https://www.purebasic.com/index.php", Filename$)
    Debug "File received and written to disk. If the remote file was not found, it will contains the webserver error."
  Else
    Debug "No file received (network error)."
  EndIf

commands.name: ReceiveHTTPMemory
commands.description: Download a file to a new memory buffer from the given URL$.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to download from.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_HTTP_Asynchronous: starts the download asynchronously. To get the memory buffer address use FinishHTTP().
#PB_HTTP_NoRedirect : don't follow automatic redirections.
#PB_HTTP_NoSSLCheck : don't check if the SSL certificate is valid (can be useful for testing purpose).
#PB_HTTP_WeakSSL : to support older servers.
#PB_HTTP_Debug : to print in the console debug information.

parameters.name: UserAgent$ (optional)
parameters.description:
Change the user agent for the HTTP request. Default user agent is set to
"Mozilla/5.0 Gecko/41.0 Firefox/41.0" for maximum compatibility.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the new memory buffer address if the download was successful, zero otherwise. MemorySize() can be
used to get the size of the downloaded item. The memory buffer needs
to be freed with FreeMemory() once finished using it. If #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous
was specified, it returns the 'HttpConnection' value needed for HTTPProgress(),
AbortHTTP() and FinishHTTP(). When using #PB_HTTP_Asynchronous, FinishHTTP() needs to be called
when the download is finished (successfully or not).
commands.remarks:
On Linux, 'libcurl' needs to be installed to have this command working (most of Linux
distributions comes with it already installed).
commands.example:
*Buffer = ReceiveHTTPMemory("http://www.purebasic.com/index.php")
  If *Buffer
    Size = MemorySize(*Buffer)
    Debug "Content: " + PeekS(*Buffer, Size, #PB_UTF8|#PB_ByteLength)
    FreeMemory(*Buffer)
  Else
    Debug "Failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: SetURLPart
commands.description: Set a specific part of the given URL$.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description:
The URL to modify.
A URL$ may contain parameters, which are useful when a scripting language
such as: (PHP) is being used on that server. The syntax is as follows: (http://www.purebasic.com/index.php3?test=1)
Here, the parameter is named "test" and its associated value is "1".

In order to set a specific part of a URL, the information provided within "URL$" must (at the minimum),
be of the following format: ("http://www.purebasic.com")

parameters.name: Parameter$
parameters.description:
The parameter to modify.
The parameters are not case-sensitive. Moreover, Parameter$ may be one of the following constants:

#PB_URL_Protocol: change the protocol of the URL$
#PB_URL_Site: change the site of the URL$
#PB_URL_Port: change the port of the URL$ (or adds it if not specified)
#PB_URL_Parameters: changes all the parameters of the URL$ (or adds it if not specified)
#PB_URL_Path: changes the path of the URL$ (or adds it if not specified)
#PB_URL_User: changes the username of the URL$ (or adds it if not specified)
#PB_URL_Password: changes the password of the URL$ (or adds it if not specified - the "user" needs to exist)

parameters.name: Value$
parameters.description: The value to assign to the given parameter or URL part.

commands.returnValue: Returns the modified URL.
commands.example:
URL$ = "http://www.test.com/hello.php3"

  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Protocol, "ftp")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Site, "www.purebasic.com")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Port, "80")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Path, "english/index.php3")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_User, "user")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, #PB_URL_Password, "pass")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, "test", "1")
  URL$ = SetURLPart(URL$, "ok", "2")

  Debug URL$ ; Will print "ftp://user:pass@www.purebasic.com:80/english/index.php3?test=1&ok=2"

commands.name: URLDecoder
commands.description: Returns a decoded URL$ which has been encoded with the HTTP format.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to decode. To encode an URL, use URLEncoder().

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the URL encoding. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_UTF8 (default)
#PB_Ascii

commands.returnValue: Returns the decoded URL.
commands.remarks:
A URL$ may not contain certain characters such as: tab, space, accent letter etc.,
therefore these characters must be encoded, which basically involves using "%" as an escape
character. If the URL$ is not in an encoded format, this function will have no effect on the
given "URL$" and the return-value of that "URL$" will remain unchanged.
commands.example:
Debug URLDecoder("http://www.purebasic.com/test%20with%20space.php3")
  ; Will print "http://www.purebasic.com/test with space.php3"

commands.name: URLEncoder
commands.description: Returns the URL$ encoded to the HTTP format.

parameters.name: URL$
parameters.description: The URL to encode.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the string before encoding it. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_UTF8 (default)
#PB_Ascii

commands.returnValue:
Returns the encoded URL.
To convert an encoded URL back to a unencoded format, use URLDecoder()
commands.remarks:
A URL$ may not contain certain characters such as: tab, space, accent letter etc.,
therefore these characters must be encoded, which basically involves using "%" as an escape
character.

Because this function use the RFC 3986 standard, some characters will not be encoded, such
as (non-exhaustive list):

"-" | "_" | "." | "!" | "~" | "*" | "'" | "(" | ")" |
";" | "/" | "?" | ":" | "@" | "&" | "=" | "+" | "$" |
"," | """ | "#" | "%" |

Anyway, if you need to encode them, you will need to use the following table:
https://www.w3schools.com/tags/ref_urlencode.asp

For example in UTF8:

"-" -> %2D | "_" -> %5F | "." -> %2E | "!" -> %21 | "~" -> %7E |

"*" -> %2A | "'" -> %27 | "(" -> %28 | ")" -> %29 | ";" -> %3B |

"/" -> %2F | "?" -> %3F | ":" -> %3A | "@" -> %40 | "&" -> %26 |

"=" -> %3D | "+" -> %2B | "$" -> %24 | "," -> %2C | """ -> %22 |

"#" -> %23 | "%" -> %25 |
commands.example:
Debug URLEncoder("http://www.purebasic.com/test with space.php3")
  ; Will print "http://www.purebasic.com/test%20with%20space.php3"
  
  Debug URLEncoder("http://www.ok.com value=zzz ?yyy/")
  ; Will print "http://www.ok.com%20value=zzz%20?yyy/"

commands.name: AddImageFrame
commands.description:
Adds a new frame to the specified image. The new frame will have the same dimension and depth
like the image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to add a frame.

parameters.name: Index (optional)
parameters.description:
The index (starting from 0) to insert the frame. If not specified the new frame will be added at the
end of the frame list.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the new frame has been successfully created, zero otherwise.

commands.name: CatchImage
commands.description: Load the specified image from the given memory area.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description:
A number to identify the loaded image. #PB_Any can
be specified to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: *MemoryAddress
parameters.description: The memory address from which to load the image.

parameters.name: Size (optional)
parameters.description:
The size of the image in bytes. The size is optional as the loader can determine from the image when to
stop reading. It is however advisable to provide a size when loading unknown images, as the loader can then handle
corrupted images correctly (without specifying the image size, a corrupt image can crash the program).

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded.
If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
The limit for the image size that can be handled depends on the operating system and the available amount of memory.
If enough memory is available, then images up to at least 8192x8192 pixels can be handled by all operating systems supported by PureBasic.

When an image is loaded, it is converted either in 24-bit (if the image depth
is less or equal to 24-bit) or in 32-bit (if the image has an alpha channel).
A loaded image can be freed by using the FreeImage() function.

This function is useful when using the 'IncludeBinary' PureBasic keyword. Then images can be packed inside
the executable. Nevertheless, use this option with care, as it will take
more memory than storing the file in an external file (the file are both in
executable memory and load in physical memory).

The image can be in BMP, icon (.ico, only on Windows) or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library.
Transparency of BMP images is not supported.
The following functions can be used to enable additional image formats:

UseJPEGImageDecoder()

UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder()

UsePNGImageDecoder()

UseTIFFImageDecoder()

UseTGAImageDecoder()

UseGIFImageDecoder()
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 148, 148, "ImageGadget", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    If CatchImage(0, ?Geebee)
      ImageGadget(0, 10, 10, 0, 0, ImageID(0))
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf
  
  DataSection
    GeeBee:
    IncludeBinary #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/Geebee2.bmp"
  EndDataSection

commands.name: CopyImage
commands.description:
Creates an identical copy of an image. If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used
for the copy.

parameters.name: #Image1
parameters.description: The source image.

parameters.name: #Image2
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new copy. #PB_Any can be specified to
auto-generate this number.

Note: The number of an existing image created using #PB_Any can not be used as the target image.
Instead, the existing image must be freed and a new number generated by passing #PB_Any here.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was copied successfully and zero if the copy could not be created.
If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

commands.name: CreateImage
syntax: Result = CreateImage(#Image, Width, Height [, Depth [, BackColor]])
commands.description: Create an empty image (with black background) which can be used to do rendering on it.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new image. #PB_Any can be specified to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The dimensions of the new image. Both the width and height must be greater than zero.

parameters.name: Depth (optional)
parameters.description:
The color depth for the new image.
Valid values can be: 24 and 32. The default is 24-bit if no depth is specified.

parameters.name: BackColor (optional)
parameters.description:
The backcolor used when the image is created.

If the image is 24-bit, use RGB() to get a valid color.

If the image is 32-bit, use RGBA() to get a valid color. For 32-bit image, special constants can be used as well:

- #PB_Image_Transparent which is similar to RGBA(255,255,255,0), white background which can help for light antialiasing.

- #PB_Image_TransparentBlack which is similar to RGBA(0,0,0,0), black background which can help for dark antialiasing.

The default backcolor is black if not specified.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created.
If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
The limit for the image size that can be handled depends on the operating system and the available amount of memory.
If enough memory is available, then images up to at least 8192x8192 pixels can be handled by all operating systems supported by PureBasic.

You can use the several other functions for acting with the created image:

StartDrawing() with ImageOutput() to draw on the created image

StartVectorDrawing() with ImageVectorOutput() to draw on the created image using vector drawing

CopyImage() to create another image from the actual one

GrabImage() to create another image from a given area of the actual one

DrawImage() with ImageID() to draw the image on actual output channel.

ImageGadget() for displaying image on an application window

ButtonImageGadget() for creating an image button on an application window

commands.name: EncodeImage
commands.description: Encode the specified image into a memory buffer.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to encode.

parameters.name: ImagePlugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The format to encode the image in. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_ImagePlugin_BMP : encode the image in BMP (default)
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG : encode the image in JPEG (UseJPEGImageEncoder() has to be used)
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000 : encode the image in JPEG2000 (UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder() has to be used)
#PB_ImagePlugin_PNG : encode the image in PNG (UsePNGImageEncoder() has to be used)

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
Parameters for the image plug-in. For now, only the quality setting is supported:
a number from 0 (worse quality) to 10 (maximum quality). Only the JPEG and JPEG 2000 plugins currently support it (default
quality is set to '7' if no flags are specified).

When an image is encoded using palletized depth (1, 4 or 8), the following
flag is available for combination:

#PB_Image_FloydSteinberg: Apply a Floyd-Steinberg dithering.

parameters.name: Depth (optional)
parameters.description:
The depth in which to save the image. Valid values are 1, 4, 8, 24 and 32.
The default value is the original image depth.
For now, only PNG encoder support palletized image format (1, 4 or 8-bit).

commands.returnValue:
Returns a pointer to a newly allocated memory buffer containing the encoded image, or zero if the encoding has failed.
MemorySize() can be used to get the size of the encoded image. FreeMemory() has to be used to free the buffer
after use.

commands.name: FreeImage
commands.description: Free the specified image and release its associated memory.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining images are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining images are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetImageFrame
commands.description: Gets the current frame index of the image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

commands.returnValue:
The current frame index (starting from 0).
If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 0.

commands.name: GetImageFrameDelay
commands.description:
Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own
delay.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to get the frame delay.

commands.returnValue: Returns the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.

commands.name: GrabImage
syntax: Result = GrabImage(#Image1, #Image2, x, y, Width, Height)
commands.description:
Create a new image with the selected area on the source image.
If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used for the grab.

parameters.name: #Image1
parameters.description: The source image.

parameters.name: #Image2
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new image. #PB_Any can be specified to
auto-generate this number.

Note: An existing image number that was created using #PB_Any can not be reused as the target image.
Instead, the existing image must be freed (if no longer needed) and a new number generated by passing #PB_Any here.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The location and size of the area to copy into the new image.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was created successfully and zero if the image could not be created.
If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image2 parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.

commands.name: ImageDepth
commands.description: Returns the depth of the #Image, as it is stored internally by PureBasic.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The kind of depth to return. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Image_InternalDepth: Returns the depth of the decoded image (default). Valid return values are:
- 24 (24-bit, 16 millions colors)
- 32 (32-bit, 16 millions colors + 8-bit alpha channel)
#PB_Image_OriginalDepth: Returns the original depth, as it was before the decoding. Valid return values are:
- 1 (1-bit, 2 colors, monochrome image)
- 4 (4-bit, 16 colors)
- 8 (8-bit, 256 colors)
- 16 (16-bit, 65536 colors)
- 24 (24-bit, 16 millions colors)
- 32 (32-bit, 16 millions colors + 8-bit alpha channel)

commands.returnValue: Returns one of the possible depth values described above.
commands.remarks:
When loading an image, PureBasic converts it either in 24-bit or in 32-bit, depending
if the source image has an alpha channel or not. Every image which has a
depth less than 24-bit will be internally converted to 24-bit.

commands.name: ImageFormat
commands.description: Return the original image format.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the image original format. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000
#PB_ImagePlugin_PNG
#PB_ImagePlugin_TGA
#PB_ImagePlugin_TIFF
#PB_ImagePlugin_BMP
#PB_ImagePlugin_ICON
#PB_ImagePlugin_GIF

If the image was not loaded from one of these formats, it will return zero. This is the case for images created with
CreateImage() or GrabImage().

commands.name: ImageFrameCount
commands.description: Returns the number of frames of the image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to get the frame count.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the frame count of the image.
If the image is not multi-frame, it will always return 1.

commands.name: ImageHeight
commands.description: Returns the height of the given image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the height of the image in pixels.

commands.name: ImageID
commands.description: Returns the ImageID of the image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the operating system handle of the image.

commands.name: ImageOutput
commands.description:
Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D rendering operation on it.
Alternatively, the ImageVectorOutput() command can be used to perform vector drawing on the image.
If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to draw on.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the
StartDrawing() function to start the drawing operation. The return-value
is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
commands.remarks: This command cannot be used with loaded icon files (*.ico).
commands.example:
StartDrawing(ImageOutput(#Image))
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopDrawing()

commands.name: ImageVectorOutput
commands.description:
Returns the OutputID of the image to perform 2D vector drawing operations on it.
If the image is multi-frame, the current frame will be used.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to draw on.

parameters.name: Unit (optional)
parameters.description:
Specifies the unit used for measuring distances on the drawing output.
The default unit for images is #PB_Unit_Pixel.

#PB_Unit_Pixel : Values are measured in pixels (or dots in case of a printer)
#PB_Unit_Point : Values are measured in points (1/72 inch)
#PB_Unit_Inch : Values are measured in inches
#PB_Unit_Millimeter: Values are measured in millimeters

commands.returnValue:
Returns the output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the
StartVectorDrawing() function to start the drawing operation. The return-value
is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
commands.remarks: This command cannot be used with loaded icon files (*.ico).
commands.example:
StartVectorDrawing(ImageVectorOutput(#Image, #PB_Unit_Millimeter))
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopVectorDrawing()

commands.name: ImageWidth
commands.description: Returns the width of the given image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the width of the image in pixels.

commands.name: IsImage
commands.description: Tests if the given image number is a valid and correctly initialized image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to test.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #Image is a valid image and zero if not.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value.
This is the correct way to ensure an image is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadImage
commands.description: Load the specified image from a file.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description:
A number to identify the loaded image. #PB_Any can
be specified to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The name of the file to load. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description: This parameter currently has no meaning. If it is specified, 0 should be used for future compatibility.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the image was loaded successfully and zero if the image could not be loaded.
If #PB_Any was specified as the #Image parameter then the auto-generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
The limit for the image size that can be handled depends on the operating system and the available amount of memory.
If enough memory is available, then images up to at least 8192x8192 pixels are can be handled by all operating systems supported by PureBasic.

When an image is loaded, it is converted either in 24-bit (if the image depth
is less or equal to 24-bit) or in 32-bit (if the image has an alpha channel).
A loaded image can be freed by using the FreeImage() function.

The image can be in BMP, icon (.ico, only on Windows) or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library.
Alpha channel is supported for 32-bit BMP images.
The following functions can be used to enable automatically more image formats:

UseJPEGImageDecoder()

UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder()

UsePNGImageDecoder()

UseTIFFImageDecoder()

UseTGAImageDecoder()

UseGIFImageDecoder()

You can use the several other functions for acting with the loaded image:

StartDrawing() with ImageOutput() to draw on the loaded image

StartVectorDrawing() with ImageVectorOutput() to draw on the created image using vector drawing

CopyImage() to create another image from the actual one

GrabImage() to create another image from a given area of the actual one

DrawImage() with ImageID() to draw the image on actual output channel.

DrawAlphaImage() with ImageID() to draw the image (with alpha channel) on actual output channel.

ImageGadget() for displaying image on an application window

ButtonImageGadget() for creating an image button on an application window

commands.name: RemoveImageFrame
commands.description: Removes the specified frame from the image.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to remove a frame.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The index (starting from 0) of the frame to remove.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the frame has been successfully removed, zero otherwise.

commands.name: ResizeImage
commands.description: Resize the #Image to the given dimension.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to resize.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description:
The new dimensions of the image. Both width and height must be greater than zero.
#PB_Ignore can be specified for width or height, so this value won't be changed.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The resize method. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Image_Smooth: Resize the image with smoothing (default).
#PB_Image_Raw : Resize the image without any interpolation.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
commands.remarks:
This function changes the handle of the
used image. Therefore it must be newly assigned e.g. to an ImageGadget() with
SetGadgetState().

This function does not work with icon images (.ico) and with a multi-frame image.

The limit for the image size that can be handled depends on the operating system and the available amount of memory.
If enough memory is available, then images up to at least 8192x8192 pixels can be handled by all operating systems supported by PureBasic.

commands.name: SaveImage
syntax: Result = SaveImage(#Image, Filename$ [, ImagePlugin [, Flags [, Depth]]])
commands.description: Saves the specified image to disk.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to save.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The file to save to. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

parameters.name: ImagePlugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The format to save the image in. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_ImagePlugin_BMP : Save the image in BMP (default)
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG : Save the image in JPEG (UseJPEGImageEncoder() has to be used)
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000 : Save the image in JPEG2000 (UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder() has to be used)
#PB_ImagePlugin_PNG : Save the image in PNG (UsePNGImageEncoder() has to be used)

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
Optional parameters for the image plug-in. For now, only the quality setting is supported:
a number from 0 (worse quality) to 10 (maximum quality). Only the JPEG and JPEG 2000 plugins currently support it (default
quality is set to '7' if no flags are specified).

When an image is saved using palettized depth (1, 4 or 8), the following
flag is available:

#PB_Image_FloydSteinberg: Apply a Floyd-Steinberg dithering.

When a 32-bit image is saved in a lower depth (24-bit or lower) the following flags are available to change the color used
to fill the transparent area:

#PB_Image_WhiteAlphaBackground: the resulting image will use white color when transparent area is found (default)
#PB_Image_BlackAlphaBackground: the resulting image will use black color when transparent area is found

parameters.name: Depth (optional)
parameters.description:
The depth in which to save the image. Valid values are 1, 4, 8, 24 and 32.
The default value is the original image depth.
For now, only BMP and PNG encoders support palletized image format (1, 4 or 8-bit).

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the operation succeeded and zero if it failed.
commands.example:
UsePNGImageEncoder()
  
  If CreateImage(0, 33, 33)
    If StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Transparent)
        Box(0, 0, 33, 33, $FF0000) ; draw a blue box and save it as PNG image file below
      StopDrawing()
    EndIf
    file$ = SaveFileRequester("Select file to save", GetCurrentDirectory(), "*.png|*.png", 0)
    If file$
      If GetExtensionPart(file$) = ""
        file$ + ".png"  ; add the file extension if needed
      EndIf
      If SaveImage(0, file$, #PB_ImagePlugin_PNG)
        MessageRequester("File created", file$)
      Else
        MessageRequester("Error", "Failed to save file")
      EndIf
    EndIf
    FreeImage(0)
  EndIf

commands.name: SetImageFrame
commands.description:
Changes the current frame of the image. If the image is not multi-frame, this function has no effect.
ImageOutput(), ImageVectorOutput(), CopyImage() and GrabImage() works on the current frame.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to use.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The index (starting from 0) of the frame to set as current.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetImageFrameDelay
commands.description:
Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame. Each frame can have its own
delay.

parameters.name: #Image
parameters.description: The image to set the frame delay.

commands.returnValue: Sets the display delay (in milliseconds) for the current image frame.

commands.name: UseGIFImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the GIF image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(), CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions. Only LoadImage() and CatchImage()
support multi-frame GIF (it will result in a multi-frame image).
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All formats are supported, including the progressive and interlaced format.

commands.name: UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(),
CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The JPEG 2000 format makes use of destructive compression (lossy), what this means, is that the picture loses a certain amount of the
original information when that picture is compressed. This compression algorithm is actually one of the best available,
it will dramatically decrease the image size without the introduction of a lot of visible artifacts.

commands.name: UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder
commands.description: Enables the JPEG 2000 image support for the SaveImage() and SaveSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The JPEG 2000 format makes use of destructive compression (lossy), what this means, is that the picture loses a certain amount of the
original information when that picture is compressed. This compression algorithm is actually one of the best available,
it will dramatically decrease the image size without the introduction of a lot of visible artifacts. This encoder has the capability to
encode 32-bit images with alpha channel.

commands.name: UseJPEGImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(),
CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
All formats are supported, including
the progressive format. The JPEG format makes use of destructive compression (lossy), what this means, is that the picture
loses a certain amount of the original information when that picture is compressed. This compression algorithm is actually one of the best available,
it will dramatically decrease the image size without the introduction of a lot of visible artifacts.

commands.name: UseJPEGImageEncoder
commands.description: Enables the JPEG (Joint Picture Expert Group) image support for the SaveImage() and SaveSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The JPEG format makes use of destructive compression (lossy), what this means, is that the picture loses a certain amount of the
original information when that picture is compressed. This compression algorithm is actually one of the best available,
it will dramatically decrease the image size without the introduction of a lot of visible artifacts.

commands.name: UsePNGImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the PNG (Portable Network Graphic) image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(),
CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
All formats are supported, including
the progressive format. The PNG format is well known by web designers, as it is now one of the more
popular formats. The PNG format makes use of non-destructive compression (lossless) which means that the picture
does not lose any information when that picture is compressed. This is actually the best lossless compression
algorithm available.

commands.name: UsePNGImageEncoder
commands.description: Enables the PNG (Portable Network Graphic) image support for SaveImage() and SaveSprite().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The PNG format is well known by web designers, as it is now one of the more
popular formats. The PNG format makes use of non-destructive compression (lossless) which means that the picture
does not lose any information when that picture is compressed. This is actually the best lossless compression
algorithm available. This encoder has the capability to encode 32-bit images with alpha channel.

commands.name: UseTGAImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the TGA (Targa) image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(),
CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The TGA format makes use of
non-destructive compression (lossless) which means that the picture does not lose any information when it is compressed.
The TGA image size is usually large, since the compression is very weak (Run Length Encoding - RLE). At this point,
the TGA alpha channel information (if any) is ignored when using this format.

commands.name: UseTIFFImageDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the TIFF image support for the CatchImage(), LoadImage(),
CatchSprite() and LoadSprite() functions.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The TIFF format is very complex and
internally supports several sub-compression formats such as: JPEG, LZW, etc. All forms of the TIFF format are supported, using this format
will result in programs which are quite large.

commands.name: ConeTwistJoint
syntax: Result = ConeTwistJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2)
commands.description: Creates a new cone twist joint between the two given entities. Cone twist can be used to attach arm or legs to body, etc.

The number to identify the new joint. #PB_Any can

commands.name: GenericJoint
syntax: Result = GenericJoint(#Joint, EntityID, TransformX, TransformY, TransformZ, EntityID2, TransformX2, TransformY2, TransformZ2)

parameters.description: The entity id associated to the joint. To get a valid entity id, use EntityID().

parameters.description: The transformation to apply for the first entity.

parameters.name: EntityID2 (optional)
parameters.description:
The second entity associated to the joint. If this parameter isn't specified, a single

commands.returnValue:

#PB_Joint_EnableSpring: sets to #True to enable spring, #False to disable it (default)

#PB_Joint_Damping : sets the damping. Values should be between 0 and 1 (0 means a very strong damping).
#PB_Joint_Position : sets the position on the axis
#PB_Joint_NoLimit : free axis position
#PB_Joint_LowerLimit : lower limit
#PB_Joint_UpperLimit : upper limit
