parameters.name: ExtraValue
parameters.description: Extra value passed to the program parameter.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The automatic parameters correspond to the parameters of the 3D engine (positions of the camera, lights, color of the material, fog...)
this function allows to make the link between the 'uniform' variable of the shader and these parameters.
commands.example: MaterialShaderAutoParameter(#Material, #PB_Shader_Fragment, #PB_Shader_CameraPosition, "camerapos", 0)

commands.name: MaterialShaderParameter
syntax: MaterialShaderParameter(#Material, ProgramType, ParameterName$, ParameterType, v1.f, v2.f, v3.f, v4.f)
commands.description: Set specific parameters to the shader.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: ProgramType
parameters.description:
Program type. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Shader_Vertex : use the vertex program.
#PB_Shader_Fragment: use the fragment program.

parameters.name: ParameterName$
parameters.description: Name of the parameter with the GLSL program to set the new value.

parameters.name: ParameterType
parameters.description:
Parameter type. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Shader_Integer: the parameter use an integer type (v2, v3 and v4 parameters are ignored)
#PB_Shader_Float : the parameter use a float type (v2, v3 and v4 parameters are ignored)
#PB_Shader_Vector3: the parameter use a Vector3 type (v4 parameter is ignored)
#PB_Shader_Vector4: the parameter use a Vector4 type

parameters.name: v1
parameters.description: First parameter value. Mandatory for all parameter types.

parameters.name: v2
parameters.description: Second parameter value. Mandatory for #PB_Shader_Vector3 and #PB_Shader_Vector4 types.

parameters.name: v3
parameters.description: Third parameter value. Mandatory for #PB_Shader_Vector3 and #PB_Shader_Vector4 types.

parameters.name: v4
parameters.description: Fourth parameter value. Mandatory for #PB_Shader_Vector4 type.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
GLSL shaders uses vec4 type to pass a color. Example:

MaterialShaderParameter(0, #PB_Shader_Fragment, 4, Red(Color)/255, Green(Color)/255, Blue(Color)/255, Alpha(Color)/255)
MaterialShaderParameter(#Material, #PB_Shader_Fragment, "bumpy", #PB_Shader_Float, 0.5,0,0,0)

commands.name: MaterialShaderTexture
commands.description: Sets the textures to use for the shader based material previous created with CreateShaderMaterial().

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The shader material to use.

parameters.name: TextureID1
parameters.description: The first texture to use. Use TextureID() to get a valid TextureID, or #Null if not needed.

parameters.name: TextureID2
parameters.description: The second texture to use. Use TextureID() to get a valid TextureID, or #Null if not needed.

parameters.name: TextureID3
parameters.description: The third texture to use. Use TextureID() to get a valid TextureID, or #Null if not needed.

parameters.name: TextureID4
parameters.description: The fourth texture to use. Use TextureID() to get a valid TextureID, or #Null if not needed.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MaterialShadingMode
commands.description: Changes the #Material shading mode.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Material_Flat : The material uses the flat mode, the lighting is done face by face.
#PB_Material_Gouraud : Performs a shading using the Gouraud algorithm (default).
#PB_Material_Phong : Performs a shading using the Phong algorithm.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Material_Solid : The material will be rendered in solid, textured mode (default).
#PB_Material_Wireframe: The material will be rendered in wireframe mode.
#PB_Material_Point : The material will be rendered using only edge points.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To get the current material shading mode, use GetMaterialAttribute().

commands.name: MaterialShininess
commands.description: Changes the shininess of the #Material (the size of the specular highlights).

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: Shininess
parameters.description: The new shininess value.

parameters.name: SpecularColor (optional)
parameters.description: The specular color to use. A valid RGB color can be created with RGB().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To get the current shininess value, use GetMaterialAttribute().

commands.name: MaterialTextureAliases
commands.description:
Set textures for use in a material script. It allows to use the same material script with dynamic
textures. In the material script, the texture reference needs to be changed from 'texture mytexture.jpg'
to 'texture_alias texture1' (or 'texture_alias texture2', 'texture_alias texture3', 'texture_alias texture4').

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: TextureID1
parameters.description:
The TextureID() to use for the first texture alias (identified as 'texture_alias texture1' in the material script),
or zero if no texture is needed.

parameters.name: TextureID2
parameters.description:
The TextureID() to use for the second texture alias (identified as 'texture_alias texture2' in the material script),
or zero if no texture is needed.

parameters.name: TextureID3
parameters.description:
The TextureID() to use for the third texture alias (identified as 'texture_alias texture3' in the material script),
or zero if no texture is needed.

parameters.name: TextureID4
parameters.description:
The TextureID() to use for the fourth texture alias (identified as 'texture_alias texture4' in the material script),
or zero if no texture is needed.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ReloadMaterial
commands.description:
Reloads a material from an OGRE script based on its name. This is useful when using
customized materials stored in script files.

parameters.name: MaterialName$
parameters.description: The material name in scripts.

parameters.name: ScriptFilename$
parameters.description: The script filename.

parameters.name: ParseScript
parameters.description:
If set to #True the 'ScriptFilename$' is parsed again to get updated material information.
If set to #False, the material from when the script was parsed first will be used.
A material can be retrieved from OGRE scripts with GetScriptMaterial().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RemoveMaterialLayer
commands.description: Removes the top most (last added) material layer.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ResetMaterial
commands.description: Resets all materials for the specified object types.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Entity: resets materials for all entities.
#PB_ParticleEmitter: resets materials for all particle emitters.
#PB_BillboardGroup: resets materials for all billboards.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RotateMaterial
commands.description: Rotates the material layer according to the angle value.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: The rotation angle, in degree.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Material_Fixed : The material is rotated of the specified 'Angle', without regards of the previous rotate function.
#PB_Material_Animated: Each frame is the material is rotated of the specified 'Angle' automatically.

parameters.name: Layer (optional)
parameters.description: The layer to rotate. The first layer is zero (if this parameter is omitted, the layer zero is rotated).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To get the current rotate value, use GetMaterialAttribute().

commands.name: ScaleMaterial
commands.description: Scales the material. The parameters 'x' and 'y' are scale factors.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description:
The scale factors (the current material size is multiplied by these values):

- a value of 1.0 means that the size isn't changed

- a value between 0.0 and 1.0 means that the material is scaled down (ie: a scale of 0.5 will be half the size)

- a value above 1.0 means that the material is scaled up (ie: a scale of 2.0 will double the size)

parameters.name: Layer (optional)
parameters.description: The layer to scale. The first layer is zero (if this parameter is omitted, the layer zero is scaled).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To get the current scale values, use GetMaterialAttribute().

commands.name: ScrollMaterial
commands.description: Scrolls the material layer according to x,y values.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The texture scroll offset, in pixels.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Material_Fixed : The material is scrolled of the specified x,y offset, without regards of the previous scroll function.
#PB_Material_Animated: Each frame is the material is scrolled of the specified x,y offset automatically.

parameters.name: Layer (optional)
parameters.description: The layer to scroll. The first layer is zero (if this parameter is omitted, the layer zero is scrolled).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: To get the current scroll values, use GetMaterialAttribute().

commands.name: SetMaterialAttribute
commands.description: Sets the specified attribute value to the given material.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute to set. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Material_DepthCheck : Enables or disables the depth check for the material.
Value can be #True (depth check enabled) or #False (depth check disabled).
#PB_Material_DepthWrite : Enables or disables the depth write for the material.
Value can be #True (depth write enabled) or #False (depth write disabled).
#PB_Material_AlphaReject: Enables alpha reject on the texture (useful for semi transparent textures like
trees, window, etc).
#PB_Material_TAM : Changes the 'Texture Addressing Mode' (TAM). It can be one of the following values:
#PB_Material_WrapTAM : wrap mode
#PB_Material_MirrorTAM: mirror mode
#PB_Material_ClampTAM : clamp mode
#PB_Material_BorderTAM: border mode
#PB_Material_EnvironmentMap: Enables environment map. It can be one of the following values:
#PB_Material_NoMap : disable environment map
#PB_Material_PlanarMap : planar environment map
#PB_Material_CurvedMap : curved environment map
#PB_Material_ReflectionMap: reflection environment map
#PB_Material_NormalMap : normal environment map
#PB_Material_ProjectiveTexturing: Enable projective texturing for this material. The value is a #Camera number to use.
#PB_Material_PointSprite : Enables or disables point sprite for the material.
If greater than zero, the value is the point size / 1000. If zero, point size is disabled.
#PB_Material_DepthBias : Enables or disables the depth bias for the material.
If greater than zero, the value is the depth bias / 1000. If zero, depth bias is disabled.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Value of the attribute to set.

parameters.name: Layer (optional)
parameters.description: The layer to use. The first layer is zero (if this parameter is omitted, the layer zero is used).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetMaterialColor
commands.description: Set the specified material color.

parameters.name: #Material
parameters.description: The material to use.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The color type to set. It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Material_AmbientColor: the color used by default, without other lighting.
#PB_Material_DiffuseColor: the color the material will reflect when it will be dynamically lighted.
For example, using a full white color will result at normal lighting (all colors
are reflected). If you use a red, then only the red colors of the material will be
reflected, resulting as a full red material (or black one, if the material doesn't
contain any red color).
#PB_Material_SpecularColor: the color the material will reflect when it will be dynamically lighted by a light
which has a specular color value. For example, using a full white color will result at
normal lighting (all colors are reflected). If you use a red, then only the red colors
of the material will be reflected, resulting as a full red material (or black one, if
the material doesn't contain any red color).
#PB_Material_SelfIlluminationColor: the color the material will emit even if no light reaches it.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: The RGB color value to set. A valid RGB value can be created with RGB().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: Abs
commands.description: Returns the absolute value of the given float value.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description:
The number from which to get the absolute value.
This function will only work correctly with float numbers.
With integers, it will fail if the integer is too large (due to a loss of precision).

commands.returnValue: Returns the absolute value. The return-value is always positive.
commands.remarks: This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Debug Abs(3.14159)  ; Will display '3.14159'
  Debug Abs(-3.14159) ; will display '3.14159'

  pif.f = -3.14159
  pid.d = -3.14159
  Debug Abs(pif)  ; Returns a float number
  Debug Abs(pid)  ; Returns a double number

commands.name: ACos
commands.description: Returns the arc-cosine of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description:
The input value. It must be
between -1.0 and 1.0 (-1.0 and 1.0 included).

commands.returnValue:
Returns the resulting angle in radian. It can be transformed into degrees
using the Degree() function.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of Cos().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Debug ACos(1)  ; will display '0.0'
  Debug Acos(-1) ; will display 'pi' (approximately 3.14159...)

commands.name: ACosH
commands.description: Returns the area hyperbolic cosine of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description:
The input value. It must be
greater than or equal to 1.

commands.returnValue: Returns the hyperbolic angle.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of CosH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Debug ACosH(1)                 ; will display '0.0'
  Debug Exp(ACosH(0.5 * Sqr(5))) ; will display '1.618033...' (the golden ratio)

commands.name: ASin
commands.description: Returns the arc-sine of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description:
The input value. It must be between
-1.0 and 1.0 (-1.0 and 1.0 included).

commands.returnValue:
Returns the resulting angle in radian. It can be transformed into degrees
using the Degree() function.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of Sin().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Debug ASin(1) ; will display '1.570796...' (pi/2)
  Debug ASin(0) ; will display '0.0'

commands.name: ASinH
commands.description: Returns the area hyperbolic sine of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description: The input value. The range of Value.f(.d) is not limited.

commands.returnValue: Returns the hyperbolic angle.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of SinH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Debug ASinH(0)        ; will display '0.0'
  Debug Exp(ASinH(0.5)) ; will display '1.618033...' (the golden ratio)

commands.name: ATan
commands.description: Returns the arc-tangent of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description: The input value. Its range is not limited.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the resulting angle in radian. It can be transformed into degrees
using the Degree() function.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of Tan().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug ATan(1) ; will display '0.785398...' (pi/4)

commands.name: ATan2
commands.description:
Calculates the angle in radian between the x axis and a line drawn in the direction specified by 'x'
and 'y'. It can be used to calculate angles between lines in 2D or to transform rectangular coordinates
into polar coordinates.

parameters.name: x.f, y.f or x.d, y.d
parameters.description: The direction of the line to calculate the angle from. Zero values are allowed.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the resulting angle in radian. The result can be transformed into degrees
using the Degree() function.
commands.remarks:
This function calculates the value ATan(y/x) and examines the sign of x and y to place
the angle in the correct quadrant. It also handles the cases where y is zero to avoid division by zero
errors.

The result is always between -#PI and +#PI. Negative angles indicate that the
line is below the x axis, positive values indicate that line is above the x axis. If 'x' and 'y' are zero
then the function returns 0.0.

This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug ATan2(10, 10) ; will display #PI/4 (45 degrees in radian)

commands.name: ATanH
commands.description: Returns the area hyperbolic tangent of the specified value.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description:
The input value. It must be between
-1.0 and 1.0 (not including -1.0 and 1.0).

commands.returnValue: Returns the hyperbolic angle.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of TanH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Exp(ATanH(0.2 * Sqr(5))) ; will display '1.618033...' (the golden ratio)

commands.name: Cos
commands.description: Returns the cosine of the specified angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description:
The input angle in radians.
Use Radian() to convert an angle from degrees to radian.

commands.returnValue: Returns the cosine of the angle. The result is always between -1.0 and 1.0.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of Cos() is ACos().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Cos(3.141593)

commands.name: CosH
commands.description: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of the specified hyperbolic angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description: The input hyperbolic angle.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the hyperbolic cosine of the angle.
The result will be greater than or equal to 1.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of CosH() is ACosH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug CosH(0)  ; will display 1.0

commands.name: Degree
commands.description: Converts the given angle from radian to degree.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description: The input angle in radian.

commands.returnValue: Returns the angle in degrees.
commands.remarks:
There is no normalization to ensure that the resulting angle is between 0 and 360.
If the input was larger than #PI*2 then the result will be larger than 360.
Likewise, a negative input will result in a negative output.

The reverse transformation can be made with the Radian() function.
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Degree(#PI/4) ; will display 45.0

commands.name: Exp
commands.description: Returns the result of the exponential function. This is the value e raised to the power 'Number'.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The input for the exponential function.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value e raised to the power 'Number'.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of Log().
This function handles and returns float or double values.

commands.name: Infinity
commands.description:
Returns the special floating-point value representing positive infinity. Negative infinity can
be calculated using "-Infinity()".
commands.returnValue:
Returns the value representing infinity. The result is a float or double value depending on whether
it is assigned to a float or double variable.
commands.remarks:
Infinity and negative infinity are special values. They behave in calculations in the way you would
generally expect. For example dividing infinity by any positive number (except 0 or infinity) will result in
infinity again. The IsInfinity() function can be used to check if a value represents
positive or negative infinity.
commands.example: Debug IsInfinity(Infinity() / 1000) ; will display 1.0

commands.name: Int
commands.description: Returns the integer part of a float number.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The input value. This can be a float or double value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the integer part by cutting off the fractional part.
commands.remarks:
This function returns an integer value. To get a quad value,
use the IntQ() function.

The integer part is created by cutting off the fractional part of the value. There is no rounding.
To perform rounding, use the Round() function.
commands.example: Debug Int(10.565)  ; will display '10'

commands.name: IntQ
commands.description: Returns the integer part of a float number as a quad.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The input value. This can be a float or double value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the integer part by cutting off the fractional part.
commands.remarks:
This function returns a quad value. The Int() function has only the
range of an integer, but it may be faster to execute on 32-bit systems.

The integer part is created by cutting off the fractional part of the value. There is no rounding.
To perform rounding, use the Round() function.

commands.name: IsInfinity
commands.description: Returns nonzero if the given value represents positive or negative infinity.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description: The value to check for infinity.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the input value represents positive or negative infinity and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
Checking for the infinity values should not be done using normal comparison, because it depends
on the hardware implementation whether infinity is considered equal to itself or not. The value
of positive infinity can be generated with the Infinity() function.

This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Result = IsInfinity(Infinity())  ; infinity
  Result = IsInfinity(Log(0))      ; -infinity
  Result = IsInfinity(1234.5)      ; a finite number
  Result = IsInfinity(NaN())       ; NaN is not the same as infinity

commands.name: IsNaN
commands.description:
Returns nonzero if the given value 'Not a Number'. This value is the result of some invalid
calculations. It can also be generated using the NaN() function.

parameters.name: Value.f or Value.d
parameters.description: The value to check for NaN.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the input value is not a number and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
NaN is a special value. Testing for it should not be done using normal comparisons because
there are actually many different values for NaN and whether or not NaN is considered equal
with itself in comparisons depends on the hardware.

This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example:
Result = IsNaN(NaN())       ; NaN
  Result = IsNaN(Sqr(-1))     ; NaN
  Result = IsNaN(1234.5)      ; a normal number
  Result = IsNaN(Infinity())  ; infinity is not NaN

commands.name: Log
commands.description: Returns the natural Log (ie log to the base e) of the given number.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The number to calculate the Log from. This must be a positive value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the natural Log of the number.
commands.remarks:
This is the inverse function of Exp().
This function handles and returns float or double values.

commands.name: Log10
commands.description: Returns the log in base 10 of the given number.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The number to calculate the log from. This must be a positive value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the log in base 10.
commands.remarks: This function handles and returns float or double values.

commands.name: Mod
commands.description: Returns the remainder of the division of Number.f(.d) by Divisor.f(.d).

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The number to divide. The input does not need to be a whole number.

parameters.name: Divisor.f or Divisor.d
parameters.description: The number by which to divide. The input does not need to be a whole number.

commands.returnValue: Returns the remainder of the division. The result has the same sign as the Number.f(.d) parameter.
commands.remarks:
This is the floating-point version of the '%' operator for integers.
This function handles and returns float or double values.

commands.name: NaN
commands.description:
Returns the special floating-point value representing 'Not a Number'. This value is returned from
invalid calculations such as calculating the square root of a negative number.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the value representing NaN. The result is a float or double value depending on whether
it is assigned to a float or double variable.
commands.remarks:
NaN is a special value. Using NaN in any calculation with other values will again return the value NaN.
The IsNaN() function can be used to check whether a variable represents the value NaN.
commands.example: Debug IsNaN(NaN() * 5 + 2) ; will display 1.0

commands.name: Pow
commands.description: Returns the given number, raised to the given power.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The mantissa.

parameters.name: Power.f(.d)
parameters.description: The exponent. If 'Number.f(.d)' is negative, the exponent must be a whole number.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of 'Number' raised to the power 'Power'.
commands.remarks:
This function handles and returns float or double values.

The symbol '^' itself is not a supported operator. This is what the Pow() function is available for.
commands.example:
Debug Pow(2.0, 3.0)    ; will display '8.0'
  Debug Pow(27.0, 1/3.0) ; will display '3.0', the cubic-root

commands.name: Radian
commands.description: Converts the given angle from degrees into radian.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description: The input angle in degree.

commands.returnValue: Returns the angle in radian.
commands.remarks:
There is no normalization to ensure that the resulting angle is between 0 and #PI*2.
If the input was larger than 360 then the result will be larger than #PI*2.
Likewise, a negative input will result in a negative output.

The reverse transformation can be made with the Degree() function.
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Radian(90) ; will display #PI/2

commands.name: Random
commands.description: Returns a random number from zero to the given maximum value (both values included).

parameters.name: Maximum
parameters.description:
The maximum value. This value needs to be positive (zero included) and
may not exceed the maximum positive integer value.

parameters.name: Minimum (optional)
parameters.description:
The minimum value. It may not exceed the maximum value. If specified, the random
number will be from the minimum value to the maximum value (both values included).
This value needs to be positive (zero included) and may not exceed the maximum positive integer value.

commands.returnValue: Returns a value from zero to the maximum value (both values included), unless a minimum value is specified.
commands.remarks:
Additionally RandomSeed() may be used to change the random number seed.
RandomData() can be used to fill a memory buffer with random data.
RandomizeArray() or RandomizeList() can be used, to randomize the elements of an array
or a list.

Note: This command uses a pseudorandom number generator which is very fast and produces
randomly looking output but it is not strong enough for cryptographic purposes.
The slower CryptRandom() command can be used if more secure random
number generation is required.
commands.example:
Repeat
    Dice = Random(6, 1)  ; get a value between 1 and 6, including 1 and 6
    Choice = MessageRequester("Roll the dice", "You got a " + Dice + ", roll again?", #PB_MessageRequester_YesNo)
  Until Choice = #PB_MessageRequester_No

commands.name: RandomData
commands.description: Fills the specified memory buffer with random data.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory address of the buffer to fill.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The size of the buffer to fill.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command uses the same random seed as the
Random() command. RandomSeed() may be used to change the random number seed.

Note: This command uses a pseudorandom number generator which is very fast and produces
randomly looking output but it is not strong enough for cryptographic purposes.
The slower CryptRandomData() command can be used if more secure
random number generation is required.
commands.example:
; Create an image with random content
  ;
  CreateImage(0, 200, 200)
  If StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
    *Buffer = DrawingBuffer()
    Pitch   = DrawingBufferPitch()

    RandomData(*Buffer, Pitch*200)

    StopDrawing()
  EndIf

  OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, "Random Image", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  ImageGadget(0, 0, 0, 200, 200, ImageID(0))

  Repeat
  Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow

commands.name: RandomSeed
commands.description: Changes the random number seed for the values returned with Random() and RandomData().

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The new seed for the random number generator.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Each time a program is started, a new seed is generated, therefore RandomSeed()
is useful only when the goal is to generate the same random numbers in the same order every time the program
is executed.

commands.name: Round
commands.description: Round the specified float number according to the given mode.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The number to round.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The rounding mode. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Round_Down : rounds down the number
#PB_Round_Up : rounds up the number
#PB_Round_Nearest: rounds to the nearest integer number (0.5 and up will round up)

commands.remarks:
To turn a floating-point number into an integer without rounding, use Int() or IntQ().
This function handles and returns float or double values.

To format a number only for the output (display a rounded decimal number) you can FormatNumber().
commands.example:
Debug Round(11.6, #PB_Round_Down)    ; Will print '11.0'
  Debug Round(-3.6, #PB_Round_Down)    ; Will print '-4.0'

  Debug Round(11.6, #PB_Round_Up)      ; Will print '12.0'
  Debug Round(-1.6, #PB_Round_Up)      ; Will print '-1.0'

  Debug Round(11.6, #PB_Round_Nearest) ; Will print '12.0'
  Debug Round(11.4, #PB_Round_Nearest) ; Will print '11.0'
  Debug Round(11.5, #PB_Round_Nearest) ; Will print '12.0'
  Debug Round(-7.5, #PB_Round_Nearest) ; Will print '-8.0'

commands.name: Sign
commands.description: Returns an integer value representing the sign of the given number.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The number to get the sign from.

commands.returnValue:
- Returns 0 if Number is zero.

- Returns 1 if Number is positive.

- Returns -1 if Number is negative.
commands.remarks:
This function handles float or double values but
returns an integer.
commands.example:
Debug Sign(-7)   ; will display -1
  Debug Sign(0)    ; will display  0
  Debug Sign(7)    ; will display  1

commands.name: Sin
commands.description: Returns the sine of the specified angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description:
The input angle in radian.
The Radian() function can be used to transform an angle from degrees to radian.

commands.returnValue: Returns the sine of the angle. The result will be between -1.0 and 1.0.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of Sin() is ASin().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Sin(1.5708)

commands.name: SinH
commands.description: Returns the hyperbolic sine of the specified hyperbolic angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description: The input angle.

commands.returnValue: Returns the hyperbolic sine of the angle.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of SinH() is ASinH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug SinH(Log(1.618033)) ; Will be approximately 0.5

commands.name: Sqr
commands.description: Returns the square root of the specified number.

parameters.name: Number.f or Number.d
parameters.description: The input number. This must be a positive value.

commands.returnValue: Returns the square root of the number.
commands.remarks: This function handles and returns float or double values.

commands.name: Tan
commands.description: Returns the tangent of the specified angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description:
The input angle in radian.
The Radian() function can be used to transform an angle from degrees to radian.

commands.returnValue: Returns the tangent of the specified angle.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of Tan() is ATan().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug Tan(0.785398) ; will be approximately '1.0'

commands.name: TanH
commands.description: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the specified hyperbolic angle.

parameters.name: Angle.f or Angle.d
parameters.description: The input angle.

commands.returnValue: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the angle.
commands.remarks:
The inverse function of TanH() is ATanH().
This function handles and returns float or double values.
commands.example: Debug TanH(Log(1.618033)) ; will display '0.447213...' (1/5 * Sqr(5))

commands.name: AllocateMemory
commands.description:
Allocates a contiguous memory area with the specified size in bytes.
The new memory area will be cleared and filled with zeros.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size in bytes for the new memory area.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Memory_NoClear: don't fill the new memory area with zeros. It can help to have faster allocation if the
allocated memory is used immediately.

commands.returnValue: Returns the address of the allocated memory, or zero if the memory cannot be allocated.
commands.remarks:
FreeMemory() can be used to return the allocated memory back to the system.
ReAllocateMemory() can be used to change the size of the allocated area.
All the allocated memory areas are automatically freed when the programs ends.

If the program crashes at this command, it is usually a result of a memory corruption at
an earlier time in the program by writing at an area outside of the allocated memory area.
Such an error can be narrowed down to the real cause using the
purifier debugger tool.
commands.example:
*MemoryID = AllocateMemory(5000)
  If *MemoryID
    Debug "Starting address of the 5000 Byte memory area:"
    Debug *MemoryID
    PokeS(*MemoryID, "Store this string in the memory area")
    FreeMemory(*MemoryID)  ; will also be done automatically at the end of program
  Else
    Debug "Couldn't allocate the requested memory!"
  EndIf

commands.name: AllocateStructure
commands.description:
Allocates a new dynamic structure item. This dynamic structure item is properly initialized
and ready to use, without the need to call InitializeStructure().
To access the structure data, a pointer associated with the specified 'StructureName' has to be used.

parameters.name: StructureName
parameters.description:
The name of the structure used to create the new dynamic item. The structure has to be already
created.

commands.returnValue: The address of the new dynamic structure item, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This command is for advanced users and shouldn't be needed for most programs. It's often a better choice
to use a structured array, list or map to store dynamic structured items.

FreeStructure() can be used to free the dynamic structure item.
All dynamic structures are automatically freed when the programs ends.

If the program crashes at this command, it is usually a result of a memory corruption at
an earlier time in the program by writing at an area outside of the allocated memory area.
Such an error can be narrowed down to the real cause using the
purifier debugger tool.
commands.example:
Structure People
    Name$
    List Friends$()
  EndStructure

  *DynamicPeople.People = AllocateStructure(People)
  *DynamicPeople\Name$ = "Fred"
  AddElement(*DynamicPeople\Friends$())
  *DynamicPeople\Friends$() = "Stef"

  Debug *DynamicPeople\Name$
  Debug *DynamicPeople\Friends$()

  FreeStructure(*DynamicPeople)

commands.name: CompareMemory
commands.description: Compares the content of two memory areas.

parameters.name: *MemoryID1, *MemoryID2
parameters.description: The addresses of the two memory areas to compare.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The amount of bytes to compare.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the two areas contain the same bytes or zero if the content does not match.

commands.name: CompareMemoryString
commands.description: Compare two strings at the specified memory addresses.

parameters.name: *String1, *String2
parameters.description: The addresses of the strings to compare.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
Character comparison mode. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_String_CaseSensitive : Case sensitive search (a=a). (default)
#PB_String_NoCase : Case insensitive search using all unicode character set (Ã¤=Ã„).
#PB_String_NoCaseAscii : Case insensitive search using only ascii character set (a=A).
Much faster than #PB_String_NoCase when full unicode support is not required.

parameters.name: Length (optional)
parameters.description:
The number of characters to compare. If this parameter is not specified or has the value -1,
the strings are compared until a null-character is reached. If the strings are not null-terminated,
this parameter must be specified.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when comparing the strings. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Compares the strings as ascii
#PB_UTF8 : Compares the strings as UTF8
#PB_Unicode: Compares the strings as unicode (default)

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_String_Equal : if String1 equals String2
#PB_String_Lower : if String1 is lower than String2
#PB_String_Greater: if String1 greater than String2

commands.name: CopyMemory
commands.description: Copy a memory area starting from the *SourceMemoryID to the *DestinationMemoryID.

parameters.name: *SourceMemoryID
parameters.description: The address where the bytes are copied from.

parameters.name: *DestinationMemoryID
parameters.description: The address where the bytes are copied to.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The amount of bytes to copy.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The source and destination buffers may not overlap. To copy memory to a destination
address that overlaps with the source buffer, use MoveMemory().

commands.name: CopyMemoryString
commands.description:
Copy the string from the specified address to the destination memory address if specified,
or at the end of the previous buffer if omitted.

parameters.name: *String
parameters.description:
The address of the string to copy. The string must be terminated with a null-character.
The string is expected to be in the PB string format.

parameters.name: @*DestinationMemoryID (optional)
parameters.description:
The pointer to a variable holding the address with the destination buffer. After the string
has been copied, the variable *DestinationMemoryID will point to the null-character at the end of the
copied string, so a further call to this function will append the new string to the previous one.

If this parameter is omitted, the address from the previous call is used.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of *DestinationMemoryID after the string was copied.
commands.example:
*Buffer = AllocateMemory(1000)
  *Pointer = *Buffer
  CopyMemoryString("Hello", @*Pointer)
  CopyMemoryString(" World")  ; This one will be put just after "Hello"
  *Pointer-4                  ; Come back from 2 characters unicode (on the 'l' of 'World')
  CopyMemoryString("LD")      ; Finally the last two letters will be uppercase
  Debug PeekS(*Buffer)

commands.name: FillMemory
commands.description: Fills the memory area with the specified value by repeatedly writing that value.

parameters.name: *Memory
parameters.description: The address of the memory area to fill.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size in bytes of the memory area to fill.

parameters.name: Value (optional)
parameters.description: The value to write into the memory area. The default is the value 0.

parameters.name: Type (optional)
parameters.description:
The type for the value. This can be one of the following constants:

#PB_Byte : Fills the memory using a byte (1 byte) value (default).
#PB_Ascii : Fills the memory using a byte (1 byte) value.
#PB_Word : Fills the memory using a word (2 bytes) value.
#PB_Unicode : Fills the memory using a word (2 bytes) value.
#PB_Character: Fills the memory using a character (2 bytes in unicode).
#PB_Long : Fills the memory using a long (4 bytes) value.
#PB_Integer : Fills the memory using an integer value (4 bytes in 32-bit executable, 8 bytes in 64-bit executable).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
*Buffer = AllocateMemory(500)

  FillMemory(*Buffer, 500) ; Fill 500 bytes of value 0 (clear the memory area)
  FillMemory(*Buffer, 500, $FF) ; Fill 500 bytes of value $FF
  FillMemory(*Buffer, 500, $BADF00D, #PB_Long) ; Fill 500 bytes of value $BADF00D

commands.name: FreeMemory
commands.description: Free the memory previously allocated with AllocateMemory(), ReAllocateMemory(), Ascii() or UTF8().

parameters.name: *MemoryID
parameters.description:
The address of the memory area to free. This must be a value returned from
either AllocateMemory() or ReAllocateMemory() or Ascii() or UTF8().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
If the program crashes at this command even though the input seems correct,
it is usually a result of a memory corruption at an earlier time in the program by writing
at an area outside of the allocated memory area.
Such an error can be narrowed down to the real cause using the
purifier debugger tool.

All remaining allocated memory blocks are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: FreeStructure
commands.description:
Free the dynamic structure item previously allocated with AllocateStructure(). There is no
need to call ClearStructure() before freeing the
structure.

parameters.name: *Item
parameters.description:
The address of the dynamic structure item to free. This must be a value returned from
AllocateStructure().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
If the program crashes at this command even though the input seems correct,
it is usually a result of a memory corruption at an earlier time in the program by writing
at an area outside of the allocated memory area.
Such an error can be narrowed down to the real cause using the
purifier debugger tool.

All remaining allocated dynamic structure items are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: MemorySize
commands.description: Returns the length of the given memory area.

parameters.name: *MemoryID
parameters.description:
The address of the memory area to get the size from. This must be a value returned from
either AllocateMemory() or ReAllocateMemory() or Ascii() or UTF8().

commands.returnValue: Returns the size of the given memory area in bytes.

commands.name: MemoryStringLength
commands.description: Returns the length (in characters) of the given zero terminated string.

parameters.name: *String
parameters.description: The address of the string to get the length from.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Reads the strings as ascii.
#PB_UTF8 : Reads the strings as UTF8
#PB_Unicode: Reads the strings as unicode (by default, see unicode mode).

Combined with one of the following value:

#PB_ByteLength: only valid when using the #PB_UTF8 flag, the result will represent bytes (not characters).
It can be useful as UTF8 has variable character lengths.

commands.returnValue: Returns the length of the string in characters.

commands.name: MoveMemory
commands.description:
Copy a memory area starting from the *SourceMemoryID to the *DestinationMemoryID.
Overlapping of the two memory areas is allowed.

parameters.name: *SourceMemoryID
parameters.description: The address where the bytes are copied from.

parameters.name: *DestinationMemoryID
parameters.description: The address where the bytes are copied to.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The amount of bytes to copy.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This command can be slower than CopyMemory(), but it ensures that the bytes are copied correctly,
even if the two memory areas overlap.

commands.name: PeekA
commands.description: Reads an ascii character (1 byte) from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the ascii character.

commands.name: PeekB
commands.description: Reads a byte (1 byte) number from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the byte.

commands.name: PeekC
commands.description:
Reads a character (2 bytes in unicode) number from
the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the character.

commands.name: PeekD
commands.description: Reads a double (8 bytes) number from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the double.

commands.name: PeekF
commands.description: Reads a float (4 bytes) from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the float.

commands.name: PeekI
commands.description: Reads an integer (4 bytes in 32-bit executable, 8 bytes in 64-bit executable) number from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the integer.

commands.name: PeekL
commands.description: Reads a long (4 bytes) number from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the long.

commands.name: PeekQ
commands.description: Reads a quad (8 bytes) number from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the quad.

commands.name: PeekS
commands.description: Reads a string from the specified memory address.

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address to read from.

parameters.name: Length (optional)
parameters.description:
The maximum number of characters to read. If this parameter is not specified or -1 is used then
there is no maximum.
The string is read until a terminating null-character is encountered or the maximum length is reached.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when reading the string. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Reads the strings as ascii.
#PB_UTF8 : Reads the strings as UTF8
#PB_Unicode: Reads the strings as unicode (default).

Combined with one of the following value:

#PB_ByteLength: only valid when using the #PB_UTF8 flag, the 'Length' will represent bytes (not characters).
It can be useful as UTF8 has variable character lengths.

commands.name: ReAllocateMemory
commands.description:
Resizes the given memory buffer to a new size. The memory may be copied to a new location in the
process if there is not enough memory available at its current location.

parameters.name: *MemoryID
parameters.description:
The address of the memory area to resize. This value must be the result of a call to
AllocateMemory() or ReAllocateMemory().

If this parameter is #Null, the command acts like AllocateMemory() and allocates
a new memory area of the given size.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size in bytes for the resized or allocated buffer.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Memory_NoClear: don't fill the extended memory area with zeros. It can help to have faster allocation if the
extended memory is used immediately. If the memory size is reduced, this flag has no effect.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the new address of the memory area if it could be resized. In this case, the old '*MemoryID' address can
no longer be used. If resizing the memory area failed (because there is not enough memory available), the result
is zero, and the '*MemoryID' address is still valid with the existing memory area and the old size.
commands.remarks:
If the size of the memory area is increased, any new bytes are initially filled with zeros unless the #PB_Memory_NoClear flag is specified.

If the program crashes at this command even though the input seems correct,
it is usually a result of a memory corruption at an earlier time in the program by writing
at an area outside of the allocated memory area.
Such an error can be narrowed down to the real cause using the
purifier debugger tool.

All remaining allocated memory blocks are automatically freed when the program ends.
commands.example:
*MemoryID = AllocateMemory(1000)
  PokeS(*MemoryID, "Store this string")
  ; do something more with it here...
  ;
  *NewMemoryID = ReAllocateMemory(*MemoryID, 2000) ; need more memory
  If *NewMemoryID
    ; work with *NewMemoryID now with size 2000
    Debug "The old contents are still here:"
    Debug PeekS(*NewMemoryID)
    ;
    FreeMemory(*NewMemoryID)
  Else
    ; resizing failed, keep working with *MemoryID (size 1000)
    ;
    FreeMemory(*MemoryID)
  EndIf

commands.name: BindMenuEvent
commands.description:
Bind a menu event to a callback. It's an additional way to handle events in PureBasic,
which works without problem with the regulars WindowEvent() / WaitWindowEvent()
commands. A menu event can be unbound with UnbindMenuEvent().

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to bind the event to.

parameters.name: MenuItem
parameters.description: The menu item within the menu to bind the event to.

parameters.name: @Callback()
parameters.description:
The callback procedure to call when the event occurs. It has to be declared like this:

Procedure EventHandler()
; Code
EndProcedure

Regular functions like EventGadget(), EventWindow(), EventMenu(), EventType() and EventData() are
available within the callback to get more information about the event.

Note: WindowEvent() and WaitWindowEvent() should never be called from inside the callback
or the program can be locked or have wrong behavior.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Procedure TestHandler()
    Debug "Test menu event"
  EndProcedure

  Procedure QuitHandler()
    Debug "Quit menu event"
    End
  EndProcedure

  OpenWindow(0, 100, 100, 200, 50, "Click test", #PB_Window_SystemMenu)

  CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
    MenuTitle("File")
      MenuItem(0, "Test")
      MenuItem(1, "Quit")

  BindMenuEvent(0, 0, @TestHandler())
  BindMenuEvent(0, 1, @QuitHandler())

  Repeat
    Event = WaitWindowEvent()
  Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow

commands.name: CloseSubMenu
commands.description: Close the current sub menu and return to the enclosing menu after a previous call to OpenSubMenu().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: For an example and a preview image see OpenSubMenu().

commands.name: CreateImageMenu
commands.description: Creates a new empty menu on the given window with support for images in the menu items.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new menu.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description: The window for the new menu. It can be obtained using the WindowID() function.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Menu_NativeImageSize: Uses the native size of images when rendering menu items (Windows only).

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the menu was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Menu parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
Once created, this menu becomes the current menu for further item additions. It's now
possible to use functions such as MenuTitle(), MenuItem(), MenuBar(), OpenSubMenu() to populate the menu.

To handle menu events properly, see the description of following functions:

WaitWindowEvent() (alternatively WindowEvent())

EventWindow()

EventMenu()
commands.example:
UsePNGImageDecoder()

  If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "Image menu Example")
    If CreateImageMenu(0, WindowID(0))    ; menu creation starts....
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open"   +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+O", LoadImage(0, #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/ToolBar/Open.png"))
        MenuItem(2, "Save"   +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+S", LoadImage(1, #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/ToolBar/Save.png"))
        MenuBar()
        MenuItem(3, "Quit"  +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+Q")
    EndIf
  
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CreateMenu
commands.description: Creates a new empty menu on the given window.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new menu.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description: The window for the new menu. It can be obtained using the WindowID() function.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the menu was created successfully, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Menu parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
To create a menu with support for images, use CreateImageMenu().

Once created, this menu becomes the current menu for further item additions. It's now
possible to use functions such as MenuTitle(), MenuItem(), MenuBar(), OpenSubMenu() to populate the menu.

To handle menu events properly, see the description of following functions:

WaitWindowEvent() (alternatively WindowEvent())

EventWindow()

EventMenu()
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "Menu Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))    ; menu creation starts....
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open"   +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+O")
        MenuItem(2, "Save"   +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+S")
        MenuItem(3, "Save as"+Chr(9)+"Ctrl+A")
        MenuItem(4, "Close"  +Chr(9)+"Ctrl+C")
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent()=#PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: CreatePopupImageMenu
commands.description: Creates a new empty popup menu with image support for its items.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new menu.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Menu_NativeImageSize: Uses the native size of images when rendering menu items (Windows only).

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the menu was created successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Menu parameter, then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
Once created, this menu becomes the current menu for further item additions. It's now
possible to use functions such as MenuTitle(), MenuItem(), MenuBar(), OpenSubMenu() to populate the menu.

DisplayPopupMenu() can be used to display this popup menu at any position on the screen.

To handle menu events properly, see the description of following functions:

WaitWindowEvent() (alternatively WindowEvent())

EventWindow()

EventMenu()
commands.example:
UsePNGImageDecoder()

  If CreateImage(0,16,16,32)
    StartDrawing(ImageOutput(0))
    Box(0,0,15,15,RGB(255,255,128))
    DrawRotatedText(-5,3, "+", 45, RGB(255,0,128))
    StopDrawing()
  EndIf

  OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 120, "Image Popup-Menu Example")

  If LoadImage(1,#PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/ToolBar/Open.png")  ; load an icon
    If CreatePopupImageMenu(0)      ; creation of the pop-up menu begins...
      MenuItem(1, "Open", ImageID(1))      ; Display the icon
      MenuItem(2, "Save")      ; just like in a normal menu...
      MenuItem(3, "Save as")
      MenuItem(4, "Quit", ImageID(0)) ; Display our own icon
      MenuBar()
      OpenSubMenu("Recent files")
        MenuItem(5, "PureBasic.exe")
        MenuItem(6, "Test.txt")
      CloseSubMenu()
    EndIf

    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()     ; check for window events

      Select Event
        Case #PB_Event_RightClick  ; right mouse button was clicked =>
          DisplayPopupMenu(0, WindowID(0))  ; now display the popup-menu

        Case #PB_Event_Menu        ; an item of the popup-menu was clicked
          Select EventMenu()       ; get the clicked menu item...
            Case 1 : Debug "Menu: Open"
            Case 2 : Debug "Menu: Save"
            Case 3 : Debug "Menu: Save as"
            Case 4 : End
            Case 5 : Debug "Menu: PureBasic.exe"
            Case 6 : Debug "Menu: Text.txt"
          EndSelect

      EndSelect
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: DisableMenuItem

commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "DisableMenuItem Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open")
        MenuItem(2, "Save")

    EndIf

commands.name: DisplayPopupMenu
commands.description: Displays a PopupMenu under the current mouse position or at the given screen location.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description:
The menu to display. It must have been created with CreatePopupMenu() or
CreatePopupImageMenu().

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description:
The window with which to associate the popup menu. This value can be obtained with
the WindowID() function.

parameters.name: x, y (optional)
parameters.description:
The location at which the menu should be displayed in screen coordinates. These are
coordinates in pixels relative to the upper-left corner of the primary monitor.

If this parameter is not specified, the menu is displayed at the current mouse position.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The popup menu will be hidden again when the user selects an item or clicks somewhere outside of
the area of the popup menu.

For an example and a preview image see the CreatePopupMenu() help.

commands.name: FreeMenu
commands.description: Frees the specified menu and all its resources.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining menus are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining menus are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetMenuItemState
commands.description: Returns the checkbox state of a menu item.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to use.

parameters.name: MenuItem
parameters.description: The menu item number to get the state of.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the menu item is checked and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: Use SetMenuItemState() to change the state of a menu item.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "GetMenuItemState Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Changed")
        SetMenuItemState(0, 1, 1)        ; set check mark for the previously created menu item
    EndIf
    Repeat
      Event = WaitWindowEvent()          ; wait for an event
      If Event = #PB_Event_Menu          ; a menu event appeared
        If EventMenu() = 1               ; first menu item was clicked
          If GetMenuItemState(0, 1) = 1  ; actual item state = check marked
            SetMenuItemState(0, 1, 0)    ; now remove the check mark
          Else                           ; actual item state = no check mark
            SetMenuItemState(0, 1, 1)    ; now set the check mark
          EndIf
        EndIf
      EndIf
    Until Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: GetMenuItemText
commands.description: Returns the text from the specified menu item.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to use.

parameters.name: Item
parameters.description: The item to get the text from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the menu item text.
commands.example:
Enumeration ; Menu items
    #New
    #Open
    #Last
  EndEnumeration
  
  ; Set multiple menu items and get their text later...
  If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 300, 100, "GetMenuItemText Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("File")
      MenuItem(#New, "New")
      MenuItem(#Open, "Open")
      For i = #Last To 10
        MenuItem(i, "Item" + Str(i))
      Next
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Select WaitWindowEvent()
        Case #PB_Event_Menu
          em = EventMenu()
          Select em
            Case #New
              Debug "pressed: " + GetMenuItemText(0, #New)
            Case #Open
              Debug "pressed: " + GetMenuItemText(0, #Open)
            Case #Last To 10
              Debug "pressed: " + GetMenuItemText(0, em)
          EndSelect
        Case #PB_Event_CloseWindow
          Break
      EndSelect
    ForEver
  EndIf

commands.name: GetMenuTitleText
commands.description: Returns the title text of the specified menu title item.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to use.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The index of the menu title item to read the title from.

commands.returnValue: Returns the text of the menu title item.

commands.name: HideMenu
commands.description: Hide or show the specified menu.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to hide or show.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
The new state for the menu. A value of 1 hides the menu and
a value of 0 shows it.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 300, 100, "HideMenu Example")
    ButtonGadget(0, 70, 10, 150, 30, "Hide/Show menu")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")
      MenuItem(1, "New")
      MenuItem(2, "Open")
    EndIf
    
    Repeat
      Select WaitWindowEvent()
        Case #PB_Event_Gadget
          Select EventGadget()
            Case 0
              ; Set the toggle status (on/off) of the menu:
              Toggle = Bool(Not Toggle)
              HideMenu(0, Toggle)
              ; Adjusts the y-position of the button according to the presence of the menu:
              If Toggle
                ResizeGadget(0, #PB_Ignore, 10 + MenuHeight(), #PB_Ignore, #PB_Ignore)
              Else
                ResizeGadget(0, #PB_Ignore, 10, #PB_Ignore, #PB_Ignore)
              EndIf
          EndSelect
        Case #PB_Event_CloseWindow
          Break
      EndSelect
    ForEver
  EndIf

commands.name: IsMenu
commands.description: Tests if the given menu is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the menu is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a menu is ready to use.

commands.name: MenuBar
commands.description: Creates a separator bar in the current menu.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "MenuBar Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))  ; here the menu creating starts....
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open")
        MenuBar()                  ; here the separator bar will be inserted
        MenuItem(4, "Close")
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: MenuHeight
commands.description:
Returns the height of the menu title bar. This allows the correct height of a window to be
calculated when using a menu.
commands.returnValue: Returns the height in pixels of the menu bar.
commands.remarks:
Linux & macOS: This command will always returns 0, as the menu bar isn't part of the window (it is always located
on the main bar at the very top of the screen). Therefore, MenuHeight() can be used seamlessly on every OS to adjust the
window size depending on the actual menu height.
commands.example: An example for the use of MenuHeight() can be found at HideMenu().

commands.name: MenuID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the given menu.

parameters.name: #Menu
parameters.description: The menu to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the ID of the menu. This sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter
"Handles and Numbers" for more information.

commands.name: MenuItem
commands.description: Creates a new item on the current menu.

parameters.name: MenuItemID
parameters.description:
A number to identify this menu item in events and
commands like SetMenuItemState(). This value should be between 0 and 65535.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description:
The text for the menu item.
On Windows you can use the special '&' character to underline a specific
letter:

"&File" will actually display: File

parameters.name: ImageID (optional)
parameters.description:
The image to be displayed next to the menu item. The menu must be created with
CreateImageMenu() or CreatePopupImageMenu() for the image to be displayed. This value can be
obtained using the ImageID() function.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The dimensions of the images are 16x16 pixels.

To have a keyboard shortcut (will be activated with the
AddKeyboardShortcut() function, except on macOS) aligned to the right side of the menu
(for example, "Save Ctrl+S") use the tab character
to give the correct space. The tab character has an ASCII code of 9 so use the function Chr() with the
number 9 to insert a tab character.
The code may look something like this:

MenuItem(1, "&Open" + Chr(9) + "Ctrl+O")

The supported modifiers are:

- "Ctrl" : Control key
- "Shift" : Shift key
- "Alt" : Alt key
- "Cmd" : Command/Apple key (OS X only)

They can be mixed together with the "+" character: "Save As" + Chr(9) + "Ctrl+Shift+S". On OS X, when a shortcut is created
in the menu, there is no need to call the AddKeyboardShortcut() function with this shortcut.

macOS: the 'Quit', 'Preferences' and 'About' items are considered as specials and need to be placed in the 'Application' menu to have the
look'n'feel of macOS applications. PureBasic supports the #PB_Menu_Quit, #PB_Menu_Preferences
and #PB_Menu_About constants
(to be specified as the 'MenuItemID') for these kind of menu items. When one of these constants is detected, the item
isn't inserted in the current menu, but in the 'Application' menu. If a shortcut was specified, it is simply ignored and
replaced by the standard one. These 3 constants aren't defined on others OS, to allow flexible numbering on these OS.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "MenuItem Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open")    ; normal item
        MenuItem(2, "&Save")   ; item with underlined character, the underline will only
                               ; be displayed, if menu is called with F10 + arrow keys
        MenuItem(3, "Quit"+Chr(9)+"Esc")   ; item with separate shortcut text
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: MenuTitle
commands.description: Creates a new title item on the menu.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description:
The text to display in the title item.

On Windows you can use the special '&' character to underline a specific
letter, if the graphic theme allows it:

"&File" will actually display: File

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: MenuTitle() can't be used in popup menus, as there are no menu titles.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 200, 100, "MenuTitle Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")      ; normal menu title with following item
        MenuItem(1, "Open")
        MenuItem(2, "Close")
      MenuTitle("&Edit")        ; menu title with underlined character, the underline
                                ; will only be displayed, when called with F10 key
        MenuItem(3, "Undo")
        MenuItem(4, "Redo")
      MenuTitle("About")        ; only menu title
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: OpenSubMenu
commands.description: Creates an empty submenu in the current menu.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description:
The text for the submenu.

Windows:

In the Text$ argument, you can use the special '&' character to underline a specific letter:
"&File" will actually display: File

parameters.name: ImageID (optional)

if the current menu was created using the CreateImageMenu() or CreatePopupImageMenu() command.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
It is not possible to rename an OpenSubMenu easily except with Windows which returns a menu number.

Ex:

SubMenu = OpenSubMenu ("New")

SetMenuItemText (0, SubMenu, "Open")

With Linux and macOS you will have to juggle with several menus or destroy and recreate it.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 200, 200, 220, 100, "SubMenu Example")
    If CreateMenu(0, WindowID(0))
      MenuTitle("Project")
        MenuItem(1, "Open")
        MenuItem(2, "Close")
        MenuBar()
        OpenSubMenu("Recent files")       ; begin submenu
          MenuItem( 3, "C:\Autoexec.bat")
          MenuItem( 4, "D:\Test.txt")

  EndProcedure

  Procedure QuitHandler()

commands.name: AddMeshManualLOD
commands.description:
Add a new level of detail (LOD) to the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically
with #MeshLOD (which is often a simplified version of #Mesh, with less details) when
displayed above the specified distance from the camera. Several LOD mesh can be used for the same
#Mesh depending of the distance.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: MeshLOD
parameters.description: The mesh to use when the distance from the camera has been reached.

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: The minimum distance from the camera where the #MeshLOD should be used instead of #Mesh.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddSubMesh
commands.description:
Add a new submesh to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh(). A mesh can have any number of
submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position. Once a submesh is created, use the following
commands to build it: MeshVertexPosition(), MeshFace() and MeshIndex().

parameters.name: Type (optional)
parameters.description:
The type of the new submesh. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Mesh_TriangleList : the submesh will be composed of a list of triangles (default).
#PB_Mesh_TriangleStrip: the submesh will be composed of a list of connected triangles (vertices are shared).
#PB_Mesh_TriangleFan : the submesh will be composed of a list of triangles sharing the same central vertex point.
#PB_Mesh_PointList : the submesh will be composed of a list of points.
#PB_Mesh_LineList : the submesh will be composed of a list of lines.
#PB_Mesh_LineStrip : the submesh will be composed of a list of connected lines (vertices are shared).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BuildMeshLOD
commands.description:
Build automatically one or several level of detail (LOD) for the mesh. The #Mesh will be replaced automatically
with less complex mesh when displayed above the specified distance from the camera. If more precise LOD
meshes are required, AddMeshManualLOD() can be used.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: NbLOD (optional)
parameters.description: Number of needed LOD for this mesh. If this parameter isn't used, then the LODs will be automatically calculated.

parameters.name: Distance (optional)
parameters.description:
The minimum distance from the camera where the first LOD mesh will be used instead of #Mesh.
For the next LOD meshs, the distance will be calculated using this formula: 'Distance / SqrF(1-ReductionValue)'.

parameters.name: ReductionValue (optional)
parameters.description:
The reduction to apply, between 0 (no reduction) and 1 (100% reduction).

Example: CreateMeshLodLevels(#Mesh, 3, 100, 0.75)

- The first reduction of the original mesh starts from 100 units of the camera, vertices number halved by 4 (75% reduction).
- The second reduction of the original mesh starts from 200 units of the camera, vertices number halved by 16.
- The third reduction of the original mesh starts from 400 units of the camera, vertices number halved by 64.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BuildMeshShadowVolume
commands.description:
Create the shadow volume for the specified #Mesh. It is required if the mesh needs to cast a shadow. It should be
done once the mesh creation is completely done, or the shadow will not match the mesh.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to act on.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: BuildMeshTangents
commands.description:
Automatically computes the tangent vectors for all vertices of the specified mesh.
Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CopyMesh
commands.description:
Creates a #NewMesh which is the exact copy of the specified #Mesh.
If #PB_Any is used
as the '#NewMesh' parameter, then the new mesh number will be returned as 'Result'.
Dynamic meshes are not supported for copy (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

If the Result equals 0, then the mesh copy has failed.
If #NewMesh already exists, then it is freed and replaced by a new one.

commands.name: CreateDataMesh
commands.description:
Creates a new #Mesh from the specified 2 dimensional array of MeshVertex type. This command allows
faster mesh creation than using CreateMesh() by preparing an array and submitting in one batch to the command.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new mesh. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Array
parameters.description:
A 2 dimensional array of type MeshVertex, which will be used to create the new mesh. The MeshVertex structure is
defined as the following:

Structure MeshVertex
x.f
y.f
z.f
NormalX.f
NormalY.f
NormalZ.f
TangentX.f
TangentY.f
TangentZ.f
u.f
v.f
Color.l
EndStructure

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The way to link vertices. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Mesh_DiagonalRegular1 : diagonals are aligned in the same way
#PB_Mesh_DiagonalRegular2 : diagonals are aligned in the other way
#PB_Mesh_DiagonalAlternate : diagonals are once in a way and once in the other way (alternate)
#PB_Mesh_DiagonalShortestLength: diagonals are between the two closest vertices
#PB_Mesh_DiagonalClosestNormal : diagonals are between the two closest normals (scalar product). Best mode but requires normals.

commands.remarks: If the #Mesh was already created, then it is freed and replaced by a new one.
