commands.name: CreateTube
syntax: Result = CreateTube(#Mesh, OuterRadius.f, InnerRadius.f, Height.f [, NbBaseSegments, NbHeightSegments)
commands.description: Create a new tube mesh.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new mesh. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: OuterRadius
parameters.description: Outer radius, in world unit, of the tube.

parameters.name: InnerRadius
parameters.description: Inner radius, in world unit, of the tube.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: Height, in world unit, of the tube.

parameters.name: NbBaseSegments (optional)
parameters.description: Number of segments used for the base of the tube (default: 16).

parameters.name: NbHeightSegments (optional)
parameters.description: Number of segments used for the height of the tube (default: 1).

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the mesh was created successfully and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any was used as the #Mesh parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
commands.example:
InitEngine3D()
  InitSprite()

  OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 640, 480, "Tube example", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID(0), 0, 0, 640, 480, 0, 0, 0)

  ; Light
  CreateLight(#PB_Any, RGB(25, 25, 180), -5, 10, 5, #PB_Light_Point)

  ; Camera
  CreateCamera(0, 0, 0, 100, 100)
  MoveCamera(0, 2, 4, 3, #PB_Absolute | #PB_Local)
  CameraLookAt(0, 0, 0, 0)

  ; Create the tube and attach it to the scene
  CreateTube(0, 0.5, 0.4, 2)
  CreateEntity(0, MeshID(0), #PB_Material_None)

  Repeat
    RenderWorld()
    FlipBuffers()
  Until WaitWindowEvent(1) = #PB_Event_CloseWindow

commands.name: FinishMesh
commands.description: Finish the creation of the current mesh started with CreateMesh().

parameters.name: StaticMesh
parameters.description:
If set to #True, the mesh will be converted to a static mesh and will be not modifiable anymore.
If set to #False, the mesh will still be modifiable with UpdateMesh(). Static meshes are faster
to render than dynamic meshes.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeMesh
commands.description:
Free the specified #Mesh. All its associated memory is released and the object may not be used
anymore.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining meshes are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining meshes are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetMeshData
syntax: Result = GetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex)
commands.description: Get internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh
parameters.description: The submesh to get the data from. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

parameters.name: DataArray()
parameters.description:
The array to receive the data. It has to be an array of type "MeshVertex" or "MeshFace"
depending of the specified flags.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description:
Specifies which kind of data needs to be retrieved. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Mesh_Vertex: DataArray() is an array of type "MeshVertex".
#PB_Mesh_Face : DataArray() is an array of type "MeshFace".

combined with:

#PB_Mesh_UVCoordinate : Get the UV coordinate information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)
#PB_Mesh_Normal : Get the normal information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)
#PB_Mesh_Color : Get the color information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)
#PB_Mesh_Tangent : Get the tangent information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)

The "MeshVertex" and "MeshFace" structures are defined like this:

Structure MeshVertex
x.f
y.f
z.f
NormalX.f ; only used if #PB_Mesh_Normal flag is set
NormalY.f ;
NormalZ.f ;
TangentX.f
TangentY.f
TangentZ.f
u.f ; only used if #PB_Mesh_UVCoordinate flag is set
v.f ;
Color.l ; only used if #PB_Mesh_Color flag is set
EndStructure

Structure MeshFace
Index.l
EndStructure

parameters.name: FirstIndex, LastIndex
parameters.description: First and last index to get the data from.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure. If success, DataArray() has been resized and contains the mesh information.

commands.name: IsMesh
commands.description:
Tests if the given #Mesh is valid and the mesh has been correctly initialized.

This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. If Result equals zero then the given mesh
has not been properly created or initialized. This is the correct way to ensure a mesh is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadMesh
commands.description: Loads a new mesh. Before loading a mesh, an archive must be specified with Add3DArchive().

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new mesh. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename of the mesh.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the mesh was successfully loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Mesh parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
Mesh is required to be in the OGRE .mesh format. A command-line tool based on assimp is available to convert
many 3d formats into the OGRE mesh, including materials and animations. It can be downloaded
here: OgreAssimpConverter.zip (Windows only). Some problems
have been reported with shadow and converted meshes, if that happen use OgreMeshUpdater.exe on the newly converted mesh and it should fix
it.

It is also possible to use existing exporter for Milkshape, Lightwave, Blender or 3DS Max. More
information may be found on the OGRE website.

commands.name: MeshDirectAdd
commands.description:
Add a new submesh to the specified #Mesh. A mesh can have any number of
submeshes. A submesh position is relative to the mesh position.

parameters.name: MeshVertexArray()
parameters.description: The array containing the submesh vertex data. It has to be an array of type "MeshVertex".

parameters.name: MeshFaceArray()
parameters.description: The array containing the submesh face data. It has to be an array of type "MeshFace".

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of the new submesh. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Mesh_TriangleList : the submesh will be composed of a list of triangles (default).
#PB_Mesh_TriangleStrip: the submesh will be composed of a list of connected triangles (vertices are shared).
#PB_Mesh_TriangleFan : the submesh will be composed of a list of triangles sharing the same central vertex point.
#PB_Mesh_PointList : the submesh will be composed of a list of points.
#PB_Mesh_LineList : the submesh will be composed of a list of lines.
#PB_Mesh_LineStrip : the submesh will be composed of a list of connected lines (vertices are shared).

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description: The default material to use for the submesh. To get a valid 'MaterialID', use MaterialID().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshFace
commands.description:
Add or update a face to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh(). The specified vertices must
exist. The first vertex index starts from 0. The created face is a triangle or a quad. MeshIndex() can be used
if the number of vertices is more than four.

parameters.name: Vertex1
parameters.description: The first vertex index used to create the face.

parameters.name: Vertex2
parameters.description: The second vertex index used to create the face.

parameters.name: Vertex3
parameters.description: The third vertex index used to create the face.

parameters.name: Vertex4 (optional)
parameters.description: The fourth vertex index used to create the face, which will result in a quad.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshID
commands.description: Returns the unique MeshID of the #Mesh. The use of this function is required especially by the CreateEntity() function.

commands.name: MeshIndex
commands.description:
Add or update a single vertex in the mesh being created with CreateMesh() or updated with UpdateMesh().
It behaves like the command MeshFace(), but with an arbitrary number of vertices. When using
the mode #PB_Mesh_LineList or #PB_Mesh_LineStrip, there are only two vertices per line,
so MeshIndex() needs to be used in this case.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The vertex index.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshIndexCount
commands.description: Return the number of indexes in the mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, it will return the number of indexes in the specified submesh. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of indexes in the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exists.

commands.name: MeshRadius
commands.description: Returns the radius of the smallest sphere which can contain the mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the radius the mesh.

commands.name: MeshVertex
syntax: MeshVertex(x, y, z, u.f, v.f, Color [, NormalX, NormalY, NormalZ])
commands.description:
Add a vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh(). Specific attributes
to the newly created vertex can be added with MeshVertexTangent(). To create a new face use MeshFace().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The position of the new vertex.

parameters.name: u
parameters.description:
The u value. This value is the X position in the texture where the vertex should map. This value is
usually between 0 and 1, where 0 is the texture X origin and 1 is the texture X end (see MeshVertexTextureCoordinate() for more information).

parameters.name: v
parameters.description:
The v value. This value is the Y position in the texture where the vertex should map. This value is
usually between 0 and 1, where 0 is the texture Y origin and 1 is the texture Y end (see MeshVertexTextureCoordinate() for more information).

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
Color of the vertex. This color can be in RGB or RGBA format
(see MeshVertexColor() for more information).

parameters.name: NormalX, NormalY, NormalZ
parameters.description: The normal vector (see MeshVertexNormal() for more information).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshVertexColor
commands.description:
Set color information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition() or MeshVertex().
To have any effect, the material associated to the mesh has to be defined with
SetMaterialColor(#Material, #PB_Material_AmbientColor, -1) and AmbientColor()() set to a positive value.
This function needs a vertex created before to apply color to it.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Color of the vertex. This color can be in RGB or RGBA format.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshVertexCount
commands.description: Return the number of vertices of the mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, it will return the number of vertices of the specified submesh. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: Returns the vertices number of the mesh, or zero if the mesh or the submesh doesn't exist.

commands.name: MeshVertexNormal
commands.description:
Set normal information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition() or MeshVertex(). The normal
vector is used to calculate lightning on an object. To automatically computes the vector
normal once the mesh is created, use NormalizeMesh().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The normal vector.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshVertexPosition
commands.description:
Add a new vertex to the current mesh previously created with CreateMesh(). To set specific attributes
to the newly created vertex, use the following commands: MeshVertexNormal(), MeshVertexTangent(), MeshVertexColor() and
MeshVertexTextureCoordinate(). If several attributes needs to be specified, MeshVertex() can be used instead.
To create a new face use MeshFace().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The position of the new vertex.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshVertexTangent
commands.description:
Set tangent information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition() or MeshVertex(). The tangent
vector is mainly used in shader scripts. To automatically compute the tangent vector
once the mesh is created, use BuildMeshTangents().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The tangent vector.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MeshVertexTextureCoordinate
commands.description:
Set UVW information to the current vertex previously added with MeshVertexPosition() or MeshVertex(). The UVW information is
used to apply the texture on the mesh.

parameters.name: u
parameters.description:
The u value. This value is the X position in the texture where the vertex should map. This value is
usually between 0 and 1, where 0 is the texture X origin and 1 is the texture X end.

parameters.name: v (optional)
parameters.description:
The v value. This value is the Y position in the texture where the vertex should map. This value is
usually between 0 and 1, where 0 is the texture Y origin and 1 is the texture Y end.

parameters.name: w (optional)
parameters.description:
The w value (for cubic textures). This value is the Z position in the texture where the vertex should map. This value is
usually between 0 and 1, where 0 is the texture Z origin and 1 is the texture Z end.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: NormalizeMesh
commands.description:
Normalize the mesh or the submesh. It will automatically compute the normal vector for all vertices
of the specified mesh or submesh. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, it will only normalize the submesh. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SaveMesh
commands.description: Save the mesh. The saved mesh can be loaded back with the LoadMesh() command.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to save.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description:
The filename and path to the new mesh file. If the filename does not include a full path, it
is interpreted relative to the current directory.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetMeshData
syntax: Result = SetMeshData(#Mesh, SubMesh, DataArray(), Flags, FirstIndex, LastIndex)
commands.description: Set internal mesh data, like vertices, face etc. Dynamic meshes are not supported (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh
parameters.description: The submesh to set the data to. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

parameters.name: DataArray()
parameters.description:
The array containing the data to set. It has to be an array of type "MeshVertex" or "MeshFace"
depending on the specified flags.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description:
Specifies which kind of data needs to be set. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Mesh_Vertex: DataArray() is an array of type "MeshVertex".
#PB_Mesh_Face : DataArray() is an array of type "MeshFace".

combined with:

#PB_Mesh_UVCoordinate : Set the UV coordinate information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)
#PB_Mesh_Normal : Set the normal information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)
#PB_Mesh_Color : Set the color information (only for #PB_Mesh_Vertex flag)

The "MeshVertex" and "MeshFace" structures are defined like this:

Structure MeshVertex
x.f
y.f
z.f
NormalX.f ; only used if #PB_Mesh_Normal flag is set
NormalY.f ;
NormalZ.f ;
TangentX.f
TangentY.f
TangentZ.f
u.f ; only used if #PB_Mesh_UVCoordinate flag is set
v.f ;
Color.l ; only used if #PB_Mesh_Color flag is set
EndStructure

Structure MeshFace
Index.l
EndStructure

parameters.name: FirstIndex, LastIndex
parameters.description: First and last index to set the data to.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero on success and zero on failure.

commands.name: SetMeshMaterial
commands.description: Set the mesh default material.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description: The default material to use for the mesh. To get a valid 'MaterialID', use MaterialID().

parameters.name: SubMesh (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, the material will be applied only to the submesh. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SubMeshCount
commands.description: Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of submeshes of the mesh.

commands.name: TransformMesh
syntax: TransformMesh(#Mesh, x, y, z, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ, RotateX, RotateY, RotateZ [, SubMesh])
commands.description:
Transform the Mesh according to the given parameters.
Dynamic meshes are not supported for transform (meshes created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag).

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to transform.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description:
New position of the mesh, relative to its node. If the submesh parameter is specified, it
specifies the new position of the submesh relative to its parent.

parameters.name: ScaleX
parameters.description:
Applies a scale factor on the X axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
scale is applied the submesh.

parameters.name: ScaleY
parameters.description:
Applies a scale factor on the Y axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
scale is applied the submesh.

parameters.name: ScaleZ
parameters.description:
Applies a scale factor on the Z axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
scale is applied the submesh.

parameters.name: RotateX
parameters.description:
Applies a rotation, in degree, on the X axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
rotation is applied to the submesh.

parameters.name: RotateY
parameters.description:
Applies a rotation, in degree, on the Y axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
rotation is applied to the submesh.

parameters.name: RotateZ
parameters.description:
Applies a rotation, in degree, on the Z axis to the mesh. If the submesh parameter is specified, the
rotation is applied to the submesh.

parameters.name: SubMesh (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, the transformation will be applied only to the submesh. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UpdateMesh
commands.description:
Start the mesh update, to modify in real time its vertices and other values. The mesh
has to be created with the #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag. Once the mesh modifications are finished,
FinishMesh() needs to be called. The mesh can use the following commands to change their
properties: MeshIndex(), MeshFace(), MeshVertexPosition(), MeshVertexNormal(), MeshVertexTangent(), MeshVertexColor() and
MeshVertexTextureCoordinate().

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh
parameters.description: The submesh index to modify. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UpdateMeshBoundingBox
commands.description:
Update the bounding box of the mesh. If a mesh has been manually modified, its bounding box has to be
recalculated, especially if the mesh is used for collisions. The bounding box is the smallest box
which can contain the whole mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ExamineMouse
commands.description:
Updates the mouse state. This function should be used before MouseDeltaX(), MouseDeltaY(), MouseX(), MouseY() or
MouseButton().
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the mouse state has been updated, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
The first call to ExamineMouse() captures the mouse to the active Screen
or 'WindowedScreen'.
The mouse is available again on your whole system after calling ReleaseMouse(#True)
or after the end of that program.

In fullscreen mode the command FlipBuffers() need to be called inside your
event loop to handle all events properly.

commands.name: InitMouse
commands.description:
Initializes the mouse environment for later use. You should call this function before any other functions in
this library. If the result is zero, no mouse is available.
commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the mouse functions are available, zero otherwise.

This function tries to open DirectX (v3.0 with NT4.0 compatibility or v7.0 otherwise); if it fails then DirectX
is either not available or is too old to be used.

commands.name: MouseButton
commands.description:
Returns zero if the specified button number is not pressed, otherwise the button is pressed.
Any number of buttons can be pressed at the same time. ExamineMouse() must be
called before this function to update the actual button's state.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following constants:

#PB_MouseButton_Left : Tests if the left mouse button is pressed
#PB_MouseButton_Right : Tests if the right mouse button is pressed
#PB_MouseButton_Middle: Tests if the middle mouse button is pressed

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the specified mouse button is pressed, zero otherwise.

commands.name: MouseDeltaX
commands.description: Returns the mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
commands.returnValue:
The mouse 'x' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved to
the left or the right since the last call. ExamineMouse() should be called before this function
to update the actual mouse position.

commands.name: MouseDeltaY
commands.description: Returns the mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
commands.returnValue:
The mouse 'y' movement (in pixels) since the last call of this function.
It can be either a negative or positive value, depending on whether or not the mouse has been moved
up or down since the last call. ExamineMouse() should be called before this function
to update the actual mouse position.

commands.name: MouseLocate
commands.description:
Changes the absolute position (in pixels) of the mouse in the current screen. This is useful when using MouseX()
or MouseY().

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The new absolute position (in pixels) of the mouse in the current screen.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MouseWheel
commands.description:
Returns the number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. ExamineMouse() should
be called before this function to update the mouse status.
commands.returnValue:
The number of ticks the mouse wheel has moved since the last function call. The value is positive
if the wheel has moved forward and negative if the wheel has moved backwards.

commands.name: MouseX
commands.description:
Returns the actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed
easily with the MouseLocate() function. ExamineMouse() should
be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
commands.returnValue: The actual mouse 'x' position (in pixels) on the current screen.

commands.name: MouseY
commands.description:
Returns the actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen. The position can be changed
easily with the MouseLocate() function. ExamineMouse() should
be called before this function to update the actual mouse position.
commands.returnValue: The actual mouse 'y' position (in pixels) on the current screen.

commands.name: ReleaseMouse
commands.description:
Locks or releases the mouse to allow its use under standard OS. This is typically called after checking
the result of IsScreenActive() function.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
#True : the mouse is released.
#False : the mouse is locked.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeMovie
commands.description: Frees the specified movie and all its resources.

parameters.name: #Move
parameters.description: The movie to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining movies are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining movies are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: InitMovie
commands.description:
Initialize the movie environment for later use. You must call this function before any other functions in
this library.
commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if initialization was successful. If zero is returned then the movie library cannot be used.
commands.remarks:
This function tries to open DirectX (v3.0 with NT4.0 compatibility or v7.0 else); if it fails then DirectX
is either not available or is too old be used.

commands.name: IsMovie
commands.description: Tests if the given #Movie number is a valid and correctly initialized movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #Movie is a valid movie and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value.
If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and
initialized, otherwise it will equal zero. This is the correct way to ensure a movie is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadMovie
commands.description: Loads the specified movie file and prepares it for playback.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description:
A number to identify the loaded movie.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The file name of the movie.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the movie was loaded correctly and zero if loading the
movie failed (format not supported or file not found).
If #PB_Any was used for the #Movie parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
InitMovie() must be called once before loading movies. Further information about the loaded movie can be
read with the MovieInfo(), MovieLength(), MovieWidth() and MovieHeight() commands.

commands.name: MovieAudio
commands.description:
Control the audio stream of a movie. Volume and balance can be modified during playback.
Changes occur immediately.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

parameters.name: Volume
parameters.description: The volume for the movie. This value can be between 0 and 100 (100 being the loudest).

parameters.name: Balance
parameters.description:
The balance for the movie. This value can be between -100 and 100
(-100 is full left, 0 is middle (normal mode) and 100 is full right).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MovieHeight
commands.description: Returns the height of the movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the height of the movie in pixels.
If the result equals -1, then no video stream is
found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.

commands.name: MovieInfo
commands.description: Returns additional information about the movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description:
The information to return.
Supported values are:

0: return the number of frame per seconds (*1000).

commands.returnValue: Returns the value specified in the 'Flags' parameter.

commands.name: MovieLength
commands.description: Returns the length of the movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the length of the movie in frames.

commands.name: MovieSeek
commands.description: Change the movie's playback position to the given frame.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

parameters.name: Frame
parameters.description: The frame to be the new playback position.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: MovieStatus
commands.description: Get the playback status of the movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

-1: Movie is paused.

0: Movie is stopped

> 0: Movie is playing. The returned value is the current frame number displayed.

commands.name: MovieWidth
commands.description: Returns the width of the movie.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the width of the movie in pixels.
If the result equals -1, then no video stream is
found (or isn't compatible), however the audio stream can still be played.

commands.name: PauseMovie
commands.description: Pauses the movie playback. Playback can be resumed using the ResumeMovie() function.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to pause.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: PlayMovie
commands.description: Start to play a movie previously loaded with LoadMovie() on the specified window.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to play.

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description:
The window to play the movie on.
This value can be easily obtained by using the WindowID() function.

It's also possible to play a movie on a full screen, simply use the result of ScreenID() as
'WindowID'.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the movie started playing correctly and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
The function ResizeMovie() can be used to resize and move the movie on this window (to not use the
full window area, for example).

commands.name: ResizeMovie
commands.description: Resize and move the movie display area on the movie window.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to resize.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The new location and size of the movie in pixels.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ResumeMovie
commands.description: Continue to play the movie, after a PauseMovie() call.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to resume.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: StopMovie
commands.description: Stop playing the movie. If the movie is played again, it will restart from the beginning.

parameters.name: #Movie
parameters.description: The movie to stop.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CatchMusic
commands.description:
Loads the specified music from the specified memory buffer.
PlayMusic() can be used to start playing the music. ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels),
FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new music module.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to load the music module from.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The buffer size.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is useful when using the 'IncludeBinary' PureBasic keyword. Then music modules can be packed inside
the executable. Nevertheless, use this option with care, as it will take
more memory than storing the music in an external file (the music is both in
executable memory and load in physical memory).
commands.example:
CatchMusic(0, ?Music, ?MusicEnd-?Music)
  End

  DataSection
    Music:
      IncludeBinary "Music.xm"
    MusicEnd:
  EndDataSection

commands.name: FreeMusic
commands.description:
Stop and remove the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic() or CatchMusic() functions from memory. Once a music has been
freed, it can't be played anymore.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining musics are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining musics are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetMusicPosition
commands.description: Returns the current pattern position of the playing music module.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to use.

commands.returnValue: The current pattern position of the playing music module. The first pattern position is zero.

commands.name: GetMusicRow
commands.description: Returns the current row position in the pattern of the playing music module.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to use.

commands.returnValue: The current row position of the playing music module. The first row position is zero.

commands.name: IsMusic
commands.description: Tests if the given music module is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the music module is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a music module is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadMusic
commands.description:
Loads the specified music module. PlayMusic() can be used to start playing the music.
ModPlug supports a lot of music formats, which includes: Protracker (4 channels),
FastTracker (up to 32 channels, 16-bit quality), Impulse Tracker, etc.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new music module.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename of the music module to load.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the music module has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.

commands.name: MusicVolume
commands.description: Change the master volume of the specified music, in real-time.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to use.

parameters.name: Volume.f
parameters.description: The new volume to set for the music. Volume values can be from 0 to 100. Can be useful for fade-in/fade-out.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: PlayMusic
commands.description: Starts to play the specified music previously loaded with the LoadMusic() or CatchMusic() functions.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to play.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetMusicPosition
commands.description: Changes the current pattern position of the playing #Music to the new one.

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to use.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: The new music module pattern position. The first pattern position starts from 0.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: StopMusic
commands.description: Stop the #Music (if it was playing).

parameters.name: #Music
parameters.description: The music module to stop. If set to #PB_All, then all the currently playing musics are stopped.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CloseNetworkConnection
commands.description: Close the specified connection.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description:
The connection to close. This is the result of either a call to
OpenNetworkConnection() or EventClient().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
If a client calls this function the server will receive a #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect event.
If this function is called from a server the connection will be closed without further notice to the client.
When a server receives a #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect event its associated client connection is automatically
closed and CloseNetworkConnection() must not be called in this case.

All remaining opened connections are automatically closed when the program ends.

commands.name: CloseNetworkServer
commands.description:
Shutdown the specified running server. All clients connected to this
server are automatically removed. The port is freed and can be reused.

parameters.name: #Server
parameters.description: The server to close.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ConnectionID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the connection.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description:
The connection to use. This is the result of either a call to
OpenNetworkConnection() or EventClient().

commands.returnValue:
Returns the system identifier.
This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for
more information.

commands.name: CreateNetworkServer
commands.description:
Create a new network server on the local computer using the specified port. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS() needs to be
called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified.

parameters.name: #Server
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new server.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description:
The port to use for the server.
Port values can range from 6000 to 7000 (this is a recommended area space,
but it can go from 0 to 65000 in reality).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
Can be one of the following values:

#PB_Network_TCP: the server will use the TCP network protocol (default)
#PB_Network_UDP: the server will use the UDP network protocol

combined with one of the following values (using the '|' operand):

#PB_Network_IPv4: create a server using IPv4 (default)
#PB_Network_IPv6: create a server using IPv6

combined with one of the following values (using the '|' operand):

#PB_Network_NoTLS : no encryption will be used for this server (default)
#PB_Network_TLSv1 : all non-deprecated TLS protocols will be supported (currently v1.2 and v1.3)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_0: TLS v1.0 protocol will be supported (warning, this protocol is deprecated for security reasons)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_1: TLS v1.1 protocol will be supported (warning, this protocol is deprecated for security reasons)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_2: TLS v1.2 protocol will be supported
#PB_Network_TLSv1_3: TLS v1.3 protocol will be supported

parameters.name: BoundIP$ (optional)
parameters.description:
The local IP address to bind the server. By default, the server is created on all available local interfaces, and accept
connections from them. It can be useful to restrict the server to only one interface (for example "127.0.0.1")
to avoid connection attempt from other interfaces. On Windows, binding only to the localhost avoid to trigger the
built-in firewall.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the server was created successfully and zero if creation
failed, for example, due to the port being already in use.
If #PB_Any was used as the #Server parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
Any number of servers can run simultaneously on the same computer, the only restriction
being that two servers can not run using the same port and the same protocol (#PB_Network_TCP and #PB_Network_UDP).
It's possible to create two servers using the same port, one using IPv4 and the other using IPv6.
NetworkServerEvent() can be used to monitor server for events.

commands.name: EventClient
commands.description: This function returns the connection of the client that sent data and is only needed on the server side.
commands.returnValue: Returns the connection of the client that caused the event.
commands.remarks: The functions GetClientIP() and GetClientPort() can be used to get more information on the client that sent data.

commands.name: EventServer
commands.description:
This function returns the number of the server which has received
data, allowing multiple servers to be managed on one computer.
It is only needed on the server side.
commands.returnValue: Returns the #Server number of the server causing the event.

commands.name: ExamineIPAddresses
commands.description:
Start examining the available IP addresses on the local computer. NextIPAddress() is used
to retrieve each IP.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the IP to examine. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Network_IPv4: examine IPv4 addresses (default).
#PB_Network_IPv6: examine IPv6 addresses. Returned addresses needs to be freed with FreeIP() after use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if examining the addresses works and zero if it failed.
commands.example:
If ExamineIPAddresses()
    Repeat
      IP = NextIPAddress()
      If IP
        Debug "IPv4: " + IPString(IP) 
      EndIf
    Until IP = 0
  EndIf

If ExamineIPAddresses(#PB_Network_IPv6)
    Repeat
      IP = NextIPAddress()
      If IP
        Debug "IPv6: " + IPString(IP, #PB_Network_IPv6) 
        FreeIP(IP)                                     
      EndIf
    Until IP = 0
  EndIf

commands.name: FreeIP
commands.description:
Free an IPv6 address. This function only works with IPv6 addresses returned by MakeIPAddress(), NextIPAddress()
and GetClientIP(), and must not be used with IPv4 addresses.

parameters.name: IPAddress
parameters.description: The IPv6 address to free.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: GetClientIP
commands.description:
This function returns the IP address of the client and should be called after EventClient().
If the connection is an IPv6 connection the returned address must be freed with FreeIP().

parameters.name: Client
parameters.description: The client for which to get the IP.

commands.returnValue: Returns the IP address of the client.

commands.name: GetClientPort
commands.description: Returns the client port and should be called after EventClient().

parameters.name: Client
parameters.description: The client for which to get the port.

commands.returnValue: Returns the port of the client.

commands.name: HostName
commands.description: Returns the computer's hostname.
commands.returnValue: Returns the host name.

commands.name: IPAddressField
commands.description: Returns the given field value of the specified IP address.

parameters.name: IPAddress
parameters.description: The IP address. For IPv6, this address needs to be created with MakeIPAddress().

parameters.name: Field
parameters.description:
The field to return. This value can be a value between 0 and 3
(0 being the leftmost value, 3 being the rightmost) for IPv4 and 0 to 7 for IPv6.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the IP. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Network_IPv4: an IPv4 address (default).
#PB_Network_IPv6: an IPv6 address.

commands.returnValue: Returns the value of the specified field, in the range 0 to 255.
commands.remarks:
This function is especially useful with:

- IPAddressGadget()

- MakeIPAddress()

commands.name: IPString
commands.description: Returns the string representation in dotted form (ie: "127.0.0.1" for IPv4 or "::1" for IPv6) of the specified numerical IPAddress.

parameters.name: IPAddress
parameters.description: The IP address. For IPv6, this address needs to be the result of MakeIPAddress(), NextIPAddress() or GetClientIP().

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The format of the IP to convert. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Network_IPv4: convert an IPv4 address (default).
#PB_Network_IPv6: convert an IPv6 address.

commands.returnValue: Returns the IP address as a string.

commands.name: MakeIPAddress
syntax: Result = MakeIPAddress(Field0, Field1, Field2, Field3 [, Field4, Field5, Field6, Field7])
commands.description: Returns the equivalent numeric value of the specified IP address.

parameters.name: Field0, Field1, Field2, Field3
parameters.description:
The individual fields of the address.
Each field can only have a value between 0 and 255.

parameters.name: Field4, Field5, Field6, Field7 (optional)
parameters.description:
The remaining individual fields for IPv6 address.
Each field can only have a value between 0 and 255.
When these fields are specified, an IPv6 address is created. When the address is no more needed, it has
to be manually freed with FreeIP(). IPv4 address must not be freed with FreeIP().

commands.returnValue: Returns the IP address.
commands.remarks:
This function is especially useful with:

- IPAddressGadget()

commands.name: NetworkClientEvent
commands.description: Checks if an event happened on a network connection created with OpenNetworkConnection().

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description: The connection to check.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened
#PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData())
#PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: The client has been disconnected (connection closed).

commands.name: NetworkServerEvent
commands.description: Checks if an event happened on one of the open network servers.

parameters.name: #Server (optional)
parameters.description:
The server to use to check the events. When used, only the events which belongs to this
server are handled, all other events are left untouched.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_NetworkEvent_None : Nothing has happened
#PB_NetworkEvent_Connect : A new client has been connected to the server (not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections)
#PB_NetworkEvent_Data : Raw data has been received (to be read with ReceiveNetworkData())
#PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect: A client has quit the server (disconnection). Its associated connection is
automatically closed, CloseNetworkConnection() must not be called for this client.
(Not available with #PB_Network_UDP connections.)
commands.remarks:
The server that received the event can be determined with EventServer(). The client that caused the event
can be determined with EventClient().

commands.name: NextIPAddress
commands.description:
Returns the next IP address of the local machine. ExamineIPAddresses() must be called
before this command.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the next IP address in numerical form. If the result is 0 then there are no more IP addresses to be examined.
If ExamineIPAddresses() is called with the #PB_Network_IPv6 format, the returned IP needs to freed with FreeIP() after use.
commands.example:
If ExamineIPAddresses()
    Repeat
      IP = NextIPAddress()
      If IP
        Debug "IPv4: " + IPString(IP) 
      EndIf
    Until IP = 0
  EndIf

If ExamineIPAddresses(#PB_Network_IPv6)
    Repeat
      IP = NextIPAddress()
      If IP
        Debug "IPv6: " + IPString(IP, #PB_Network_IPv6) 
        FreeIP(IP)                                     
      EndIf
    Until IP = 0
  EndIf

commands.name: OpenNetworkConnection
syntax: Connection = OpenNetworkConnection(ServerName$, Port [, Flags [, TimeOut [, LocalIP$ [, LocalPort]]]])
commands.description:
Opens a network connection to the specified server. To support TLS encryption, UseNetworkTLS() needs to be
called before this command and a TLS flag needs to be specified.

parameters.name: ServerName$
parameters.description:
The server to connect to. This can be an
IP address or a full name (ie: "127.0.0.1" or "ftp.home.net").

parameters.name: Port
parameters.description: The port on the server to connect to.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Network_TCP: The connection will use the TCP network protocol (default)
#PB_Network_UDP: The connection will use the UDP network protocol. The connection will not be
explicitly created, as UDP is a connectionless protocol, but it will add an
entry in the PureBasic management stack and allow to send data via UDP using
the regular SendNetworkData() (and related) functions.

combined with one of the following values (using the '|' operand):

#PB_Network_IPv4: open the connection using IPv4 (default)
#PB_Network_IPv6: open the connection using IPv6

combined with one of the following values (using the '|' operand):

#PB_Network_NoTLS : no encryption will be supported for this connection (default)
#PB_Network_TLSv1 : all non-deprecated TLS protocols will be supported (currently v1.2 and v1.3)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_0: TLS v1.0 protocol will be supported (warning, this protocol is deprecated for security reasons)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_1: TLS v1.1 protocol will be supported (warning, this protocol is deprecated for security reasons)
#PB_Network_TLSv1_2: TLS v1.2 protocol will be supported
#PB_Network_TLSv1_3: TLS v1.3 protocol will be supported

parameters.name: TimeOut (optional)
parameters.description:
The maximum time (in milliseconds) before aborting the connection attempt. Usually, it shouldn't be
set to a too low value (less than 5000 milliseconds), as initializing a connection over the net
can take some time.

parameters.name: LocalIP$ (optional)
parameters.description: The local IP address to bind the connection to.

parameters.name: LocalPort (optional)
parameters.description:
The local port to bind the connection to. By default a random local port is automatically chosen for the new connection,
but it can be overridden with this parameter.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the connection identifier for the opened connection if the connection was established correctly.
If there was an error the result is zero.

commands.name: ReceiveNetworkData
commands.description:
Receives raw data from the specified client. This function can be used by both client and server applications
and should be called only after having received a #PB_NetworkEvent_Data event.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description:
The connection to receive data from.
On the server side 'Connection' is the client which has send the data (can be easily obtained with
EventClient()).
On client side, 'Connection' is returned by OpenNetworkConnection().

parameters.name: *DataBuffer
parameters.description: The memory address to receive the data to.

parameters.name: DataBufferLength
parameters.description: The length of the buffer to receive data to.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the number of bytes received. If 'Result' is equal to DataBufferLength then more data is available to be read.
If an error occurred on the connection (link broken, connection close by the server etc...) 'Result' will be -1.
commands.remarks: On UDP connections, the maximum 'DataBufferLength' is 2048. On TCP connections, the maximum 'DataBufferLength' is 65536.

commands.name: SendNetworkData
commands.description:
Sends raw data to the specified client. This function can be used by both
client and server applications.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description:
The connection to send data to.
On the server side, 'Connection' is the client which should receive this data.
On the client side, 'Connection' is returned by OpenNetworkConnection().

parameters.name: *MemoryBuffer
parameters.description: The address of the data to send.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The length of the data to send.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the number of bytes actually sent. If the number of bytes returned is not equal
to the 'Length' parameter the receiving buffer of the user is probably full.
If nothing could be sent then 'Result' will equal -1.
commands.remarks: On UDP connections, the maximum 'Length' is 2048. On TCP connections, the maximum 'Length' is 65536.

commands.name: SendNetworkString
commands.description:
Send a string to the specified client. This function can be used by both
client and server applications.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description:
The connection to send the string to.
On the server side, 'Connection' is the client which should receive this data.
On the client side, 'Connection' is returned by OpenNetworkConnection().

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to send.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when sending the string. This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : sends the strings as ASCII
#PB_UTF8 : sends the strings as UTF8 (default)
#PB_Unicode: send the strings as unicode

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of bytes sent.
commands.remarks:
SendNetworkString() provides a solution to quickly send strings. The string will be sent without the
terminating null-character, and can be received using ReceiveNetworkData(), after
NetworkServerEvent() / NetworkClientEvent() returned #PB_NetworkEvent_Data).
In unicode mode the string is sent as UTF-8, which is processor independent (unlike UTF-16 which is tied to processor endianness).
There is no ReceiveNetworkString() command.

commands.name: ServerID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the server.

parameters.name: #Server
parameters.description: The server to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the system identifier.
This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter Handles and Numbers for
more information.

commands.name: UseNetworkTLS
commands.description: Enable and configure TLS support for network library. This command must be called before using CreateNetworkServer() or OpenNetworkConnection() with the TLS flags.

parameters.name: PrivateKey$ (optional)
parameters.description:
The private key to use for TLS when using CreateNetworkServer(). When using TLS only with OpenNetworkConnection(), this parameter is not needed. It should be in following format:

"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"+#LF$+ ""+#LF$+
"-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"

parameters.name: Certificate$ (optional)
parameters.description:
The certificat to use for TLS when using CreateNetworkServer(). When using TLS only with OpenNetworkConnection(), this parameter is not needed. It should be in following format:

"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"+#LF$+ ""+#LF$+
"-----END CERTIFICATE-----"

parameters.name: CaCertificate$ (optional)
parameters.description: The intermediate authority certificate who issued the 'Certificate$' to use for TLS when using CreateNetworkServer(). When using TLS only with OpenNetworkConnection(), this parameter is not needed. It should be in the same format than 'Certificate$'.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Timeout = 15000 ; 15 secs overall timeout

  PrivateKey$ = "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"+#LF$+
         ""+#LF$+
         "-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"

  Cert$ = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"+#LF$+
          ""+#LF$+
          "-----END CERTIFICATE-----"

  UseNetworkTLS(PrivateKey$, Cert$)
  If CreateNetworkServer(0, 20252, #PB_Network_TCP | #PB_Network_IPv4 | #PB_Network_TLSv1, "127.0.0.1")
    Debug "TLS Server launched on 127.0.0.1:20252 - Waiting for connections..."
    
    Repeat
      Select NetworkServerEvent()
        Case #PB_NetworkEvent_Data
          
          Debug "Data recieved !"
          ClientID = EventClient()
          *Buffer = AllocateMemory(1000)
          If *Buffer
            Debug ReceiveNetworkData(ClientID, *Buffer, 1000)
          
            Debug "String: "+PeekS(*Buffer, -1, #PB_UTF8)
            SendNetworkString(ClientID, "Well received !!!")
            
            FreeMemory(*Buffer)
          EndIf
          
        Case #PB_NetworkEvent_None
          Delay(100) ; Don't steal the whole CPU time while waiting for connection
          Timeout - 100
      EndSelect
          
    Until Timeout <= 0
    
    Debug "Closing server after " + Str(Timeout/1000) + " secs timeout"
    
    CloseNetworkServer(0)
  Else
    Debug "Can't create the TLS server"
  EndIf

Timeout = 150000 ; 15 secs overall timeout

  UseNetworkTLS()

  Connection = OpenNetworkConnection("127.0.0.1", 20252, #PB_Network_TCP | #PB_Network_IPv4 | #PB_Network_TLSv1)
  If Connection
    
    ; Send some string to the server to test
    SendNetworkString(Connection, "GET / HTTP/1.1" + #CRLF$ + "Host: www.purebasic.fr" + #CRLF$ + #CRLF$)
    
    Repeat
      Select NetworkClientEvent(Connection)
        Case #PB_NetworkEvent_Data
          *Buffer = AllocateMemory($FFFF)
          If *Buffer
            Length = ReceiveNetworkData(Connection, *Buffer, MemorySize(*Buffer))
            Received$ + PeekS(*Buffer, Length, #PB_UTF8 | #PB_ByteLength)
            Debug "Recieved string: "+ Received$
            FreeMemory(*Buffer)
          EndIf
          
        Case #PB_NetworkEvent_Disconnect
          Debug "Disconnected"
          Break
          
        Case #PB_NetworkEvent_None
          Delay(100)
          Timeout - 100
          
      EndSelect
    Until Timeout <= 0
    
    CloseNetworkConnection(Connection)
  Else
    Debug "Can't open the connection on 127.0.0.1:20252"
  EndIf

commands.name: AttachNodeObject
commands.description: Attaches an existing object to a node.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description: The node to use.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object to attach. The supported objects are the following:

- Entity : use EntityID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Sound3D: use SoundID3D() as 'ObjectID'.
- Text3D : use Text3DID() as 'ObjetID'.
- Camera : use CameraID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Light : use LightID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Node : use NodeID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Mesh : use MeshID() as 'ObjectID' (supported only if #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag is set).
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() as 'ObjectID'.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() as 'ObjectID'.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: An object can be detached from a node with DetachNodeObject().

commands.name: CreateNode
commands.description: Creates a new node at the specified position.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new node.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description:
The absolute position in the world of the new node.
By default the new node is created at position "0, 0, 0".

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the node was successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Node parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

commands.name: DetachNodeObject
commands.description: Detaches a previously attached object from a node.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description: The node to use.

parameters.name: ObjectID
parameters.description:
The object to detach. The supported objects are the following:

- Entity : use EntityID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Sound3D: use SoundID3D() as 'ObjectID'.
- Camera : use CameraID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Light : use LightID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Node : use NodeID() as 'ObjectID'.
- Mesh : use MeshID() as 'ObjectID' (supported only if #PB_Mesh_Dynamic flag is set).
- BillboardGroup : use BillboardGroupID() as 'ObjectID'.
- ParticleEmitter: use ParticleEmitterID() as 'ObjectID'.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: An object can be attached to a node with AttachNodeObject().

commands.name: FreeNode
commands.description:
Frees the specified node created with CreateNode() before.
All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used anymore. The attached objects are not freed automatically,
and can be re-used.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description: The node to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining nodes are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining nodes are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: IsNode
commands.description: Tests if the given node is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description: The node to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the node is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a node is ready to use.

commands.name: MoveNode
commands.description: Move the specified node.

parameters.name: #Node
parameters.description: The node to move.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position of the node.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The move mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative move, from the current node position (default).
#PB_Absolute: absolute move to the specified position.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: NodeFixedYawAxis

parameters.name: VectorX, VectorY, VectorZ (optional)

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateNodeAnimation
syntax: Result = CreateNodeAnimation(#NodeAnimation, NodeID, Length, Interpolation, RotationInterpolation)
commands.description:
Creates a new node animation of the specified length. A node animation doesn't exist physically in the
3D world, it is an virtual track to move a node (and its attached object) easily around the world.

parameters.name: #NodeAnimation
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new node animation. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: NodeID
parameters.description: The node to move automatically. NodeID() can be use to get a valid node identifier.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The length of the new animation (in milliseconds).

parameters.name: Interpolation
parameters.description:
The type of interpolation to apply between points. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_NodeAnimation_Linear: each points will be linked together using a straight line, which can result to abrupt direction change
#PB_NodeAnimation_Spline: each points will be linked together using a spline, which results in smooth direction change, but is also slower.

parameters.name: RotationInterpolation
parameters.description:
The type of interpolation for the rotation to apply between points. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_NodeAnimation_LinearRotation: each points will be linked together using a straight line, which can result to abrupt rotation
#PB_NodeAnimation_SphericalRotation: each points will be linked together using a curve, which results in smoother rotation, but is also slower.

commands.returnValue:
Returns zero if the #NodeAnimation can't be created. If #PB_Any is used
as '#NodeAnimation' parameter, the new node animation number is returned.

commands.name: CreateNodeAnimationKeyFrame
commands.description:
Create a new keyframe for the #NodeAnimation. A keyframe is a point in the world at a specified time.
When the node animation will be played, it will follow every keyframe and thus moving from points
to points. The move will be interpolated to respect the time constraint. For example, if the first
keyframe is set at time 0, the second at time 1000 and the third at time 3000, going from
the first keyframe to the second will takes 1000 milliseconds, and going from the second keyframe to the third will takes 2000 milliseconds.
The overall animation will take 3000 milliseconds.

parameters.name: #NodeAnimation
parameters.description: The node animation to use.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description:
The time in the animation to set the keyframe (in milliseconds). This value has to be between zero and the 'Length'
defined in CreateNodeAnimation().

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new keyframe position in the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeNodeAnimation
commands.description:
Frees a node animation and releases all its associated memory. This node animation must not be used
(by using its number with the other functions in this library) after
calling this function, unless you create it again.

parameters.name: #NodeAnimation
parameters.description: The node animation to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining node animations are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining node animations are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.description: Returns the #NodeAnimation keyframe pitch.

Returns the #NodeAnimation weight. The weight is useful when playing several animations at once.

The current node animation weight (value between 0.0 and 1.0). If the weight is 0, then the animation

syntax: SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameRotation(#NodeAnimation, KeyFrame, x, y, z [, w, Mode])

The node animation keyframe index. The first keyframe index is zero. If the keyframe

commands.name: SetNodeAnimationKeyFrameScale
commands.description:
Changes the keyframe scale factor for the #NodeAnimation. The scale factor will be
applied to the node associated to the animation.

parameters.name: #NodeAnimation
parameters.description: The node animation to use.

parameters.name: #Keyframe
parameters.description:
The node animation keyframe index. The first keyframe index is zero. If the keyframe
doesn't exists, this function has no effect.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The new keyframe 'x' scale factor. If this value is 1.0, no scaling will be applied on the 'x' axis.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The new keyframe 'y' scale factor. If this value is 1.0, no scaling will be applied on the 'y' axis.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: The new keyframe 'z' scale factor. If this value is 1.0, no scaling will be applied on the 'z' axis.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The scale factor will resize the node by multiplying its size with the given factor:

- a scale factor of 1.0 will not affect the size of the node

- a scale factor of 2.0 will double the size of the node

- a scale factor of 0.5 will half the size of the node

parameters.name: Length
