commands.name: ErrorAddress
commands.description:
Returns the memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error.
This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall() or OnErrorGoto().
commands.returnValue: The memory address of the assembly instruction that caused the current error.

commands.name: ErrorCode
commands.description:
Returns the error code of the currently handled error. This command only returns a meaningful value
if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall() or OnErrorGoto().
commands.returnValue:
One of the following values:

#PB_OnError_InvalidMemory : Read or write operation on an invalid location
#PB_OnError_Floatingpoint : Floating-point error
#PB_OnError_Breakpoint : Debugger breakpoint reached (non-PureBasic breakpoints)
#PB_OnError_IllegalInstruction : Attempt to execute an illegal instruction
#PB_OnError_PriviledgedInstruction: Attempt to execute a privileged (system-) instruction
#PB_OnError_DivideByZero : Division by zero (Windows only)

Linux and Mac OSX report #PB_OnError_Floatingpoint for division by zero errors.

In addition, every OS may have more possible error values. On Windows, custom errors can be raised with
the RaiseError() command.

commands.name: ErrorFile
commands.description:
Returns the filename of the source code or includefile where the current error occurred.
This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall() or OnErrorGoto().

The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual file name.
To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options
or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling
from the command-line.
commands.returnValue:
The filename of the error, or "OnError line support disabled" if the OnError lines support is disabled.
(A simple way to check if the OnError lines support is enabled is to check if the result of ErrorLine() is not -1.)

commands.name: ErrorLine
commands.description:
Returns the line number in the source code where the current error occurred.
This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall() or OnErrorGoto().

The tracking of line numbers needs to be enabled on compilation for this command to return the actual line number.
To enable this feature, enable the "Enable OnError lines support" checkbox in the compiler options
or specify the /LINENUMBERING (Windows) or --linenumbering (Linux, Mac OSX) command-line switch when compiling
from the command-line.
commands.returnValue: The line number of the error, or -1 if the OnError lines support is disabled.

commands.name: ErrorMessage
commands.description: Returns an error-message for the given error code in english.

parameters.name: ErrorCode (optional)
parameters.description: A specific error code. See ErrorCode() for the available error codes.

commands.returnValue:
The message for the currently handled error. If the 'ErrorCode' parameter is set,
an english error-message for this specific error will be returned.

commands.name: ErrorRegister
commands.description:
Returns the content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error.
This command only returns a meaningful value if there was an error handled by OnErrorCall() or OnErrorGoto().

parameters.name: Register
parameters.description:
The available register constants depend on the CPU type for which the program is compiled. The following values are available:

x86:

#PB_OnError_EAX
#PB_OnError_EBX
#PB_OnError_ECX
#PB_OnError_EDX
#PB_OnError_EBP
#PB_OnError_ESI
#PB_OnError_EDI
#PB_OnError_ESP
#PB_OnError_Flags

x64:

#PB_OnError_RAX
#PB_OnError_RCX
#PB_OnError_RDX
#PB_OnError_RBX
#PB_OnError_RSP
#PB_OnError_RBP
#PB_OnError_RSI
#PB_OnError_RDI
#PB_OnError_R8
#PB_OnError_R9
...
#PB_OnError_R15
#PB_OnError_Flags

commands.returnValue: The content of the specified CPU register at the time of the error.

commands.name: ErrorTargetAddress
commands.description:
After an error with the code #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory, this command returns the memory address which
was read/written when the error occurred. This command has no meaning for other error codes.
commands.returnValue: The memory address which was read/written when the error occurred, after a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error.

commands.name: ExamineAssembly
commands.description:
Initializes the disassembling at the given address or address range.

Important: The disassembly commands use the Udis86 disassembler library
to decode the instructions. This library is released under the BSD license which can be viewed here.
If ExamineAssembly() and the related commands are used in a program that is to be made public, the above linked
licence text must be included with the software.

parameters.name: *Address
parameters.description: The address of the first instruction to disassemble.

parameters.name: *EndAddress (optional)
parameters.description:
If specified, the disassembling will end (NextInstruction() will return zero) as soon as *EndAddress is reached.
If not specified, the disassembling will run until NextInstruction() is no longer called.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if disassembling is possible, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
DisableDebugger ; do not disassemble any debugger related instructions
  
  Code_Start:
    ; Place code to be disassembled here
    a = (Random(100) * 5) + 2000
  Code_End:
  
  Text$ = "Disassembled code: " + Chr(13)  
  If ExamineAssembly(?Code_Start, ?Code_End)
    While NextInstruction()
      Text$ + RSet(Hex(InstructionAddress()), SizeOf(Integer)*2, "0")
      Text$ + " " + InstructionString() + Chr(13)
    Wend
  EndIf
  
  MessageRequester("Result", Text$)

commands.name: InstructionAddress
commands.description: Returns the address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction().
commands.returnValue: The address of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to NextInstruction().

commands.name: InstructionString
commands.description:
Returns a string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to
NextInstruction().
commands.returnValue:
A string representation of the instruction that was disassembled by a call to
NextInstruction().

commands.name: NextInstruction
commands.description:
Disassembles the next instruction after a call to ExamineAssembly(). Information
about the disassembled instruction can be read with InstructionString() and
InstructionAddress().
commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the instruction was successfully disassembled, zero otherwise ('*EndAddress'
that was specified in ExamineAssembly() was reached).

commands.name: OnErrorCall
commands.description:
Changes the action taken if an error occurs to call the specified handler procedure. The handler
can display information about the error to the user using the commands of this library and do any
needed cleanup to shutdown the application. The program will end as soon as the handler returns.

parameters.name: @ErrorHandler()
parameters.description:
The address of a procedure of the following form:

Procedure ErrorHandler()
; Your code here
EndProcedure

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Procedure ErrorHandler()
    MessageRequester("OnError test", "The following error happened: " + ErrorMessage())
  EndProcedure

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "Test start")

  OnErrorCall(@ErrorHandler())
  Pokes(10, "Hello World") ; Cause a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "This should never be displayed")

commands.name: OnErrorDefault
commands.description:
Changes the action taken when an error occurs back to the system default. This usually means displaying
an error dialog and exiting the program, but it may also mean to just ignore certain errors. To exit
the program on every error, use OnErrorExit().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
When using the OnError library inside a DLL the best practice is to set the error handler
at the beginning of every public DLL function and reset it back to the default with this command
before returning to the caller to make sure there is no interference between the OnError library and
any exception handling done by the calling program.
commands.example:
Procedure ErrorHandler()
    MessageRequester("OnError test", "The following error happened: " + ErrorMessage())
  EndProcedure

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "Test start")

  OnErrorCall(@ErrorHandler())
  OnErrorDefault()         ; Comment this to get the handler call instead of the system error handling
  Pokes(10, "Hello World") ; Cause a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "This should never be displayed")

commands.name: OnErrorExit
commands.description:
Changes the action taken if an error occurs to directly exit the program, even if the default action
on the system is not to exit the program on this kind of error. The system may display an error dialog
or print an error-message on the console on exit.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
To exit the program silently and suppress any system message, use OnErrorCall() and
end the program from the error handler.
commands.example:
MessageRequester("OnError test", "Test start")

  OnErrorExit()
  Pokes(10, "Hello World") ; Cause a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "This should never be displayed")

commands.name: OnErrorGoto
commands.description:
Changes the action taken when an error occurs to jump to the specified label address and continue
program execution there. After the jump to the label, the functions of this library can be used
to get further information about the error.

parameters.name: ?LabelAddress
parameters.description: The address of a label in the program to jump to.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The program stack will not be adjusted before jumping to the label, so local variables
should not be accessed as they may not be reachable anymore. It is also not safe to continue normal
program execution after an error as things like the return address of a procedure may be wrong
if the stack is no longer correct. The best practice is just to gather and display information
about the error and then exit the program.
commands.example:
MessageRequester("OnError test", "Test start")

  OnErrorGoto(?ErrorHandler)
  Pokes(10, "Hello World") ; Cause a #PB_OnError_InvalidMemory error

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "This should never be displayed")
  End

  ErrorHandler:
  MessageRequester("OnError test", "The following error happened: " + ErrorMessage())
  End

commands.name: RaiseError
commands.description:
Artificially create the given error. The appropriate error action will be taken (call of the error handler
or program termination by the system if no handler is set). The ErrorNumber will be available inside the
error handler with the ErrorCode() command.

parameters.name: ErrorNumber
parameters.description:
On Windows, the error number can include application defined errors. The value can be between 0 and 268435455 (a 27bit number).
On Linux or Mac OSX, only the following errors can be raised:

#PB_OnError_InvalidMemory : Read or write operation on an invalid location
#PB_OnError_Floatingpoint : Floating-point error
#PB_OnError_Breakpoint : Debugger breakpoint reached (non-PureBasic breakpoints)
#PB_OnError_IllegalInstruction : Attempt to execute an illegal instruction
#PB_OnError_PriviledgedInstruction: Attempt to execute a privileged (system-) instruction

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Procedure ErrorHandler()
    MessageRequester("OnError test", "The following error happened: " + ErrorMessage())
  EndProcedure

  MessageRequester("OnError test", "Test start")

  OnErrorCall(@ErrorHandler())
  RaiseError(#PB_OnError_InvalidMemory)
  
  MessageRequester("OnError test", "This should never be displayed")

commands.name: AddPackDirectory
commands.description: Add a new empty directory to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: DirectoryName$
parameters.description: The empty directory name to be added to the pack.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the empty directory has been successfully added to the packfile.

commands.name: AddPackFile
commands.description:
Add and compress the file to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack().
Adding a large file can take a long time. PackerCallback() can be used to monitor or abort the compression.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename$ to add to the pack.

parameters.name: PackedFilename$
parameters.description: The filename to use in the archive to store the file.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the file has been successfully added to the packfile.
If the file can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.
commands.example:
UseZipPacker()
  
  Path$ = #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/" ; path to the PureBasic examples data/media files
  PackFile$ = GetTemporaryDirectory() + "PureBasicTest.zip"  ; path to the pack file which should be created and opened later
  If CreatePack(0, PackFile$)
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "Data/world.png", "Data/world.png")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "Data/test.pref", "Data/test.pref")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "Data/CdPlayer.ico", "Data/CdPlayer.ico")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "2DDrawing.pb", "2DDrawing.pb")
    ClosePack(0)
    Debug "PackFile successfully created: " + PackFile$
  Else
    Debug "Error creating the pack file!"
  EndIf
  
  Path$ = GetTemporaryDirectory() + "PureBasicTestTree/"  ; path to a directory into which the pack files should be extracted
  If OpenPack(0, PackFile$)
    If (CreateDirectory(Path$) And CreateDirectory(Path$ + "Data/")) Or FileSize(Path$ + "Data/") = -2
      If ExaminePack(0)
        Debug "Extracting archive into: " + Path$
        While NextPackEntry(0)
         Debug " - date: " + FormatDate("%mm/%dd/%yyyy %hh:%ii:%ss", PackEntryDate(0))
         Debug " - name: " + PackEntryName(0) + ", size: " + PackEntrySize(0)
          If UncompressPackFile(0, Path$ + PackEntryName(0), PackEntryName(0)) = -1
            Debug "Error: unsuccessful unpacking of file: " + PackEntryName(0)
          EndIf
        Wend
      Else
        Debug "Error examining the pack file!"
      EndIf
      ClosePack(0)
      RunProgram(Path$)  ; open the directory with the unpacked files
    Else
      Debug "Error while creating the folder to unpack the archive contents!"  
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Error opening the pack file!"
  EndIf

commands.name: AddPackMemory
commands.description:
Add and compress the memory buffer to the specified pack previously created with CreatePack().
PackerCallback() can be used to monitor or abort the compression.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to add to the pack.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the memory to add to the pack.

parameters.name: PackedFilename$
parameters.description: The filename to use in the archive to store the memory buffer.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the buffer has been successfully added to the packfile.
If the memory buffer can't be compressed, it will be stored as is in the packfile.

commands.name: CatchPack
commands.description:
Open a previously existing pack file from memory. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered
with one of the following command: UseZipPacker(), UseLzmaPacker(), UseTarPacker(), UseBriefLZPacker().
Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description:
A number to identify pack file to open. #PB_Any can be used as
a parameter to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: *MemoryAddress
parameters.description: The memory address where the pack file is located.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the pack file in bytes.

parameters.name: Plugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The plugin to use, if more than one packer plugin has been registered. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_PackerPlugin_BriefLZ: use the BriefLZ packer to open the pack file. UseBriefLZPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip : use the Zip packer to open the pack file. UseZipPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma : use the Lzma packer to open the pack file. UseLzmaPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Tar : use the Tar packer to open the pack file. UseTarPacker() has to be called to have any effect.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any
was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

commands.name: ClosePack
commands.description: Close the specified pack file.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to close. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining packs are closed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining opened packs are automatically closed when the program ends.

commands.name: CompressMemory
syntax: Result = CompressMemory(*Buffer, Size, *Output, OutputSize [, Plugin [, Level]])
commands.description:
Compress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be
at least as long as the buffer to compress. PackerCallback() can be used to monitor or abort the compression.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to compress.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the memory to compress.

parameters.name: *Output
parameters.description: The memory buffer to store the compressed data.

parameters.name: OutputSize
parameters.description: The memory buffer size to store the compressed data.

parameters.name: Plugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The plugin to use, if more than one packer plugin has been registered. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_PackerPlugin_BriefLZ: use the BriefLZ packer to compress the memory. UseBriefLZPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip : use the Zip packer to compress the memory. UseZipPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma : use the Lzma packer to compress the memory. UseLzmaPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.

parameters.name: Level (optional)
parameters.description:
The compression level to use. It is an integer value ranging from 0 (lower compression ratio, faster compression) to 9 (higher compression ratio,
slower compression).

commands.returnValue:
Return the compressed size if the buffer has been successfully compressed, zero otherwise.
If the buffer data can't be compressed (already compressed data generally don't compress anymore), it will return zero.

commands.name: CreatePack
commands.description:
Create a new empty pack file. If the file already exists, it will be replaced with a new empty file.
Before creating a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered with one of the following
command: UseZipPacker(), UseBriefLZPacker().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new pack file. #PB_Any can be used as
a parameter to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename for the new pack file.

parameters.name: Plugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The plugin to use, if more than one packer plugin has been registered. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_PackerPlugin_BriefLZ: use the BriefLZ packer to create the pack file. UseBriefLZPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip : use the Zip packer to create the pack file. UseZipPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma : use the Lzma packer to create the pack file (also known as 7z archive). UseLzmaPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Tar : use the Tar packer to create the pack file. UseTarPacker() has to be called to register the plugin.
It can be combined with #PB_Packer_Gzip or #PB_Packer_Bzip2 to create compressed tar archive.

parameters.name: Level (optional)
parameters.description:
The compression level to use. It is an integer value ranging from 0 (lower compression ratio, faster compression) to 9 (higher compression ratio,
slower compression).

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any
was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

UseZipPacker()

; Create the packed file
If CreatePack(0, "mycompressedfiles.zip")

; add your files
AddPackFile(0, "Image1.bmp", "Image1.bmp")
AddPackFile(0, "Image2.bmp", "Image2.bmp")
AddPackFile(0, "mywave1.wav", "mywave1.wav")
AddPackFile(0, "mywave2.wav", "mywave2.wav")
ClosePack(0)
EndIf

commands.name: ExaminePack
commands.description:
Start to examine the pack content. NextPackEntry() has to be called to list the entries found
in the pack file. The pack has to be previously opened with OpenPack() or CatchPack(). Packs being created
with CreatePack() can not be examined.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the pack can be examined, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
UseZipPacker()

  ; Open the packed file
  If OpenPack(0, "mycompressedfiles.zip") 
    
    ; List all the entries
    If ExaminePack(0)
      While NextPackEntry(0)
        Debug "Name: " + PackEntryName(0) + ", Size: " + PackEntrySize(0)
      Wend
    EndIf
    
    ClosePack(0)
  EndIf

commands.name: IsPack
commands.description: Tests if the given pack number is a valid and correctly initialized pack.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to test.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #Pack is a valid pack and zero if not.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value.
This is the correct way to ensure an pack is ready to use.

commands.name: NextPackEntry
commands.description:
Go to the next entry in the pack file. ExaminePack() has to be called before calling this command.
To get more information about the current entry, use PackEntrySize(), PackEntryType() and PackEntryName().
To uncompress the current entry, use UncompressPackMemory() or UncompressPackFile().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the pack contain another entry, zero otherwise.

commands.name: OpenPack
commands.description:
Open a previously existing pack file. Before opening a pack file, at least one packer has to be registered
with one of the following command: UseZipPacker(), UseLzmaPacker(), UseTarPacker(), UseBriefLZPacker().
Once opened, the pack content can be listed with ExaminePack().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description:
A number to identify pack file to open. #PB_Any can be used as
a parameter to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename for the pack file to open.

parameters.name: Plugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The plugin to use, if more than one packer plugin has been registered. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_PackerPlugin_BriefLZ: use the BriefLZ packer to open the pack file. UseBriefLZPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip : use the Zip packer to open the pack file. UseZipPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma : use the Lzma packer to open the pack file. UseLzmaPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Tar : use the Tar packer to open the pack file. UseTarPacker() has to be called to have any effect.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the pack file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any
was used as the #Pack parameter then the generated pack number is returned.

UseZipPacker()

; Open the packed file
If OpenPack(0, "mycompressedfiles.zip")

; List all the entries
If ExaminePack(0)
While NextPackEntry(0)
Debug "Name: " + PackEntryName(0) + ", Size: " + PackEntrySize(0)
Wend
EndIf

ClosePack(0)
EndIf

commands.name: PackEntryDate
commands.description: Returns the file date of the current pack entry, set with NextPackEntry().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: DateType (optional)
parameters.description:
The type of the date to return. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Date_Created : returns the file creation date.
#PB_Date_Accessed: returns the last file access date.
#PB_Date_Modified: returns the last file modification date (Standard).

commands.returnValue: Returns the file date or -1 if no date is available.
commands.example: For an example see the AddPackFile() command.

commands.name: PackEntryName
commands.description: Returns the name of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the name of the current entry.

commands.name: PackEntrySize
commands.description: Returns the size of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The size type to get. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Packer_UncompressedSize: returns the uncompressed size of the entry (default).
#PB_Packer_CompressedSize : returns the compressed size of the entry.
This is only supported for BriefLZ archives.

commands.returnValue: Returns the size of the current entry.

commands.name: PackEntryType
commands.description: Returns the type of the current entry, set with NextPackEntry().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns one of the following values:

#PB_Packer_File : the current entry is a file
#PB_Packer_Directory: the current entry is a directory

commands.name: PackerCallback
commands.description:
Set a callback to monitor or abort the compression for CompressMemory(), AddPackFile() and AddPackMemory().
The callback will be called at regular intervalls during the compression process.

parameters.name: @Callback()
parameters.description:
The address of a callback function to call. It must have the following form:

Procedure Callback(Current.q, Total.q)
;
; Returns #True as result to continue to compress, or #False to abort.
;
ProcedureReturn Result
EndProcedure

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
UseZipPacker()
   
  ; The callback will be called at regular intervall, to allow to display
  ; some progress or abort the compression. It must match the following declaration.
  ;
  Procedure Callback(Current.q, Total.q)
    Debug "Progress: " + Current + " bytes / "+ Total + " bytes"
    
    ProcedureReturn #True ; Returns #True to continue to compress, or #False to abort
  EndProcedure
    
  ; Install the callback for all the future packer compression  
  PackerCallback(@Callback())
  
  ; Allocate 50 GB of memory to compress it
  *Buffer = AllocateMemory(50*1024*1024, #PB_Memory_NoClear)
  
  ; The output buffer a bit bigger than source, just in case
  *Output = AllocateMemory(51*1024*1024, #PB_Memory_NoClear)

  CompressedSize = CompressMemory(*Buffer, MemorySize(*Buffer), *Output, MemorySize(*Output))

  Debug "Compressed length: " + CompressedSize + " bytes"

commands.name: UncompressMemory
commands.description:
Uncompress the buffer content into the output buffer. The output buffer length needs to be
at least as long as the buffer to uncompress.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to uncompress.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the memory to uncompress.

parameters.name: *Output
parameters.description: The memory buffer to store the uncompressed data.

parameters.name: OutputSize
parameters.description:
The memory buffer size to store the uncompressed data. It must be at least of the size of the
uncompressed data.

parameters.name: Plugin (optional)
parameters.description:
The plugin to use, if more than one packer plugin has been registered. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_PackerPlugin_BriefLZ: use the BriefLZ packer to uncompress the memory. UseBriefLZPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Zip : use the Zip packer to uncompress the memory. UseZipPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Lzma : use the Lzma packer to uncompress the memory. UseLzmaPacker() has to be called to have any effect.
#PB_PackerPlugin_Jcalg1 : use the Jcalg1 packer to uncompress the memory. UseJcalg1Packer() has to be called to have any effect.

commands.returnValue: Return the uncompressed size if the buffer has been successfully uncompressed, -1 otherwise.

commands.name: UncompressPackFile
commands.description:
Uncompress into the specified filename from the current pack entry being
examined with ExaminePack() and NextPackEntry(). If the filename already
exists, it will erased and replaced with the new uncompressed data.

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename to uncompress the current pack entry.

parameters.name: PackedFilename$ (optional)
parameters.description:
The packed filename entry to uncompress. If this parameter is not specified, the current entry being
examined with ExaminePack() and NextPackEntry() is uncompressed.

commands.returnValue: Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the filename, -1 otherwise.
commands.example:
UseZipPacker()
  
  Path$ = #PB_Compiler_Home + "examples/sources/Data/" ; path to the PureBasic examples data/media files
  PackFile$ = GetTemporaryDirectory() + "PureBasicTest.zip"  ; path to the pack file which should be created and opened later
  If CreatePack(0, PackFile$)
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "world.png", "world.png")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "test.pref", "test.pref")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "CdPlayer.ico", "CdPlayer.ico")
    AddPackFile(0, Path$ + "Background.bmp", "Background.bmp")
    ClosePack(0)
    Debug "PackFile successfully created: " + PackFile$
  Else
    Debug "Error creating the pack file!"
  EndIf
  
  Path$ = GetTemporaryDirectory() + "PureBasicTest/"  ; path to a directory into which the pack files should be extracted
  If OpenPack(0, PackFile$)
    If CreateDirectory(Path$) Or FileSize(Path$) = -2
      If ExaminePack(0)
        Debug "Extracting archive into: " + Path$
        While NextPackEntry(0)
          Debug " - name: " + PackEntryName(0) + ", size: " + PackEntrySize(0)
          If UncompressPackFile(0, Path$ + PackEntryName(0), PackEntryName(0)) = -1
            Debug "Error: unsuccessful unpacking of file: " + PackEntryName(0)
          EndIf
        Wend
      EndIf
      ClosePack(0)
      RunProgram(Path$)  ; open the directory with the unpacked files
    Else
      Debug "Error while creating the folder '" + Path$ + "' to unpack the archive contents!"
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Error opening the pack file!"
  EndIf

commands.name: UncompressPackMemory
commands.description:
Uncompress into the memory buffer from the current pack entry being
examined with ExaminePack() and NextPackEntry().

parameters.name: #Pack
parameters.description: The pack to use.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to uncompress the pack entry.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the memory to uncompress the pack entry.

parameters.name: PackedFilename$ (optional)
parameters.description:
The packed filename entry to uncompress. If this parameter is not specified, the current entry being
examined with ExaminePack() and NextPackEntry() is uncompressed.

commands.returnValue: Return the uncompressed size if the pack entry has been successfully uncompressed into the memory buffer, -1 otherwise.

commands.name: UseBriefLZPacker
commands.description:
Enable BriefLZ compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library.
The created archives are a custom format created for PureBasic.
BriefLZ compression is very fast and the packer is very small, it could be the right choice for
program which needs a small executable size. Uncompress is also very fast, but compress ratio
is not as good as Zip or Lzma.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UseJcalg1Packer
commands.description:
Enable Jcalg1 uncompress support to the packer library. This is an old algorithm which was
used in previous version of PureBasic, so it is still available to allow to support old
compressed files. Compression and archive support is no more available. This packer
is only available on Windows x86 (32-bit). This packer is deprecated and no more supported.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UseLzmaPacker
commands.description:
Enable Lzma compress, uncompress and 7z archive support to the packer library.
Lzma compression is considered as one of the best available multipurpose compression algorithm. It provides very good compress ratio
and fast uncompress. Compressing can be slow.

For more information: Wikipedia - Lzma.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UseTarPacker
commands.description:
Enable Tar compress, uncompress and Tar archive support to the packer library.
Bzip2 and Gzip compression are both supported. Compressing and uncompressing Tar archives are usually fast.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: UseZipPacker
commands.description:
Enable Zip compress, uncompress and archive support to the packer library. The created pack will be compatible
with other Zip archives in 2.0 format. The created archive size can be up to 2GB.

For more information: Wikipedia - Zip.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateParticleEmitter
syntax: Result = CreateParticleEmitter(#ParticleEmitter, Width, Height, Depth, Type, [, x.f, y.f, z.f])
commands.description: Creates a new empty particle emitter of the given size.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new particle emitter.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Width, Height, Depth
parameters.description:
The size of the new particle emitter (respectively x,y and z dimension).
The default size of the future Particles can be specified with the ParticleSize() function.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Particle_Point: The emitter is a single point
#PB_Particle_Box : The emitter is a box, with an width, height and depth

parameters.name: x, y, z (optional)
parameters.description: The initial position of the particle emitter in the world.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the particle emitter has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
If #PB_Any was used as #ParticleEmitter
parameter then the auto-generated number of the new particle emitter will be
returned.

commands.name: DisableParticleEmitter
commands.description: Enables or disables the particle emitter. When disabled, no more particle are emitted.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
It can take the following values:

#True : The particle emitter is disabled.
#False: The particle emitter is enabled.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeParticleEmitter
commands.description:
Frees the particle emitter. All its associated memory is released and this object can't be used
anymore.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining particle emitters are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining particle emitters are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetScriptParticleEmitter
commands.description: Gets a particle emitter defined in an OGRE script file.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new particle emitter. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The name of the particle emitter in the OGRE script file. This name is case-sensitive.

commands.returnValue:
Zero if the particle emitter isn't found or can't be loaded from script files. If #PB_Any is used
as '#ParticleEmitter' parameter, the new particle emitter number is returned.

commands.name: HideParticleEmitter
commands.description: Hides or shows the specified particle emitter.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description:
It can take the following values:

#True : the particle emitter is hidden
#False: the particle emitter is shown

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: IsParticleEmitter
commands.description: Tests if the given particle emitter is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the particle emitter is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a particle emitter is ready to use.

commands.name: MoveParticleEmitter
commands.description: Move the specified particle emitter.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to move.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new position of the particle emitter.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Relative: relative move, from the current particle emitter position (default).
#PB_Absolute: absolute move to the specified position.

combined with one of the following values:

#PB_Local : local move.
#PB_Parent: move relative to the parent position.
#PB_World : move relative to the world.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleAcceleration
commands.description: Changes the particles acceleration vector. It can be useful to simulate gravity, wind, etc.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The acceleration (force) vector to apply to all particles.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleAngle
commands.description: Changes the particle angle when emitted.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: RangeStart, RangeEnd
parameters.description:
The particle range (in degree) between 0 and 360. For example a range of 45 to 90 will only emit particle with
an random angle between 45 and 90 degrees.

parameters.name: SpeedRangeStart, SpeedRangeEnd
parameters.description:
Specify the rotation speed range of the emitted particle. A random rotation speed will be picked from this range when
a new particle is emitted.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
To avoid display glitchs, the particle material should be configured to be non-repeatable using
SetMaterialAttribute(Material, #PB_Material_TAM, #PB_Material_ClampTAM).

commands.name: ParticleColorFader
commands.description: Changes the particles color fader rate.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: RedRate, GreenRate, BlueRate, AlphaRate
parameters.description:
The color channels fader rate to apply, per second. Examples values and their effect:

0: no change will be applied
-1: will subtract 256 to the color component every second.
1: will add 256 to the color component every second.
-0.25: will subtract 64 to the color component every second.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleColorRange
commands.description:
Changes the particles color range for the particle emitter. Every emitted particle
will get a random value, within the 'StartColor' and 'EndColor' range (gradient
between these two color).

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: StartColor

commands.name: ParticleMaterial
commands.description:
Assigns a material to the specified particle emitter.
This material will be used by all the particles of this emitter. An
emitter can only have one material assigned at once.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: MaterialID
parameters.description: The new material to use for this particle emitter. A valid 'MaterialID' can be easily obtained with the MaterialID() function.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleScaleRate
commands.description: Changes the current particle emitter scale rate.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.description:
The new particle emitter scale rate. The default rate is 0, which means the particle will be the same size.
When using a value greater than 0, the particle size will be increase over time (each second, the rate will be added to the current size).
When using a value lower than 0, the particle size will be decreased over time (each second, the rate will be subtracted from the current size).

For example:

A rate of 10 will increase the particle size of 10 units per second.

A rate of -2 will decrease the particle size of 2 units per second.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleSize
commands.description:
Change the particles dimensions. Particles are 2D planes (billboards) which always face the
camera. All particles in an emitter always have the same size.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: Width, Size
parameters.description: The new size of the particles, in world unit.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleSpeedFactor
commands.description: Changes the current particle emitter speed factor.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: Factor
parameters.description:
The new particle emitter speed factor. The default speed factor is 1. When using a value
greater than 1, then the emitting speed will be increased. When using a value
lower than 1, then the emitting speed will be decreased. For example, using a speed factor
of 4.5, will have the particle emitting speed multiplied by 4.5.
Using a speed factor of 0.5, will have the particle emitting speed divised by 2.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleTimeToLive
commands.description:
Change the particles time to live for the particle emitter. Every particle
will live at least 'MinimumTime' and at most the 'MaximumTime' (in world time
unit). A random value, within this range, will be used by every particle emitted.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: MinimumTime
parameters.description: The minimum time for a particle before being freed.

parameters.name: MaximumTime
parameters.description: The maximum time for a particle before being freed.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ParticleVelocity

Changes the particles velocity. A random velocity value, picked in the 'Minimum' and 'Maximum' range,
will be used by every particle emitted.

parameters.name: #ParticleEmitter
parameters.description: The particle emitter to use.

parameters.name: Minimum
parameters.description: The minimum velocity for a particle.

parameters.name: Maximum
parameters.description: The maximum velocity for a particle.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ClosePreferences
commands.description: Closes a preference file previously opened with OpenPreferences() or created with CreatePreferences().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Choose the group "Window"
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
  
  ; Display the "w" key of this group
  MessageRequester("Info", "w = " + ReadPreferenceLong ("w", 0))
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: CreatePreferences
commands.description: Creates a new empty preference file. If the file already exists, the file is erased.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename of the new preference file.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Preference_NoSpace : no spaces will be put around the equal sign joining key and values.
It can be useful when dealing with external preferences files which doesn't
accept spaces around equal sign.
#PB_Preference_GroupSeparator: add an empty line between the groups to ease readability of the file.
#PB_Preference_NoBOM : Don't add the UTF-8 BOM when writing the file. The file will still be written using UTF-8 encoding.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the file has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
Once created, the functions like WritePreferenceString() can be used to write data. When values are written in preferences,
it's possible to read them back with the functions like ReadPreferenceString().

To remove a key or a group, use RemovePreferenceKey() and RemovePreferenceGroup().
To create or change the current group, use PreferenceGroup().

Once all write operations are done, ClosePreferences() needs to be called to really write the preferences back to disk.
commands.example:
; Create a preference file named Setup.ini
  CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Setup.ini")
  
  ; Create a group named "Window"
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
    WritePreferenceLong("X", 10)      ; X = 10
    WritePreferenceLong("Y", 10)      ; Y = 10
    WritePreferenceLong("W", 800)     ; W = 800
    WritePreferenceLong("H", 600)     ; H = 600
    WritePreferenceFloat("%", 20)     ; % = 20.000000
    WritePreferenceString("Title", "PureNote") ; Title = "PureNote"
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: ExaminePreferenceGroups
commands.description:
Starts the enumeration of all the groups found in the current preference file. NextPreferenceGroup()
can be used to list all the group found.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Examine groups
  ExaminePreferenceGroups()
  While NextPreferenceGroup() ; While group exists
    MessageRequester("Groups", PreferenceGroupName())  ; Display this group
  Wend
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: ExaminePreferenceKeys
commands.description:
Starts the enumeration of all the keys found in the current group of the preference file. The current group can be selected with
PreferenceGroup() or by examining all groups with ExaminePreferenceGroups().
NextPreferenceKey() can be used to list all the keys found.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the enumeration has been successfully started, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Select a group
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
  
  ; Examine keys in the group 'Window'
  ExaminePreferenceKeys()
  While NextPreferenceKey() ; While a key exists
    Debug "Key group 'Window': " + PreferenceKeyName() + " = " + PreferenceKeyValue()  ; Display the key with its data
  Wend
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: FlushPreferenceBuffers
commands.description: Ensures that all preferences changes are written to disk.
commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the preferences has been successfully written the disk. If an error occurred (ie: disk full, disk error),
it will return zero.

commands.name: NextPreferenceGroup
commands.description:
Retrieves information about the next group found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceGroups().
To get the name of the group, use PreferenceGroupName(). The current examined preference group will also be used
when values are read from the preferences or when the keys are examined with ExaminePreferenceKeys().
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if more groups are available in the current enumeration, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Examine groups
  ExaminePreferenceGroups()
  While NextPreferenceGroup() ; While group exists
    MessageRequester("Groups", PreferenceGroupName())  ; Display this group
  Wend
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: NextPreferenceKey
commands.description:
Retrieves information about the next key found in the enumeration started with ExaminePreferenceKeys().
To get the name and the value of the key, use PreferenceKeyName() and
PreferenceKeyValue().
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if more keys are available in the current enumeration, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Select a group
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
  
  ; Examine keys in the group 'Window'
  ExaminePreferenceKeys()
  While  NextPreferenceKey() ; While a key exists
    MessageRequester("Key group 'Window'", PreferenceKeyName() + " = " + PreferenceKeyValue())  ; Display the key with its data
  Wend
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: OpenPreferences
commands.description: Opens a previously existing preference file.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename of the preference file.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Preference_NoSpace: no spaces will be put around the equal sign joining key and values.
It can be useful when dealing with external preferences files which doesn't
accept spaces around equal sign.
#PB_Preference_GroupSeparator: add an empty line between the groups to ease readability of the file.

parameters.name: Encoding (optional)
parameters.description:
To force a string encoding when reading the preference file. If an UTF-8 BOM is found in at the start of
the file, this parameter is ignored and UTF-8 will be used. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_UTF8 : The file will be read as UTF-8, even if it doesn't have a BOM.
#PB_Ascii: The file will be read as Ascii, unless there an UTF-8 BOM. If the preferences are written back to file, it will be using UTF-8.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the file has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
If the file wasn't found or can't be opened, it is still possible to use the read functions and it
will return the specified default value. It is very useful to initialize in one step the program variables.
The functions like ReadPreferenceString() can be used to read the preference values stored in the file.

To remove a key or a group, use RemovePreferenceKey() and RemovePreferenceGroup().
To create or change the current group, use PreferenceGroup().

It is possible to change existing values with WritePreferenceString() and similar functions.

Once all write operations are done, ClosePreferences() needs to be called to really write the preferences back to disk
(if it has been modified inbetween).
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Examine Groups
  ExaminePreferenceGroups()
  ; For each group
  While NextPreferenceGroup()
    text$ = text$ + PreferenceGroupName() + #LF$ ; its name
    ; Examine keys for the current group  
    ExaminePreferenceKeys()
    ; For each key  
    While  NextPreferenceKey()                      
      text$ = text$ + PreferenceKeyName() + " = " + PreferenceKeyValue() + #LF$ ; its name and its data
    Wend
    text$ = text$ + #LF$
  Wend

  ; Display all groups and all keys with data
  MessageRequester("test.pref", text$)

  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: PreferenceComment
commands.description: Writes a new comment line in the current preference file.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The new comment to write.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Creating the file prefs.txt
  If CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")

    PreferenceComment("The coordinates of the window.") ; Write a comment
    PreferenceComment("") ; Write a comment (empty line)

    PreferenceGroup("Window")
      WritePreferenceLong ("X", 100)
      WritePreferenceLong ("Y", 125)

      ClosePreferences()
    
      RunProgram(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")
  EndIf

commands.name: PreferenceGroup
commands.description:
Creates a new group (in the form: [Name$]) or changes the current group in the preference file.
All following read or write operations will be restricted to this group.
To move outside of any groups, an empty 'Name$' can be used.

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The new group name.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the group was already created, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
If the group does not exist yet, it will not be created immediately. It will instead be created once
the first key is written to it. This allows to use the PreferenceGroup() function to test if a group exists
without creating many empty groups. The group search is case-insensitive.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Select a group
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
  
  ; Examine keys in the group 'Window'
  ExaminePreferenceKeys()
  While  NextPreferenceKey() ; While a key exists
    MessageRequester("Keys from the 'Window' group", PreferenceKeyName() + " = " + PreferenceKeyValue())  ; Display the key with its data
  Wend
  
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: PreferenceGroupName
commands.description: Returns the name of the current group being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceGroups() or previously selected with PreferenceGroup().
commands.returnValue: The name of the current group being enumerated with ExaminePreferenceGroups() or previously selected with PreferenceGroup().
commands.example:

  While NextPreferenceGroup() ; While group exists

  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: PreferenceKeyName

To get the value of the key, use PreferenceKeyValue().

commands.name: PreferenceKeyValue

commands.name: ReadPreferenceDouble
commands.description: Try to read the specified associated 'Key$' value.

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description: The key to read the value from. If the key is inside a group, PreferenceGroup() has to be used to change the current group.

parameters.name: DefaultValue
parameters.description:
The default value to return if the key isn't found or the
preference file haven't been opened correctly (file missing for example).

commands.returnValue:
The value associated to the specified key, as a double number. if the key isn't found
the default value is returned.
commands.example:
; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(#PB_Compiler_Home +"examples/sources/Data/test.pref")
  
  ; Open the group 'Window'
  PreferenceGroup("Window")
  
  ; Examine keys until w = 800
  NextPreferenceKey() ; x = 0
  NextPreferenceKey() ; y = 0
  NextPreferenceKey() ; w = 800
  
  ; Read the key
  key$ = PreferenceKeyName()
  
  ; Display the key and its data with different format
  MessageRequester("Integer key", Str(ReadPreferenceInteger(key$, 0)))
  MessageRequester("Float key", StrF(ReadPreferenceFloat(key$, 0), 6))
  MessageRequester("Double key", StrD(ReadPreferenceDouble(key$, 0), 15))
  MessageRequester("Long key", Str(ReadPreferenceLong(key$, 0)))
  MessageRequester("Quad key", Str(ReadPreferenceQuad(key$, 0)))
  MessageRequester("String key", ReadPreferenceString(key$, "0"))
    
  ; Close the preference file
  ClosePreferences()

commands.name: RemovePreferenceGroup
commands.description: Removes the specified 'Group$' and all its keys.

parameters.name: Group$
parameters.description: The group name to remove.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Create the preference file prefs.txt
  If CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt", #PB_Preference_GroupSeparator)

    PreferenceGroup("Window")
      WritePreferenceLong ("X", 100)
      WritePreferenceLong ("Y", 125)
      WritePreferenceString("Title", "PureNote")
      
      PreferenceGroup("event")
      WritePreferenceString("percentage", "percentage")
      WritePreferenceFloat("%", 100)
      
    ClosePreferences()
    
    RunProgram(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")
  EndIf  
    
  MessageRequester("Info", "Delete the group 'event' ")
  
  ; Open a preference file
  OpenPreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")
  
  ; Delete the group 'event'  
  RemovePreferenceGroup("event")
  
  ClosePreferences()
    
  RunProgram(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")

  MessageRequester("Info", "Delete the key 'Title' ")
