commands.name: WritePreferenceDouble
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated double value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The double value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example: See the example at WritePreferenceFloat()

commands.name: WritePreferenceFloat
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated float value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The float value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Create the preference file prefs.txt
  If CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt", #PB_Preference_GroupSeparator)
    PreferenceGroup("Window")
      WritePreferenceString("Title", "PureNote") 
      WritePreferenceLong ("X", 100)
      WritePreferenceLong ("Y", 125)
      WritePreferenceInteger("I", 1024) 
      WritePreferenceQuad("Q", 9223372036854775807)
      WritePreferenceFloat("%", 20.10)
      WritePreferenceDouble("D", 0.0123456789 )
    ClosePreferences()   
    RunProgram(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"Prefs.txt")
  EndIf

commands.name: WritePreferenceInteger
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated integer value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The integer value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Create a 'test.ini' preference file in the users temp folder.
  ; Since we don't store many values, we don't create PreferenceGroups...
  If CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"test.ini")
    WritePreferenceInteger("x", 35)
    WritePreferenceInteger("y", 46)
    WritePreferenceInteger("w", 200)
    WritePreferenceInteger("h", 100)
    ClosePreferences()
  Else
    Debug "Error: Can't create the 'test.ini' file!"
  EndIf
  
  ; Read that file and output the values
  If OpenPreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"test.ini")
    Debug ReadPreferenceInteger("x", 0)
    Debug ReadPreferenceInteger("y", 0)
    Debug ReadPreferenceInteger("w", 400)
    Debug ReadPreferenceInteger("h", 600)
    ClosePreferences()
  Else
    Debug "Error: Can't open the 'test.ini' file!"
  EndIf

commands.name: WritePreferenceLong
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated long value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The long value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example: See the example at WritePreferenceFloat()

commands.name: WritePreferenceQuad
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated float value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The quad value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example: See the example at WritePreferenceFloat()

commands.name: WritePreferenceString
commands.description:
Creates or changes the specified key and its associated string value under the form: 'Key$ = Value' in the
preference file, previously created with CreatePreferences() or opened
with OpenPreferences().

parameters.name: Key$
parameters.description:
The key name to write. If PreferenceGroup() has been
used, then the write is restricted to the current group. If the key was already created,
its associated value is replaced with the new specified value.

parameters.name: Value$
parameters.description: The string value to associate with the key.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
; Create a 'ColorList.ini' preference file
  ; Note: In this case the data values must be unique (no duplicate keys).
  If CreatePreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"ColorList.ini", #PB_Preference_NoSpace)
    WritePreferenceString("FF0000", "")
    WritePreferenceString("00FF00", "")
    WritePreferenceString("0000FF", "")
    WritePreferenceString("FF00FF", "")
    ClosePreferences()
  Else
    Debug "Error: Can't create the 'ColorList.ini' file!"
  EndIf
  
  ; Read the 'ColorList.ini' file and output the keys (which are the data here)
  If OpenPreferences(GetTemporaryDirectory()+"ColorList.ini")
    ExaminePreferenceKeys()
    While NextPreferenceKey()
      Debug PreferenceKeyName()
    Wend
    ClosePreferences()
  Else
    Debug "Error: Can't read the 'ColorList.ini' file!"
  EndIf

commands.name: DefaultPrinter
commands.description:
Selects the default printer as the current printer for print operation. This function has to be
called before all other printer functions. Once DefaultPrinter() has been successfully called, StartPrinting() is used to actually start printing.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if a default printer is available, zero otherwise.

commands.name: NewPrinterPage
commands.description:
Creates a new empty page. The previous page is sent to the printer and can't be modified anymore. It has to be called inside a
StartDrawing()/StopDrawing() block.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If PrintRequester()
    If StartPrinting("Two sheets")
      If StartDrawing(PrinterOutput())
        DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_Transparent)
        DrawText(10, 10, "First page !", RGB(0, 0, 0))
        
        ; Tell the printer to start a new page
        NewPrinterPage()
        
        DrawText(10, 10, "Second page !", RGB(0, 0, 0))
        
        StopDrawing()
      EndIf
      
      StopPrinting()
    EndIf
  EndIf

commands.name: PrinterOutput
commands.description:
Returns the OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartDrawing() function.
Drawing on the printer will be performed using pixel based drawing operations.
commands.returnValue: The OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartDrawing() function.
commands.remarks:
Drawing on a printer using pixel based drawing may reduce printing quality and adds
extra complexity because the printers resolution must be taken into account. Vector based
drawing using PrinterVectorOutput() should be preferred, as it provides resolution independent
functions for high-quality printing.
commands.example:
StartDrawing(PrinterOutput())
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopDrawing()

commands.name: PrinterPageHeight
commands.description: Returns the height of the drawing area.
commands.returnValue:
The height of the drawing area, in pixels. The number changes with the DPI of the printer. This means
than a document printed at 75 DPI will have a drawing area 4 times smaller than a document printed at
150 DPI. This value refers to the client area, the one you can write on. It doesn't count the
hardware printer margins, but doesn't add any 'soft' margins.

commands.name: PrinterPageWidth
commands.description: Return the width of the drawing area.
commands.returnValue:
The width of the drawing area, in pixels. The number changes with the DPI of the printer. This means
than a document printed at 75 DPI will have a drawing area 4 times smaller than a document printed at
150 DPI. This value refers to the client area, the one you can write on. It doesn't count the
hardware printer margins, but doesn't add any 'soft' margins.

commands.name: PrinterVectorOutput
commands.description: Returns the OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartVectorDrawing() function.

parameters.name: Unit (optional)
parameters.description:
Specifies the unit used for measuring distances on the drawing output.
The default unit for printer output is #PB_Unit_Point.

#PB_Unit_Pixel : Values are measured in pixels (or dots in case of a printer)
#PB_Unit_Point : Values are measured in points (1/72 inch)
#PB_Unit_Inch : Values are measured in inches
#PB_Unit_Millimeter: Values are measured in millimeters

commands.returnValue: The OutputID of the current printer to be used with the StartVectorDrawing() function.
commands.example:
StartVectorDrawing(PrinterVectorOutput(#PB_Unit_Point))
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopVectorDrawing()

commands.name: PrintRequester
commands.description:
Open a regular print requester, to choose the printer and do some adjustments. This function must be
called before all other printer functions. Once PrintRequester() has been successfully called,
StartPrinting() is used to actually start printing.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the user successfully selected a printer, zero otherwise.

commands.name: StartPrinting
commands.description: Initializes the printer and starts the print operation.

parameters.name: JobName$
parameters.description: The name to be shown in the printer spooler and which identifys the new print operation.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the print operation has been started successfully, zero otherwise.

commands.name: StopPrinting
commands.description: Stop all the print operations and send the data to the printer.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AvailableProgramOutput
commands.description: Returns the number of bytes available to be read from the programs output.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() using the #PB_Program_Read flag.

commands.returnValue: The number of bytes available to be read from the programs output.
commands.remarks:
The output may be read with either ReadProgramString() or ReadProgramData().

However, ReadProgramString() or ReadProgramData() remains blocked indefinitely if the
program requests the intervention of the user. For example, return a yes/no choice to
the program to continue.

commands.name: CloseProgram
commands.description:
Closes the connection with the given program (which was started with RunProgram())
and frees all related data.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to close. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This does not terminate the program, it only closes the connection with it. To terminate the program,
call KillProgram() first. Also if the program terminated normally, this function must still be
called to properly release all data.

If the program was started with the #PB_Program_Write flag, CloseProgram() will cause the program
to receive an EOF (end of file) on its standard input. This condition can also be produced without directly
closing the connection to the program by calling WriteProgramData() with the special
#PB_Program_Eof value.

commands.name: CountProgramParameters
commands.description: Returns the number of parameters specified on the command line (or via RunProgram()).
commands.returnValue: The number of parameters specified on the command line (or via RunProgram()).
commands.remarks: ProgramParameter() may be used to read the individual parameters.

commands.name: EnvironmentVariableName
commands.description:
Returns the name of the current environment variable currently examined
with ExamineEnvironmentVariables() and NextEnvironmentVariable().
EnvironmentVariableValue() may be used to return its value.
commands.returnValue:
The name of the current environment variable currently examined
with ExamineEnvironmentVariables() and NextEnvironmentVariable().

commands.name: EnvironmentVariableValue
commands.description:
Returns the value of the current environment variable currently examined
with ExamineEnvironmentVariables() and NextEnvironmentVariable().
EnvironmentVariableName() may be used to return its name.
commands.returnValue:
The value of the current environment variable currently examined
with ExamineEnvironmentVariables() and NextEnvironmentVariable().

commands.name: ExamineEnvironmentVariables
commands.description:
Starts to examine the environment block of the program.

NextEnvironmentVariable(), EnvironmentVariableName()
and EnvironmentVariableValue() may be used to read the individual environment variables.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the environment block can be read, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; Will output all environment variables of the program
  ;
  OpenConsole()
  If ExamineEnvironmentVariables()
    While NextEnvironmentVariable()
      PrintN(EnvironmentVariableName() + " = " + EnvironmentVariableValue())
    Wend
  EndIf
  PrintN("")
  PrintN("Press Enter to quit.")
  Input()

commands.name: GetEnvironmentVariable
commands.description: Returns the content of the specified environment variable from the programs environment block.

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The name of the environment variable to get.

commands.returnValue: The environment variable value, or an empty string if the environment variable does not exist.

commands.name: IsProgram
commands.description: Tests if the given program is a program that is executed by the RunProgram() function.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the program is executed by the RunProgram() function, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value.

commands.name: KillProgram
commands.description: Immediately terminates the given program (which was previously started with RunProgram()).

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to kill. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This terminates the program, but it does not close the connection with the program object of
the terminated program. CloseProgram() must still be called to properly free all data
associated with the program.

commands.name: NextEnvironmentVariable
commands.description:
This function must be called after ExamineEnvironmentVariables().
It will go step-by-step through the environment variables of the program.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if there is still more variables to read, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
Use EnvironmentVariableName() and
EnvironmentVariableValue() to get the name and content of the current
variable.

commands.name: ProgramExitCode
commands.description: Returns the exitcode that was returned when the given program ended.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

commands.returnValue: The exitcode that was returned when the specified program ended.
commands.remarks:
This function should only be used after the given program has ended.
Use ProgramRunning() or WaitProgram() to make sure of that.

The exitcode allows for a single value to be returned from the program, back to the program that
executed it. This is usually used to indicate either the error or the success of the program.
Please note, that due to OS limitation on OS X and Linux the supported exitcode are in the range of 0 - 255.

To return an exitcode from a PB program, use the optional value with the End statement:

End 1 ; returns the exitcode 1

commands.name: ProgramFilename
commands.description:
Returns the full path and filename of this program and may be used to find where the program is
installed or the executable name. GetPathPart() or GetFilePart() may be used to get the path or filename
of the program from the return string.
commands.returnValue:
The full path and filename of this program.

If used inside a DLL, this function returns the path and filename of the DLL, not the main program
that loaded it.

commands.name: ProgramID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier for the given program. This is the so called "Process ID" or "PID".

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

commands.returnValue:
The unique system identifier for the given program.

If the identifier cannot be returned, -1 will be returned.

This will happen if RunProgram() is used to open a file in another program, like
RunProgram("Source.pb").

Note: the value returned here is not a handle (unlike with most other ...ID() functions). Rather, it is
the Process ID which may be viewed within the Taskmanager. To get a process handle, use the OpenProcess_() API.

Note: The returned value may be false if the process is launched by a wrapper as is the
case with Windows 10 and UWP (Universal Windows Platform) applications launched by
ApplicationFrameHost.exe (AFH).

commands.name: ProgramParameter
commands.description: Gets the next parameter string that was passed to the executable when it was launched.

parameters.name: Index (optional)
parameters.description: If specified, the parameter for that index will be returned. The first parameter index starts from 0.

commands.returnValue:
The next parameter value, or an empty string if no more parameters are found. If index is specified
it will return the specified parameter value.
commands.remarks:
This function is especially useful for console programs, where the user passes
one or more parameter at the program start.

Note: Relying on the return of an empty string to detect the last parameter is not a good practice,
since the function also returns an empty string if an empty string was passed in "" on the command-line.
The preferred method which should be used to get all parameters, is to get the count with CountProgramParameters()
and then to call ProgramParameter() as often as needed.

To check the behaviour of this function, or do several tests, please read the 'Executable command-line' paragraph
in the page IDE Compiler options.
commands.example:
MyProgram.exe MyText.txt /FAST "Special Mode"

If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 520, 510, "Example...", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    EditorGadget(0, 5, 5, 510, 500, #PB_Editor_WordWrap)
    path$ = ProgramParameter()
    If FileSize(path$) >= 0
      If ReadFile(0, path$)
        Text$ = ReadString(0, #PB_File_IgnoreEOL)
      EndIf
      SetGadgetText(0, Text$)
    EndIf
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ProgramRunning
commands.description: Tests if the specified program is still running.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero as long as the program has not yet ended, zero otherwise.
If the program has been run with #PB_Program_Read flag, it will return nonzero as long there is something to read,
even if the program is already ended.

commands.name: ReadProgramData
commands.description:
Reads data from the given programs output (stdout) and puts it in the specified buffer.
This function waits until there is data available to read from the program. To prevent this wait,
AvailableProgramOutput() may be used first to check if there is
something to read.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Read flag.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory buffer to read the data into. A memory buffer can be created for example with AllocateMemory().

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size to read, in bytes. The buffer should be large enough to handle this size.

commands.returnValue: The number of bytes actually read.
commands.remarks:
The function reads up to 'size' bytes, but also less if not that much is available
(but it will not return zero bytes because it always waits for some data to read).

However, the function remains blocked indefinitely if the program requests the
intervention of the user. For example, return a yes / no choice to the program to continue.

commands.name: ReadProgramError
commands.description:
Reads a line from the specified programs error output (stderr).
Unlike ReadProgramData(), this function doesn't halt the program flow if no error output is available.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Error flag.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when reading the error output.
The default format can be affected with the #PB_Program_Ascii, #PB_Program_Unicode and
#PB_Program_UTF8 flags for RunProgram().
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Reads the error output as ascii
#PB_UTF8 : Reads the error output as UTF8 (default)
#PB_Unicode: Reads the error output as unicode

commands.returnValue: The error string, or an empty string if there is no error output.

commands.name: ReadProgramString
commands.description:
Reads a line from the output (stdout) of the given program.
This function waits until there is data available to read from the program. To prevent this wait,
AvailableProgramOutput() may be used first to check if there is
something to read. This function also waits until a full line of output is available. If not line-based
or raw output is to be read, ReadProgramData() may be used.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Read flag.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when reading the output.
The default format can be affected with the #PB_Program_Ascii, #PB_Program_Unicode and
#PB_Program_UTF8 flags for RunProgram().
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Reads the output as ascii
#PB_UTF8 : Reads the output as UTF8 (default)
#PB_Unicode: Reads the output as unicode

commands.returnValue: A string created from program output.
commands.remarks:
However, the function remains blocked indefinitely if the program requests the
intervention of the user. For example, return a yes / no choice to the program to continue.

commands.name: RemoveEnvironmentVariable
commands.description: Removes the given environment variable from the programs environment block.

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The environment variable to remove.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: RunProgram
syntax: Result = RunProgram(Filename$ [, Parameter$, WorkingDirectory$ [, Flags [, SenderProgram]]])
commands.description: Launches an external program.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The executable name including its path.

parameters.name: Parameters$ (optional)
parameters.description: Specifies the command line parameters that will be passed to the program.

parameters.name: WorkingDirectory$ (optional)
parameters.description: Specifies the directory that will then be the current directory for the launched program.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination (using '|' OR operator) of the following values:

#PB_Program_Wait : Wait until the launched program quits
#PB_Program_Hide : Launch the program in invisible mode
#PB_Program_Open : Open the program to communicate with it or get information about it.
#PB_Program_Read : Read the programs console output. (stdout)
#PB_Program_Write : Write to the input of the program. (stdin)
#PB_Program_Error : Read the error output of the program. (stderr)
#PB_Program_Connect: Connect another programs output to this programs input.
#PB_Program_Ascii : Default read/write operation are in ASCII.
#PB_Program_Unicode: Default read/write operation are in Unicode.
#PB_Program_UTF8 : Default read/write operation are in UTF8 (default).

A program executed with #PB_Program_Open must be closed with CloseProgram().
The 'Read', 'Write', 'Error' and 'Connect' flags require the #PB_Program_Open flag to be set as well.

When using the #PB_Program_Connect flag, another program must have been started before with
#PB_Program_Open and #PB_Program_Read. The number returned when running this
program must be passed as the 'SenderProgram' parameter to RunProgram().

The following functions may be used with a program that has been executed with the #PB_Program_Open flag:

- IsProgram(): check if the program number represents a valid program executed by RunProgram().

- ProgramID(): returns the OS ProcessID for the program.

- ProgramRunning(): check if the program is still running.

- WaitProgram(): wait for the program to end.

- KillProgram(): terminate the program.

- ProgramExitCode(): get the exitcode of the program.

- CloseProgram(): close the connection to the program.

The following functions may be used for programs executed with the 'Read', 'Write' and 'Error' flags:

- AvailableProgramOutput(): check if the programs output is available.

- ReadProgramString(): read a string from the programs output.

- ReadProgramData(): read data from the programs output.

- ReadProgramError(): read a string from the programs error output.

- WriteProgramString(): write a string to the programs input.

- WriteProgramData(): write data to the programs input.

parameters.name: SenderProgram (optional)
parameters.description:
Needed in conjunction with the #PB_Program_Connect flag, must contain the returned number of
another program started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Open and #PB_Program_Read flags.
The output of the sender program will
be sent directly to the input of the now executed program. Several programs may be connected in this way,
to 'pipe' data through that group of connected programs.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the program has been successfully launched, zero otherwise.

If #PB_Program_Open was included in the Flags, the return-value is a number that
identifies the program. It may be used in calls to get information about the program such as
ReadProgramString() or ProgramExitCode()
or other functions mentioned above.
commands.example:
; Executes the PB compiler with the /? option and displays the output
  ;
  Compiler = RunProgram(#PB_Compiler_Home+"compilers/pbcompiler", "-h", "", #PB_Program_Open | #PB_Program_Read)
  Output$ = ""
  If Compiler
    While ProgramRunning(Compiler)
      If AvailableProgramOutput(Compiler)
        Output$ + ReadProgramString(Compiler) + Chr(13)
      EndIf
    Wend
    Output$ + Chr(13) + Chr(13)
    Output$ + "Exitcode: " + Str(ProgramExitCode(Compiler))
    
    CloseProgram(Compiler) ; Close the connection to the program
  EndIf
  
  MessageRequester("Output", Output$)

commands.name: SetEnvironmentVariable
commands.description:
Creates an environment variable in the environment block of this program with given name and value.
If a variable with this name already existed, its content will be changed to the new value.

The environment block of the program is passed on to other programs executed with
RunProgram(), so this method may be used to pass on information to a program
executed by this program. (The executed program may use GetEnvironmentVariable()
to read the variables.)

parameters.name: Name$
parameters.description: The environment variable name.

parameters.name: Value$
parameters.description: The new value for the environment variable.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: WaitProgram
commands.description:
Halts the execution of the code until the specified program has ended or the optional timeout
is reached.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram().

parameters.name: Timeout (optional)
parameters.description: The timeout to use, in milliseconds.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the program has ended, zero if the timeout was reached.

commands.name: WriteProgramData
commands.description: Writes the data from the buffer to the specified programs input (stdin).

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Write flag.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description:
The memory buffer to write the data from.
The special value #PB_Program_Eof can be used instead of a real memory buffer to make
the program receive an EOF (end of file) in its input (which tells the program that there will be no more input).
The 'Size' parameter is ignored in this case. After calling WriteProgramData() with this special value,
no more input may be written to the program.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size to write.

commands.returnValue: The number of bytes actually written.

commands.name: WriteProgramString
commands.description: Writes the given string to the specified programs input (stdin).

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Write flag.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description:
The string to write. There is no newline written to the program after the string. To include the newline,
WriteProgramStringN() may be used. To write raw data to the program,
WriteProgramData() may be used. This function may also be used to send
an EOF (end of file) to the program which tells the program that there will be no more input.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when writing the string to the program input.
The default format can be affected with the #PB_Program_Ascii, #PB_Program_Unicode and
#PB_Program_UTF8 flags for RunProgram().
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Writes the string as ascii
#PB_UTF8 : Writes the string as UTF8 (default)
#PB_Unicode: Writes the string as unicode

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: WriteProgramStringN
commands.description: Writes the given string to the specified programs input (stdin) with an extra newline character.

parameters.name: Program
parameters.description: The program to use. It must have been started before with RunProgram() and the #PB_Program_Write flag.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description:
The string to write. An extra newline character will be appended to the string.
To write a string without a newline, use WriteProgramString(). To write raw data to the program,
WriteProgramData() may be used. This function may also be used to send
an EOF (end of file) to the program which tells the program that there will be no more input.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use when writing the string to the program input.
The default format can be affected with the #PB_Program_Ascii, #PB_Program_Unicode and
#PB_Program_UTF8 flags for RunProgram().
This can be one of the following values:

#PB_Ascii : Writes the string as ascii
#PB_UTF8 : Writes the string as UTF8 (default)
#PB_Unicode: Writes the string as unicode

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CountRegularExpressionGroups
commands.description:
Returns the number of groups defined in the #RegularExpression.
The matches of regular expression groups can be accessed with functions
like RegularExpressionGroup().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

commands.returnValue: The number of groups defined in the regular expression.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". The groups are numbered as they appear in the
regular expression from left to right. The first group has index 1.

commands.name: CreateRegularExpression
commands.description: Create a new regular expression using the specified pattern.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new regular expression.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Pattern$
parameters.description: The regular expression which will be applied to the string to match, extract or replace.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_RegularExpression_DotAll : '.' matches anything including newlines.
#PB_RegularExpression_Extended : whitespace and '#' comments will be ignored.
#PB_RegularExpression_MultiLine : '^' and '$' match newlines within data.
#PB_RegularExpression_AnyNewLine: recognize 'CR', 'LF', and 'CRLF' as newline sequences.
#PB_RegularExpression_NoCase : comparison and matching will be case-insensitive

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the regular expression was created successfully and zero if not. If #PB_Any was used
for the #RegularExpression parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
If an error has been detected in the pattern, the result will be zero. To get more
information about the error, see RegularExpressionError().
commands.remarks: If a regular expression isn't used anymore, use FreeRegularExpression() to free up some resources.
commands.example:
; This expression will match every word of 3 letter which begin by a lower case letter,
  ; followed with the character 'b' and which ends with an uppercase letter. ex: abC
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[A-Z]")
    Debug MatchRegularExpression(0, "abC") ; Will print 1
    Debug MatchRegularExpression(0, "abc") ; Will print 0
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: ExamineRegularExpression
commands.description:
Starts matching the #RegularExpression against the given String$. Individual
matches can be iterated using the NextRegularExpressionMatch() function.
From each match, the matching string, its position/length and any groups within
the match can be extracted with the appropriate function.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to apply the regular expression on.

commands.returnValue:
Returns non-zero if the matching was started successfully. Whether an actual match
was found can be determined by calling NextRegularExpressionMatch().
commands.example:
; This expression will match every word of 3 letter which begin by a lower case letter,
  ; followed with the character 'b' and which ends with an uppercase letter. ex: abC
  ; Each match is printed with its position in the original string.
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[A-Z]")
    If ExamineRegularExpression(0, "abC ABc zbA abc")
      While NextRegularExpressionMatch(0)
        Debug "Match: " + RegularExpressionMatchString(0)
        Debug "    Position: " + Str(RegularExpressionMatchPosition(0))
        Debug "    Length: " + Str(RegularExpressionMatchLength(0))
      Wend
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: ExtractRegularExpression
commands.description: Extracts strings according to the #RegularExpression into an array.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to apply the regular expression on.

parameters.name: Array$()
parameters.description:
The extracted strings will be stored in this array. The array is automatically resized
to the number of element matching the expression found in the specified string.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of elements matching the regular expression in the string.
commands.example:
; This expression will match every word of 3 letter which begin by a lower case letter,
  ; followed with the character 'b' and which ends with an uppercase letter. ex: abC
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[A-Z]")
    Dim Result$(0)
    NbFound = ExtractRegularExpression(0, "abC ABc zbA abc", Result$())
    For k = 0 To NbFound-1
      Debug Result$(k)
    Next
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: FreeRegularExpression
commands.description: Free the specified #RegularExpression and release its associated memory.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: Free the regular expression. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining regular expressions are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining regular expressions are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: IsRegularExpression
commands.description: Tests if the given #RegularExpression number is a valid and correctly initialized, regular expression.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #RegularExpression is a valid regular expression and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and
initialized, otherwise it will equal zero. This is the correct way to ensure a regular expression is ready to use.

commands.name: MatchRegularExpression
commands.description: Tests the string against the #RegularExpression.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to apply the regular expression on.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the string matches the regular expression, returns zero otherwise.
commands.example:
; This expression will match every word of 3 letter which begin by a lower case letter,
  ; followed with the character 'b' and which ends with an uppercase letter. ex: abC
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[A-Z]")
    If MatchRegularExpression(0, "abC ABc zbA abc")
      Debug "The string match !"
    Else
      Debug "No pattern found in the string"
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: NextRegularExpressionMatch
commands.description:
Iterates over all regular expression matches in the target string
after a call to ExamineRegularExpression().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() must have been
called on this regular expression.

commands.returnValue:
Returns non-zero if another match was found. If there are no more matches
in the string, the result is zero.
commands.remarks:
The following functions can be used to get information about the current match:

- RegularExpressionMatchString(): Get the current matching string

- RegularExpressionMatchPosition(): Get the position of the current match

- RegularExpressionMatchLength(): Get the length of the current match

- RegularExpressionGroup(): Extract the matching string of a group

- RegularExpressionGroupPosition(): Get the position (within the match) of a group

- RegularExpressionGroupLength(): Get the length of a group

- RegularExpressionNamedGroup(): Extract the matching string of a named group

- RegularExpressionNamedGroupPosition(): Get the position (within the match) of a named group

- RegularExpressionNamedGroupLength(): Get the length of a named group
commands.example: See ExamineRegularExpression() for an example.

commands.name: RegularExpressionError
commands.description: Returns an human readable error (in english) about the latest failure of CreateRegularExpression().
commands.returnValue: Returns an human readable error (in english) about the latest failure of CreateRegularExpression().
commands.example:
; Here we put an extra bracket '[', so there is a syntax error in the regular expression
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[[A-Z][]")
    Debug "Success"
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: RegularExpressionGroup
commands.description:
Extract the string matched by a group within the regular expression
after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: The index of the group to extract. The first group has index 1.

commands.returnValue: Returns the string matched by the regular expression group.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". The groups are numbered as they appear in the
regular expression from left to right. The first group has index 1.
The CountRegularExpressionGroups() function can be used to find out the number
of groups in a regular expression.

As an alternative, the RegularExpressionNamedGroup() function can be used.
commands.example:
; This expression matches a color setting string (with value red, green or blue)
  ; The colors are grouped with () and the color value is extracted in case of a match
  ;  
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "color=(red|green|blue)")
    If ExamineRegularExpression(0, "style=bold, color=blue, margin=50")
      While NextRegularExpressionMatch(0)
        Debug "The color is " + RegularExpressionGroup(0, 1)
      Wend
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: RegularExpressionGroupLength
commands.description:
Returns the length of the specified regular expression group
after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: The index of the group. The first group has index 1.

commands.returnValue: Returns the character position of the group.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". The groups are numbered as they appear in the
regular expression from left to right. The first group has index 1.
The CountRegularExpressionGroups() function can be used to find out the number
of groups in a regular expression.

As an alternative, the RegularExpressionNamedGroupLength() function can be used.

commands.name: RegularExpressionGroupPosition
commands.description:
Returns the position (within the current matching string) of the specified group
after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: The index of the group. The first group has index 1.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the character position of the group within the matching string
(not within the original input string!).
The first character of the match has position 1.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". The groups are numbered as they appear in the
regular expression from left to right. The first group has index 1.
The CountRegularExpressionGroups() function can be used to find out the number
of groups in a regular expression.

As an alternative, the RegularExpressionNamedGroupPosition() function can be used.

commands.name: RegularExpressionMatchLength
commands.description:
Returns the length in characters of the current matching string
after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

commands.returnValue: The length of the current match in characters.
commands.example: See ExamineRegularExpression() for an example.

commands.name: RegularExpressionMatchPosition
commands.description:
Returns the position within the input string (passed to ExamineRegularExpression())
of the current match after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

commands.returnValue:
The position of the match within the original string. The first character
in the string is at position 1.
commands.example: See ExamineRegularExpression() for an example.

commands.name: RegularExpressionMatchString
commands.description:
Returns the string that matched the #RegularExpression in the last call
to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

commands.returnValue: The sub-string that matched the regular expression.
commands.example: See ExamineRegularExpression() for an example.

commands.name: RegularExpressionNamedGroup
commands.description:
Extract the string matched by a named group within the regular expression
after a call to NextRegularExpressionMatch().

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description:
The regular expression to use. ExamineRegularExpression() and
NextRegularExpressionMatch() must have been called on this regular expression.

parameters.name: GroupName$
parameters.description: The name of the group to extract. The group name is case sensitive.

commands.returnValue: Returns the string matched by the regular expression group.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". Groups can either accessed by index using functions
like RegularExpressionGroup() or they can be assigned a name using the
"(?<name>)" syntax as shown in the example below.
commands.example:
; This expression matches a color setting string (with value red, green or blue)
  ; The colors are grouped with () which has the name "col" assigned to it.
  ; This color name is then extracted
  ;  
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "color=(?<col>red|green|blue)")
    If ExamineRegularExpression(0, "style=bold, color=blue, margin=50")
      While NextRegularExpressionMatch(0)
        Debug "The color is " + RegularExpressionNamedGroup(0, "col")
      Wend
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

with braces "(" and ")". Groups can either accessed by index using functions
like RegularExpressionGroupLength() or they can be assigned a name using the

commands.returnValue:
Returns the character position of the group within the matching string
(not within the original input string!).
The first character of the match has position 1.
commands.remarks:
Groups in a regular expression are defined by surrounding a sub-expression
with braces "(" and ")". Groups can either accessed by index using functions
like RegularExpressionGroupPosition() or they can be assigned a name using the

commands.name: ReplaceRegularExpression
commands.description: Replaces all strings matching the #RegularExpression with 'ReplaceString$'.

parameters.name: #RegularExpression
parameters.description: The regular expression to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to apply the regular expression on.

parameters.name: ReplaceString$
parameters.description: The string to use to replace the matched expression.

commands.returnValue: Returns a new string with all matched expressions replaced with 'ReplaceString$'.
commands.remarks:
Back references (usually described as \1, \2, etc.) are not supported. ExtractRegularExpression()
combined with ReplaceString() should achieve the requested behaviour.
commands.example:
; This expression will match every word of 3 letter which begin by a lower case letter,
  ; followed with the character 'b' and which ends with an uppercase letter. ex: abC
  ;    
  If CreateRegularExpression(0, "[a-z]b[A-Z]")
    Result$ = ReplaceRegularExpression(0, "abC ABc zbA abc", "---")
    Debug Result$ ; Will print "--- ABc --- abc"
  Else
    Debug RegularExpressionError()
  EndIf

commands.name: ColorRequester
commands.description:
Opens the standard requester to choose a color. The chosen color is returned
under a 24-bit number containing the red, green and blue value, as usual.

parameters.name: CurrentColor (optional)
parameters.description: Sets the default color when the requester is opened. RGB() can be used to get a valid color.

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue:
The selected color, or -1 if the user canceled the requester. To easily get each RGB component value, Red(), Green()
and Blue() can be used.
commands.example:
Color = ColorRequester()
  If Color > -1
    a$ = "You have selected following color value:" + Chr(10)  ; Chr(10) only needed
    a$ + "24 Bit value: " + Str(Color)              + Chr(10)  ; for line-feed
    a$ + "Red value:    " + Str(Red(Color))         + Chr(10)
    a$ + "Green value:  " + Str(Green(Color))       + Chr(10)
    a$ + "Blue value:   " + Str(Blue(Color))
  Else  
    a$ = "The requester was canceled."
  EndIf
  MessageRequester("Information", a$, 0)
  End

commands.name: FontRequester
syntax: Result = FontRequester(FontName$, FontSize, Flags [, Color [, Style [, ParentID]]])
commands.description:
Opens the standard requester to choose a font. The functions SelectedFontColor(), SelectedFontName(), SelectedFontSize()
and SelectedFontStyle() can be used after a successful
call to get the needed information about the selected font.

parameters.name: FontName$
parameters.description: The default font name to use when the requester is opened.

parameters.name: FontSize
parameters.description: The default font size to use when the requester is opened.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_FontRequester_Effects : Enable the requesters effects, including color chooser (Windows only).

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description: Sets the default color when the requester is opened. A valid color value you can get with the function RGB().

parameters.name: Style (optional)
parameters.description: Sets the default style when the requester is opened. See SelectedFontStyle() for available styles.

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if a font has been chosen, zero if the user canceled the requester.
commands.example:
FontName$ = "Arial"   ; set initial font  (could also be blank)
  FontSize  = 14        ; set initial size  (could also be null)
  Result = FontRequester(FontName$, FontSize, #PB_FontRequester_Effects)
  If Result
    Message$ = "You have selected following font:"  + #LF$ 
    Message$ + "Name:  " + SelectedFontName()       + #LF$
    Message$ + "Size:  " + Str(SelectedFontSize())  + #LF$
    Message$ + "Color: " + Str(SelectedFontColor()) + #LF$
    If SelectedFontStyle() & #PB_Font_Bold
      Message$ + "Bold" + #LF$
    EndIf
    If SelectedFontStyle() & #PB_Font_StrikeOut
      Message$ + "StrikeOut" + #LF$
    EndIf
    If SelectedFontStyle() & #PB_Font_Underline
      Message$ + "Underline" + #LF$
    EndIf
  Else 
    Message$ = "The requester was canceled."
  EndIf
  
  MessageRequester("FontRequester", Message$, #PB_MessageRequester_Ok)

commands.name: InputRequester
syntax: Text$ = InputRequester(Title$, Message$, DefaultText$ [, Flags [, ParendID]])
commands.description: Opens a blocking input requester to enter some text.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description: Title of the requester.

parameters.name: Message$
parameters.description: Message displayed before the input field.

parameters.name: DefaultText$
parameters.description: Default text in the input field.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_InputRequester_Password: set the field type as 'password'. The displayed text will be hidden.
#PB_InputRequester_HandleCancel: If specified, the special value #PB_InputRequester_Cancel will be returned when the user cancels the requester.

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue: Returns the text in the input field, or an empty string if the requester has been closed without hitting the "OK" button.
commands.example:
Input$ = InputRequester("Title", "Please make your input:", "I'm the default input.")

  If Input$ > ""
    a$ = "You entered in the requester:" + Chr(10)  ; Chr(10) only needed
    a$ + Input$                                                  ; for line-feed
  Else  
    a$ = "The requester was canceled or there was nothing entered."
  EndIf
  MessageRequester("Information", a$, 0)

commands.name: MessageRequester
commands.description:
Opens a blocking requester to display some information. The program execution
is totally stopped until the user close the requester.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description: The title of the requester window.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text displayed in the requester window.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following value:

#PB_MessageRequester_Ok : to have the 'ok' only button (default)
#PB_MessageRequester_YesNo : to have 'yes' or 'no' buttons
#PB_MessageRequester_YesNoCancel : to have 'yes', 'no' and 'cancel' buttons

Combined with one of the following value:

#PB_MessageRequester_Info : displays an info icon
#PB_MessageRequester_Warning: displays a warning icon
#PB_MessageRequester_Error : displays an error icon

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue:
It can be one of the following constants:

#PB_MessageRequester_Yes : the 'yes' button was pressed
#PB_MessageRequester_No : the 'no' button was pressed
#PB_MessageRequester_Cancel : the 'Cancel' button was pressed
commands.example:
MessageRequester("Information", "Just a short information text.", #PB_MessageRequester_Ok | #PB_MessageRequester_Info)

Result = MessageRequester("Title", "Please make your input:", #PB_MessageRequester_YesNo)
  a$ = "Result of the requester was: "
  If Result = #PB_MessageRequester_Yes    ; pressed Yes button
    a$ + "Yes"
  Else                                    ; pressed No button
    a$ + "No"
  EndIf
  MessageRequester("Information", a$, #PB_MessageRequester_Ok)

Result = MessageRequester("Title", "Please make your input:", #PB_MessageRequester_YesNoCancel) 
  a$ = "Result of the previously requester was: "
  If Result = #PB_MessageRequester_Yes       ; pressed Yes button
    a$ + "Yes"
  ElseIf Result = #PB_MessageRequester_No    ; pressed No button
    a$ + "No"
  Else                                       ; pressed Cancel button or Esc
    a$ + "Cancel"
  EndIf
  MessageRequester("Information", a$, #PB_MessageRequester_Ok)

commands.name: NextSelectedFilename
commands.description:
After OpenFileRequester() with #PB_Requester_MultiSelection, it returns the next selected
file (if any).
commands.returnValue: A filename, or an empty string if there are no more selected filenames.
commands.example:
Filename$ = OpenFileRequester("Choose some files","","",0, #PB_Requester_MultiSelection)

  While Filename$ 
    Debug Filename$ 
    Filename$ = NextSelectedFilename() 
  Wend

commands.name: OpenFileRequester
syntax: Filename$ = OpenFileRequester(Title$, DefaultFile$, Pattern$, PatternPosition [, Flags [, ParentID]])
commands.description:
Opens the standard requester for the user to choose a file. The title can be
specified to replace the default one. The DefaultFile$ is useful to initialize
the requester in the right directory and with the right filename.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description: The title of the requester window.

parameters.name: DefaultFile$
parameters.description: The default file displayed when the requester is opened.

parameters.name: Pattern$
parameters.description:
A standard filter which allow to display only the files which
end with such or such extension. It has to be in the following form : "Text
file | *.txt | Music file | *.mus;*.mod" The pattern always works in pairs: name
(which really appears in the filter) and extension (ie: *.txt). Several
extensions can be specified for a single type by using the ; (semi-colon)
separator (not supported on OSX, the requester always displays all files).

parameters.name: PatternPosition
parameters.description:
Specifies which pattern must be the default. It begins from 0 up to the number of pattern
minus 1 (because the index for the first pattern begins at 0). Once the requester has been closed,
SelectedFilePattern() can be used to get back the selected pattern (not supported on OSX).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a one of the following values:

#PB_Requester_MultiSelection: Enable the multiselection. (see NextSelectedFilename())

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue: The selected filename, or an empty string if the requester has been canceled by the user.
commands.remarks:
The returned 'Filename$' can be easily split into file, path and extension string with the following
functions: GetFilePart(), GetPathPart() and GetExtensionPart().
commands.example:
StandardFile$ = "C:\autoexec.bat"   ; set initial file+path to display
  ; With next string we will set the search patterns ("|" as separator) for file displaying:
  ;  1st: "Text (*.txt)" as name, ".txt" and ".bat" as allowed extension
  ;  2nd: "PureBasic (*.pb)" as name, ".pb" as allowed extension
  ;  3rd: "All files (*.*) as name, "*.*" as allowed extension, valid for all files
  Pattern$ = "Text (*.txt;*.bat)|*.txt;*.bat|PureBasic (*.pb)|*.pb|All files (*.*)|*.*"
  Pattern = 0    ; use the first of the three possible patterns as standard
  File$ = OpenFileRequester("Please choose file to load", StandardFile$, Pattern$, Pattern)
  If File$
    MessageRequester("Information", "You have selected following file:" + Chr(10) + File$, 0)
  Else
    MessageRequester("Information", "The requester was canceled.", 0) 
  EndIf

commands.name: PathRequester
commands.description: Opens the standard path requester for the user to select a path.

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description: The title of the requester window.

parameters.name: InitialPath$
parameters.description: The initial path to use when the requester is opened.

parameters.name: ParentID (optional)
parameters.description: The parent window identifier. A valid window identifier can be retrieved with WindowID().

commands.returnValue: The selected path, or an empty string if the requester has been canceled by the user.
commands.remarks: The path is returned with the terminating '\' on Windows, or the terminating '/' on Linux and OS X.
commands.example:
InitialPath$ = "C:\"   ; set initial path to display (could also be blank)
  Path$ = PathRequester("Please choose your path", InitialPath$)
  If Path$
    MessageRequester("Information", "You have selected following path:"+Chr(10)+Path$, 0)
  Else
    MessageRequester("Information", "The requester was canceled.", 0) 
  EndIf

commands.remarks:

StandardFile$ = "C:\autoexec.bat"   ; set initial file+path to display
  ; With next string we will set the search patterns ("|" as separator) for file displaying:
  ;  1st: "Text (*.txt)" as name, ".txt" and ".bat" as allowed extension
  ;  2nd: "PureBasic (*.pb)" as name, ".pb" as allowed extension
  ;  3rd: "All files (*.*) as name, "*.*" as allowed extension, valid for all files
