commands.name: SelectedFilePattern
commands.description: Returns the selected pattern index chosen with OpenFileRequester() or SaveFileRequester().
commands.returnValue:
The selected pattern index chosen with OpenFileRequester() or SaveFileRequester().
The first pattern is at position 0.
commands.example:
StandardFile$ = "C:\autoexec.bat"        ; initial path + file
  Pattern$ = "Text (*.txt)|*.txt;*.bat|"   ; set first pattern  (index = 0)
  Pattern$ + "PureBasic (*.pb)|*.pb|"      ; set second pattern (index = 1)
  Pattern$ + "Bmp (*.bmp)|*.bmp|"          ; set third pattern  (index = 2)
  Pattern$ + "Jpeg (*.jpg)|*.jpg|"         ; set fourth pattern (index = 3)
  Pattern$ + "All files (*.*)|*.*"         ; set fifth pattern  (index = 4)
  Pattern = 1    ; use the second of the five possible patterns as standard

  ; Now we open a filerequester, you can change the pattern and will get the index after closing
  File$ = OpenFileRequester("Please choose file to load", StandardFile$, Pattern$, Pattern)
  Index = SelectedFilePattern()
  If Index > -1
    MessageRequester("Information", "Following pattern index was selected: "+Str(Index), 0)
  Else
    MessageRequester("Information", "The requester was canceled.", 0)
  EndIf

commands.name: SelectedFontColor
commands.description: Returns the color of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
commands.returnValue:
The color of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
To get individual color RGB values Red(), Green() and Blue() can be used.

commands.name: SelectedFontName
commands.description: Returns the name of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
commands.returnValue:
The name of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester(). This
name can be used directly by the LoadFont() function.

commands.name: SelectedFontSize
commands.description: Returns the size of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
commands.returnValue: The size of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().

commands.name: SelectedFontStyle
commands.description: Returns the style of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
commands.returnValue:
The style of the font chosen by the user with the FontRequester().
It can contain one or several of the following values:

#PB_Font_Bold : Font is bold.
#PB_Font_Italic: Font is italic.

To test if a value is present, use the '&' (bitwise AND) operator:

If SelectedFontStyle() & #PB_Font_Bold
; The font is bold
EndIf

commands.name: GetRuntimeDouble
commands.description: Returns the double value of the runtime object.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to get the value from. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

- Constant: the object name is '#ConstantName' (case insensitive).

When accessing public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the double value of the specified object, or zero if not found. As zero is a valid double
value, IsRuntime() can be used to determine if the runtime object really exists. If the variable
is of integer or float type, it is automatically converted to double.

commands.name: GetRuntimeInteger
commands.description:
Returns the integer value of the runtime object. If the runtime object is a procedure,
it returns the procedure address.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to get the value from. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

- Constant: the object name is '#ConstantName' (case insensitive).

- Procedure: the object name is 'ProcedureName()' (case insensitive).

When accessing public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the integer value of the specified object, or zero if not found. As zero is a valid integer
value, IsRuntime() can be used to determine if the runtime object really exists. If the variable
is of float or double type, it is automatically converted to integer. If the runtime object is a procedure,
it returns the procedure address.

commands.name: GetRuntimeString
commands.description: Returns the string value of the runtime object.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to get the value from. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

- Constant: the object name is '#ConstantName' (case insensitive).

When accessing public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the string value of the specified object, or an empty string if not found. As an empty string is a valid string
value, IsRuntime() can be used to determine if the runtime object really exists.

commands.name: IsRuntime
commands.description: Checks if the specified object is declared as runtime.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to check. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

- Constant: the object name is '#ConstantName' (case insensitive).

- Procedure: the object name is 'ProcedureName()' (case insensitive).

When accessing public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the specified object has been declared as runtime, zero otherwise.

commands.name: SetRuntimeDouble
commands.description: Changes the double value of the runtime object.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to set the value of. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

When setting public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The new double value to set.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetRuntimeInteger
commands.description: Changes the integer value of the runtime object.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to set the value of. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

When setting public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The new integer value to set.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetRuntimeString
commands.description: Changes the string value of the runtime object.

parameters.name: Object$
parameters.description:
Name of the object to set the value of. The following objects are supported:

- Variable: the object name is 'VariableName' (case insensitive).

When setting public module items, the module prefix name is mandatory, even if UseModule is used.

parameters.name: Value$
parameters.description: The new string value to set.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ScintillaGadget
syntax: Result = ScintillaGadget(#Gadget, x, y, Width, Height, @Callback())
commands.description: Creates a new scintilla editing control in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: @Callback()
parameters.description:
The address of a procedure to receive events from the control. It must be defined
as follows, where 'Gadget' is the gadget number of the control and *scinotify points to a structure
with information on the event:

Procedure ScintillaCallBack(Gadget, *scinotify.SCNotification)
; You code here
EndProcedure

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #Gadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
The following events are supported through EventType():

#PB_EventType_RightClick

After creation, Scintilla specific commands may be sent to the control with the
ScintillaSendMessage() command. In addition common gadget commands like
ResizeGadget() or HideGadget() may be used
with the control as well.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 330, 90, "ScintillaGadget", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    
    ScintillaGadget(0, 10, 10, 320, 70, 0)
    
    ; Output set to red color
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_STYLESETFORE, 0, RGB(255, 0, 0))
    
    ; Set the initial text to the ScintillaGadget
    *Text=UTF8("This is a simple ScintillaGadget with text...")
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_SETTEXT, 0, *Text)
    FreeMemory(*Text) ; The buffer made by UTF8() has to be freed, to avoid memory leak
    
    ; Adding a second line of text with linebreak before
    Text$ = Chr(10) + "Second line"
    *Text=UTF8(Text$)
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_APPENDTEXT, StringByteLength(Text$, #PB_UTF8), *Text)
    FreeMemory(*Text)
    
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ScintillaSendMessage
commands.description: Sends a message to the scintilla control to perform a specific task.

parameters.name: #Gadget
parameters.description: The scintilla gadget to use.

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description:
The message to send. More information about the possible messages may be found on the
Scintilla Homepage.
The #SCI_[...] constants representing the possible values are already defined
in PureBasic.

parameters.name: Param (optional)
parameters.description: The first custom parameter for the specified message. Default value if not specified is zero.

parameters.name: LParam (optional)
parameters.description: The second custom parameter for the specified message. Default value if not specified is zero.

commands.returnValue: The result of the message sent.
commands.example:
#num_indicator = 0
  
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 330, 90, "ScintillaGadget", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  
    ScintillaGadget(0, 5, 5, 320, 80, 0)
    *Text = UTF8("This is a simple ScintillaGadget with text..." + #LF$ + "More text" + #LF$ + "Even more text!")
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_SETTEXT, 0, *Text)
    FreeMemory(*Text) ; The buffer made by UTF8() has to be freed, to avoid memory leak
    
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_INDICSETSTYLE, #num_indicator, #INDIC_STRAIGHTBOX) ; first indicator with style 8 (0-19)
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_INDICSETFORE, #num_indicator, #Red)                ; first indicator with red color
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_SETINDICATORCURRENT, #num_indicator, #INDIC_STRAIGHTBOX) ; set the indicator as the current one
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_INDICSETUNDER, #num_indicator, 1)   ; set indicator under the text, i.e. doesn't obscure it
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_INDICSETALPHA, #num_indicator, 127) ; set transparency
    nLine = 1 ; line number starts from 0
    start = ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_POSITIONFROMLINE, nLine)
    length = ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_GETLINEENDPOSITION, nLine) - start
    ScintillaSendMessage(0, #SCI_INDICATORFILLRANGE, start, length) ; start and length
    
    Repeat : Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: ChangeGamma
commands.description:
Changes the Gamma for the current screen. This only works in full screen mode (not in windowed mode). Red,
Green and Blue channels intensity can be changed individually. This function can be used to do full screen fade-in/fade-out,
color splashing etc. If it does not do anything, then the hardware does not support it (no emulation is
provided, due to the high number of operations required to perform it in software).

parameters.name: RedIntensity, GreenIntensity, BlueIntensity
parameters.description: The new intensity to apply. Valid values for each channel are from 0 to 255.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example: ChangeGamma(255, 255, 0)   ; Will remove completely the blue channel from the screen

commands.name: ClearScreen
commands.description: Clear the whole screen with the specified color.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
The color to use to clear the screen. RGB() can be used to get a valid color value.
A table with common colors is available here.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: ClearScreen() has to be always called outside a StartDrawing() : StopDrawing() block.

commands.name: CloseScreen
commands.description:
Close the current screen (either windowed or full screen mode). After closing a screen, all the sprites
must be reloaded as the screen format has been lost and the video memory released. An application or game
can switch from full screen to windowed mode on the fly without any problem.
commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ExamineScreenModes
commands.description:
Starts to examine the available screen modes on the local computer. The screen modes list can be
retrieved with the help of the NextScreenMode() function.
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the screen modes has been successfully listed, zero otherwise.

commands.name: FlipBuffers
commands.description:
Flip the back and front buffers of the current screen. The invisible area is now visible and vice versa,
which allowss to do a 'double-buffering' effect (flicker free graphical displays).
A screen must have been opened with OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen(). The way the buffer are flipped
(with or without synchronization) is set by OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen().
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
FlipBuffers() has to be called outside a StartDrawing() : ... : StopDrawing() program block.

FlipBuffers() must be called in each event loop on a fullscreen to handle
events for joystick / keyboard" /
mouse properly.

commands.name: IsScreenActive
commands.description:
Games and full screen applications using PureBasic functions run under a multitasking environment.
This means that the user can switch back from full screen to the normal
desktop. This change can be detected with this function and appropriate actions should be taken,
such as ReleaseMouse(), pause the game, stop the sounds etc. This function must be called after FlipBuffers(),
as the events are handled inside FlipBuffers().
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the screen is still active, zero otherwise.

commands.name: NextScreenMode
commands.description:
This function should be called after ExamineScreenModes(). It will go step-by-step into
the screen modes list. The current screen mode information can be retrieved with the following
functions: ScreenModeWidth(), ScreenModeHeight(), ScreenModeDepth() and ScreenModeRefreshRate().
commands.returnValue: Nonzero if there is another screenmode to be listed, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
InitSprite()

  If ExamineScreenModes()
    While NextScreenMode()
      Debug Str(ScreenModeWidth())+"x"+Str(ScreenModeHeight())+"x"+Str(ScreenModeDepth())+"@"+Str(ScreenModeRefreshRate())+"Hz"
    Wend
  EndIf

commands.name: OpenScreen
syntax: Result = OpenScreen(Width, Height, Depth, Title$ [, FlipMode [, RefreshRate]])
commands.description:
Opens a new screen according to the specified 'Width', 'Height' and 'Depth'.
InitSprite() has to be called successfully before using this command. The
opened screen is created with 2 video buffers to allow double
buffering, especially useful for games. The buffers can be manipulated with
the FlipBuffers() function.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description:
The screen resolution, in pixels. The specified resolution has to be supported
or the screen won't be created. ExamineScreenModes() can be used to get a full list of supported resolution.

parameters.name: Depth
parameters.description:
It can be one the following values:

16: 65000 colors, fixed palette
24: 16 Mo colors, fixed palette
32: 16 Mo colors, faster than 24-bit mode, allows alpha blending

parameters.name: Title$
parameters.description:
The title for the application which will be displayed when switching back to the desktop.
(Windows only). It will be displayed in the taskbar, so it's recommended to use a title
related to the application name.

parameters.name: FlipMode (optional)
parameters.description:
Sets the screen synchronization methods used when flipping buffers (also known as 'Vertical blank synchronization').
It can have one of the following values:

#PB_Screen_NoSynchronization : disable synchronization
#PB_Screen_WaitSynchronization : enable synchronization (default value)
#PB_Screen_SmartSynchronization: enable synchronization, with a CPU saver routine when the program doesn't consume
all the CPU time (full screen mode only)

Waiting for the screen synchronization allows the flip to be perfect (no 'tearing'
or other visible artifacts) because the flip is performed when the screen has been fully drawn (and when the
screen spot is outside of visible screen area). This also link the flip frequency to the actual screen refresh, ie: for 60Hz screen it
could have at most 60 flip per seconds, etc.

parameters.name: RefreshRate (optional)
parameters.description:
Set the refresh rate (in Hz) for the new screen. If it can't be handled, then OpenScreen() will fail.
ExamineScreenModes() can be used to get a full list of supported refresh rates.

Note: on Windows, the refresh rate could be locked or forced by the video card drivers, so it could be inaccurate.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the screen has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
The Requester functions cannot be used on screens
created with OpenScreen.

To open a screen area on a regular window, see OpenWindowedScreen().

commands.name: OpenWindowedScreen
syntax: Result = OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID, x, y, Width, Height [, AutoStretch, RightOffset, BottomOffset [, FlipMode]])
commands.description:
Open a new screen area according to given parameters on the given Window, which must be
opened before using OpenWindow(). InitSprite() has to be called successfully before using this command.
The "windowed screen" is able to use the hardware acceleration the same way than
full-size OpenScreen() function. As a window is opened, the window events have to be processed with WindowEvent()
to have the correct behaviour. All the events needs to be processed before flipping the buffers (see the examples
below).

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description: The window to use to create the screen. WindowID() can be used to get a valid window identifier.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The screen position in the specified window, in pixels.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The screen resolution, in pixels.

parameters.name: AutoStretch (optional)
parameters.description:
If set to #True, then the screen area will automatically resize (and its contents will be zoomed
to new screen size) when the window size changes.

parameters.name: RightOffset, BottomOffset (optional)
parameters.description: Define the margin on the right and bottom of the window, in pixels (for statusbar for example).

parameters.name: FlipMode (optional)
parameters.description:
Sets the screen synchronization methods used when flipping buffers (also known as 'Vertical blank synchronization').
It can have one of the following values:

#PB_Screen_NoSynchronization : disable synchronization
#PB_Screen_WaitSynchronization : enable synchronization (default value)
#PB_Screen_SmartSynchronization: enable synchronization, with a CPU saver routine when the program doesn't consume
all the CPU time (full screen mode only)

Waiting for the screen synchronization allows the flip to be perfect (no 'tearing'
or other visible artifacts) because the flip is performed when the screen has been fully drawn (and when the
screen spot is outside of visible screen area). This also link the flip frequency to the actual screen refresh, ie: for 60Hz screen it
could have at most 60 flip per seconds, etc.

The opened screen is created with 2 video buffers to allow you to do double buffering, especially useful for games.
The buffers can be manipulated with the FlipBuffers() function.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the screen has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: Only one windowed screen can be opened at one time. The screen dimension can't be greater than the window size or artefacts can occurs.
commands.example:
If InitSprite() = 0
    MessageRequester("Error", "Can't open screen & sprite environment!", 0)
    End
  EndIf
  
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 220, 160, "A screen in a window...", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    ButtonGadget(0, 170, 135, 45, 20, "Quit")

    If OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID(0), 0, 0, 160, 160)
      CreateSprite(0, 20, 20)
      If StartDrawing(SpriteOutput(0))
        Box(0, 0, 20, 20, RGB(255, 0, 155))
        Box(5, 5, 10, 10, RGB(155, 0, 255))
        StopDrawing()
      EndIf
    Else
      MessageRequester("Error", "Can't open windowed screen!", 0)
      End
    EndIf
  EndIf
  
  direction = 2
  Repeat
    ; It's very important to process all the events remaining in the queue at each frame
    ;
    Repeat
      Event = WindowEvent()
      
      Select Event 
        Case #PB_Event_Gadget
          If EventGadget() = 0
            End
          EndIf
        
        Case #PB_Event_CloseWindow
          End 
      EndSelect
    Until Event = 0
  
    FlipBuffers() 
    ClearScreen(RGB(0, 0, 0))
    DisplaySprite(0, x, x)
    x + direction
    If x > 140 : direction = -2 : EndIf
    If x < 0   : direction =  2 : EndIf
    Delay(1)
  ForEver

If InitSprite() = 0
    MessageRequester("Error", "Can't open screen & sprite environment!", 0)
    End
  EndIf
  
  If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 420, 200, "A screen in a window...", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_SizeGadget | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
    CreateStatusBar(0, WindowID(0))
      AddStatusBarField(420)
      
    StatusBarText(0, 0, "Automatically zoomed screen area when changing window size...")
    
    If OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID(0), 0, 0, 420, 200, #True, 0, 20)
  
      CreateSprite(0, 50, 50) ; Create an empty sprite, will be whole black
        
      Repeat
        ; It's very important to process all the events remaining in the queue at each frame
        ;
        Repeat
          Event = WaitWindowEvent(10)
          
          If Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
            End
          EndIf
        Until Event = 0
        
        FlipBuffers()
        ClearScreen(RGB(0, 0, 200)) ; A blue background
        
        DisplaySprite(0, 10, 10)  ; Display our black box at the left-top corner
        DisplaySprite(0, 260, 10) ; Display our black box at the right-top corner
      ForEver
      
    Else
      MessageRequester("Error", "Can't open windowed screen!", 0)
    EndIf
  EndIf

commands.name: ScreenDepth
commands.description: Returns the current screen depth, previously opened with OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen().
commands.returnValue: The current screen depth, or zero if no screen is opened. Depth is a value between 8 and 32.

commands.name: ScreenHeight
commands.description: Returns the current screen height, previously opened with OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen().
commands.returnValue: The current screen height, or zero if no screen is opened.

commands.name: ScreenID
commands.description: Returns the OS ScreenID.
commands.returnValue:
The OS ScreenID.

On Windows this is a normal WindowID so any function which needs such an ID can use it, like
PlayMovie() for example.

commands.name: ScreenModeDepth
commands.description:
Returns the depth of the current screenmode listed with ExamineScreenModes() and
NextScreenMode() functions.
commands.returnValue:
The depth of the current listed screenmode. Depth can be either 8, 15, 16, 24 or 32-bit depending
on the graphic card.

commands.name: ScreenModeHeight
commands.description:
Returns the height of the current screenmode listed with ExamineScreenModes() and
NextScreenMode() functions.
commands.returnValue: The height (in pixels) of the current listed screenmode.

commands.name: ScreenModeRefreshRate
commands.description:
Returns the refresh-rate of the current screenmode listed with ExamineScreenModes() and
NextScreenMode() functions.
commands.returnValue: The refresh-rate (in hertz) of the current listed screenmode.
commands.remarks: On OS X, many notebook and monitors returns 0.

commands.name: ScreenModeWidth
commands.description:
Returns the width of the current screenmode listed with ExamineScreenModes() and
NextScreenMode() functions.
commands.returnValue: The width (in pixels) of the current listed screenmode.

commands.name: ScreenOutput
commands.description:
Returns the OutputID of the currently used screen to perform 2D rendering operations on it. It will use
the PureBasic 2DDrawing library and can only be used within a StartDrawing() /
StopDrawing() block. The memory allocated in ScreenOutput() is released on StopDrawing().
commands.returnValue: The OutputID of the currently used screen to perform 2D rendering operations on it.
commands.remarks:
On Linux and OS X, ScreenOutput() copies the whole screen buffer back to main memory to do 2D drawing operations
(OpenGL doesn't allow direct buffer access). Therefore drawing on a screen is very slow and should be avoided.
ScreenOutput() has to be called in the same thread where OpenScreen() was called.

The use of InitEngine3D() is forbidden, ScreenOutput() returns 0.
commands.example:
StartDrawing(ScreenOutput())
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopDrawing()

commands.name: ScreenWidth
commands.description: Returns the current screen width, previously opened with OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen().
commands.returnValue: The current screen width, or zero if no screen is opened.

commands.name: SetFrameRate
commands.description:
Set the frame rate (in frames per second) for the current screen. This is especially useful
for windowed screen mode where there is no refresh rate for the screen. This function
sets the maximum number of times per second that the FlipBuffers() function is called.

parameters.name: FrameRate
parameters.description: The new framerate to set.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddScreenGadgetItem
commands.description: Add an item to the specified #ScreenGadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description:
The item index where the new item should be inserted. To add
the item at the start, use a value of 0. To add this item to the end of the current
item list, use a value of -1. Remember that when you add an item that all current
items which come after the new one will have their positions increased by 1.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The new item text.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The following gadgets are supported:

- ComboBoxScreenGadget()

- ListViewScreenGadget()

- PanelScreenGadget()

commands.name: ButtonImageScreenGadget
syntax: Result = ButtonImageScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, ImageID [, Flags])
commands.description: Creates a button with an image in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
The identification number of the new gadget.
#PB_Any can be used to automatically generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description: The gadget image identification number. Use ImageID() to get this ID from an image.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description: Not supported.

commands.returnValue:
Returns a non-zero value on success, zero otherwise.
If #PB_Any was used for the #ScreenGadget parameter, then the return value is the gadget ID number, generated automatically.

commands.name: ButtonScreenGadget
syntax: Result = ButtonScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$)
commands.description: Creates a button gadget in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to display on the button.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to control the gadget:

- SetScreenGadgetText(): Changes the text of the ButtonGadget.

- GetScreenGadgetText(): Returns the text of the ButtonGadget.

commands.name: CheckBoxScreenGadget
syntax: Result = CheckBoxScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$)
commands.description: Creates a checkbox gadget in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to display at the right of the checkbox.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to control the gadget:

- GetScreenGadgetState() can be used to get the current gadget state (checked or unchecked).

- SetScreenGadgetState() can be used to change the gadget state (checked or unchecked).

commands.name: ClearScreenGadgetItems
commands.description: Clears all the items from the specified #ScreenGadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The Gadget must be one of the following types:

- ComboBoxScreenGadget()

- ListViewScreenGadget()

- PanelScreenGadget()

commands.name: CloseScreenGadgetList
commands.description: Closes the current gadget list creation and go back to the previous GadgetList.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This function is supported by the following gadgets:

- ContainerScreenGadget()

- PanelScreenGadget()

- ScrollAreaScreenGadget()

commands.name: CloseScreenWindow
commands.description: Close the specified window.

parameters.name: #ScreenWindow
parameters.description: The window to close. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining windows are closed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining opened windows are automatically closed when the program ends.

commands.name: ComboBoxScreenGadget
syntax: Result = ComboBoxScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
commands.description:
Creates a ComboBox gadget in the current GadgetList. Once a ComboBox
is created, its list of items is empty.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget

This function is supported by the following gadgets:

- ListViewScreenGadget(): returns the currently selected item index, -1 if none is selected.

commands.name: InitScreenGadgets
commands.description: Initializes the ScreenGadget library.

commands.description: Send an event to the GUI system. It is required to have ScreenWindowEvent() working.

parameters.name: MouseX, MouseY
parameters.description: The new mouse coordinate to use.

parameters.name: LeftMouseButton
parameters.description:
Left mouse button state. It can be one of the following values:

0: left mouse button is released.
1: left mouse button is pushed.

parameters.name: Text$ (optional)
parameters.description: The text to use as input.

parameters.name: SpecialKey (optional)
parameters.description:
The special key to use as key press. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Key_Back
#PB_Key_Delete
#PB_Key_Return
#PB_Key_Up
#PB_Key_Down
#PB_Key_Left
#PB_Key_Right

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
;
  ; Typical code to use to send to the GUI system with actual mouse and keyboard events
  ;
  If ExamineKeyboard() And ExamineMouse()
    Input$ = KeyboardInkey()
    
    InputEvent(MouseX(), MouseY(), MouseButton(#PB_MouseButton_Left), Input$, 0)
  EndIf

commands.name: IsScreenGadget
commands.description: Tests if the given gadget is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the gadget is valid, zero otherwise.

This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value.

commands.name: OpenScreenGadgetList
commands.description:
Use the specified gadget as a GadgetList, to dynamically add new gadgets

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

commands.remarks:
This function is supported by the following gadgets:

commands.name: OpenScreenWindow
syntax: Result = OpenScreenWindow(#ScreenWindow, x, y, InnerWidth, InnerHeight, Title$ [, Flags])
commands.description:
Opens a new window on the current screen according to the specified parameters.
The new window becomes the active window. All possible events in a window are handled with ScreenWindowEvent().

parameters.name: #ScreenWindow
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new window.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The initial position of the window on the screen (unless one of the center flags is used).

parameters.name: InnerWidth, InnerHeight

The initial size of the client area of the window (without borders and window
decorations).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the window has been successfully opened, zero otherwise.

syntax: Result = OptionScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$)
commands.description:
Creates an OptionGadget in the current GadgetList. The first time this function is called,
a group is created and all following calls of OptionScreenGadget() will add a gadget to
this group. To finish the group, just create a gadget of another type. These kind of gadgets
are very useful as only one gadget from the group can be selected at any time.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to display, near the selection button.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks: To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

commands.name: PanelScreenGadget
syntax: Result = PanelScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height)
commands.description: Creates a panel gadget in the current GadgetList. Once a panel is created, its list of panels is empty.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to act on the gadget:

- AddScreenGadgetItem(): Add a panel.

- RemoveScreenGadgetItem(): Remove a panel.

- CountScreenGadgetItems(): Count the number of panels.

- ClearScreenGadgetItems(): Remove all panels.

- SetScreenGadgetState(): Change the active panel.

- GetScreenGadgetState(): Get the index of the current panel.

#PB_Panel_ItemWidth : Returns the width of the inner area where the gadgets are displayed.
#PB_Panel_ItemHeight: Returns the height of the inner area where the gadgets are displayed.
#PB_Panel_TabHeight : Returns height of the panel tabs on top of the gadget.

You must call AddScreenGadgetItem() to add a panel before you can create other
gadgets inside the panel gadget. The next gadgets will then be created automatically in the new panel.
This is very convenient. When the PanelGadget item has been filled with all the
needed gadgets, CloseScreenGadgetList() must be called to return to the previous GadgetList.
This means that a PanelGadget can be created inside another PanelGadget.

commands.name: ScreenVirtualSize
commands.description:
Defines the virtual screen dimensions to automatically adjust the position of gadgets to the resolution.

This command is useful when the screen resolution is not known in advance.

parameters.name: VirtualWidth, VirtuelHeight
parameters.description: The virtual dimensions of the screen.

commands.returnValue:
Of type float, corresponding to the minimum (actual width / virtual width, actual height / virtual height).
This value can then be used to adjust the font size.
commands.remarks: If this command is used, the position and size of the gadget must be defined in these virtual dimensions.
commands.example:

  SetScreenGadgetFont(#PB_Default, LoadFont(0, "Arial", 24*fontratio))

commands.name: ScreenWindowAnimation
syntax: ScreenWindowAnimation(#ScreenWindow, Meaning, Duration [, Fading [, Zoom, [,x [,y [, Rotation]]]])
commands.description: Makes the window appear/disappear with an animation.

parameters.name: #ScreenWindow
parameters.description: The window to be animated.

parameters.name: Meaning
parameters.description:
1: appearance
2: disappearance
3: Appearance and disappearance

parameters.name: Duration
parameters.description: In millisecond.

parameters.name: Fading (optional)
parameters.description: 0 or 1.

parameters.name: Zoom (optional)
parameters.description: 0 or 1.

parameters.name: x (optional)
parameters.description: -1: the window appears/disappears from the left, 1: from the left, 0: no horizontal movement.

parameters.name: y (optional)
parameters.description: -1: the window appears/disappears from the top, 1: from the bottom, 0: no vertical movement.

parameters.name: Rotation (optional)
parameters.description: In degrees.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ScreenWindowEvent
commands.description:
Checks if an event has occurred on any of the opened windows. InputEvent() needs to be used to
send events to the GUI system to be able to have window events.

ScreenWindowEvent() returns the next event from the event queue and returns zero when there are no more events.
It doesn't wait for the next event - it always returns immediately.
commands.returnValue:
Possible Events are:

#PB_Event_Gadget : a ScreenGadget has been used
#PB_Event_CloseWindow : the window close gadget has been pushed
#PB_Event_SizeWindow : the window has been resized
#PB_Event_MoveWindow : the window has been moved
#PB_Event_ActivateWindow : the window has been activated (got the focus)

commands.name: ScrollAreaScreenGadget
syntax: Result = ScrollAreaScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, ScrollAreaWidth, ScrollAreaHeight, ScrollStep)
commands.description:
Creates a ScrollArea gadget in the current GadgetList. It's very useful when a gadget is
too big to fit the window dimension. In that case, it can be put into a scrollarea. All the
scrolling is handled automatically by the gadget. This is a container gadget, intended
to have one or several gadget in its scroll area. Once the gadget is created,
all future created gadgets will be created inside the scroll area. When all the needed
gadgets have been created, CloseScreenGadgetList() must be called to return to the
previous GadgetList. OpenScreenGadgetList() can be used later to add others gadgets
on the fly in the scroll area.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: ScrollAreaWidth, ScrollAreaHeight
parameters.description:
The dimensions of the scrollable area inside the gadget. These can also be smaller than the outer dimensions, in
this case scrolling will be disabled.

parameters.name: ScrollStep (optional)
parameters.description: The amount of pixels to scroll when the user presses the scroll bar arrows.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.

commands.name: ScrollBarScreenGadget
syntax: Result = ScrollBarScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Minimum, Maximum, PageLength [, Flags])
commands.description: Creates a scrollbar gadget in the current GadgetList. It's widely used when displaying only a part of an object.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Minimum, Maximum
parameters.description:
The range of values that the scrollbar can take. These values should be between 0 and 10,000 to avoid
limitations on some operating systems.

parameters.name: PageLength
parameters.description:
The amount of values that are part of the current displayed "page".

For example you can have a picture
which is 100 pixels width and you only see 25 pixels. What you see is a called a 'page',
in this example, the page length will be 25, the Minimum will be 0 and the Maximum will be 100.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_ScrollBar_Vertical : The scrollbar is vertical (instead of horizontal, which is the default).

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

The following functions can be used to act on this gadget:

- GetScreenGadgetState(): Returns the current slider position (value between the Minimum-Maximum range).

- SetScreenGadgetState(): Changes the current slider position.

commands.name: SetScreenGadgetFont
commands.description: Change the font of a gadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
The gadget to use.
If the value of #ScreenGadget is #PB_Default, then the default font used by new gadgets is changed by the new value.

parameters.name: FontID
parameters.description: The font identification number to use. FontID() can be used to get a valid FontID.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetScreenGadgetState
commands.description: Changes the current state of the specified #ScreenGadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description: The new gadget state.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This function is supported by the following gadgets:

- CheckBoxScreenGadget(): 1 to check it, 0 otherwise.

- ComboBoxScreenGadget(): change the currently selected item.

- ImageScreenGadget(): change the current image of the gadget.

- ListViewScreenGadget(): change the currently selected item. If -1 is specified, it will remove the selection.

- OptionScreenGadget(): 1 to activate it, 0 otherwise.

- PanelScreenGadget(): change the current panel.

- ProgressBarScreenGadget(): change progress bar value.

- ScrollBarScreenGadget(): change the current slider position.

commands.name: SetScreenGadgetText
commands.description: Change the gadget text content of the specified gadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description: The gadget to use.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The new gadget text.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
This function is supported by the following gadgets:

- ButtonScreenGadget(): change the text of the ButtonGadget.

- ComboBoxScreenGadget(): Set the displayed text. If the ComboBoxGadget is not editable, the text must be in the dropdown list.

- EditorScreenGadget(): change the text content of the editor gadget. If you want to add several lines of text at once, separate them with "Chr(13)+Chr(10)".

- ListViewScreenGadget(): selects the item that exactly matches the given text.

- StringScreenGadget(): change the content of the StringGadget.

- TextScreenGadget(): change the content of the TextGadget.

commands.name: SplitterScreenGadget
syntax: Result = SplitterScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, #ScreenGadget1, #ScreenGadget2 [, Flags])
commands.description:
Creates an area divided into two parts (horizontally or vertically), each containing a gadget thread.

The divider bar can be moved freely by the user and the two associated gadgets will be resized automatically.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
The identification number of the new gadget.
#PB_Any can be used to automatically generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget1, #ScreenGadget2
parameters.description: The gadgets, which should be placed inside the splitter area.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description: #PB_Splitter_Vertical: The area will be separated vertically.

commands.returnValue:
Returns a non-zero value on success, zero otherwise.
If #PB_Any was used for the #ScreenGadget parameter, then the return value is the gadget ID number, generated automatically.

commands.name: StringScreenGadget
syntax: Result = StringScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Content$ [, Flags])
commands.description:
Creates a String gadget in the current GadgetList.
This gadget accepts only one line of text. To get multi-line input, use the EditorScreenGadget() function.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Content$
parameters.description: The initial text content.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_String_ReadOnly : Read-only mode. No text can be entered.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
Later the content can be changed with SetScreenGadgetText() and received with GetScreenGadgetText().

The following events are supported through ScreenEventType():

#PB_ScreenEventType_Change : The text has been modified by the user.
#PB_ScreenEventType_Focus : The StringGadget got the focus.
#PB_ScreenEventType_LostFocus : The StringGadget lost the focus.

To add a 'mini help' to this gadget, use ScreenGadgetToolTip().

commands.name: TextScreenGadget
syntax: Result = TextScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Text$)
commands.description:
Creates a text gadget in the current GadgetList. This is a basic text area for displaying,
not entering, text.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new gadget. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to display.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero on success, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used as the #ScreenGadget parameter
then the return-value is the auto-generated gadget number on success.
commands.remarks:
The content can be changed with the function SetScreenGadgetText() and can be
obtained with GetScreenGadgetText().

This Gadget doesn't receive any user events, and ScreenGadgetToolTip() can't be used with it.

commands.name: TrackBarScreenGadget
syntax: Result = TrackBarScreenGadget(#ScreenGadget, x, y, Width, Height, Min, Max [, Flags])
commands.description: Creates a Cursor gadget in the current GadgetList.

parameters.name: #ScreenGadget
parameters.description:
The identification number of the new gadget.
#PB_Any can be used to automatically generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y, Width, Height
parameters.description: The position and dimensions of the new gadget.

parameters.name: Min, Max
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum values used by the gadget. Must be defined with integer values.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description: #PB_TrackBar_Vertical: The gadget is vertical.

commands.returnValue:
Returns a non-zero value on success, zero otherwise.
If #PB_Any was used for the #ScreenGadget parameter, then the return value is the gadget's ID number, generated automatically.

commands.name: AvailableSerialPortInput
commands.description: Returns the number of remaining bytes in the serial port input buffer.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

commands.returnValue: The number of remaining bytes in the serial port input buffer.

commands.name: AvailableSerialPortOutput
commands.description: Returns the number of remaining bytes in the serial port output buffer.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

commands.returnValue: The number of remaining bytes in the serial port output buffer.

commands.name: CloseSerialPort
commands.description: Closes the serial port previously opened with OpenSerialPort().

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to close. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining serial ports are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining opened serial ports are automatically closed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetSerialPortStatus
commands.description: Returns the specified serial port status.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_SerialPort_RI : Get RI signal status (0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_DCD: Get DCD signal status (0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_DSR: Get DSR signal status (0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_CTS: Get CTS signal status (0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_XonCharacter : Character used for Xon/Xoff handshaking sequence (between 1 and 255)
#PB_SerialPort_XoffCharacter: Character used for Xon/Xoff handshaking sequence (between 1 and 255)

commands.returnValue: Returns the specified serial port status, according to the specified attribute.

commands.name: IsSerialPort
commands.description: Tests if the given serial port is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the serial port is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a serial port is ready to use.

commands.name: OpenSerialPort
syntax: Result = OpenSerialPort(#SerialPort, SerialPortName$, Bauds, Parity, Data, Stop.f, HandshakeMode, InputBufferSize, OutputBufferSize)
commands.description: Opens a serial port for use.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new serial port.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: SerialPortName$
parameters.description:
Text identifier for the serial port, for example "COM1" on
Windows or "/dev/ttyS0" on Linux.

parameters.name: Bauds
parameters.description:
Defines the speed of the serial connection and can be one of the following values:

50, 75, 110, 150, 300, 600, 1200, 1800, 2400
4800, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 or 115200

parameters.name: Parity
parameters.description:
Defines how the parity will be handled on the connection. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_SerialPort_NoParity : No parity
#PB_SerialPort_EvenParity : Even parity
#PB_SerialPort_MarkParity : Mark parity
#PB_SerialPort_OddParity : Odd parity
#PB_SerialPort_SpaceParity: Space parity

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: Defines the data length, in byte (usually 7 or 8).

parameters.name: Stop
parameters.description: Sets the number of stop bits (1, 1.5 or 2).

parameters.name: HandshakeMode
parameters.description:
The handshake mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_SerialPort_NoHandshake : No handshaking
#PB_SerialPort_RtsHandshake : No handshaking but RTS is set to 1
#PB_SerialPort_RtsCtsHandshake : RTS/CTS
#PB_SerialPort_XonXoffHandshake: Xon/Xoff

parameters.name: InputBufferSize
parameters.description: Defines the size of the input buffer, in bytes.

parameters.name: OutputBufferSize
parameters.description: Defines the size of the output buffer, in bytes.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the serial port was successfully opened, zero otherwise
(it may be already in use, or the parameters are wrong). If #PB_Any was used
for the #SerialPort parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.example:
If OpenSerialPort(0, "COM1", 300, #PB_SerialPort_NoParity, 8, 1, #PB_SerialPort_NoHandshake, 1024, 1024)
    Debug "Success"
  Else
    Debug "Failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: ReadSerialPortData
commands.description:
Reads an arbitrary amount of data from the #SerialPort. If the input buffer was empty, this function will block
until data is available. To check if data is available, use AvailableSerialPortInput().

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The memory address to use to put the read data.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The length to read from the serial port, in bytes. The specified buffer should be large enough to handle it.

commands.returnValue:
The number of bytes which are actually read. It can be less than the requested length.
If a read error has occurred, it will return zero.

commands.name: SerialPortError
commands.description: Returns the error on the serial port when ReadSerialPortData(), WriteSerialPortData() or WriteSerialPortString() failed.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

commands.returnValue:
Can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_SerialPort_RxOver: An input buffer overflow has occurred.
There is either no room in the input buffer
or a character was received after the end-of-file (EOF)
#PB_SerialPort_OverRun: A character-buffer overrun has occurred.
The next character is lost.
#PB_SerialPort_RxParity : The hardware detected a parity error.
#PB_SerialPort_Frame : The hardware detected a framing error.
#PB_SerialPort_Break : The hardware detected a break condition.
#PB_SerialPort_TxFull : The application tried to transmit a character but the output buffer was full.
#PB_SerialPort_IOE : An I/O error occurred during communications with the device.
#PB_SerialPort_WaitingCTS : Specifies whether transmission is waiting for the CTS (clear-to-send) signal to be sent.
#PB_SerialPort_WaitingDSR : Specifies whether transmission is waiting for the DSR (data-set-ready) signal to be sent.
#PB_SerialPort_WaitingRLSD : Specifies whether transmission is waiting for the RLSD (receive-line-signal-detect) signal to be sent.
#PB_SerialPort_XoffReceived: Specifies whether transmission is waiting because the XOFF character was received.
#PB_SerialPort_XoffSent : Specifies whether transmission is waiting because the XOFF character was transmitted.
Transmission halts when the XOFF character is transmitted to a system that takes the next
character as XON, regardless of the actual character.
#PB_SerialPort_EOFSent: Specifies whether the end-of-file (EOF) character has been received.

commands.name: SerialPortID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the serial port.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

commands.returnValue:
Returns the ID of the serial port. This function is useful when another library or API commands requires a
serial port reference.

commands.name: SerialPortTimeouts
syntax: SerialPortTimeouts(#SerialPort, RIT, RTTC, RTTM, WTTC, WTTM)
commands.description: Changes the default serial port timeouts.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: RIT
parameters.description:
RIT stands for 'ReadIntervalTimeout'. Specifies the maximum time, in milliseconds, which are allowed to elapse
between the arrival of two characters on the communications line. Default value is 100 ms.

parameters.name: RTTC
parameters.description:
RTTC stands for 'ReadTotalTimeoutConstant'. Specifies the constant, in milliseconds, used to calculate the
total time-out period for read operations. For each read operation, this value is added to the
product of the ReadTotalTimeoutMultiplier member and the requested number of bytes. Default value is 100 ms.

parameters.name: RTTM
parameters.description:
RTTM stands for 'ReadTotalTimeoutMultiplier'. Specifies the multiplier, in milliseconds, used to calculate
the total time-out period for read operations. For each read operation, this value is multiplied
by the requested number of bytes to be read. Default value is 10 ms.

parameters.name: WTTC
parameters.description:
WTTC stands for 'WriteTotalTimeoutConstant'. Specifies the constant, in milliseconds, used to calculate the
total time-out period for write operations. For each write operation, this value is added to the
product of the WriteTotalTimeoutMultiplier member and the number of bytes to be written. Default value is 10 ms.

parameters.name: WTTM
parameters.description:
WTTM stands for 'WriteTotalTimeoutMultiplier'. Specifies the multiplier, in milliseconds, used to calculate the
total time-out period for write operations. For each write operation, this value is multiplied by
the number of bytes to be written. Default value is 100 ms.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SetSerialPortStatus
commands.description: Changes the specified serial port status.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: Attribute
parameters.description:
The attribute to set. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_SerialPort_DTR: set DTR signal status (value can be 0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_RTS: set RTS signal status (value can be 0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_TXD: Set TXD signal status (value can be 0 or 1)
#PB_SerialPort_XonCharacter : Character used for Xon/Xoff handshaking sequence (value can be between 1 and 255). Default value is $11.
#PB_SerialPort_XoffCharacter: Character used for Xon/Xoff handshaking sequence (value can be between 1 and 255). Default value is $13.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The attribute value to set. See 'attribute' description to see which value is applicable.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenSerialPort(0, "COM1", 300, #PB_SerialPort_NoParity, 8, 1, #PB_SerialPort_XonXoffHandshake, 1024, 1024)
    SetSerialPortStatus(0, #PB_SerialPort_XonCharacter, 8)
    SetSerialPortStatus(0, #PB_SerialPort_XoffCharacter, 9)
    Debug "Success"
  Else
    Debug "Failed"
  EndIf

commands.name: WriteSerialPortData
commands.description: Writes an arbitrary amount of data to the specified serial port.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to write.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The buffer length to write, in bytes.

commands.returnValue: The number of bytes written to the serial port, or zero if the operation has failed.
commands.remarks: To check how much data is available in the output buffer, use AvailableSerialPortOutput().

commands.name: WriteSerialPortString
commands.description: Writes a string to the specified serial port.

parameters.name: #SerialPort
parameters.description: The serial port to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to write.

parameters.name: Format (optional)
parameters.description:
The string format to use. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Ascii : the string will be written in ascii format.
#PB_UTF8 : the string will be written in UTF8 format (default).
#PB_Unicode : the string will be written in unicode (UTF16) format.

commands.returnValue: The number of bytes written to the serial port, or zero if the operation has failed.
commands.remarks: To check how much data is available in the output buffer, use AvailableSerialPortOutput().

commands.name: AddSkeletonAnimationKeyFrame
syntax: AddSkeletonAnimationKeyFrame(#Mesh, AnimationName$, Bone$, Time, RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ, RotationW, Mode [, TranslateX, TranslateY, TranslateZ [, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ]])
commands.description: Creates a new step for the specified animation. A skeleton animation can be created with CreateSkeletonAnimation().

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: AnimationName$
parameters.description: The name of the animation to add the step.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description: The bone name to use.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description:
The time in the animation to set the keyframe (in milliseconds). This value has to be between zero and the 'Length'
defined in CreateSkeletonAnimation().

parameters.name: RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ, RotationW
parameters.description: The bone rotation for this step.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The mode to use for the bone rotation. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Orientation_PitchYawRoll : 'RotationX' (pitch), 'RotationY' (yaw), 'RotationZ' (roll), applied in this order (default).
#PB_Orientation_Quaternion : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ', 'RotationW' for quaternion values
#PB_Orientation_AngleAxis : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for rotation axis, and 'RotationW' for the angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_Direction : alias for #PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZN
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVX : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector X), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVY : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector Y), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZ : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector Z), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVXN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -X), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVYN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -Y), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -Z), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).

parameters.name: TranslateX, TranslateY, TranslateZ (optional)
parameters.description: The bone translation for this step.

parameters.name: ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ (optional)
parameters.description: The bone scale for this step.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateBone
syntax: CreateBone(#Mesh, Bone$, ParentBone$, x, y, z, RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ, RotationW, Mode)
commands.description: Creates a new bone for the specified #Mesh. If the mesh doesn't have a skeleton, it has to be created with CreateSkeleton() before using this command.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: Bone$
parameters.description: The new bone name.

parameters.name: ParentBone$
parameters.description: The parent bone name. If this string value is empty, the bone is created at the root of the skeleton.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The new bone coordinate, in world unit.

parameters.name: RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ, RotationW
parameters.description: The new bone rotation.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
The mode to use for the bone rotation. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Orientation_PitchYawRoll : 'RotationX' (pitch), 'RotationY' (yaw), 'RotationZ' (roll), applied in this order (default).
#PB_Orientation_Quaternion : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ', 'RotationW' for quaternion values
#PB_Orientation_AngleAxis : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for rotation axis, and 'RotationW' for the angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_Direction : alias for #PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZN
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVX : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector X), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVY : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector Y), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZ : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector Z), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVXN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -X), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVYN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -Y), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).
#PB_Orientation_DirectionLDVZN: 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector (local direction vector -Z), and 'RotationW' for angle (in degree).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateSkeleton
commands.description: Creates or replaces the skeleton of the #Mesh.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new mesh. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateSkeletonAnimation
commands.description:
Creates a new skeleton animation. A skeleton has to be created for this mesh with CreateSkeleton().
The new animation is empty and steps have to be created with AddSkeletonAnimationKeyFrame().

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: AnimationName$
parameters.description: The name of the animation.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: The length of the animation (in milliseconds).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FinishBoneAssignment
commands.description: Finish bone assignments for a mesh, previously started with VertexBoneAssignment().

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh
parameters.description: The submesh to use. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: VertexBoneAssignment
commands.description:
Assign a vertex to a bone (the same vertex can be assigned to several bones: the sum of
bone weight must be equals to 1). Once the vertex assignment is finished, FinishBoneAssignment() has to be called.

parameters.name: #Mesh
parameters.description: The mesh to use.

parameters.name: SubMesh
parameters.description: The submesh to get the data from. The first submesh index is 0 (main mesh).

parameters.name: VertexIndex
parameters.description: The vertex index. The first index is 0.

parameters.name: BoneIndex
parameters.description: The bone index, in creation order. The first index is 0.

parameters.name: Weight
parameters.description: The bone weight, must be between 0 and 1.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CustomSortArray
commands.description:
Sorts the specified array, according to the given options using a custom procedure
to compare array elements. The array may have a structure or one of
basic type: byte, word, long, integer, string or float.
Multi-dimensioned arrays are not supported.

parameters.name: ArrayName()
parameters.description: The array to sort.

parameters.name: @CompareProcedure()
parameters.description:
The address of a procedure to compare array elements. The procedure must have two parameters that will receive
the memory address of the two elements to compare and return one of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Greater: The first element is greater than the second one.
#PB_Sort_Equal : Both elements are equal.
#PB_Sort_Lesser : The first element is lesser than the second one.

The compare procedure is called very often during the sorting process so it should do as little work as possible and
be fast to execute.

parameters.name: Options (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Ascending : Sort the array in ascending order (lower values first). This is the default.
#PB_Sort_Descending: Sort the array in descending order (higher values first)

parameters.name: Start, End (optional)
parameters.description:
The index of the first and last element in the array that should be sorted. If these parameters
are not specified, then the whole array is sorted.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Structure CustomStruct
    Value$
  EndStructure
  
  ; Sort by numeric value in the string element in the structure
  Procedure CustomCompare(*a.CustomStruct, *b.CustomStruct)
    If Val(*a\Value$) < Val(*b\Value$)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Lesser
    ElseIf Val(*a\Value$) > Val(*b\Value$)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Greater
    Else
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Equal
    EndIf
  EndProcedure
  
  Dim Test.CustomStruct(6)
  
  Test(0)\Value$ = "0005"
  Test(1)\Value$ = "2"
  Test(2)\Value$ = "42"
  Test(3)\Value$ = "7"
  Test(4)\Value$ = "23"
  Test(5)\Value$ = "100"
  Test(6)\Value$ = "101"
  
  CustomSortArray(Test(), @CustomCompare(), #PB_Sort_Ascending)
  
  For i = 0 To 6
    Debug Test(i)\Value$
  Next

; Sort float elements by absolute value (ignoring the sign)
  Procedure AbsCompare(*a.Float, *b.Float)
    If Abs(*a\f) < Abs(*b\f)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Lesser
    ElseIf Abs(*a\f) > Abs(*b\f)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Greater
    Else
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Equal
    EndIf
  EndProcedure
  
  Dim Test.f(4)
  Test(0) = 2.5
  Test(1) = -3.0
  Test(2) = 0
  Test(3) = 12
  Test(4) = -100
  
  CustomSortArray(Test(), @AbsCompare())
  
  For i = 0 To 4
    Debug Test(i)
  Next

commands.name: CustomSortList
commands.description:
Sorts the specified list, according to the given options using a custom procedure
to compare list elements. The list may have a structure or one of
basic type: byte, word, long, integer, string or float.

parameters.name: ListName()
parameters.description: The list to sort.

parameters.name: @CompareProcedure()
parameters.description:
The address of a procedure to compare list elements. The procedure must have two parameters that will receive
the memory address of the two elements to compare and return one of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Greater: The first element is greater than the second one.
#PB_Sort_Equal : Both elements are equal.
#PB_Sort_Lesser : The first element is lesser than the second one.

The compare procedure is called very often during the sorting process so it should do as little work as possible and
be fast to execute.

parameters.name: Options (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Ascending : Sort the list in ascending order (lower values first). This is the default.
#PB_Sort_Descending: Sort the list in descending order (higher values first)

parameters.name: Start, End (optional)
parameters.description:
The index of the first and last element in the list that should be sorted. If these parameters
are not specified, then the whole list is sorted.

The first list element is at position 0, the next at 1 and so on.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
Structure CustomStruct
    Value$
  EndStructure
  
  ; Sort by numeric value in the string element in the structure
  Procedure CustomCompare(*a.CustomStruct, *b.CustomStruct)
    If Val(*a\Value$) < Val(*b\Value$)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Lesser
    ElseIf Val(*a\Value$) > Val(*b\Value$)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Greater
    Else
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Equal
    EndIf
  EndProcedure
  
  NewList Test.CustomStruct()
  
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "0005"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "2"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "42"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "7"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "23"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "100"
  AddElement(Test()) : Test()\Value$ = "101"
  
  CustomSortList(Test(), @CustomCompare(), #PB_Sort_Ascending)
  
  ForEach Test()
    Debug Test()\Value$
  Next

; Sort float elements by absolute value (ignoring the sign)
  Procedure AbsCompare(*a.Float, *b.Float)
    If Abs(*a\f) < Abs(*b\f)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Lesser
    ElseIf Abs(*a\f) > Abs(*b\f)
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Greater
    Else
      ProcedureReturn #PB_Sort_Equal
    EndIf
  EndProcedure
  
  NewList Test.f()
  AddElement(Test()) : Test() = 2.5
  AddElement(Test()) : Test() = -3.0
  AddElement(Test()) : Test() = 0
  AddElement(Test()) : Test() = 12
  AddElement(Test()) : Test() = -100
  
  CustomSortList(Test(), @AbsCompare())
  
  ForEach Test()
    Debug Test()
  Next

commands.name: SortArray
commands.description:
Sorts the specified array, according to the given options. The array may be of one of
basic type: byte, word, long, integer, string or float. For structured
arrays, use SortStructuredArray(). Multi-dimensioned arrays are not supported.

parameters.name: ArrayName()
parameters.description: The array to sort.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Ascending : Sort the array in ascending order (lower values first)
#PB_Sort_Descending: Sort the array in descending order (higher values first)
#PB_Sort_NoCase : Sort the string array without case sensitivity (a=A, b=B etc..)

parameters.name: Start, End (optional)
parameters.description:
The index of the first and last element in the array that should be sorted. If these parameters
are not specified, then the whole array is sorted.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Fixed strings are not supported by the sort routine. If an array is not fully filled, then null elements will be sorted first in ascending order and
last in descending order.

NaN numbers are not accepted when sorting as it produces random results.

commands.name: SortList
commands.description:
Sorts the specified list, according to the given options. The list may be of one of
basic type: byte, word, long, integer, string or float.
For structured list, use SortStructuredList().

#PB_Sort_Ascending : Sort the list in ascending order (lower values first)

#PB_Sort_NoCase : Sort the string list without case sensitivity (a=A, b=B etc..)

parameters.name: Start, End (optional)
parameters.description:
The index of the first and last element in the list that should be sorted. If these parameters
are not specified, then the whole list is sorted.

The first list element is at position 0, the next at 1 and so on.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SortStructuredArray
syntax: SortStructuredArray(ArrayName(), Options, OffsetOf(Structure\Field), TypeOf(Structure\Field) [, Start, End])
commands.description:
Sorts the specified structured array, according to the given options.
The array must have an associated structure.

parameters.name: ArrayName()
parameters.description: The array to sort.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_Sort_Ascending : Sort the array in ascending order (lower values first)
#PB_Sort_Descending: Sort the array in descending order (higher values first)
#PB_Sort_NoCase : Sort the string array without case sensitivity (a=A, b=B etc..)

parameters.name: OffsetOf(Structure\Field)
parameters.description:
Offset of the field in the structure.
OffsetOf() may be used to retrieve the field offset in the structure associated to the array.

parameters.name: TypeOf(Structure\Field)
parameters.description:
The field type of the field in the structure. It has to match the real structure field type.
TypeOf() may be used to automatically retrieve the field type.
Available types are:

#PB_Byte : The structure field to sort is a byte (.b)
#PB_Word : The structure field to sort is a word (.w)
#PB_Long : The structure field to sort is a long (.l)
#PB_String : The structure field to sort is a string (.s or $, fixed strings are not supported)
#PB_Float : The structure field to sort is a float (.f)
#PB_Double : The structure field to sort is a double (.d)
#PB_Quad : The structure field to sort is a quad (.q)
#PB_Character: The structure field to sort is a character (.c)
#PB_Integer : The structure field to sort is an integer (.i)
#PB_Ascii : The structure field to sort is an ascii character (.a)
#PB_Unicode : The structure field to sort is a unicode character (.u)

parameters.name: Start, End (optional)
parameters.description:
The index of the first and last element in the array that should be sorted. If these parameters
are not specified, then the whole array is sorted.

commands.remarks:
Fixed strings are not supported by the sort routine.
If an array is not fully filled, then null elements will be sorted first in ascending order and last in descending order.

NaN numbers are not accepted when sorting as it produces random results.
commands.example:
Structure Animal
    Name$
    Speed.l
  EndStructure

  Dim Animals.Animal(2)

  Animals(0)\Name$ = "Tiger"
  Animals(0)\Speed = 10

  Animals(1)\Name$ = "Jaguar"
  Animals(1)\Speed = 40

  Animals(2)\Name$ = "Zebra"
  Animals(2)\Speed = 30

  SortStructuredArray(Animals(), 0, OffsetOf(Animal\Name$), TypeOf(Animal\Name$))

  For k=0 To 2
    Debug Animals(k)\Name$+" - Speed: "+Str(Animals(k)\Speed)
  Next

  SortStructuredArray(Animals(), 0, OffsetOf(Animal\Speed), TypeOf(Animal\Speed))

  For k=0 To 2
    Debug Animals(k)\Name$+" - Speed: "+Str(Animals(k)\Speed)
  Next
