commands.name: CatchSound
commands.description:
Load a WAV (in PCM format, ADPCM is not supported) or any other format supported by the SoundPlugin library
found at the specified address. The following functions can be used to enable automatically more sound formats:

UseFLACSoundDecoder()

UseOGGSoundDecoder()

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new sound. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: *Buffer
parameters.description: The buffer to use to create the sound. This is a regular memory address.

parameters.name: Size (optional)
parameters.description:
The buffer size (in bytes). With WAV files, this parameter doesn't need to be
specified. With other sound decoders, it has to be specified.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be the following value:

#PB_Sound_Streaming: Enable streaming playback (only supported for FLAC and OGG))

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the sound has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
The "?" is a pointer to a label. More information about pointers and memory access can be found
in the relating chapter here.
commands.example:
CatchSound(0, ?Music)
  End

  DataSection
    Music: 
      IncludeBinary "Sound.wav"

commands.name: FreeSound
commands.description:
Stops and removes a sound previously loaded with LoadSound() or CatchSound() from memory. Once a sound has been
freed, it can't be played anymore.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining sounds are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining sounds are automatically freed when the program ends.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home + "Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing 
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: GetSoundFrequency
commands.description: Get the current frequency of the sound.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to use. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag.

commands.returnValue: Returns the current frequency (in Hz) of the sound.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop, 20)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "The average frequency is " + Str(GetSoundFrequency(0))+" Hz")
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: GetSoundPosition
commands.description: Get the current sound position.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode used to get the position. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Sound_Frame : the position is returned in frame (default).
#PB_Sound_Millisecond: the position is returned in milliseconds.

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to get the position. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag.

commands.returnValue: The current sound position or -1 if an error occurred.
commands.remarks: Sounds loaded with the #PB_Sound_Streaming flag are not supported.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads 2 sounds
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home + "Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      If LoadSound(1, #PB_Compiler_Home + "Examples/3D/Data/Roar.ogg")
        
        ; The siren is playing 
        PlaySound(0)
        
        ; Display the position
        Repeat
          Pos = GetSoundPosition(0, #PB_Sound_Millisecond)
          Delay(100)     ; Wait 100 ms
          Debug Pos      ; Display the position
          If Pos > 1000  ; Stop after 1 second
            Break
          EndIf
        ForEver
        
        ; Then 2 sounds are playing together
        PlaySound(1)
        
        MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.") 
        End
      EndIf
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: InitSound
commands.description:
Initializes the sound environment. This function must be always called before
any other sound function and should always check its result. If the sound environment fails,
it's absolutely necessary to disable all the sound functions calls.

parameters.name: NbMaxChannels (optional)
parameters.description:
Sets the maximum number of channels to use simultaneously to play sounds. It can range from 1 to 254 (the default value if this
parameter is not specified is 64).

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the sound environment has been setup correctly, zero otherwise (for example if no sound card is available).
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop) ; Start playing the sound in a loop
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
    EndIf
    End
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: IsSound

If IsSound(0) = 0
    MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is not valid.") 
  EndIf

If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system

    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")

  EndIf

commands.name: PauseSound

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to use. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag. If #PB_All is specified, all the channels of the sound are paused.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: Sounds loaded with the #PB_Sound_Streaming flag are not supported.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to pause.")
      PauseSound(0)  ; Pause
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to resume.")

      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: PlaySound
commands.description: Start to play the specified sound.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to play.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

0 : no flag
#PB_Sound_Loop : play the sound continuously (starts again when end is reached)
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel: play the sound in a new channel instead of stopping the
previously played sound. This allows to use the same sound and to play it on different
channels at once. 'Result' will be new allocated channel, and can be used by the
other sound commands like SoundVolume(), SoundPan() etc.

parameters.name: Volume (optional)
parameters.description:
Sets the initial volume of the #Sound. The valid values are from 0 (no volume) to 100 (full volume).
The default value is 100.

commands.returnValue: The channel number, if the #PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag is used.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop, 20)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
    EndIf
    End
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: SetSoundFrequency
commands.description:
Set the new frequency, in real-time, for the sound.
The new frequency value is saved for the sound, so it's not needed to call it every time.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Frequency
parameters.description: The sound new frequency (in Hz) to set. Valid values are from 1000 Hz to 100000 Hz.

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to use. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag. If #PB_All is specified, all the channels of the sound are affected.

commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system

      MessageRequester("Info", "The average frequency is " + Str(GetSoundFrequency(0))+" Hz")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home + "Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      
      ; The siren is playing
      PlaySound(0)
      
      ; Change the position at 2 seconds
      SetSoundPosition(0, 2000, #PB_Sound_Millisecond)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "Ok to stop.") 
      End 
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: SoundLength
commands.description: Get the length of the sound.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The mode used to get the length. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Sound_Frame : the length is returned in frame (default).
#PB_Sound_Millisecond: the length is returned in milliseconds.

commands.returnValue: The length of the sound, or -1 if an error occurred.
commands.remarks: Sounds loaded with the #PB_Sound_Streaming flag are not supported.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop, 20)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "The length of the sound is "+ Str(SoundLength(0)) + " frames.")
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "The length of the sound is "+ Str(SoundLength(0, #PB_Sound_Millisecond)) + " ms.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: SoundPan
commands.description:
Sets the new pan value, in real-time, for the #Sound. The pan value is saved for the #Sound, so it's not
needed to call it every time. The panning is a way to play a sound on a stereo equipment.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Pan
parameters.description:
The new pan value. Valid values are from -100 (full left) to 100 (full right).
If the pan value is zero, then the sound is played on right and left speaker, equally.

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to use. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop, 20)
      
      MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is playing in stereo.")
      
      SoundPan(0, -100)
      MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is playing only on the left channel.")
      
      SoundPan(0, 100)
      MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is playing only on the right channel.")
      
      SoundPan(0, 0)
      MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is playing in stereo.")
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: SoundStatus
commands.description: Get the current sound status.

parameters.name: #Sound
parameters.description: The sound to use.

parameters.name: Channel (optional)
parameters.description:
The channel to use. It's the value returned by PlaySound() when using the
#PB_Sound_MultiChannel flag.

commands.returnValue:
The current sound status. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_Sound_Stopped: the sound is stopped.
#PB_Sound_Playing: the sound is playing.
#PB_Sound_Paused : the sound is paused.
#PB_Sound_Unknown: the sound is in an unknown state (an error occurred when getting the state).
commands.example:
Procedure SelectStatus(Status)
    Select Status
      Case #PB_Sound_Stopped
        MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is stopped.")
        
      Case #PB_Sound_Playing
        MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is playing.")
        
      Case  #PB_Sound_Paused
        MessageRequester("Info", "The sound is paused.")
        
      Case #PB_Sound_Unknown
        MessageRequester("Info", "Status unknown.")
        
      Default
        MessageRequester("Info", "Status unknown.")
        
    EndSelect
  EndProcedure
  
  If InitSound()           ; Initialize Sound system
    UseOGGSoundDecoder()   ; Use ogg files
    
    ; Loads a sound from a file
    If LoadSound(0, #PB_Compiler_Home +"Examples/3D/Data/Siren.ogg")
      ; The sound is playing
      PlaySound(0, #PB_Sound_Loop, 20)
      SelectStatus(SoundStatus(0))
      
      PauseSound(0)
      SelectStatus(SoundStatus(0))
      
      ResumeSound(0)
      SelectStatus(SoundStatus(0))
      
      StopSound(0)
      SelectStatus(SoundStatus(0))
      
      FreeSound(0) ; The sound is freed
      End
    EndIf
  Else
    Debug "Warning! The sound environment couldn't be initialized. So no sound commands can be used..."
  EndIf

commands.name: FreeSound3D

Stop and remove a 3D sound previously loaded with LoadSound3D() from memory. Once a sound has been
freed, it can't be played anymore.

parameters.description: The 3D sound to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining 3D sounds are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: IsSound3D
commands.description: Tests if the given sound is valid and correctly initialized.

parameters.name: #Sound3D
parameters.description: The sound to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the sound is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a sound is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadSound3D
commands.description: Loads a mono WAV or OGG sound file. The sound has to be mono, as stereo sounds don't allow spacial positioning.

parameters.name: #Sound3D
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new sound.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The sound filename to load.

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be the following value:

#PB_Sound3D_Streaming: Enable sound streaming playback

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the sound has been successfully loaded, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
A sound doesn't hold its position. It can be attached to a node object to have its own position.

parameters.name: #Sound3D

parameters.name: Flags (optional)

It can be the following value:

#PB_Sound3D_Loop: play the sound continuously (starts again when end is reached)

parameters.name: Maximum

The distance from the sound location when the sound can still be heard. Above this distance, the sound will

parameters.name: #Sound3D

parameters.name: Volume

commands.name: StopSound3D
commands.description: Stops the specified sound (if it was playing).

parameters.name: #Sound3D

are stopped.

commands.name: UseFLACSoundDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) sound support for CatchSound() and LoadSound().
Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Since FLAC is a non-destructive compression codec, the file size will remain quite large, especially compared to
OGG for example. This allows for a reduction in file size, while still retaining all the
original sound information.

For more information: Wikipedia - FLAC.

commands.name: UseOGGSoundDecoder
commands.description:
Enables the OGG (OGG Vorbis) sound support for CatchSound() and LoadSound().
Sound streaming is supported for this plug-in.
commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The OGG format uses destructive compression (lossy) which entails the loss of some of the original information when it is compressed.
This is actually one of the best lossy compression algorithms available, which can dramatically decrease the sound file size without
the introduction of unnecessary audio artifacts.

For more information: Wikipedia - OGG.

commands.name: CatchSprite
commands.description:
Loads the specified sprite from the given memory area.
A screen should be opened with OpenScreen() or OpenWindowedScreen() before loading a sprite.
Sprites can be in BMP format or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library.
A catched sprite can be freed by using the FreeSprite() function. The 'CatchSprite' function is useful when
using the 'IncludeBinary' PureBasic keyword. The images can be packed inside
the executable. Nevertheless, use this option very carefully, as it will take
more memory than storing the file in an external file (the file will be in both
executable memory and loaded into physical memory).

The following functions can be used to enable automatically more image formats:

UseJPEGImageDecoder()

UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder()

UsePNGImageDecoder()

UseTIFFImageDecoder()

UseTGAImageDecoder()

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new sprite. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: *MemoryAddress
parameters.description: The memory address holding the image used to create the sprite.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values (with the '|' operator):

#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision: Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision().
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending : Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite().
The image format has to support it (only PNG and TIFF for now).

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the sprite has been created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
The "?" is a pointer to a label. More information about pointers and memory access can be found
in the relating chapter here.
commands.example:
Debug CatchSprite(0, ?Pic)

  DataSection
    Pic: 
      IncludeBinary "Sprite.bmp"
  EndDataSection

commands.name: ClipSprite
commands.description:
Adds a clip zone to the specified sprite. For example, if a sprite is 100*100 (Width*Height) and
a clipping zone is added as x=10, y=10, Width=20, Height=20 then when the sprite is displayed, only the rectangular
area starting from x=10, y=10 with width=20 and height=20 will be displayed.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to clip.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The clipping start position (in pixels). #PB_Default can be used as value to remove the clipping.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The clipping size (in pixels). #PB_Default can be used as value to remove the clipping.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
On some older gfx cards the clipping with ClipSprite() doesn't work properly,
if the sprite is larger than the used screen.

commands.name: CopySprite
commands.description: Copy the #Sprite1 to #Sprite2.

parameters.name: #Sprite1
parameters.description: The source sprite to copy.

parameters.name: #Sprite2
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new copied sprite. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number. If #Sprite2 doesn't exists, it is created.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values (with the '|' operator):

#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision: Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision().
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending : Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite().

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the sprite has been copied, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Sprite2 parameter then the generated number is returned on success.

commands.name: CreateSprite
commands.description:
Creates an empty sprite with the specified dimensions. SpriteOutput() can be used
to draw on the sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new sprite. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The size of the new sprite (in pixels).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values (with the '|' operator):

#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision: Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision().
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending : Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite().
#PB_Sprite_Transparent : Sprite is created fully transparent (alpha channel value set to 0). If used, DrawingMode() should be set to #PB_DrawingMode_AllChannels when using SpriteOutput().

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the sprite has been created, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks: CreateSprite() has to be called in the same thread where OpenScreen() was called.
commands.example:
InitSprite()
   
  OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 640, 480, "A screen in a window...", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_SizeGadget | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered)
  If OpenWindowedScreen(WindowID(0), 0, 0, 640, 480, #True, 0, 0)
    
    CreateSprite(0, 64, 64, #PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending | #PB_Sprite_Transparent)
    If StartDrawing(SpriteOutput(0))
      DrawingMode(#PB_2DDrawing_AllChannels)
      Circle(16, 16, 8, RGBA(255, 0, 0, 255)) ; Opaque red circle
      Circle(32, 32, 8, RGBA(0, 255, 0, 128)) ; Semi transparent green circle
      StopDrawing()
    EndIf
      
    Repeat
      Repeat ; It's very important to process all the events remaining in the queue at each frame
        Event = WindowEvent()
        If Event = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
          End
        EndIf
      Until Event = 0
      
      ClearScreen(RGB(128, 128, 128)) ; Grey background
      
      DisplayTransparentSprite(0, 300, 200)
      
      FlipBuffers()
    ForEver
        
  Else
    Debug "Can't open windowed screen!"
  EndIf

commands.name: DisplaySprite
commands.description:
Displays the #Sprite at the specified position on the current screen.
As there is no transparent color or blending, this function is faster than DisplayTransparentSprite().
This function is clipped, so it's perfectly legal to display the sprite outside of the screen.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to display.

parameters.name: x.f, y.f
parameters.description:
The coordinate (in pixels) in the screen where the sprite will be displayed.
They can be specified as float numbers to be between physical pixels, the engine
will automatically interpolate the sprite to smooth the display (not supported on DirectX9 and DirectX11 subsystems).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: DisplayTransparentSprite
commands.description:
Display the #Sprite at the specified position on the current screen. The default
transparent color is 0 (black - this color will not be displayed).
It's possible to change the transparent color with TransparentSpriteColor().
This function is clipped, so it's perfectly legal to display the sprite outside of the screen.
The sprite has to be created with #PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending flag to use this command.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to display.

parameters.name: x.f, y.f
parameters.description:
The coordinate (in pixels) in the screen where the sprite will be displayed.
They can be specified as float numbers to be between physical pixels, the engine
will automatically interpolate the sprite to smooth the display (not supported on DirectX9 and DirectX11 subsystems).

parameters.name: Intensity (optional)
parameters.description:
The intensity level used to display the sprite. Valid value are from 0 (fully transparent)
to 255 (fully opaque). Default value is 255.

parameters.name: Color (optional)
parameters.description:
The solid color used to display the sprite. The sprite will be rendered in only one color.
To get a valid color, use RGB().

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: FreeSprite
commands.description: Removes the specified sprite from memory. It's not possible to use the sprite anymore after calling this function.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining sprites are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining sprites are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GrabSprite
syntax: Result = GrabSprite(#Sprite, x, y, Width, Height [, Flags])
commands.description: Grabs the screen content from the area x, y, Width, Height and creates a new sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new grabbed sprite. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: The position in the screen used to start the grab (in pixels).

parameters.name: Width, Height
parameters.description: The size of the grab (in pixels).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values (with the '|' operator):

#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision: Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision().
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending : Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite(). The default transparent color
set with TransparentSpriteColor() is automatically applied.

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the sprite has been grabbed, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
GrabSprite() should be always called outside a StartDrawing() : StopDrawing() block.

The transparent sprite color is automatically applied when using AlphaBlending flag.

commands.name: InitSprite
commands.description:
Initializes the sprite environment for later use. You must put this function at
the top of your source code if you want to use the sprite functions.
commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the initialization of the sprite environment has succeeded, zero otherwise.
You should always test this result to see if the sprite environment has been correctly
initialized. If not you must quit the program or disable all the calls to the sprite
related functions.

This function tries to initialize DirectX 9, so if it fails,
it's probably because DirectX is not found or is a previous version.

commands.name: IsSprite
commands.description: Tests if the given #Sprite number is a valid and correctly initialized, sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to use.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if #Sprite is a valid sprite and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value. If the 'Result' is not zero then the object is valid and
initialized, otherwise it will equal zero. This is the correct way to ensure a sprite is ready to use.

commands.name: LoadSprite
commands.description:
Load the specified sprite into memory for immediate use. A screen should be opened with OpenScreen() or
OpenWindowedScreen() before loading a sprite.

The sprite can be in BMP format or any other format supported by the ImagePlugin library.
The following functions can be used to enable automatically more image formats:

UseGIFImageDecoder()

UseJPEGImageDecoder()

UseJPEG2000ImageDecoder()

UsePNGImageDecoder()

UseTIFFImageDecoder()

UseTGAImageDecoder()

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new loaded sprite. #PB_Any can
be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: Name of the image file used to create the sprite.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values (with the '|' operator):

#PB_Sprite_PixelCollision: Add special information to handle pixel collision through SpritePixelCollision().
#PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending : Sprite is created with per pixel alpha-channel support, needed for DisplayTransparentSprite().
The image format has to support it (only PNG and TIFF for now).

commands.returnValue:
Nonzero if the sprite has been loaded, zero otherwise. If #PB_Any was used
for the #Sprite parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
Sprites shouldn't be larger than the used screenmode. Using larger sprites possibly works on some
hardware, on others not. Better split your large sprite to several smaller ones.

commands.name: RotateSprite
commands.description: Rotates the specified #Sprite to the given 'Angle'.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to rotate.

parameters.name: Angle.f
parameters.description: Angle value, in degree (from 0 to 360). The rotation is performed clockwise.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description:
It can be one the following values:

#PB_Absolute: the angle is set to the new angle.
#PB_Relative: the angle is added to the previous angle value.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SaveSprite
commands.description:
Saves the specified sprite to a file. By default, the saved image will be in 24-bit BMP format.
Very useful for screenshots when used with the GrabSprite() function.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to save.

parameters.name: Filename$
parameters.description: The filename to use for the saved sprite.

parameters.name: ImagePlugin (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following constant:

#PB_ImagePlugin_BMP : Save the image in BMP (default).
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG : Save the image in JPEG (the function UseJPEGImageEncoder() has to be used).
#PB_ImagePlugin_JPEG2000: Save the image in JPEG2000 (the function UseJPEG2000ImageEncoder() has to be used).
#PB_ImagePlugin_PNG : Save the image in PNG (the function UsePNGImageEncoder() has to be used).

parameters.name: Flags (optional)
parameters.description:
Additional control over saving for the specified plug-in. For now, only quality setting is supported:
a number from 0 (worse quality) to 10 (maximum quality). Only the JPEG and JPEG 2000 plugins currently support it (default
quality is set to '7' if no flags are specified).

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the sprite has been successfully saved, zero otherwise.

commands.name: SpriteBlendingMode
commands.description:
Changes the way the sprite are blended with the background (when using DisplayTransparentSprite()).
This function is for advanced users only. The result can differ depending of the underlying subsystem:
for example OpenGL and DirectX doesn't behave the same.

parameters.name: SourceMode, DestinationMode
parameters.description:
Both source and destination mode can be one of the following values:

#PB_Sprite_BlendZero
#PB_Sprite_BlendOne
#PB_Sprite_BlendSourceColor
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertSourceColor
#PB_Sprite_BlendDestinationColor
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertDestinationColor
#PB_Sprite_BlendSourceAlpha
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertSourceAlpha
#PB_Sprite_BlendDestinationAlpha
#PB_Sprite_BlendInvertDestinationAlpha

The default values are SpriteBlendingMode(#PB_Sprite_BlendSourceAlpha, #PB_Sprite_BlendInvertSourceAlpha).

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SpriteCollision
syntax: Result = SpriteCollision(#Sprite1, x1, y1, #Sprite2, x2, y2)
commands.description: Tests if the two sprites are overlapping.

parameters.name: #Sprite1
parameters.description: The first sprite to test.

parameters.name: x1, y1
parameters.description: Coordinates of the first sprite, in pixels.

parameters.name: #Sprite2
parameters.description: The second sprite to test.

parameters.name: x2, y2
parameters.description: Coordinates of the second sprite, in pixels.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the two sprites are overlapping, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This routine compares the rectangular areas around the sprites, giving a very fast
but not very accurate function (depending on the shapes of your sprites).
Very useful for fast arcade games. Zoomed sprites are also supported.

For a more exact collision check use SpritePixelCollision().

commands.name: SpriteDepth
commands.description: Returns the color depth of the specified sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to use.

commands.returnValue: The color depth of the specified sprite.

commands.name: SpriteHeight
commands.description: Returns the height (in pixels) of the specified sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to use.

commands.returnValue: The height (in pixels) of the specified sprite.

commands.name: SpriteID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the given sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to use.

commands.returnValue:
The ID of the sprite. This sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra chapter
"Handles and Numbers" for more information.

commands.name: SpriteOutput
commands.description: Returns the OutputID of the sprite to perform 2D rendering operation on it.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to draw on.

commands.returnValue:
The output ID or zero if drawing is not possible. This value should be passed directly to the
StartDrawing() function to start the drawing operation. The return-value
is valid only for one drawing operation and cannot be reused.
commands.remarks: SpriteOutput() has to be called in the same thread where OpenScreen() was called.
commands.example:
StartDrawing(SpriteOutput(#Sprite))
    ; do some drawing stuff here...
  StopDrawing()

commands.name: SpritePixelCollision
syntax: Result = SpritePixelCollision(#Sprite1, x1, y1, #Sprite2, x2, y2)
commands.description:
Tests if the two sprites are overlapping. #PB_Sprite_PixelCollision
has to be specified at the sprite creation to have this command working.

parameters.name: #Sprite1
parameters.description: The first sprite to test.

parameters.name: x1, y1
parameters.description: Coordinates of the first sprite, in pixels.

parameters.name: #Sprite2
parameters.description: The second sprite to test.

parameters.name: x2, y2
parameters.description: Coordinates of the second sprite, in pixels.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the two sprites are overlapping, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This routine performs a transparent pixel exact collision check, giving a slower but very accurate result.
To optimize the comparison you should always remove as many transparent pixels as possible so that
the sprite size is fully used by the sprite (i.e. do not have large transparent borders around
the actual image of the sprite). Zoomed sprites are also supported.

For a faster collision check based only on rectangular bounds, use SpriteCollision().

Attention, it does not work with sprites that have been rotated or transformed.

commands.name: SpriteQuality
commands.description: Changes the way the sprites are rendered.

parameters.name: Quality
parameters.description:
The display sprite quality. Can be one the following values:

#PB_Sprite_NoFiltering : No filtering, faster but ugly when zooming/rotating (default).
#PB_Sprite_BilinearFiltering: Bilinear filtering, slower but clean when zooming/rotating.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: SpriteWidth
commands.description: Returns the width (in pixels) of the specified sprite.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to use.

commands.returnValue: The width (in pixels) of the specified sprite.

commands.name: TransformSprite
syntax: TransformSprite(#Sprite, x1, y1, [z1], x2, y2, [z2], x3, y3, [z3], x4, y4, [z4])
commands.description:
Transforms the sprite to the new given coordinates. This is typically used to perform
real-time transformations. Warning, as a sprite is a combination of 2 triangles, the transformation
could looks strange. If one of the optional 'z' parameter is specified, all need to be specified.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to transform.

parameters.name: x1, y1
parameters.description: First point coordinate, in pixel

parameters.name: x2, y2
parameters.description: Second point coordinate, in pixel

parameters.name: x3, y3
parameters.description: Third point coordinate, in pixel

parameters.name: x4, y4
parameters.description: Fourth point coordinate, in pixel

parameters.name: z1, z2, z3, z4
parameters.description: The 'z' value, which specify the depth of the points.

commands.name: TransparentSpriteColor
commands.description:
Use the specified color as the transparent sprite color (when displayed with DisplayTransparentSprite()). Only one
color can be set as the transparent color and the previous alpha channel values are lost. If the sprite already have alpha information, this command is probably not needed.
The sprite has to be created with #PB_Sprite_AlphaBlending flag to use this command.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description:
The sprite to use. If #PB_Default is used, then the default color (black - RGB(0,0,0)) is changed to the new given
one and all future loaded or created sprites will use this color as the transparent one.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description:
The new color to handle as transparent color. RGB() can be used to get a valid color value.
A table with common colors is available here.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: ZoomSprite
commands.description: Zooms the specified #Sprite from the given dimension.

parameters.name: #Sprite
parameters.description: The sprite to zoom.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: New sprite width (in pixels). If #PB_Default is specified, the initial sprite width is restored.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: New sprite height (in pixels). If #PB_Default is specified, the initial sprite height is restored.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: AddStaticGeometryEntity
syntax: AddStaticGeometryEntity(#StaticGeometry, EntityID, x, y, z [, ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ [, RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ [, RotationW, Mode]]])
commands.description:
Add an entity to the specified #StaticGeometry. The original entity is left untouched by this function and
can be freed after the add. The same entity can be added multiple times.

parameters.name: #StaticGeometry
parameters.description: StaticGeometry to use.

parameters.name: EntityID
parameters.description: The EntityID of the entity to add to the static geometry.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: The position of the entity in the static geometry.

parameters.name: ScaleX, ScaleY, ScaleZ (optional)
parameters.description: The scale factor to apply to the added entity.

parameters.name: RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ (optional)
parameters.description: The rotation to apply to the added entity.

parameters.name: RotationW (optional)
parameters.description: The rotation to apply to the added entity (only used for #PB_Orientation_Quaternion and #PB_Orientation_Direction).

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
The rotation mode. It can be one of the following values:

#PB_Orientation_PitchYawRoll: 'RotationX' (pitch), 'RotationY' (yaw), 'RotationZ' (roll), applied in this order (default).
#PB_Orientation_Quaternion : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ', 'RotationW' for quaternion values
#PB_Orientation_Direction : 'RotationX', 'RotationY', 'RotationZ' for direction vector, and 'RotationW' for rotation (roll).

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Once all the entities have been added, the command BuildStaticGeometry() has to be called to generate
the static geometry.

commands.name: BuildStaticGeometry
commands.description: Build the final static geometry. Once created, a static geometry can't be modified anymore.

parameters.name: #StaticGeometry
parameters.description: StaticGeometry to use.

commands.returnValue: None.

commands.name: CreateStaticGeometry
syntax: Result = CreateStaticGeometry(#StaticGeometry, Width, Height, Length, EnableShadows)
commands.description: Create an empty static geometry.

parameters.name: #StaticGeometry
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new static geometry. #PB_Any
can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Width (in world unit) of the static geometry.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: Height (in world unit) of the static geometry.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: Length (in world unit) of the static geometry.

parameters.name: EnableShadows
parameters.description: Enables or disables dynamic shadows casting on the static geometry. Set to #True to enable it, #False otherwise.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the static geometry has been successfully created and zero if not. If #PB_Any
was used for the #StaticGeometry parameter then the generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
If another static geometry was previously loaded with the same #StaticGeometry number, then the
older static geometry will be automatically freed when creating the new one.

commands.name: FreeStaticGeometry
commands.description: Free the given StaticGeometry, previously initialized by CreateStaticGeometry().

parameters.name: #StaticGeometry
parameters.description: The static geometry to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining static geometries are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining static geometries are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: IsStaticGeometry
commands.description: Tests if the given #StaticGeometry is a valid and correctly initialized static geometry.

parameters.name: #StaticGeometry
parameters.description: The static geometry to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #StaticGeometry is a valid static geometry and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks:
This function is bulletproof and can be used with any value.
If Result is not zero then the object is valid and initialized,
otherwise it returns zero. This is a good way to check that a static geometry is ready to use.

commands.name: AddStatusBarField
commands.description:
Adds a field to the current status bar previously created with CreateStatusBar().
Each new field is created after the previous one.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description:
The width of the new field in pixels. If set to #PB_Ignore then the field
will be resized to fill the remaining free space on the status bar. Multiple fields can have a width of #PB_Ignore,
in which case the free space will be divided evenly among these fields.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
The following commands can be used to set or change the content of the status bar field:

- StatusBarText()

- StatusBarImage()

- StatusBarProgress()

See CreateStatusBar() for an example.

commands.name: CreateStatusBar
commands.description:
Create and add an empty #StatusBar to the specified WindowID.
Once the bar is created, AddStatusBarField() can be
used to setup the different parts of the bar.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description:
A number to identify the new status bar.
#PB_Any can be used to auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: WindowID
parameters.description: The window on which the status bar should be created. WindowID() can be used to get this value.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the status bar has been successfully created, zero otherwise.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 440, 50, "StatusBar", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered | #PB_Window_SizeGadget)
    If CreateStatusBar(0, WindowID(0))
      AddStatusBarField(90)
      AddStatusBarField(100)
      AddStatusBarField(#PB_Ignore) ; automatically resize this field
      AddStatusBarField(100)
    EndIf

    StatusBarText(0, 0, "Area normal")
    StatusBarText(0, 1, "Area borderless", #PB_StatusBar_BorderLess)
    StatusBarText(0, 2, "Area right", #PB_StatusBar_Right) 
    StatusBarText(0, 3, "Area centered", #PB_StatusBar_Center)

    Repeat
    Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: FreeStatusBar
commands.description: Free the given status bar.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining status bars are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks: All remaining status bars are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: IsStatusBar
commands.description: Tests if the given status bar number is a valid and correctly initialized status bar.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar number to test.

commands.returnValue: Nonzero if the status bar is valid, zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a status bar is ready to use.

commands.name: StatusBarHeight
commands.description:
Returns the height in pixel of the #StatusBar. This is useful for correct calculation on window height
when using a statusbar.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to use.

commands.returnValue: The height in pixels of the status bar.

commands.name: StatusBarID
commands.description: Returns the unique system identifier of the status bar.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to use.

commands.returnValue:
The system identifier. This result is sometimes also known as 'Handle'. Look at the extra
chapter Handles and Numbers for more information.

commands.name: StatusBarImage
commands.description: Sets the specified status bar field to display an image.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to use.

parameters.name: Field
parameters.description: The index of the field to put the image on. The first field index starts from zero.

parameters.name: ImageID
parameters.description: The image to set to the specified status bar field. It can be easily obtained by using ImageID().

parameters.name: Appearance (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be used to alter the look of the field with the following values:

#PB_StatusBar_Raised : raised borders (has no effect on OS X and Windows with theme enabled)
#PB_StatusBar_BorderLess: without border
#PB_StatusBar_Center : center the icon in the field
#PB_StatusBar_Right : align the icon to the right of the field

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 340, 50, "StatusBarImage", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered | #PB_Window_SizeGadget)
    If CreateStatusBar(0, WindowID(0))
      AddStatusBarField(120)
      AddStatusBarField(170)
    EndIf

    If LoadImage(0, "cube16.ico")     ; change path/filename to your own image (or icon)
      StatusBarImage(0, 0, ImageID(0))
      StatusBarImage(0, 1, ImageID(0), #PB_StatusBar_Right) 
    EndIf  

    Repeat
    Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: StatusBarProgress
syntax: StatusBarProgress(#StatusBar, Field, Value [, Appearance [, Min, Max]])
commands.description: Display a progress bar in the specified 'Field' in the given '#StatusBar'.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to use.

parameters.name: Field
parameters.description: The field index to set the progress bar. The first field index starts from zero.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description:
This specifies the current progress (relative to the current minimum and maximum).
To update this value simply call this command again with a different value.

parameters.name: Appearance (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be used to alter the look of the field with the following values:

#PB_StatusBar_Raised : raised borders (has no effect on OS X and Windows with theme enabled)
#PB_StatusBar_BorderLess: without border

parameters.name: Min, Max (optional)
parameters.description:
Specifies the boundaries of the progress bar. If they are not specified
or have the value #PB_Ignore then current boundaries will be used.
The default 'Min' and 'Max' values for newly created status bar fields are 0 and 100.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.example:
If OpenWindow(0, 0, 0, 340, 50, "StatusBarProgress", #PB_Window_SystemMenu | #PB_Window_ScreenCentered | #PB_Window_SizeGadget)
    If CreateStatusBar(0, WindowID(0))
      AddStatusBarField(120)
      AddStatusBarField(170)
    EndIf

    StatusBarText(0, 0, "ProgressBar !")
    StatusBarProgress(0, 1, 25)
    
    Repeat
    Until WaitWindowEvent() = #PB_Event_CloseWindow
  EndIf

commands.name: StatusBarText
commands.description: Sets the text for the specified status bar field.

parameters.name: #StatusBar
parameters.description: The status bar to use.

parameters.name: Field
parameters.description: The index of the field to set the text on. The first field index starts from zero.

parameters.name: Text$
parameters.description: The text to set to the specified status bar field.

parameters.name: Appearance (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be used to alter the look of the field with the following values:

#PB_StatusBar_Raised : raised borders (has no effect on OS X and Windows with theme enabled)
#PB_StatusBar_BorderLess: without border
#PB_StatusBar_Center : center the text in the field
#PB_StatusBar_Right : align the text to the right of the field

commands.name: Bin
commands.description: Converts a quad numeric number into a string, in binary format.

parameters.description: The number to convert.

parameters.name: Type (optional)
parameters.description:
If the value should be handled as another type, one of the following value can be specified:

#PB_Quad : The value is handled as a quad number, ranging from 0 to 18446744073709551615 (default)
#PB_Byte : The value is handled as a byte number, ranging from 0 to 255
#PB_Ascii : The value is handled as a ascii character, ranging from 0 to 255
#PB_Word : The value is handled as a word number, ranging from 0 to 65535
#PB_Unicode: The value is handled as a unicode character, ranging from 0 to 65535
#PB_Long : The value is handled as a long number, ranging from 0 to 4294967296

commands.returnValue: A string holding the binary representation of the specified value.

commands.name: Chr
commands.description: Returns a string created with the given character value.

parameters.name: CharacterValue
parameters.description:
The unicode character value. It must be a value between 0 and $D7FF or between $E000 and $FFFF.
The range between $D800 and $DFFF is reserved for surrogate characters.

commands.returnValue: Returns a string created with the given character value. If the value is invalid, it will returns an empty string.
commands.remarks:
A table with all Ascii values and their relating figures may be found here.

This command works in Unicode and then
returns the related characters associated to the given value.

Debug Chr(8364) ; will display "€"
Debug Chr($BC) ; will display "¼"
Debug Chr($BD) ; will display "½"
commands.example:
Debug Chr(33) ; Will display "!"

Debug Chr($2630) ; ☰
  Debug Chr($25BC) ; ▼
  For i = 65 To 90
      Debug Chr(i)
  Next

commands.name: EscapeString

#PB_String_EscapeXML : escape the string using the XML escape characters. This can be useful to easily put any string in a

commands.name: FindString
commands.description: Find the 'StringToFind$' within the given 'String$'.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to use.

parameters.name: StringToFind$
parameters.description: The string to find.

parameters.name: StartPosition (optional)
parameters.description:
The start position to begin the search. The first valid character index is 1.
If this parameter isn't specified, the whole string is searched.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be one of the following values:

#PB_String_CaseSensitive: case sensitive search (A≠a) (default).
#PB_String_NoCase : case insensitive search (A=a).

commands.returnValue:
Returns the position (in character) of the string to find, or zero is the string isn't found. The first character index is 1.

commands.example:
String$ = "This is a simple line...."
  
  Repeat
  Last = Position
  Position = FindString(String$ , "i", Position + 1)
  If Position > 0
    Debug "'i' found at position: " + Position
  EndIf
  Until Not Position
  
  Debug "Last position 'i' was found: " + Last

parameters.description: The string to remove.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:

#PB_String_CaseSensitive: case sensitive remove (A≠a) (default)
#PB_String_NoCase : case insensitive remove (A=a)

syntax: String$ = ReplaceString(String$, StringToFind$, ReplacementString$ [, Mode [, StartPosition [, NbOccurrences]]])
commands.description:
Try to find any occurrences of 'StringToFind$' in the given 'String$' and replace them
with 'ReplacementString$'.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to use.

parameters.name: StringToFind$
parameters.description: The string to find.

parameters.name: ReplacementString$
parameters.description: The string to use as replacement.

parameters.name: Mode (optional)
parameters.description:
It can be a combination of the following values:

#PB_String_CaseSensitive : Case sensitive search (A≠a) (default)
#PB_String_NoCase : Case insensitive search (A=a)

parameters.name: StartPosition (optional)
parameters.description:
Specifies the character position to start the replacement. The first character position is 1.
If omitted the whole string is used.

parameters.name: NbOccurrences (optional)
parameters.description:
Specifies how many strings should be replaced before stopping the operation. If omitted, all strings
are replaced.

commands.returnValue: A new string with the replaced strings.
commands.remarks:
Up to PB6.30 there was a #PB_String_InPlace 'Mode' for in-place replacing, which isn't supported anymore.
For more informations see the Migration from PureBasic 6.30 to 6.40 guide.
commands.example:
Debug ReplaceString("This is Art", " is", " was") ; Will display "This was Art"

  test$ = "Hello again, hello again"
  Result$ = ReplaceString(test$, "HELLO", "oh no...", #PB_String_NoCase, 10) ; Will display "Hello again, oh no... again"
  Debug Result$

commands.name: Str
commands.description: Convert a signed quad number into a string.

parameters.name: Value.q
parameters.description: The value to convert.

commands.returnValue: A string holding the converted value.

Floats must be converted with StrF(), doubles with StrD() and unsigned numbers with StrU().
It is possible to omit this command when concatenating string and integer, it will then use the default behaviour of Str().
commands.example:
Value.q = 100000000000000001
  Debug "Result: " + Str(Value)

commands.name: StrD
commands.description: Converts a double number into a string.

parameters.name: Value.d
parameters.description: The value to convert.

parameters.name: NbDecimal (optional)
parameters.description:
The maximum number of decimal places for the converted number. If omitted, it will be set to 10 decimal places, with removing the trailing zeros.
The number will be rounded to the nearest decimal place (compare with Round()), if 'NbDecimal' is smaller than existing decimal places of 'Value.d'.

Signed integer numbers have to be converted with Str() and unsigned numbers with StrU().
It is possible to omit this command when concatenating string and double, it will then use the default behaviour of StrD().

Value.d = 10.54

  Debug "Result: " + Value           ; same as previous line
  Debug "Result: " + StrD(Value, 2)  ; we want a result with two decimal places, no rounding needed as we have only two
  Debug "Result: " + StrD(Value, 0)  ; we want a result with no decimal places, so the value is rounded

commands.example:
value.f = 10.54

  Debug "Result: " + value          ; same as previous line
  Debug "Result: " + StrF(value,2)  ; we want a result with two decimal places, no rounding needed as we have only two
  Debug "Result: " + StrF(value,0)  ; we want a result with no decimal places, so the value is rounded

commands.name: Val
commands.description:
Converts a string into a quad numeric value. The string may be an integer in
decimal, hexadecimal (with '$' prefix) or binary (with '%' prefix) format.
The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to convert.

commands.returnValue: The numeric value of the string.
commands.remarks: Strings holding a 32-bit floats may be converted with ValF() and 64-bit floats with ValD().
commands.example:
Debug Val("1024102410241024") ; will print '1024102410241024'.
  Debug Val("$10FFFFFFFF")      ; will print '73014444031'.
  Debug Val("%1000")            ; will print '8'.

commands.name: ValD
commands.description:
Converts a string into a double value. The string must be a double in
decimal or in scientific (exponent) format. The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to convert.

commands.returnValue: The double value of the string.
commands.remarks:
Strings holding an integer can also be converted with Val(), and 32-bit floats with ValF() (with less accuracy than ValD()).

"NaN", "-Infinity" and "+Infinity" are allowed.
commands.example:
Debug ValD("10.000024") ; will display 10.000024
  Debug ValD("1.2345e-2") ; will display  0.012345

commands.name: ValF
commands.description:
Converts a string into a float value. The string must be a float in
decimal or in scientific (exponent) format. The number parsing stops at the first non numeric character.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to convert.

commands.returnValue: The float value of the string.
commands.remarks:
Strings holding an integer can also be converted with Val() and 64-bit floats with ValD() (with more accuracy than ValF()).

"NaN", "-Infinity" and "+Infinity" are allowed.
commands.example:
Debug ValF("10.75")     ; will display 10.75
  Debug ValF("1.2345e+3") ; will display 1234.5

commands.name: AppendStringBuilderString
commands.description: Append a string to the end of the current string builder content.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to append.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the string was successfully appended and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
This function efficiently appends the string to the internal buffer, growing the buffer as needed.
Multiple calls to this function can be chained together to build complex strings efficiently.
commands.example:
CreateStringBuilder(0)
  
  For i = 1 To 500
    AppendStringBuilderString(0, "Line " + Str(i))
    AppendStringBuilderString(0, #CRLF$)
  Next
    
  Result$ = GetStringBuilderString(0)
  Debug Result$

commands.name: AppendStringBuilderStringN
commands.description: Append a string and a newline character to the end of the current string builder content.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to use.

parameters.name: String$
parameters.description: The string to append.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the string was successfully appended and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
This function efficiently appends the string and the newline character to the internal buffer, growing the buffer as needed.
Multiple calls to this function can be chained together to build complex strings efficiently.
commands.example:
CreateStringBuilder(0)
  
  For i = 1 To 500
    AppendStringBuilderStringN(0, "Line " + Str(i))
  Next
    
  Result$ = GetStringBuilderString(0)
  Debug Result$

commands.name: CreateStringBuilder
commands.description: Create a new string builder object.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description:
The number to identify the new string builder. #PB_Any can be used to
auto-generate this number.

parameters.name: IncrementLength (optional)
parameters.description:
The length (in characters) by which the internal buffer will grow when more space is needed. If not specified,
a default increment length of 8192 characters will be used.

commands.returnValue:
Returns nonzero if the string builder was created successfully and zero if there was an error.
If #PB_Any was used as the #StringBuilder parameter then the new generated number is returned on success.
commands.remarks:
A new string builder starts with an empty string. Use AppendStringBuilderString() or AppendStringBuilderStringN() to add content to it.
When finished building the string, use GetStringBuilderString() to retrieve the final result.
commands.example:
CreateStringBuilder(0)

  AppendStringBuilderString(0, "Hello ")
  AppendStringBuilderString(0, "World!")
    
  Result$ = GetStringBuilderString(0)
  Debug Result$

commands.name: FreeStringBuilder
commands.description: Free the specified string builder and release its associated memory.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to free. If #PB_All is specified, all the remaining string builders are freed.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Once the string builder is freed, it may not be used anymore.

All remaining opened string builders are automatically freed when the program ends.

commands.name: GetStringBuilderString
commands.description: Get the current built string.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to use.

commands.returnValue: Returns the current built string. If the string builder is empty or invalid, an empty string is returned.
commands.remarks:
This function returns the complete string that has been built through multiple calls to AppendStringBuilderString() or AppendStringBuilderStringN().
After calling this function, it's still possible to continue to append strings to the string builder.

commands.name: IsStringBuilder
commands.description: Test if the given #StringBuilder number is a valid and correctly initialized string builder object.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to check.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if #StringBuilder is a valid string builder and zero otherwise.
commands.remarks: This function is bulletproof and may be used with any value. This is the correct way to ensure a string builder is ready to use.

commands.name: ResetStringBuilder
commands.description: Reset the string builder to an empty string, clearing all previously appended content.

parameters.name: #StringBuilder
parameters.description: The string builder to reset.

commands.returnValue: Returns nonzero if the string builder was successfully reset and zero if there was an error.
commands.remarks:
This function clears the internal buffer and returns the string builder to its initial empty state.
This is useful when you want to reuse a string builder for building a new string.

commands.name: CocoaMessage
syntax: Result = CocoaMessage(ReturnValueAddress, Object, Method$ [, ParameterValue [, Parameter$, [, ParamaterValue, ...]]])
commands.description:
For advanced users. Available on OS X only, it allows to easily send an Objective-C message to the OS X framework and access
any API. Usually Objective-C use brackets to have a clear syntax for messages. As PureBasic doesn't have built-in Objective-C
support, it needs to emulate it, so the syntax is a bit different. Once learnt, it's easy to call the required API.
To get more examples, please read the following thread on the forums.

parameters.name: ReturnValueAddress
parameters.description:
If the API call return a structure or a type different than 'integer', this field is used to set the returning result.
An address to the structure or variable needs to be specified. If zero is specified, the result will be ignored.

parameters.name: Object
parameters.description:
The object on which the Objective-C methods will be called. It can be zero if the method is a static method
(mostly when creating an object).

parameters.name: Method$
parameters.description:
The method to call on the object, usually followed by a semicolon (':'). If the method needs a structure as parameter, '@'
needs to be appended after the semicolon. If the method expect a string as parameter, '$' can be appended after the
semicolon, so the string will be automatically converted in a temporary NSString. This is not required, but it can be useful
and ease the coding. If the method isn't supported by the object, a debugger message will be raised at runtime.

parameters.name: ParameterValue (optional)
parameters.description: The parameter value associated to the previous method.

parameters.name: Parameter$ (optional)
parameters.description: The next method parameter. PureBasic support up to 7 method parameters.

commands.returnValue: Integer return value. Useful for object creation id.
commands.remarks:
PureBasic has already setup a temporary memory pool which is flushed every time WindowEvent() or WaitWindowEvent() is called. If you need
to release big objects immediately, you will have to create a local memory pool around your calls.

commands.name: ComputerName
commands.description: Returns the computer name.
commands.returnValue: Returns the computer name.
commands.example: Debug "Computer name: "+ComputerName()

commands.name: CountCPUs
commands.description: Returns the number of CPU cores available.

parameters.name: Type (optional)
parameters.description:
The CPU type to request. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_System_CPUs : the total number of CPU cores installed in the computer (default).
#PB_System_ProcessCPUs : the available CPU cores for the current process. This is useful as the OS
can limit a process to use only a small number of CPU.

commands.returnValue: Returns the number of CPU cores available.

commands.name: CPUName
commands.description: Returns the name of the CPU.
commands.returnValue:
Returns the name of the CPU (the full vendor information). There is no standardized output across
CPU, so this information shouldn't be used to identify the CPU at runtime, but can be useful for logging
purpose.
commands.example: Debug CPUName() ; Could print: "Intel(R) Core(TM) i7 CPU         860  @ 2.80GHz"

commands.name: Delay
commands.description: Halts the program execution for the specified amount of time.

parameters.name: Time
parameters.description: The delay time in milliseconds. The actual delay may be longer than the specified time.

commands.returnValue: None.
commands.remarks:
Delay is especially useful in event loops with WindowEvent() or
ExamineKeyboard(), so these functions do not "eat" the entire CPU power.

In fact, this function halts the current thread.

commands.name: DoubleClickTime
commands.description:
Returns the system setting for the double-click time. If two mouse clicks happen within this
time, they are considered a double-click.
commands.returnValue: Returns the double-click time in milliseconds.
commands.remarks:
This function can be used to make mouse handling in a screen or CanvasGadget()
consistent with the overall system settings.

commands.name: ElapsedMilliseconds
commands.description:
Returns the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since a specific time
in the past.
commands.returnValue: Returns the elapsed time in milliseconds.
commands.remarks:
The absolute value returned is of no use since it varies depending
on the operating system. Instead, this function should be used to calculate time
differences between multiple ElapsedMilliseconds() calls.

This function is relatively accurate: it may have a slight variation, depending
on which operating system it is executed on, this is due to the fact that some
systems have a lower timer resolution than others.
commands.example:
StartTime.q = ElapsedMilliseconds()     ; Get the actual value
  Delay(1000)                             ; Wait 1000 milliseconds
  Debug ElapsedMilliseconds() - StartTime ; Displayed value should be about 1000 milliseconds

commands.name: MemoryStatus
commands.description: Returns the specified memory type information.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description:
The type of memory to get. It can be one of the following value:

#PB_System_TotalPhysical: the total amount of installed memory, in bytes
#PB_System_FreePhysical : the available memory, in bytes
#PB_System_TotalVirtual : the total virtual memory size, in bytes (Windows only)
#PB_System_FreeVirtual : the available virtual memory size, in bytes (Windows only)
#PB_System_TotalSwap : the total swap memory size, in bytes (Windows and Linux only)
#PB_System_FreeSwap : the available swap memory size, in bytes (Windows and Linux only)
#PB_System_PageSize : the memory page size, in bytes (usually 4KB).

commands.returnValue: Returns the specified memory type information.
